Headlines: New $1 billion fund aims to steer antibiotic companies in tough market
Description: Several large drugmakers including Merck & Co Inc  and Pfizer Inc  on Thursday unveiled a $1 billion fund to bolster struggling antibiotic companies and sustain a pipeline for new treatments.

Headlines: ByteDance evaluates changes to corporate structure of TikTok
Description: ByteDance is looking to make changes to the corporate structure of its short video app TikTok, a company spokesperson said on Thursday.

Headlines: Wells Fargo preparing to cut thousands of jobs: Bloomberg Law
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  is preparing to cut thousands of jobs starting later this year, Bloomberg Law reported https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/wells-fargo-is-readying-thousands-of-job-cuts-to-start-this-year on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Exclusive: Crypto exchange Coinbase readies landmark stock market listing, sources say
Description: Coinbase Inc has started plans for a stock market listing that could come as early as this year, making it the first major U.S. cryptocurrency exchange to go public, according to three people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: British retail to lose further 5,000 jobs in blow to economy
Description: Britain's high street faces more than 5,000 job cuts after two of its biggest names said that customers were unlikely to return to their old shopping habits after the coronavirus crisis, in the latest blow to the country's ailing economy.

Headlines: American Airlines delays HK flights over new COVID-19 testing rules
Description: American Airlines Group Inc said on Thursday it delayed flights to Hong Kong, a day after the city introduced mandatory virus tests for all arriving crew members.

Headlines: VW's Skoda boss Maier to step down at end of July
Description: Bernhard Maier, chairman of Czech carmaker Skoda Auto, part of the Volkswagen Group , will leave his post at the end of July after nearly five years, the company said on Thursday.

Headlines: France urges no sackings at Airbus as workers march over jobs
Description: The French government backed union calls to avoid compulsory job cuts at Airbus on Thursday as several hundred workers marched from the company's headquarters to Toulouse-Blagnac airport.

Headlines: TikTok says removed over 49 million videos in second half of 2019
Description: Social media app TikTok said on Thursday it removed more than 49 million videos from its platform in the second half of last year for violating its guidelines.

Headlines: Speedy removal of Huawei would cost UK, operators: Vodafone and BT
Description: Britain's rebound from COVID-19 could be harmed if the government demands a speedy removal of telecoms equipment made by China's Huawei from mobile networks, Vodafone and BT warned on Thursday.

Headlines: Brazilian airline Gol says expects to lose 3.20 reais per share in the second quarter
Description: Brazil's Gol Linhas Aereas Inteligentes  said on Thursday it expects to lose 3.20 reais per share in the second quarter, and that it could reduce its fleet by 30 more aircraft in 2021-2.

Headlines: Wells Fargo pledges $400 million in support of small business after PPP payout
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  will donate over $400 million toward helping small businesses recover from the coronavirus pandemic, giving away all proceeds from its participation in the Payroll Protection Program.

Headlines: Mexico's Aeromexico sees passenger traffic drop 86.1% in June
Description: Mexican carrier Aeromexico said on Thursday that passenger traffic dropped 86.1% in June when compared to the same month the previous year after the coronavirus pandemic eroded demand for air travel.

Headlines: The man who led Wirecard into insolvency
Description: On the night of June 18, Wirecard AG’s new compliance chief stayed up late at his office in the company’s low-rise headquarters in the Munich suburb of Aschheim to pore over the payment firm’s books.

Headlines: Alstom offers French factory sale to clinch Bombardier deal
Description: France's TGV high-speed train maker Alstom  on Thursday offered to sell a French rail factory and make other concessions to win European Commission approval for its planned purchase of Bombardier Inc's  transportation business.

Headlines: Malaysia's AirAsia seeks nearly $500 million in funding: report
Description: Malaysia's AirAsia Group Bhd is looking to raise 2 billion ringgit ($469 million), its CEO was quoted as saying by the Nikkei Asian Review on Thursday, a day after its auditor cast doubt on the airline's ability to continue as a going concern.

Headlines: British retailer Boots to cut 4,000 jobs
Description: Health and beauty retailer Boots, one of the best-known names on Britain's shopping streets, plans to cut 4,000 jobs and close 48 optician stores, in the latest major blow to the country's retail sector from the COVID-19 crisis.

Headlines: Trading, underwriting soften profit plunge for some U.S. banks
Description: Trading and underwriting revenue could provide some comfort for big Wall Street banks that begin reporting results next week, although second-quarter profits likely plunged because of the coronavirus pandemic's impact on lending.

Headlines: Another 1,300 jobs at risk in UK retail sector as John Lewis shuts eight stores
Description: British department store chain John Lewis said on Thursday it would close eight stores, putting around 1,300 jobs at risk in another blow to the UK retail sector after the coronavirus pandemic accelerated a shift to online shopping.

Headlines: Airbus first-half deliveries hit 16-year low despite June bounce
Description: Airbus  deliveries rose 50% in June compared with May and reached their highest level since the coronavirus crisis spread to Europe in March, but the accelerating recovery failed to prevent first-half deliveries from sliding to a 16-year low.

Headlines: Tesla 'very close' to level 5 autonomous driving technology, Musk says
Description: U.S. electric vehicle maker Tesla Inc  is "very close" to achieving level 5 autonomous driving technology, Chief Executive Elon Musk said on Thursday, referring to the capability to navigate roads without any driver input.

Headlines: YouTube not obliged to inform on film pirates, Europe's top court says
Description: Google's YouTube is not required to hand over the email or IP address of users who upload films illegally to its video platform, Europe's top court ruled on Thursday, saying there must be a balance between protecting personal data and copyright.

Headlines: Aston Martin's first SUV rolls off production line
Description: Aston Martin's  first sport utility vehicle rolled off the production line on Thursday, key to hopes of a turnaround at the luxury carmaker which has seen changes in management and ownership over the last few months amid a torrid performance.

Headlines: Samsung 'definitely can' supply a 5G network to UK, executive says
Description: Samsung executive vice president Woojune Kim said the company was in active commercial discussions with European operators to supply network equipment, and was investing its resources in 4G, 5G and 6G rather than legacy technology.

Headlines: Rooftop revolution: Coronavirus chill upends solar power industry
Description: The booming rooftop solar panel industry nosedived overnight when the coronavirus forced homeowners to rein in spending and keep their distance from would-be installers.

Headlines: Gilead to deliver more remdesivir to Europe from autumn: WiWo
Description: Gilead Sciences Inc  plans to make more of its drug remdesivir available for Germany and Europe from autumn and will decide how much each country gets based on the rate of infection, the drugmaker's Germany boss told a German magazine.

Headlines: Bond investors wait for more headlines on EU recovery fund
Description: Euro zone bond yields held their ground on Thursday with investors' main focus expected to be any new developments on the European Union's recovery fund, which aims to help the region's economy recover from the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: UK's Sunak: too early to predict shape of recovery from recession
Description: Britain is facing a significant recession but it is too early to tell how quickly the economy will be able to recover, British finance minister Rishi Sunak said on Thursday.

Headlines: UK's Sunak: we must watch interest rates and debt costs
Description: British finance minister Rishi Sunak said on Thursday it was important to be alert to possible changes in interest rates, adding it was likely the cost of servicing debt would be included in the government's future budget rules.

Headlines: UK's Sunak says will start to fix budget deficit once outlook clearer
Description: British finance minister Rishi Sunak on Thursday said he would act to put public finances back on a sustainable footing in the medium term, when he has a clearer view of the economic recovery from the COVID-19 crisis.

Headlines: Ant Group listing would be fillip for Hong Kong's flagging IPO market
Description: An initial public offering from Alibaba's  Ant Group by year-end would give equity capital markets in Hong Kong a timely boost after a new security law cast in doubt the city's future as a global financial centre, analysts said on Thursday.

Headlines: China's market euphoria trumps political risk in Hong Kong
Description: Investors in China's soaring stock market are increasingly turning to Hong Kong for bargains, egging on an investment boom on the back of large tech listings and shaking off fears of political risks in the bruised financial hub.

Headlines: Ford's quarterly China sales rise for the first time in 3 years
Description: Ford Motor Co  said its China vehicle sales increased 3% in April-June from a year earlier, its first quarterly sales rise in the world's bigggest auto market in almost three years.

Headlines: Bain Capital extends deadline for Japan's Nichiigakkan bid for second time
Description: U.S. buyout fund Bain Capital said on Thursday it had extended its deadline for a $1 billion buyout offer for Japanese nursing home operator Nichiigakkan Co for a second time.

Headlines: Aboriginal groups call for Rio to lose human rights status after caves blast
Description: Aboriginal and human rights groups on Thursday called for miner Rio Tinto Ltd  to be stripped of its status as a human rights leader following its destruction of an Aboriginal sacred site showing evidence of 46,000 years of human habitation.

Headlines: Johnson & Johnson's Cilag to sell up to 11.8 million Idorsia shares
Description: Johnson & Johnson's  Cilag Holding will offer up to approximately 11.8 million existing ordinary shares in Idorsia Ltd  in an accelerated bookbuilding to commence on Wednesday, the transaction's bookrunner said.

Headlines: Facebook takes down accounts and pages of Trump ally Roger Stone
Description: Facebook Inc  on Wednesday removed 50 personal and professional pages connected to U.S. President Donald Trump's longtime adviser Roger Stone, who is due to report to prison next week.

Headlines: Study suggests most Uber, Lyft drivers in Seattle not poorly paid
Description: Most ride-hail workers in Seattle are part-time drivers whose earnings are roughly in line with the city's median, a study of data provided by Uber and Lyft showed, defying some perceptions of drivers working full-time for little pay.

Headlines: Nasdaq ends at record high as Wall Street rises with tech shares
Description: U.S stocks rose on Wednesday and the Nasdaq hit a record closing high, supported by technology shares as early signs of an economic rebound offset concern about further lockdowns due to a jump in coronavirus cases across the country.

Headlines: TikTok's ad launch faces challenges from U.S. ban threat, hoaxes
Description: TikTok’s launch on Wednesday of a new platform to court small business advertisers is fraught with challenges, especially after the Trump administration's threat this week to impose a ban on China-based social media apps.

Headlines: Facebook suspends disinformation network tied to staff of Brazil's Bolsonaro
Description: Facebook Inc  on Wednesday suspended a network of social media accounts it said were used to spread divisive political messages online by employees of Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro and two of his sons.

Headlines: Carlos Ghosn's accused smugglers unlikely to win quick bail
Description: A U.S. judge said she is unlikely to quickly release a Massachusetts father and son being held on charges they helped smuggle former Nissan Motor Co  chairman Carlos Ghosn out of Japan.

Headlines: United Airlines sending 'gut punch' furlough warnings to 36,000 workers
Description: United Airlines  said on Wednesday it was preparing to send notices of potential furloughs to 36,000 U.S.-based frontline employees, or about 45% of staff, as travel demand hit by the coronavirus pandemic struggles to recover.

Headlines: Nonprofits urge Johnson & Johnson to halt sales of Baby Powder globally
Description: More than 170 nonprofit groups on Wednesday called for Johnson & Johnson to stop selling its talc-based Johnson’s Baby Powder world-wide, citing concerns that it contains cancer-causing asbestos, according to a statement from advocacy group Black Women for Wellness.

Headlines: Furloughs at U.S. legacy airlines could help low-cost carriers like Southwest
Description: U.S. legacy airlines with lackluster employee demand for early exit packages face large furloughs in the fall, signaling higher post-pandemic labor costs because union contracts require airlines to furlough in reverse order of seniority.

Headlines: U.S. DoJ examining Wirecard as part of probe into alleged bank-fraud conspiracy: WSJ
Description: The U.S. Department of Justice is examining whether German payment company Wirecard AG  played a critical role in an alleged $100 million bank-fraud conspiracy connected to an online marijuana marketplace, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Dollar tumbles to two-week low as Nasdaq hit record closing high
Description: The dollar dropped to two-week lows on Wednesday, showing reduced safe-haven appeal for now, as U.S. tech stocks rallied and commodity prices firmed, even as sentiment remained cautious amid a resurgence of new coronavirus cases globally, particularly in the United States.

Headlines: Federal judge throws out GM's racketeering lawsuit against Fiat Chrysler
Description: A federal judge on Wednesday threw out a racketeering lawsuit General Motors Co had filed against smaller rival Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV, saying the No. 1 U.S. automaker's alleged injuries were not caused by FCA's alleged violations.

Headlines: Fed officials suggest U.S. recovery may be stalling
Description: Federal Reserve officials raised fresh doubts on Wednesday about the durability of the U.S. recovery, while new business surveys highlighted developing risks from the relentless coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Nvidia eclipses Intel as most valuable U.S. chipmaker
Description: Nvidia  has overtaken Intel  for the first time as the most valuable U.S. chipmaker.

Headlines: Global shares rise despite coronavirus fears; gold gains
Description: Global stocks rose on Wednesday as recovery hopes overcame fears that a surge in coronavirus cases would slow the U.S. economy, but many investors still sought safety on pandemic worries, driving gold prices above $1,800 an ounce for the first time since 2011.

Headlines: Warren Buffett donates $2.9 billion to Gates Foundation, family charities
Description: Warren Buffett has donated roughly $2.9 billion of Berkshire Hathaway Inc  stock to four family charities and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the latest but not largest contribution in his plan to give away his fortune.

Headlines: Oil settles higher on improving U.S. gasoline demand
Description: Oil prices settled higher on Wednesday as U.S. gasoline consumption showed signs of a recovery, but price gains were limited by rising crude inventories and an increase in coronavirus infections.

Headlines: JPMorgan puts plans for Ohio office return on hold indefinitely
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  is pulling back on returning some of its 18,000 employees to work at offices in Columbus, Ohio, after coronavirus cases in the state jumped, the bank said on Wednesday.

Headlines: 'Weaponized' Facebook fails to protect civil rights, audit says
Description: Facebook Inc's decisions to allow controversial posts by President Donald Trump established a "terrible precedent" that could allow the platform to be "weaponized to suppress voting," an external civil rights audit found on Wednesday.

Headlines: Explainer: What 1.1 million foreign students contribute to the U.S. economy
Description: The Trump administration said on Monday that foreign university students will have to leave the country if their classes are all taught online - clouding the future of tens of thousands of enrollees and potentially straining budgets at schools struggling to reopen during the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Exclusive: EU secures potential COVID-19 drugs from Roche, Germany's Merck
Description: The European Commission has struck deals with drugmakers Roche  and Merck KGaA  to secure supplies of experimental treatments for COVID-19, a Commission source told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Commerzbank board meets amid leadership void after top resignations
Description: Commerzbank's  supervisory board formally accepted the resignation of its chief executive at a meeting on Wednesday amid a continuing leadership vacuum at the top of Germany's No. 2 bank.

Headlines: Air Canada assesses Spartan Bioscience's COVID-19 testing technology
Description: Air Canada  said on Wednesday it was working with Spartan Bioscience Inc to assess using the Ottawa-based biotechnology company's portable COVID-19 testing technology in the aviation sector.

Headlines: Workers rights allegations fail to deter Boohoo's sell-side backers
Description: Two-thirds of analysts covering fashion retailer Boohoo  retained a "buy" recommendation on the company's stock despite a 45% drop in less than a week following allegations of dire conditions at its supplier factories.

Headlines: U.S. office, apartment vacancy rates rise marginally in second quarter: Reis
Description: U.S. office and apartment vacancy rates rose marginally in the second quarter from a year earlier, as property owners were yet to feel the full impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, according to real estate research firm Reis Inc.

Headlines: 'Death Cross' strikes U.S. dollar as COVID-19 cases grow
Description: A resurgent coronavirus pandemic in the United States and the prospect of improving growth abroad are souring some investors on the dollar, threatening a years-long rally in the currency.

Headlines: Tesla's Musk approaches a $1.8 billion bonanza
Description: Tesla Inc's blistering stock rally is putting Chief Executive Elon Musk in reach of a payday potentially worth $1.8 billion, his second jackpot from the electric car maker in about two months.

Headlines: U.S. tech giants face hard choices under Hong Kong's new security law
Description: U.S. tech giants face a reckoning over how Hong Kong's security law will reshape their businesses, with their suspension of processing government requests for user data a stop-gap measure as they weigh options, people close to the industry say.

Headlines: U.S. will act to deny China access to Americans' data, says Pompeo
Description: The Trump administration will take steps to ensure the Chinese government does not gain any access to the private information of American citizens through telecommunications and social media, U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Wednesday, when asked if the U.S. was planning to ban Chinese-owned app Tiktok.

Headlines: HSBC and Nokia drag European stocks lower amid virus worries
Description: HSBC and Nokia dragged European shares lower on Wednesday as a surge in coronavirus cases appeared to threaten a recovery in the global economy, while Britain's plan to head off an unemployment crisis cushioned a fall in London's domestically focused stocks.

Headlines: Bayer puts Roundup future claims settlement on hold
Description: Bayer  was forced on Wednesday to delay part of a proposed settlement of allegations that its widely used weedkiller Roundup caused cancer after a U.S. judge questioned its plan to deal with future claims.

Headlines: Walmart makes new push into healthcare with insurance business
Description: Walmart Inc  is making its latest move into the healthcare space with its own insurance business, the company said on its website.

Headlines: End of an era? Series of U.S. setbacks bodes ill for big oil, gas pipeline projects
Description: A rapid-fire succession of setbacks for big energy pipelines in the United States this week has revealed an uncomfortable truth for the oil and gas industry: environmental activists and landowners opposed to projects have become good at blocking them in court.

Headlines: Dutch court to question ING and ex-CEO Hamers in money laundering case
Description: A Dutch court on Wednesday said it wanted to question the Dutch bank ING  and its former chief executive Ralph Hamers, now heading for UBS, to determine whether to reopen a case that led to ING being fined for lax prevention of money laundering.

Headlines: SEAT urges Spain to 'wake up' and promote electric cars
Description: Spain needs to "wake up" and follow other European countries in giving more incentives for electric cars, the head of Volkswagen's  Spanish brand SEAT said on Wednesday.

Headlines: VW's SEAT plans five billion euros in investments in 2020-2025
Description: Volkswagen's  Spanish brand SEAT said on Wednesday it plans 5 billion euros in investments in 2020-2025, mainly in new R&D, equipment and electric cars, after investing 3.3 billion in 2016-2020.

Headlines: Walgreens partners with VillageMD to open primary care clinics at drug stores
Description: Walgreens Boots Alliance Plc  said on Wednesday it had partnered with primary care provider VillageMD to open doctor offices attached to its drugstores across the United States, as the pharmacy chain looked to expand its healthcare services.

Headlines: Trump administration says pandemic aid saved 51 million jobs. Did it?
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration touted its $660 billion small business pandemic aid program this week as a "wild success," unveiling data that showed the initiative saved 51 million jobs.

Headlines: Airbus workers stage rare protest over job cuts
Description: Thousands of Airbus workers marched alongside an airport runway in France and staged an 'empty chair' protest in Germany on Wednesday to protest against plans to cut up to 15,000 jobs.

Headlines: Apple expands independent repair shop program to Europe, Canada
Description: Apple Inc said on Wednesday it is expanding a program to supply repair parts, tools and manuals for iPhones to independent repair shops in 32 countries in Europe as well as Canada.

Headlines: Rivals Royal Caribbean, Norwegian Cruise Line team up to plan restart
Description: (This July 6 story corrects spelling of Richard Fain's name.)

Headlines: EU investigates decision to hire BlackRock to advise on green rules for banks
Description: The European Commission's decision to hire BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager, to advise it on new environmental rules for banks, has triggered an investigation by the European Ombudsman following complaints by several lawmakers and a civil group.

Headlines: Cars, a cocktail and a celebrity: South Koreans succumb to Tesla fever
Description: From an eponymous cocktail to eager buyers following the shipping routes of long-awaited cars, Tesla Inc  is having a moment in South Korea, particularly among tech-savvy professionals.

Headlines: Exclusive: Alibaba's Ant plans Hong Kong IPO, targets valuation over $200 billion, sources say
Description: Ant Group, the fintech arm of Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba, plans a Hong Kong float as soon as this year and targets a valuation of more than $200 billion, said two sources with knowledge of the matter.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler says South American market share 15.9% in second quarter
Description: Fiat Chrysler  said on Wednesday its market share in South America stood at 15.9% in the second quarter, when car sales in the region plummeted due to the new coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Boohoo reviews British supply chain after factory report fallout
Description: Boohoo  commissioned an independent review of its supply chain in Britain on Wednesday after a damaging media report about dire factory working conditions put the brakes on the online fast fashion retailer's meteoric rise.

Headlines: Ruling in EU Apple tax case due next Wednesday: Ireland
Description: The European Union's second highest court will next week rule in an appeal by Apple  and Ireland against an EU ruling for the U.S. company to pay 13 billion euros ($16 billion) in back taxes, the Irish government said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Huawei says U.S. sanctions have no immediate impact on UK 5G supplies
Description: U.S. sanctions targeting China's Huawei have had no immediate impact on its ability to supply 5G equipment to Britain, a senior company executive said on Wednesday, calling for more time to understand the full repercussions of the restrictions.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. probing allegations TikTok violated children's privacy - sources
Description: The Federal Trade Commission and the U.S. Justice Department are looking into allegations that popular app TikTok failed to live up to a 2019 agreement aimed at protecting children's privacy, according to two people interviewed by the agencies.

Headlines: Germany insists self-regulation not enough for Facebook
Description: Germany is determined to expand its attempts to regulate online hate speech even as Facebook  promises to do more to clean up its site after a global advertiser boycott, with politicians saying the issue is too important to leave to self-regulation.

Headlines: Coronavirus 'collateral damage' hits U.S. rural power providers
Description: When the coronavirus pandemic left Ron Mueller without a market for the 3,200 piglets his hog breeding operation cranks out weekly and facing huge bills, his local electricity provider offered to cut the Illinois farmer some slack.

Headlines: AirAsia shares in biggest daily fall as auditor flags 'going concern' doubts
Description: Shares in Malaysia's AirAsia Group Bhd  tumbled more than 17% on Wednesday in their biggest daily fall after the auditor cast doubt on the budget carrier's ability to continue as a going concern due to the coronavirus travel slump.

Headlines: Cannabis firms see jump in insurance costs to protect leaders as investors sue
Description: Canadian and U.S. cannabis companies are facing a spike in already high costs of insurance to protect top executives from personal liability, following a slew of lawsuits by disgruntled investors alleging fraud and misinformation, with more such action expected.

Headlines: Nokia shares fall on concerns over potential loss of Verizon business
Description: Shares in Nokia  fell up to 8% in Wednesday trade on concerns that the Finnish company was losing the business of its key client Verizon  in the United States.

Headlines: U.S. airlines move toward federal loans as COVID-19 surge threatens demand, jobs
Description: The largest U.S. air carriers have all signed letters of intent on federal loans to help them weather the novel coronavirus, with United Airlines warning employees on Tuesday that a surge in outbreaks was hitting bookings, threatening a travel rebound and jobs.

Headlines: Tesla China sold 14,954 Model 3 vehicles in June, up 35% on the month
Description: U.S. electric vehicle maker Tesla Inc  sold 14,954 Shanghai-made Model 3 vehicles in China in June, up 35% month-on-month, according to the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).

Headlines: Analysts cut earnings estimate for Asian companies for fifth straight month
Description: Analysts cut their forward 12-month earnings estimates for Asian companies for a fifth consecutive month in June, citing the economic fallout from the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Credit Suisse aims for 100% of securities venture in China growth plan
Description: Credit Suisse  wants to raise its China securities joint venture stake to 100% and increase its market share after getting the regulatory green light to take a majority holding, the head of its Asia business said.

Headlines: Some 83% of German firms with foreign exposure complain of collapsing revenues
Description: Around four-fifths of German firms with foreign exposure have experienced a collapse in revenues as a result of the coronavirus crisis, and 93% expect global economic conditions to improve only in 2021 or later, according to a survey.

Headlines: As insurers face hefty pandemic losses, newcomers see chance to step in
Description: Commercial insurers are facing hefty claims from the coronavirus crisis but are also seeing a steep rise in premiums – tempting companies and industry veterans to raise capital, launch new businesses or expand into new lines.

Headlines: Chinese factories to face headwinds in next phase of post-lockdown recovery
Description: Orders for infrastructure materials and equipment have helped industrial output recover faster in China than most places emerging from COVID-19 lockdowns, but further expansion will be hard to attain without stronger broad-based demand and exports.

Headlines: U.S. says Ghosn wired money to man who helped him flee Japan
Description: Carlos Ghosn, the former Nissan Motor Co chairman, wired $862,500 last year to a company managed by one of the two men who later helped him escape from Japan, U.S. prosecutors said in a Tuesday court filing.

Headlines: Disney says Walt Disney World reopening is on track for Saturday
Description: Walt Disney Co  will stick to its plans to reopen its Walt Disney World theme parks in Orlando, Florida, to a limited number of guests on Saturday, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.

Headlines: Boeing settles nearly all Lion Air 737 MAX crash claims: filing
Description: Boeing Co has reached settlement agreements in more than 90% of the wrongful death claims filed in federal court after the 2018 crash of a Lion Air 737 MAX in Indonesia that killed all 189 people on board, a court filing on Tuesday said.

Headlines: Pence says U.S. to maintain 'strong stand' on TikTok
Description: U.S. Vice President Mike Pence said on Tuesday the United States would "continue to take a strong stand" regarding Chinese entities that threaten U.S. security, including potentially the social media app TikTok.

Headlines: GSK to develop plant-based COVID-19 vaccine with Canada's Medicago
Description: The world's largest vaccine-maker GSK has put its vaccine booster technology to work in a potential new COVID-19 shot, to be developed with a Canadian biopharmaceutical company backed by tobacco company Philip Morris.

Headlines: Movie theater chains sue New Jersey over coronavirus-related closures
Description: Six movie theater chains, including AMC Entertainment, Cinemark and Regal Cinemas, have sued New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy for refusing to let them resume operations, even after allowing churches, retailers and indoor shopping malls to reopen during the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Facebook ad boycott organizers see 'no commitment to action' in Zuckerberg meeting
Description: Organizers of a growing Facebook Inc  advertising boycott said they saw "no commitment to action" after meeting with Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg on Tuesday.

Headlines: Wall Street drops after strong rally as COVID-19 cases mount
Description: U.S. stocks fell on Tuesday, adding to losses into the close, as investors took profits a day after the S&P 500 logged its longest streak of gains this year and as new U.S. coronavirus cases rose further.

Headlines: Walmart's membership program set to launch in July: Recode
Description: Walmart Inc is close to launching its membership program, a direct competitor for online retail giant Amazon.com Inc's Prime service, Recode reported on Tuesday, citing sources.

Headlines: Levi Strauss warns of weak second half on pandemic woes, to cut 700 jobs
Description: Levi Strauss & Co  on Tuesday cautioned its business would be hit in the second half of the year, even as the denim apparel maker's sales have been improving at its reopened stores, following government-mandated COVID-19 lockdowns.

Headlines: Hospital led by biotech billionaire Soon-Shiong approved for PPP aid
Description: A Pennsylvania hospital led by biotech billionaire Patrick Soon-Shiong won approval for up to $5 million in federal aid for small businesses under a coronavirus pandemic loan program, government data show.

Headlines: Stocks, oil slip but Chinese stocks rally a sixth day
Description: Investor caution over renewed coronavirus-related lockdowns buoyed the dollar and snapped a five-day rally in most world equity markets on Tuesday, but was not enough to halt a hot streak in Chinese stocks.

Headlines: Oil steadies as economic data overshadows coronavirus worries
Description: Oil prices settled little changed on Tuesday as demand concerns due to a new surge in coronavirus cases overshadowed  U.S. government forecasts for lower production.

Headlines: Huawei says U.S. pressure on Brazil threatens long delays in 5G rollout
Description: A Huawei Technologies executive warned that Brazil could suffer years of delay in deploying a 5G telecoms network and higher costs if it succumbs to mounting U.S. pressure to snub the Chinese equipment supplier.

Headlines: Fed's Mester says full recovery a long way off, more fiscal help needed
Description: A resurgence in coronavirus cases across the country is making consumers more cautious, and more fiscal stimulus is needed to help the economy recover fully from the crisis, Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank President Loretta Mester said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Fed's Clarida says there is more the Fed can and will do
Description: With the surge in coronavirus cases threatening the U.S. recovery, Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Richard Clarida had a message on Tuesday: the U.S. central bank is not going to sit idly, even if a double dip recession is not the base case scenario.

Headlines: Dollar rises as virus worries hurt risk appetite
Description: The U.S. dollar rose against a basket of currencies on Tuesday, holding above the near two-week low hit in the previous session, as investors turned uneasy over new coronavirus flare-ups and local lockdowns in some countries.

Headlines: Aircraft lessor Avolon cancels 27 Boeing 737 MAX jets
Description: Aircraft lessor Avolon on Tuesday announced the cancellation of an additional 27 Boeing  737 MAX planes after cancelling 75 of the jets in April as it grapples with the fallout of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: The quarter after the half: Why the next three months are key for stocks
Description: Central bank firepower helped stock market bulls finish the first half of 2020 on a high. Now the rally hinges on follow-through in the third-quarter from economic data, company earnings and the coronavirus newsflow.

Headlines: Fairyland, baker, tennis club: a snapshot of pandemic aid in one city
Description: A roster of businesses receiving a piece of the $660 billion U.S. Paycheck Protection Program illustrates how deeply the government's pandemic aid has reached into the everyday lives of Americans, yet at the same time how unevenly and fleetingly.

Headlines: Epstein red flags, Russian models land Deutsche Bank $150 million fine
Description: Deutsche Bank will pay a $150 million fine from a New York regulator for allowing disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein to make payments to Russian models and withdraw suspicious amounts of cash during five years as a client.

Headlines: PPP loans roughly in line with industry payrolls, but some stand out
Description: Paycheck Protection Program loans to restaurants and hotels fell short of their share of small-business employment, according to details on the program released Monday by the U.S. Treasury Department and the Small Business Administration.

Headlines: United Airlines warns of lower bookings, furloughs: source
Description: United Airlines  has warned of booking declines and potential furloughs due to new travel restrictions in an internal presentation to the carrier's employees, a person with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: U.S. government awards Novavax $1.6 billion for coronavirus vaccine

Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  is eliminating terms like "blacklist," "master" and "slave" from its internal technology materials and code as it seeks to address racism within the company, said two sources with knowledge of the move.

Headlines: Embraer union seeks planemaker's board ouster after failed Boeing deal
Description: A union representing workers at Embraer filed a lawsuit on Friday seeking to dismiss the company's board, after a $4.2 billion deal with Boeing Co  collapsed amid the pandemic, claims the Brazilian planemaker said were an act of "bad faith."

Headlines: Air France and sister airline to cut 7,580 jobs
Description: Air France  confirmed plans to cut some 7,500 jobs including 1,000 at sister airline HOP! on Friday, as staff protested over its response to the collapse in travel due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Air France and HOP! airlines to cut 7,580 jobs
Description: Air France  plans to cut just over 7,500 jobs following the coronavirus-related collapse in air travel, the flag carrier said on Friday.

Headlines: Canada's biggest banks join boycott of Facebook platforms

Headlines: Turkish suspect tells court Ghosn mused on Hollywood movie of escape from Japan

Headlines: Rolls-Royce reviewing balance sheet options after COVID-19 hit
Description: British aerospace engineer Rolls-Royce  said on Friday it was reviewing a range of options to strengthen its balance sheet and position itself for recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: Daimler seeks to sell French factory in production overhaul
Description: Daimler  will seek to sell its factory in Hambach, France, as part of an overhaul of its production system, the German carmaker said on Friday, prompting France's finance minister to urge the company to reconsider.

Headlines: Fiat, PSA stick to merger deal after dividend cut report
Description: Fiat Chrysler (FCA) and PSA said on Friday they were sticking to the merger plan signed last year after a newspaper said the carmakers were looking at spinning off assets to cut a planned 5.5 billion euro ($6.2 billion) cash payout to FCA shareholders.

Headlines: French finance minister urges Daimler to reconsider plan to sell Hambach site
Description: French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire urged German carmaker Daimler  on Friday to reconsider plans to sell its factory in Hambach, France.

Headlines: Dollar rises as risk appetite tempered by rising COVID-19 cases in U.S.
Description: The dollar edged up on Friday but was set for its biggest weekly fall since the start of June, as a sentiment boost from better-than-expected jobs data in the United States was tempered by surging coronavirus cases.

Headlines: Global Markets: COVID recovery vs COVID reality
Description: World shares stalled near a four-month high on Friday and the industrial bellwether metal copper scuffed its longest weekly winning streak in nearly three years, as nagging coronavirus nerves tempered the recent recovery run.

Headlines: Audi, EnBW to turn electric car batteries into grid support tools
Description: German carmaker Audi  and utility EnBW  are setting up an electric car battery operation at EnBW's Heilbronn plant to build scaleable storage facilities by the end of this year, drawing on retired batteries to help power grids.

Headlines: After Wirecard review, Singapore launches probe into Citadelle, Senjo Group
Description: Singapore authorities said they launched an investigation into Citadelle Corporate Services, Senjo Group and its subsidiaries after scrutinising collapsed German payments firm Wirecard's  local operations.

Headlines: Uber widens taxi app to Japan's Tokyo but ride-sharing still barred
Description: Uber Technologies  launched a ride-hailing smartphone application in Tokyo on Friday in partnership with three domestic taxi firms, even as strict regulations block its popular ride-sharing service in Japan.

Headlines: Boeing communications chief resigns over decades-old article on women in combat
Description: Boeing Co's  communications chief Niel Golightly abruptly resigned on Thursday, following an employee's complaint over an article the former U.S. military pilot wrote 33 years ago arguing women should not serve in combat.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank eyes payment systems, including Wirecard: Handelsblatt
Description: Deutsche Bank  is on the lookout for expansion opportunities in the area of payments systems, the lender's strategy director said in response to a question about the lender's interest in Wirecard's  assets.

Headlines: Wall Street shifts bets to big pharma as COVID-19 vaccine race progresses
Description: Wall Street is moving some bets on COVID-19 vaccines to large pharmaceutical companies with robust manufacturing capabilities, signaling that a love affair with small biotech firms might be ending after the sector’s best quarter in almost 20 years.

Headlines: GM's China sales drop 5% in second quarter, underperforms industry recovery
Description: General Motors Co's  vehicle sales in China dropped 5.3% between April and June from the corresponding period last year,  underperforming the industry average amid a recovery from the coronavirus fallout on the world's biggest auto market.

Headlines: Nissan's China sales grew 4.5% in June
Description: Japanese automaker Nissan Motor  said on Friday its sales in China grew 4.5% in June from a year earlier to 136,929 vehicles, as the world's biggest auto market recovered from its coronavirus low.

Headlines: HSBC to invest further in China amid political strife over Hong Kong law
Description: HSBC Holdings Plc  said on Friday it would make new investments in its wealth management and insurance operations in mainland China.

Headlines: Australia's Westpac to pay $5.5 million for staff underpayment, cites calculation errors
Description: Australia's Westpac Banking Corp  on Friday said it will have to pay A$8 million ($5.5 million) to around 8,000 employees who were found to have been underpaid their long-service leave entitlements due to calculation errors.

Headlines: Factbox: Growing list of Australian companies underpaying staff
Description: Some of Australia's biggest companies have been caught up in underpayment scandals, prompting the federal government to say it would introduce tougher laws that criminalise what it called "wage theft" and ban executives from being company directors if they were involved.

Headlines: Citi targets more growth in Saudi Arabia after adding over 20 bankers in two years
Description: Citigroup  is planning to hire more bankers in Saudi Arabia for its direct custody business after adding more than 20 for onshore capital markets in the last two years, its Europe, Middle East and Africa head said.

Headlines: Wirecard debt that facilitated SoftBank investment put up for auction
Description: Convertible bonds that were part of a complex transaction that allowed Japan's SoftBank Group  to buy a stake in now-collapsed payments company Wirecard and then de-risk the transaction have been put up for sale in an auction.

Headlines: Japan asks U.S. to extradite men accused of helping ex-Nissan boss Ghosn flee
Description: Japan has formally asked the United States to extradite a former Green Beret and his son accused of helping former Nissan Motor Co boss Carlos Ghosn flee the country while he was awaiting trial on financial charges.

Headlines: Delta amends credit facility to include stricter covenants
Description: Delta Air Lines Inc  said on Thursday it has amended its $2.65 billion credit facility agreement with covenants, which include restricting the U.S. airline's ability to pay dividends or repurchase stock before Sept. 30, 2021.

Headlines: How Moderna executives are cashing in on COVID-19 vaccine stock speculation
Description: Biotech firm Moderna Inc could reap tens of billions of dollars in sales and stock appreciation if it wins the race for a COVID-19 vaccine. If it loses, the early-stage company’s value could crash.

Headlines: Shares in Aeromexico bounce back after sharp losses
Description: Shares in Aeromexico climbed as much as 27% on Thursday after nosediving a day earlier on the Mexican airline's announcement it had started bankruptcy proceedings as the coronavirus pandemic battered business.

Headlines: Tesla denies reports of firing employees who chose to stay at home
Description: Tesla Inc  on Thursday denied media reports and said it had not fired employees who chose to stay at home during the coronavirus pandemic over safety concerns at the carmaker's California factory.

Headlines: Global stocks jump on strong U.S. jobs data; COVID-19 caution lingers
Description: A measure of stocks across the globe rose for a fourth straight day on Thursday after June U.S. payrolls grew by a record 4.8 million, but investors also flocked to the safe-haven dollar and U.S. Treasuries on concerns about surging COVID-19 cases in many U.S. states.

Headlines: Facebook hit with complaint alleging widespread bias against Black workers
Description: A Black Facebook Inc worker on Thursday filed a complaint claiming the social media giant's stated commitment to diversity and civil rights, including its support for the Black Lives Matter movement, masks widespread discrimination against Black workers.

Headlines: Wall Street closes higher after biggest payrolls jump on record
Description: Wall Street closed higher and the Nasdaq reached an all-time closing high on Thursday as investors headed into their long holiday weekend buoyed by a record surge in payrolls, which provided assurance that the U.S. economic recovery was well under way.

Headlines: Factbox: More companies join Facebook ad boycott bandwagon

Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve's massive stash of bonds and other assets slipped for a third straight week to its smallest size since mid-May, data released by the central bank on Thursday showed.

Description: U.S. companies are expanding and opening new plants in the Dominican Republic as they diversify their supply chains, moves that will help offset the economic impact of the new coronavirus pandemic, the Dominican economy minister said.

Description: Each day, employees at Farley's East cafe in Oakland, California fix about 200 turkey, ham and egg salad sandwich lunch plates to be distributed free to the homeless, hungry school-age kids, medical professionals at Covid-19 testing sites, and others in need.

Headlines: Luckin Coffee's Lu holds on to chairman role
Description: Luckin Coffee Inc  said on Thursday co-founder Charles Zhengyao Lu will stay on as chairman of the embattled coffee chain after a proposal to oust him, stemming from an internal fraud investigation, failed to get board approval.

Headlines: U.S dollar gains on worries about resurgent coronavirus pandemic
Description: The U.S. dollar rose on Thursday, regaining its safe-haven appeal, as investors worried that the resurgence of U.S. coronavirus cases could erase the summer's employment gains.

Headlines: Fed's Powell continued to talk frequently with Mnuchin, lawmakers in May
Description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell continued to talk regularly with Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin and key U.S. lawmakers in May as the United States began to turn the corner on the economic fallout from the coronavirus pandemic, Fed records released on Thursday showed.

Description: The U.S. State Department warned top American companies including Walmart Inc, Apple Inc and Amazon.com Inc over risks faced from maintaining supply chains associated with human rights abuses in China's western Xinjiang province, according to a letter seen by Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: Investors rethink yield curve control horizon as Fed raises doubts
Description: Investors are dialing back expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve may soon move to implement yield curve control, with some of them welcoming skepticism from the central bank in considering such a move.

Description: The world's No. 3 planemaker Embraer SA  said on Thursday it was negotiating buyouts, signaling likely cuts in its workforce due to the coronavirus pandemic that has hammered the travel industry.

Description: Boeing Co  is pulling the plug on its 747 jumbo jet, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

Description: Global M&A activity tumbled to its lowest level in more than a decade in the second quarter, according to data provider Refinitiv, as companies gave up on expansion plans to focus on protecting their balance sheets and employees in the wake of the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Cineworld delays U.S., UK cinema reopenings to end of July
Description: Cineworld  on Tuesday delayed the reopening of its cinemas in the United States and Britain until the end of July, citing changes to the release schedules for some of the big summer movies.

Headlines: Federated Hermes questions HSBC's stance on Hong Kong law
Description: HSBC  investor Federated Hermes said it has questions about the bank's support for China's new security law for Hong Kong, the second investor in Europe's biggest bank in recent weeks to voice concerns about the lender's stance.

Headlines: Cerberus wants well over 7,000 Commerzbank job cuts: source
Description: Cerberus wants Commerzbank  to cut far more than a reported 7,000 jobs as part of plans by Germany's second biggest bank to reduce costs, a person familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: BMW to source battery cells produced using renewable energy
Description: German carmaker BMW  on Tuesday said its electric cars will use battery cells produced using renewable energy, a step which will compel the biggest suppliers to source more non-coal generated electricity.

Headlines: Cerberus wants well more than 7,000 job cuts at Commerzbank - source
Description: Cerberus wants Commerzbank  to cut far more than 7,000 jobs as part of the bank's efforts to trim costs, a person familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Boeing begins crucial certification test flights for grounded 737 MAX
Description: Boeing Co began a series of long-delayed flight tests of its redesigned 737 MAX with regulators at the controls on Monday, hoping to win approval and rebuild its reputation after fatal crashes that toppled its leaders and grounded the jet worldwide.

Headlines: UK economy shows biggest drop in 40 years in early 2020
Description: Britain's economy shrank by the most since 1979 in early 2020 as households slashed their spending, according to official data that included the first few days of the coronavirus lockdown.

Headlines: Japan to delay 'womenomics' target for female leaders by up to a decade: media
Description: Japan will delay by up to a decade its target to raise the percentage of women in leadership posts to 30% - part of Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's campaign to empower women - after failing to hit the deadline this year, domestic media have reported.

Headlines: China's factory activity quickens, but pandemic drags on exporters and recovery
Description: China's factory activity expanded at a stronger pace in June after the government lifted lockdowns and stepped up investment, but persistent weakness in export orders suggests the coronavirus crisis will remain a drag on the economy for some time.

Headlines: Wirecard North America seeks buyer, distances itself from German company
Description: Wirecard North America Inc, a unit of German payments company Wirecard AG, on Monday said it has put itself up for sale, days after the troubled parent firm filed for insolvency.     The U.S.-based unit, which was bought by Wirecard in 2016, said an investment bank is coordinating the sale process. The unit was formerly known as Citi Prepaid Card Services.

Headlines: Environmental groups propose tailings dam safety standards
Description: Mining companies should be required to buy private insurance for tailings dams and their board of directors should be held legally responsible for any disasters, a coalition of 140 environmental groups said in a report published on Tuesday.

Headlines: Tim Tam maker Arnott's loses 50 jobs in first cuts since KKR buyout
Description: Arnott's, maker of Tim Tam biscuits and other snacks, is shedding about 50 staff, a representative told Reuters, the first such cuts since U.S. private equity firm KKR & Co Inc  bought one of Australia's best-known brands last year.

Headlines: Wall Street ends higher on Boeing bump, stimulus eyed
Description: Wall Street stocks closed higher on Monday and the S&P 500 was poised to clinch its biggest quarterly percentage gain since 1998 as investors hoped for a stimulus-backed economic rebound, while a surge in Boeing shares helped boost the blue-chip Dow.

Headlines: China service sector grows at fastest pace in seven months in June: official PMI
Description: Activity in China's services sector expanded at its fastest pace in 7 months in June, official data showed on Tuesday, suggesting consumer confidence is rapidly recovering even as Beijing ramps up coronavirus curbs after a resurgence in infections in the capital.

Headlines: Reddit bans 'The_Donald' forum amid broad social media crackdown
Description: Social media site Reddit on Monday shut down r/The_Donald, a forum which long served as a popular online home base for fans of President Donald Trump, saying it violated the site's hate speech rules.

Headlines: Cirque du Soleil files for bankruptcy protection as COVID-19 cancels shows
Description: Canada's Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group filed for bankruptcy protection on Monday as the COVID-19 pandemic forced the famed circus operator to cancel shows and lay off its artistes.

Headlines: Unions sue three Nevada casino properties, claiming dangerous working conditions
Description: Unions representing 60,000 hospitality workers in Las Vegas and Reno, Nevada, are suing three casino properties over allegations of dangerous working conditions.

Headlines: Norwegian Air cancels 97 Boeing MAX and Dreamliners, claims compensation
Description: Norwegian Air  has cancelled orders for 97 Boeing  aircraft and will claim compensation from the U.S. plane maker for the grounding of the 737 MAX and for 787 engine troubles that hit its bottom line, the Oslo-based carrier said on Monday.

Headlines: Coronavirus rekindles global trade disputes
Description: At the start of the year, U.S.-China tensions were easing after their Phase I trade deal, while Washington, Brussels and Tokyo agreed on new global trading rules to curb subsidies. A relative calm had set in.

Headlines: Canada federal court dismisses drugmakers' plea challenging drug price rules
Description: The federal court of Canada on Monday dismissed a plea by drugmakers challenging the Canadian government's new regulations aimed at lowering prices of patented drugs that could potentially lead them to lose billions over a decade.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs says it's climbing toward Fed's capital demands
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  has already boosted capital measures and is working to meet the Federal Reserve's benchmark for October, the Wall Street bank said in a statement on Monday.

Headlines: Automakers rev up discounts to beat coronavirus sales blues
Description: In the midst of a raging pandemic, Belal Bilto, 26, a sales executive and a Manhattan resident bought a midsize pickup Jeep Gladiator this month for just over $48,000, lured by a discount of about $5,000 on the list price and a seven-year, no-interest loan.

Headlines: Credit Suisse taps Santangelo as global co-head of healthcare
Description: Credit Suisse Group AG  has named Rob Santangelo as a global co-head of its healthcare investment banking group, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: Tesla's Musk calls on workers to help company break even in second quarter
Description: Tesla Inc  chief Elon Musk in an internal email called on employees to work hard to allow the electric car maker to break even in the second quarter despite the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: U.S. still poised for 'V-shaped recovery' despite reopening setbacks: Trump adviser
Description: The U.S. economy still appears headed for a "V-shaped recovery" despite some setbacks in efforts to reopen state economies that had been shuttered for the coronavirus, a top White House adviser said on Monday.

Headlines: Wall Street leads stocks' rebound, sterling dips
Description: A gauge of stocks across the world rose on Monday, led by a rebound on Wall Street, even as rising COVID-19 cases threaten to stall the recovery of the world's largest economy.

Headlines: Fed's Powell stresses uncertainty, challenges facing U.S. economy
Description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Monday said the outlook for the world's biggest economy is "extraordinarily uncertain" and will depend both on containing the coronavirus and on government efforts to support the recovery.

Headlines: Chesapeake asks to cancel pipeline contracts, sets drilling cuts
Description: Chesapeake Energy Corp  on Monday sought bankruptcy court approval to cancel $311 million in pipeline contracts, setting up a battle with U.S. regulators and operators including Energy Transfer LP, according to court filings.

Headlines: Fed opens primary market corporate bond facility
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve on Monday kicked off a long-awaited program to buy newly minted corporate bonds directly from companies, launching the last of the several programs created to stabilize financial markets rocked by the coronavirus.

Headlines: Exclusive: Facebook ad boycott campaign to go global, organizers say
Description: Organizers of a Facebook Inc  advertising boycott campaign that has drawn support from a rapidly expanding list of major companies are now preparing to take the battle global to increase pressure on the social media company to remove hate speech.

Headlines: Factbox: More companies join Facebook ad boycott bandwagon
Description: A long list of companies have pulled advertising from Facebook Inc  in support of a campaign that called out the social media giant for not doing enough to stop hate speech on its platforms.

Headlines: New York Times ends partnership with Apple News
Description: The New York Times Co said on Monday it will end its partnership with Apple News, effective June 29, at a time when the publisher is shifting focus to a digital subscription-based model.

Headlines: Dollar edges higher before quarter-end
Description: The greenback edged higher on Monday as investors positioned for quarter-end and weighed an increase in coronavirus cases in some U.S. states against improving economic data.

Headlines: Pandemic leads to six months of global market mayhem
Description: Probably the best thing to say about world financial markets so far this year is simply that it has been quite a ride.

Headlines: Oil rises on improving economic data but new coronavirus cases loom
Description: Oil prices rose about $1 a barrel on Monday, after bullish data from Asia and Europe, but investors are wary about sharp spikes in new coronavirus infections around the world.

Headlines: Ford pauses U.S. social media advertising, calls for hate speech to be 'eradicated' from content
Description: Ford Motor Co  said on Monday it would pause advertising on all social media platforms in the United States for the next 30 days, joining a growing list of companies that have stopped spending on Facebook Inc  in support of a campaign that called out the company for not doing enough to stop hate speech on its platform.

Headlines: Geneva motor show postponed until 2022: organizers
Description: The organizers of the Geneva International Motor Show said on Monday that they would not organize the event in 2021.

Headlines: Gilead prices COVID-19 drug remdesivir at $2,340 per patient in developed nations
Description: Gilead Sciences Inc on Monday priced its COVID-19 antiviral remdesivir at $2,340 per patient for wealthier nations and agreed to send nearly all of its supply of the drug to the United States over the next three months.

Headlines: Italy picks former Poste Italiane CEO to head re-nationalised Alitalia
Description: The Italian government has picked former Poste Italiane  CEO Francesco Caio as Chairman of Alitalia, Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte said, as the carrier prepares to return under state control after 11 years of private management.

Headlines: Germany's Henkel joins Facebook advertising boycott
Description: German consumer goods group Henkel  will join a boycott of advertising on Facebook , a spokesman said on Monday.

Headlines: Ryanair UK pilots to decide by Wednesday on plan to limit job losses
Description: Ryanair's British pilot union is to announce on Wednesday whether its members have backed an agreement brokered with management to mitigate the loss of 334 pilot jobs by agreeing to series of measures including a 20% pay cut, the union said.

Headlines: Fed's Daly says 'far too early' to judge U.S. recovery
Description: It is "far too early" to judge the strength of the recovery in the world's largest economy as it reopens after extended coronavirus shutdowns, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly told reporters on a conference call on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. appeals court stays order requiring GM, FCA meet to resolve GM lawsuit
Description: A U.S. appeals court on Monday stayed a lower court's order requiring officials from General Motors Co  and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles  to resolve GM's racketeering lawsuit.

Headlines: From New York to Houston, flood risk for real estate hubs ramps up
Description: The number of properties in the United States in danger of flooding this year is 70% higher than government data estimates, research released on Monday shows, with at-risk hot spots in Houston, New York, Los Angeles and Chicago.

Headlines: Airbus close to slashing jobs as CEO confirms 40% output drop
Description: Airbus  was finalising an imminent restructuring plan involving thousands of job cuts on Monday as its chief executive confirmed plans to hold output down by 40% for two years.

Headlines: Mike Ashley's Frasers Group takes Hugo Boss stake over 10%
Description: Mike Ashley's Frasers Group, formerly Sports Direct, said on Monday it has raised its stake in German fashion house Hugo Boss  to 10.1% through stocks and derivatives, part of his drive to take the British sportswear retailer upmarket.

Headlines: Coty to buy 20% stake in Kim Kardashian West's $1 billion beauty line
Description: Coty Inc said on Monday it would buy a 20% stake in reality TV star Kim Kardashian West's makeup brand KKW, as the cosmetics maker looks to cash in on the demand for celebrity-owned products.

Headlines: U.S. home contracts post record jump, factory activity improves in Texas
Description: Contracts to buy U.S. previously owned homes rebounded by the most on record in May, suggesting the housing market was starting to turn around after being hammered by the COVID-19 pandemic along with the rest of the economy.

Headlines: Wirecard collapse leads to call for German parliamentary inquiry
Description: Germany's opposition called on Monday for a parliamentary inquiry into the collapse of payments firm Wirecard after a global fraud that left a gaping hole in its books went undiscovered by auditors and regulators for years.

Headlines: A cash cliff spells trouble for U.S. unemployed, and everyone else
Description: Judith Ramirez is bracing for July. That's when the hotel housekeeper and her electrician husband - who have both been out of work for three months -  expect their combined unemployment benefits to drop by more than half, and their deferred $1,500 monthly mortgage payment on their Honolulu home to come due.

Headlines: H&M's online second-hand shop Sellpy launches in Germany
Description: Swedish online second-hand shop Sellpy, which is majority-owned by fashion giant H&M, has launched in Germany in a first step outside its home market as it bets on shoppers trending towards more sustainable consumption.

Headlines: BlackRock sees big risk of U.S. easing pandemic support too soon
Description: There is a significant risk that the policy response to the coronavirus crisis in the United States could be scaled back too soon, BlackRock Investment Institute's global chief investment strategist Mike Pyle said on Monday.

Headlines: Amazon to pay $500 million in one-time bonuses to front-line workers
Description: Amazon.com Inc said on Monday it would spend $500 million on one-time bonuses to its front-line employees and partners working through the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: U.S. pending home sales jump a record 44.3% in May
Description: Contracts to buy U.S. previously owned homes rebounded by the most on record in May, suggesting the housing market was starting to turn around after being hammered by the COVID-19 pandemic along with the rest of the economy.

Headlines: Nissan to launch 7 models in Africa to pursue growth
Description: Nissan Motor Co  aims to launch seven new models in Africa over the next two years, company executives said on Monday, as the Japanese automaker seeks to focus on high-growth markets to try to weather the impact of the COVID-19 crisis.

Headlines: Exclusive: India plans incentives for auto companies to boost exports - sources
Description: India is drawing up an incentive scheme for the autos sector aimed at doubling exports of vehicles and components in the next five years, four sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Germany agrees to terminate contract with accounting watchdog
Description: Germany will cancel its contract with the country's accounting watchdog FREP, a justice ministry spokesman said on Monday, after payments company Wirecard filed for insolvency last week in one of Germany's biggest fraud scandal.

Headlines: Latin America's airline apocalypse signals a future with weak competition
Description: Bankrupt LATAM Airlines  and Avianca Holdings   are dramatically retrenching their once grand ambitions amid the COVID-19 pandemic, reducing competition in Latin America as they mull once-unthinkable cooperation with rivals.

Headlines: LVMH-backed Australian swimsuit brand in administration due to virus
Description: Seafolly Pty Ltd, an Australian swimsuit maker part-owned by French fashion giant LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE , appointed administrators on Monday citing a sales downturn from the coronavirus, the latest casualty of the health crisis in the country's retail sector.

Headlines: KKR, Apollo among suitors for National Australia Bank's wealth unit: sources
Description: KKR & Co Inc  and Apollo Global Management Inc  are among potential buyers which have conducted due diligence on National Australia Bank's  wealth management unit, three sources familiar with matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Credit Suisse appoints new CEO for business in Israel
Description: Credit Suisse  on Monday appointed Hila Goldenberg as chief executive officer of its business in Israel.

Headlines: Nissan denies corporate conspiracy to oust ex-chairman Ghosn
Description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd  on Monday blasted suggestions in media reports of a conspiracy within the company to oust former chairman Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: Philippines promises 'thorough' probe of Wirecard, looking at three local payment firms
Description: The Philippines' anti-money laundering agency on Monday said it would conduct a "swift and thorough" investigation into scandal-hit German payments firm Wirecard AG and that it has drawn up an initial list of people and entities of interest.

Headlines: Japan automakers' May global sales drop 38% as lockdowns weigh
Description: Japanese automakers' global sales declined 38% in May, in the third straight month of big falls as most automotive factories and dealerships remained closed due to coronavirus lockdowns.

Headlines: China's factory activity likely slowed in June on subdued global demand, Reuters poll shows
Description: China's factory activity likely grew for the fourth month June but the pace may be waning, as global demand stayed subdued while a fresh coronavirus outbreak in the Chinese capital and rising worldwide cases threaten to undermine a gradual domestic recovery.

Headlines: Yield curve control a double-edged sword for BOJ as low rates strain banks
Description: The Bank of Japan's push to keep borrowing costs low to cushion the economic blow from the coronavirus is coming at the expense of the country's lenders, which are already buckling under the strain of decades of ultra-low interest rates.

Headlines: Exclusive: Boeing 737 MAX certification flight tests to begin on Monday - sources
Description: Pilots and test crew members from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and Boeing Co  are slated to begin a three-day certification test campaign for the 737 MAX on Monday, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Sony sees software subscription as future for data-analyzing image sensors
Description: Sony Corp's image sensor business aims to replicate PlayStation's success to address its reliance on a handful of manufacturers in the fickle smartphone market: It plans to sell software by subscription for data-analyzing sensors in situ.

Headlines: Japan's Takeda expects $200 million operating loss related to Novartis' Xiidra withdrawal
Description: Takeda Pharmaceutical Co Ltd  said on Monday it anticipates an operating loss of about $200 million related to Novartis AG's decision to withdraw a marketing application for the dry-eye drug Xiidra.

Headlines: Japanese bank predicts years of gloom for tourist hub Osaka
Description: Tetsuya Kan, head of a major regional bank in Osaka, said it will take two more years for the western Japan prefecture to recover from the damage caused by COVID-19, which has crushed the city's once thriving tourism and retail sectors.

Headlines: Shale pioneer Chesapeake Energy files for bankruptcy
Description: Chesapeake Energy Corp  filed for Chapter 11 on Sunday, becoming the largest U.S. oil and gas producer to seek bankruptcy protection in recent years as it bowed to heavy debts and the impact of the coronavirus outbreak on energy markets.

Headlines: Chesapeake Energy's bankruptcy delivers hit to reeling pipeline, service firms
Description: Chesapeake Energy Corp's bankruptcy will pile more pain onto leading energy service and pipeline companies whose revenues were already being slammed during the latest collapse in oil prices, according to energy analysts and corporate filings.

Headlines: SoftBank to repurchase $1.9 billion of corporate bonds
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp  said on Monday it will repurchase up to 200 billion yen ($1.9 billion) of its domestic unsecured corporate bonds from June 30 to July 17, part of its plan to pay down debt.

Headlines: Pepsi joining Facebook ad boycott, FOX Business Network reports
Description: PepsiCo Inc  will stop advertising on Facebook Inc , FOX Business Network reported https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/pepsi-facebook-ad-boycott on Sunday, citing sources.

Headlines: Mexico's Interjet to gradually reopen more routes from July
Description: Mexico's Interjet airline will begin restarting national and international routes in July, the company said on Sunday, as airlines across the world pin their hopes on recovering demand as some coronavirus pandemic restrictions on travel ease.

Headlines: Amazon workers in Germany to go on strike over coronavirus infections
Description: Workers at six Amazon sites in Germany will go on strike on Monday in protest over safety after some staff at logistics centres tested positive for coronavirus, labour union Verdi said.

Headlines: U.S. confirms Boeing 737 MAX certification flights could start Monday
Description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) confirmed Sunday it had approved key certification test flights for the grounded Boeing  737 MAX that could begin as soon Monday.

Headlines: Big tobacco, big oil and Buffett join Fed's portfolio
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve bought $428 million in bonds of individual companies through mid-June, making investments in household names like Walmart and AT&T as well as in major oil firms, tobacco giant Philip Morris International Inc, and a utility subsidiary of billionaire Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway holding company.

Headlines: Starbucks to pause paid advertising across social media to help stop hate speech
Description: Starbucks Corp  will pause advertising on all social media platforms as it explores the best ways to help stop the spread of hate speech, the company said in a statement on Sunday.

Headlines: Germany to sever ties with accounting watchdog after Wirecard scandal
Description: The German government plans to terminate its contract with the country's accounting watchdog after payments company Wirecard filed for insolvency last week in one of Germany's biggest fraud scandals, a government official said on Sunday.

Headlines: Ryanair bypasses union, threatens base closures in Irish pilot talks
Description: Ryanair  has threatened to close two regional bases and axe up to 120 pilot jobs unless pilots in its home Irish market bypass their union and directly accept a pay cut, a memo seen by Reuters said.

Headlines: Spanish airline Iberia will downsize due to coronavirus: CEO
Description: Spanish airline Iberia will reduce the size of its fleet, the number of destinations it flies to and how frequently as the coronavirus pandemic continues to drag on demand, its chief executive officer said in a newspaper interview.

Headlines: China's big three airlines take delivery of domestically made ARJ21 aircraft
Description: China's three biggest state-owned airlines on Sunday took delivery of their first ARJ21 aircraft, a short haul 90-seater aircraft made by state-run Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC).

Headlines: Under Armour to discontinue record apparel partnership with UCLA
Description: Athletic apparel maker Under Armour  said on Saturday it will discontinue its partnership with UCLA - a 15-year, $280 million accord announced in 2016 that was billed as the largest apparel deal in the history of American collegiate sports.

Headlines: Some Disneyland workers protest reopening plans amid pandemic
Description: Workers at California's Disneyland Resort protested from their cars on Saturday, arguing that the Walt Disney Co  has not agreed to adequate protections for employees when the destination reopens to the public amid a pandemic.

Headlines: American Airlines CEO sees 10%-20% extra staff in July 2021, 'hard' to avoid furloughs
Description: American Airlines Group Inc  expects to have between 10% and 20% more workers than needed in July 2021, Chief Executive Doug Parker told employees at a town hall this week, and said that avoiding furloughs will be difficult.

Headlines: Germany's beleaguered Wirecard to proceed with business after insolvency
Description: Wirecard, the German scandal-hit payments company,  said on Saturday it would proceed with business activities after filing for insolvency and expects a provisional administrator to be appointed by judicial authorities shortly.

Headlines: Delta to warn pilots about possible furloughs, offers early retirement
Description: Delta Air Lines  said late on Friday it will soon send warning notices to about 2,500 pilots regarding possible furloughs at the airline, as the industry takes a huge blow after the coronavirus pandemic slashed air travel demand.

Headlines: Grounded jets sit out coronavirus pandemic in Pyrenees
Description: At the airport of Tarbes in France, row upon row of empty jets in liveries from Asia to Africa sit nose to tail on the tarmac, waiting out the coronavirus crisis in the foothills of the Pyrenees.

Headlines: German development bank could lose 100 million euros from Wirecard insolvency
Description: Germany's state development bank KfW could lose 100 million euros ($112.17 million) after payments company Wirecard filed for insolvency, a spokesman said on Saturday.

Headlines: Amazon, SoftBank held talks over Russian online retailer Ozon, shareholder says
Description: Global retail giant Amazon  and Japanese SoftBank  have made approaches to Russian conglomerate Sistema  about a possible acquisition of its online retailer Ozon, Sistema's majority owner Vladimir Evtushenkov said on Saturday.

Headlines: New York court subpoenas Etihad, Fitch in $1.2 billion debt battle

Headlines: Carlyle buys 20% stake in Piramal Pharma businesses
Description: U.S.-based Carlyle Group Inc has agreed to buy a 20% stake in the pharmaceutical unit of Indian conglomerate Piramal Enterprises Ltd for about $490 million, the companies said in a statement on Saturday.

Headlines: Facebook will label newsworthy posts that break rules as ad boycott widens
Description: Facebook Inc said on Friday it will start labeling newsworthy content that violates the social media company's policies, and label all posts and ads about voting with links to authoritative information, including those from politicians.

Headlines: GM seeks U.S. appeals court ruling to continue legal fight with Fiat Chrysler
Description: General Motors Co on Friday asked a U.S. appeals court to allow it to continue pursuing its civil racketeering suit against rival Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV, rejecting a lower court judge's belittling of the complaint.

Headlines: Investors eye economic data, stimulus measures as stocks rally stalls
Description: Upcoming U.S. economic data and deadlines for renewing some fiscal stimulus measures in July could prove key tests for an equities rebound that has wavered in recent weeks.

Description: Wells Fargo & Co  employees will be working from home till at least Sept. 7 due to the coronavirus pandemic, Bloomberg reported on Friday.

Description: The piercing boom of illegal fireworks in New York is music to the ears of Joe VanOudenhove, who runs a legal fireworks business in Pennsylvania.

Description: Wall Street's major indexes tumbled more than 2% on Friday as several U.S. states imposed business restrictions in response to a surge in coronavirus cases.

Description: (This June 9 story corrects to remove reference to speaking with Gupta at his office)

Description: Luckin Coffee Inc  said on Friday its board had proposed to remove its chairman, Charles Zhengyao Lu, following an internal probe into the fabrication of the embattled coffee chain's annual sales numbers.

Description: The European Union is investigating Germany's financial regulator over the collapse of payments company Wirecard in a rare move that heaps embarrassment on Berlin days before it is due to take over the EU's rotating presidency.

Description: A Filipino lawyer embroiled in a multi-billion dollar fraud at Wirecard, Mark Tolentino, told Reuters that he was surprised to be linked to the German payments firm and that he was the "victim of a frame-up".
