Description: The United States has secured almost a third of the first 1 billion doses planned for AstraZeneca's experimental COVID-19 vaccine by pledging up to $1.2 billion, as world powers scramble for medicines to get their economies back to work.

Headlines: Facebook's Zuckerberg embraces remote work beyond Silicon Valley
Description: Facebook Inc will permanently embrace remote work even after coronavirus lockdowns ease, Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said on Thursday, accelerating the tech sector's geographic diversification away from its home in Silicon Valley.

Headlines: Proxy adviser ISS recommends vote 'against' executive pay at Alphabet
Description: Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) has recommended shareholders of Google-parent Alphabet Inc to vote "against" the company's proposed executive pay at its annual meet in June, according to a report seen by Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: SoftBank Group's sale of 5% telco unit stake to raise $2.9 billion
Description: SoftBank Group Corp said on Friday its planned sale of 5% in its domestic telco SoftBank Corp would fetch  310.2 billion yen ($2.9 billion), as part of a programme to raise $41 billion through asset sales.

Headlines: Nvidia forecasts sales above estimates, powered by data center results
Description: Nvidia Corp  on Thursday forecast second-quarter revenue above analysts' estimates, as demand surges for its chips used in the data centers that power the shift to working remotely because of the new coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Wall Street finishes down as U.S.-China tensions heighten trade deal worries
Description: Wall Street ended lower on Thursday, a day after hitting two-month highs, on a fresh wave of China-U.S. tensions that raised doubts about the trade deal reached early this year between the world's two largest economies.

Headlines: GM starts to reopen plants in Mexico
Description: General Motors Co  said that it was on Thursday gradually restarting the transmissions and motors lines at its Mexican plants in Ramos Arizpe in the northern state of Coahuila and in the central city of Silao.

Headlines: Hewlett Packard Enterprise lays out $1 billion savings plan, pay cuts
Description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise  on Thursday unveiled a plan targeting gross savings of at least $1 billion by 2022 and cut the base salaries of top executives by 25% as the software maker seeks to weather the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Lear Corp asks some Mexico workers to restart activity on Friday
Description: U.S. auto parts maker Lear Corp has asked some workers in Mexico to restart activity on Friday, including training sessions on safety, the company said in a message to employees.

Headlines: Senators attempt to advance bill lengthening coronavirus business loan terms
Description: Negotiators in the U.S. Senate reached agreement on Thursday on legislation that would double the period of time in which small businesses can use Paycheck Protection Program loans, to 16 weeks from the current eight-week limit, according to a Senate aide.

Headlines: Indiana mattress business adapts to lure customers back
Description: Lauren Taylor is figuring out what’s required to run a mattress store in the age of a deadly pandemic.

Headlines: U.S. meat inventories tightened as virus shut slaughterhouses: USDA
Description: U.S. frozen pork inventories fell in April, when they typically rise, and beef inventories dropped more than normal as the coronavirus pandemic shut slaughterhouses and prompted grocers to limit customers' buying, government data showed on Thursday.

Headlines: Top safety official at Waymo self-driving unit stepping down
Description: Alphabet Inc’s Waymo self-driving unit said on Thursday that its chief safety officer, Debbie Hersman, was stepping down but would remain as a consultant to the company.

Headlines: 'I've not yet signed Renault loan', says French finance minister
Description: France's Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said he has not signed off on a 5 billion euro ($5.47 billion) state-guaranteed loan to help Renault  cope with the fallout from the coronavirus, and that discussions continued.

Headlines: Stocks slip on U.S.-China tensions; oil rises to 2-1/2-month high
Description: Global equities slid on Thursday on concerns about the long-term impact of the new coronavirus and resurgent U.S.-China tensions, though oil markets ignored those worries and marched to 2-1/2 month highs.

Headlines: Macy's to be 'smaller company' as loss to hit $1 billion in quarter amid lockdowns
Description: Macy's Inc  said on Thursday it could rack up operating losses of up to $1.11 billion in the first quarter, as the department store operator was forced to shut stores due to lockdowns aimed at curbing the spread of the new coronavirus.

Headlines: Brent at highest since March on U.S. stock draw, recovering demand
Description: Global benchmark Brent rose more than 1% on Thursday to its highest since March, supported by lower U.S. crude inventories, OPEC-led supply cuts and recovering demand as governments ease coronavirus restrictions on people's movements.

Headlines: How big unions smooth the way for Amazon worker protests
Description: Warehouse employees last month staged a walkout in Michigan to demand safer working conditions at their facility. So did workers in New York, Illinois and Minnesota.

Headlines: U.S. labor market struggles as layoffs spread despite businesses reopening
Description: Millions more Americans filed for unemployment benefits last week, more than two months after a shutdown of the country to deal with the coronavirus crisis, pointing to a second wave of layoffs in industries not initially impacted by closures caused by the pandemic.

Headlines: Americans splurge at Walmart, Target as stimulus checks kick in
Description: The Trump Administration's coronavirus relief payment provided a fillip to sales of major retailers in April as millions of Americans used the money to buy everything from video games to sewing machines even as the country struggles with record job losses.

Headlines: Southwest to limit seats sold on each flight through July -CEO
Description: Southwest Airlines Co  will continue to limit bookings on its flights through at least July to give passengers space between seats, CEO Gary Kelly told shareholders on Thursday, mirroring a plan by competitor Delta Air Lines Inc .

Headlines: Exclusive: Baidu considers leaving the Nasdaq to boost its valuation - sources
Description: Chinese search engine giant Baidu Inc  is considering delisting from the U.S. Nasdaq and moving to an exchange closer to home to boost its valuation amid rising tension between the United States and China over investments, three sources said.

Headlines: Michigan Governor Whitmer further opens state economy ahead of Trump visit
Description: Michigan's governor announced more steps to re-open the state's economy on Thursday, offering timelines for the resumption of some businesses and allowing some social gatherings as long as guidelines to curb the spread of the coronavirus are observed.

Headlines: Mnuchin sees U.S. economic bottom in second quarter, 'gigantic increase' fourth quarter
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Thursday he believes the U.S. economy will "bottom out" in the second quarter and start to improve with the third quarter, with a "gigantic increase" in fourth quarter activity.

Headlines: Morgan Stanley CEO: too early to consider restarting share buybacks
Description: Morgan Stanley's  Chief Executive Officer James Gorman told shareholders on Thursday that it is too early for him or anyone on the board of directors to consider reinstating the bank's share buyback program.

Headlines: Uber has spent $19 million on coronavirus financial assistance for drivers
Description: Uber Technologies Inc on Thursday for the first time detailed how much it has spent to support its ride-hail drivers and food delivery workers during the coronavirus crisis, which has battered the company and forced it to lay off thousands of employees.

Headlines: U.S. state unemployment payments in April jump five-fold from February
Description: Unemployment payments jumped to at least $16.2 billion in April, up more than five-fold from February, as layoffs attributed to the coronavirus pandemic swept through the economy.

Headlines: Largest asset manager wins backing for jumbo board
Description: BlackRock Inc  said all of its 16 director nominees received strong investor support at its annual meeting on Thursday, at which Chief Executive Laurence Fink defended the size of the company's large board.

Headlines: Amazon pushes Prime Day to September as it returns to normalcy: WSJ
Description: Amazon.com Inc is scheduling its annual Prime Day shopping event for September and allowing unlimited shipments of non-essential goods to warehouses, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: U.S. existing home sales post largest decline in nearly 10 years
Description: U.S. home sales logged their biggest drop in nearly 10 years in April as the novel coronavirus pandemic upended the labor market and broader economy, undercutting demand for housing.

Headlines: Best Buy sees margin pressure as online demand raises delivery spend
Description: Best Buy Co Inc  said on Thursday it expects profit margins to be under pressure in the second quarter, as it spends more on expanding delivery services to support a surge in online shopping from people staying at home due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: The slow reopen: Retail visits edge up, broader economic measures still unmoved
Description: The U.S. continued its cautious reemergence from a coronavirus-linked shutdown over the past week, with measures of retail foot traffic slowly increasing but broader indexes of economic activity still stalled.

Headlines: TJX says sales recovering after coronavirus slump
Description: TJX Cos Inc  said it was seeing very strong sales at its stores reopened post-coronavirus lockdowns, offering hope of a swift recovery after a huge quarterly loss due to closures and a resulting decline in sales, sending its shares up 6% on Thursday.

Headlines: Starbucks recoups nearly two-thirds of comparable U.S. sales as stores reopen
Description: Starbucks Corp  said on Thursday it had regained nearly two-thirds of its comparable U.S. store sales from the prior year, as it reopened stores and modified operations due to the coronavirus-related restrictions.

Headlines: Gap rushes in more robots to warehouses to solve virus disruption
Description: U.S. apparel chain Gap Inc  is speeding up its rollout of warehouse robots for assembling online orders so it can limit human contact during the coronavirus pandemic, the company told Reuters.

Headlines: Lufthansa closes in on $10 billion state rescue deal
Description: Lufthansa  is in advanced talks over a 9 billion euros ($9.9 billion) state bailout that would see Germany take a 20% stake in its flagship airline, as countries battle to save an aviation industry hammered by the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: U.S. leveraged loan defaults at six-year high as coronavirus hits businesses
Description: The monthly tally of defaults in the U.S. leveraged loan market has hit a six-year high, data from Fitch Ratings showed, as companies are either missing payments or filing for bankruptcy because of the fallout from the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Traders Beware: U.S. taps new tools to find fraud in volatile commodities market
Description: When the U.S. Department of Justice charged a handful of JP Morgan Chase & Co  traders in 2018 and 2019 with alleged commodities futures manipulation, it wasn't the first time the government had probed the bank's metals trading activities.

Headlines: While U.S. economy slides, heartland auto dealers cry out for more trucks
Description: Jerry Bill is worried the novel coronavirus could hurt business at the Des Moines auto dealership he runs, but not because of a shortage of buyers for the big Ram pickups on his lot.

Headlines: Japan to seek extradition of men arrested in U.S. over Ghosn escape
Description: Japan said on Thursday it was working to secure the rapid extradition of two men arrested in the United States on charges of enabling the dramatic escape of former Nissan Motor Co boss Carlos Ghosn from the country.

Headlines: In SoftBank slides, tofu, a goose and unicorns underpin sales pitch
Description: A chastened Masayoshi Son summed up SoftBank Group Corp's  record $13 billion operating loss on stage this week with a striking image: unicorns tumbling into the "valley of the coronavirus".

Headlines: Sellers beware: Price collapse triggers bartering over oil and gas deals
Description: The collapse in oil prices to 21-year lows has led potential buyers of oil and gas fields to try and renegotiate deals already agreed at higher prices, with the first examples emerging of sellers having their hand forced.

Headlines: Israeli anti-viral mask maker Sonovia eyes Nasdaq listing this year
Description: Israel's Sonovia Ltd, which makes washable and reusable anti-viral masks, is considering going public on Nasdaq by the end of this year, its chief technology officer said.

Headlines: U.S. arrests two men wanted by Japan over ex-Nissan boss Carlos Ghosn's escape
Description: U.S. authorities on Wednesday arrested a former U.S. Army Special Forces soldier and another man in Massachusetts wanted by Japan on charges that they enabled the escape of former Nissan Motor Co boss Carlos Ghosn out of the country.

Headlines: SoftBank to sell $3.1 billion worth of Japan telco unit stake
Description: SoftBank Group Corp  said it plans to sell 5% of its domestic telco SoftBank Corp , currently worth $3.1 billion, as part of a programme to raise $41 billion through asset sales.

Headlines: JPMorgan plans to hire a dozen research analysts for China brokerage: sources
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  plans to hire at least 12 equity research analysts in China this year, two people with knowledge of the matter said, in its first major mainland hiring push as it takes advantage of eased ownership rules for financial firms.

Headlines: Wanted: New head of WTO. Must thrive under global pressure and conflict
Description: Against the backdrop of a global pandemic, steep recession, intensifying U.S-China tensions and rising protectionism, the WTO needs to name a leader. Only the resilient should apply.

Headlines: Britons spurned by banks caught in a coronavirus credit crunch
Description: When a payroll glitch left Natalie Gallagher so short of cash this month she couldn't afford her bus fare to work, she turned to her usual lender Amigo for an emergency top-up loan.

Headlines: Exclusive: Schlumberger names new top executives to oversee corporate overhaul
Description: Schlumberger, the world's largest oilfield services firm, will reshuffle top executives and operations in coming months to deal with this year's historic decline in the oil industry, according to a memo to employees.

Headlines: Canada Goose lays off 125 workers
Description: Retailer Canada Goose Holdings Inc said on Wednesday it has laid off 125 workers, about 2.5% of its global workforce, as part of steps to cope with the impact of COVID-19 on its business.

Headlines: Mastercard to allow staff to work from home until virus fears subside
Description: Mastercard Inc  will not ask employees to return to its worldwide corporate offices until they are comfortable that the sometimes fatal coronavirus is under control with vaccines or other measures, a senior executive told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Japan 'closely communicating' with U.S. after arrest of two men over Ghosn escape: source
Description: Japan is closely communicating with relevant U.S. authorities following the U.S. arrest of two men on charges they enabled former Nissan Motor Co chairman Carlos Ghosn to escape from Japan last year, a Japanese government source said on Thursday.

Headlines: Nissan says it has noted U.S. arrests in Ghosn case, reserves right for legal measures
Description: Nissan Motor Co said on Thursday it still reserves the right to take further legal measures in the case of its ousted former Chairman Carlos Ghosn, after the United States arrested two men on charges they enabled his escape from Japan.

Headlines: Volkswagen admits car ad racist, apologizes
Description: Volkswagen  withdrew on Wednesday an advert posted on its official Instagram page for its Golf cars that it admitted was racist and insulting, saying it would investigate how it came about and draw consequences.

Headlines: U.S. regulators open door to possible tightening of Huawei chip curb
Description: U.S. regulators are open to making changes to close what some see as a loophole in a new rule aimed at curbing global chip sales to blacklisted Chinese telecoms equipment maker Huawei Technologies Ltd, two U.S. officials said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Four Democratic U.S. senators warn against Uber buying Grubhub
Description: Four Democratic lawmakers, led by Senator Amy Klobuchar, wrote to antitrust enforcers on Wednesday to warn that plans by Uber Technologies Inc, owner of Uber Eats, to buy rival online food delivery company Grubhub Inc would "raise serious competition issues" in many cities.

Headlines: U.S. airlines step up safety measures in preparation for recovery
Description: U.S. carriers JetBlue Airways Corp and United Airlines Holdings Inc announced fresh safety measures on Wednesday aimed at restoring confidence in air travel as several executives pointed to signs domestic demand is improving.

Headlines: Expedia signals May rebound as cancellations stabilize
Description: Online travel booking company Expedia Group Inc  on Wednesday pointed to demand recovering in May as cancellation rates stabilize, overshadowing a bigger-than-expected quarterly  loss and sending its shares up nearly 4%.

Headlines: Wall Street climbs on stimulus hopes, as S&P, Nasdaq hit multi-month highs
Description: The three major averages on Wall St. notched their fourth gain in five sessions on Wednesday as investors again bet on a swift economic recovery from coronavirus-driven lockdowns and the potential for more stimulus measures from the Federal Reserve.

Headlines: Higher dose of Gilead-Galapagos drug meets ulcerative colitis study goals
Description: Gilead Sciences Inc  and partner Galapagos NV  said on Wednesday only a higher dose of their experimental drug filgotinib showed greater effectiveness than placebo in a pivotal study testing it in ulcerative colitis patients.

Headlines: Ford shuts two U.S. assembly plants due to COVID-19 infections
Description: Ford Motor Co on Wednesday closed two U.S. assembly plants as the coronavirus pandemic wreaked early havoc with the No. 2 U.S. automaker's plan to restart North American production and begin making its most profitable vehicles again.

Headlines: At Fiat Chrysler's Brazil plant, production resumes with safety checks
Description: Before going to work these days, employees at the Brazilian unit of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles  have to get a health check using a mobile app every morning.

Headlines: Fed debates longer-term crisis-fighting plan, minutes show
Description: Federal Reserve policymakers, still working to fully roll out a multi-trillion-dollar effort to shore up financial markets and an economy cratered by the coronavirus pandemic, last month dove into a new debate: how best to support the economy during a recovery they now agree could be slower and more fraught than initially thought.

Headlines: Oil gains, stocks rally on renewed recovery hopes
Description: Crude prices rose and a gauge of global equities broke out of a three-week trading range on Wednesday as investors bet on a rapid recovery from the coronavirus-induced recession.

Headlines: Germany agrees on rescue package for Lufthansa: media
Description: The German government has agreed on final details of a rescue package for airline carrier Lufthansa , media reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Oil rises on lower U.S. stocks, firmer demand
Description: Oil prices rallied on Wednesday after U.S. crude inventories fell in the most recent week, but gains were capped by worries over the economic fallout from the coronavirus pandemic and weak refining margins.

Headlines: U.S. travelers pick car rentals over flights for holidays: travel website Kayak
Description: Travel website Kayak is seeing more demand for car rentals than air travel from customers looking to avoid crowds and stay closer to home as U.S. states reopen, Chief Executive Officer Steve Hafner told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Northern Trust shutting fund; an outlier or sign of future risk?
Description: Northern Trust Corp's decision to liquidate a $1.8-billion prime money market fund was seen as an outlier event by industry analysts on Wednesday, but one that could portend more problems depending on how the economy fares.

Headlines: Senate passes bill that could block Chinese firms from U.S. securities exchanges
Description: The U.S. Senate passed legislation on Wednesday that could prevent some Chinese companies from listing their shares on U.S. exchanges unless they follow standards for U.S. audits and regulations.

Headlines: Air France axes A380, Emirates seen cutting deliveries
Description: The world's largest airliner, the Airbus  A380, took a step closer to the aviation archives on Wednesday as Air France said it would permanently axe its grounded fleet and sources said Emirates was in talks to reduce remaining deliveries.

Headlines: FCA-PSA deal terms 'set in stone' for 50-50 merger
Description: Terms of a planned merger between Fiat Chrysler  and Peugeot-owner PSA  are set in stone, FCA's chairman said on Wednesday, brushing off talk that some aspects of the deal might be re-negotiated because of the COVID-19 crisis.

Headlines: Apollo Global invests $1.75 billion in U.S. supermarket operator Albertsons
Description: Buyout firm Apollo Global Management  said on Wednesday it has invested $1.75 billion in Albertsons Companies Inc, a sign of confidence in the debt-laden U.S. supermarket operator whose fortunes have picked up in the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Trump administration abruptly postpones New Mexico oil and gas auction
Description: The Trump administration abruptly postponed an auction of oil and gas leases in New Mexico that had been scheduled to begin on Wednesday morning without providing a reason for the move.

Headlines: U.S. workplace safety agency steps up COVID-19 inspections
Description: The U.S. Labor Department will expand inspections of businesses to reduce job-site hazards related to the new coronavirus as employees begin returning to work across the country, although the policy falls short of demands by worker advocates.

Headlines: BlackRock willing to lower ask on Argentine restructuring counter to 50-55 cents: source
Description: BlackRock Inc  is willing to drop the ask in a debt restructuring proposal to the Argentine government to between 50-55 cents on the dollar and had made the suggestion to its creditor committee, a source familiar with the group's discussions said.

Headlines: Zalando proposes Rent The Runway CEO to join board
Description: German online fashion retailer Zalando  proposed on Wednesday that Jennifer Hyman, the chief executive of U.S. clothing rental firm Rent the Runway, joins its supervisory board, replacing Alexander Samwer.

Headlines: Canada recommends masks, says emergency loans have no cap but many limits
Description: There will be no cap on the size of Canada's emergency loans to large companies harmed by the coronavirus pandemic but there will be multiple restrictions, the government said on Wednesday, as it recommended wearing masks in public for the first time.

Headlines: Target's online sales surge eases coronavirus pain
Description: A surge in Target Corp's  online sales due to panic buying during the coronavirus crisis helped the big-box retailer post better-than-expected quarterly results on Wednesday, even as it grappled with soaring operational costs.

Headlines: Dow shuts Midland operations after flood waters sweep in
Description: Dow Inc said on Wednesday it has shut down all operating units at its headquarters in Midland, Michigan, after flood waters breached its sites following the collapse of two dams.

Headlines: U.S. House to vote on extending small business coronavirus loan program
Description: Lawmakers in the U.S. House of Representatives plan to vote again next week on giving small businesses more time to utilize their coronavirus aid under the Paycheck Protection Program, House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said on Wednesday.

Headlines: JPMorgan to use common desks to make offices easier to clean after pandemic
Description: When JPMorgan Chase & Co  staff return to offices in regions slowly re-opening from the coronavirus lockdown, some may be required to sit at common desks, or "hot desks," a temporary seating arrangement that management hopes will make it easier to clean, according to a memo seen by Reuters.

Headlines: France wants Renault to maintain its French plants
Description: The French government will insist on preserving Renault  production plants in France and wants it to remain the carmaker's global centre for engineering, research, innovation and development, Prime Minister Edouard Philippe said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Renault to re-open its Sandouville plant on Friday: union source
Description: French carmaker Renault  will re-open its Normandy-based Sandouville plant in northwestern France on Friday, a trade union source told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Lowe's says surging sales will not last
Description: Lowe's Cos Inc  warned on Wednesday that high spending on do-it-yourself projects by people hunkered down at home due to coronavirus lockdowns would taper off in the coming months, as a deep economic recession looms on the horizon.

Headlines: OPEC chief says oil market responding well to record OPEC+ cut
Description: OPEC is encouraged by a rally in oil prices and strong adherence to its latest output cut, its secretary general said, although sources say the group has not ruled out further steps to support the market.

Headlines: Johnson & Johnson to stop selling talc baby powder in U.S. and Canada
Description: Johnson & Johnson will stop selling its talc Baby Powder in the United States and Canada, it announced on Tuesday, saying demand had fallen in the wake of what it called "misinformation" about the product's safety amid a barrage of legal challenges.

Headlines: Britain's Rolls-Royce to axe 9,000 jobs in air travel slump
Description: Rolls-Royce  plans to cut at least 9,000 jobs, or more than a sixth of its workforce, in the latest blows to the UK economy and aviation industry dealt by the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Britain ready to support Rolls-Royce employees over job cuts
Description: Britain's government stands ready to help those affected by a plan at engine maker Rolls-Royce  to cut at least 9,000 jobs, a spokesman for Prime Minister Boris Johnson said on Wednesday.

Headlines: JPMorgan directors reelected, former Exxon executive overcomes opposition
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  shareholders voted to reelect all of the bank's board members on Tuesday, including a former Exxon Mobil Corp  CEO who drew criticism from environmental groups and New York City's comptroller and pension system leader.

Headlines: Unions say Ryanair exaggerating COVID threat to undermine conditions
Description: Several Ryanair trade unions say they will resist an attempt to cut pay and conditions for a five-year period, citing management promises of a swift recovery from the coronavirus crisis and the fact its CEO has committed to a pay cut for just one year.

Headlines: Nestle to build new plant-based food facility in China under $100 million investment plan
Description: Food giant Nestle  said on Wednesday it would spend 100 million swiss francs ($103.58 million) on expanding its manufacturing footprint in China to include a new plant-based food facility and widen its production lines.

Headlines: Luckin Coffee shares crash on delisting risk
Description: Shares in Luckin Coffee Inc  slumped almost 40% to a record low in premarket trade on Wednesday, as they resumed trading after more than a month's halt and a day after the Chinese coffee chain said it received a delisting notice from Nasdaq .

Headlines: Harley plans to ship fewer models to U.S. dealers: WSJ
Description: Harley-Davidson Inc  is reopening its factories this week at lower production rates and sending dealers a narrower range of motorcycles, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: German court ends diesel case against Volkswagen CEO, Chairman
Description: A German court said on Wednesday it was ending proceedings against the chairman and chief executive of Volkswagen AG  after the carmaker agreed to pay a fine of 9 million euros ($9.9 million) over the diesel emissions scandal.

Headlines: SoftBank-backed Ola follows Uber with job cuts as revenue sinks
Description: SoftBank Group-backed Indian ride-hailing company Ola will cut 1,400 jobs, or about 35% of its workforce, as it navigates a strict coronavirus lockdown that has halted 95% of its business, company chief Bhavish Aggarwal told employees on Wednesday.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank chairman to stand down in 2022
Description: Deutsche Bank's  chairman Paul Achleitner said he intends to step down when his term ends in 2022, heralding a new era at Germany's largest lender as it struggles to become profitable.

Headlines: Norwegian Air's lessors take majority ownership
Description: Lessors including AerCap and BOC Aviation  are now the biggest shareholders in Norwegian Air  after the budget carrier completed a debt restructuring and secured a long-sought credit guarantee from Norway's government.

Headlines: Delta CEO: More summer flights seen as U.S. travel slowly rises
Description: Delta Air Lines Inc  is likely to increase capacity this summer by adding flights in June and July as U.S. domestic travel slowly picks up amid the novel coronavirus pandemic, its chief executive officer said on Wednesday.

Headlines: AT&T shuts Venezuela subscription TV unit, citing U.S. sanctions
Description: AT&T Inc  said on Tuesday it was shutting its DirecTV subscription access to Venezuela due to U.S. sanctions, cutting off a key source of entertainment for millions of people stuck in their homes under a strict coronavirus quarantine.

Headlines: Mining companies rush to shield indigenous communities from coronavirus
Description: Big mining companies that rely on indigenous workforces or operate near remote communities have acted fast to curb the spread of the coronavirus and avoid a public health crisis that could damage their reputations.

Headlines: Dutch government's 2019 purchase of Air France-KLM shares 'irregular': audit office
Description: A 2019 move by the Dutch government to buy a 14% stake in Air France-KLM  was not in accordance with the country's laws, the Netherlands' Court of Audit ruled on Wednesday.

Headlines: Coronavirus crushes Australia's dividends with banks leading the decline
Description: Australia has made the deepest dividend cuts globally this year, with more than $6 billion deferred or cancelled as companies conserve cash to ride out the coronavirus, turning foreign investors wary of the country's normally high-yielding firms.

Headlines: Germany approves new powers to block foreign takeovers in healthcare
Description: Germany gave itself new powers to veto hostile foreign takeover bids for healthcare companies on Wednesday, a measure designed to ensure a continuous supply of essential products during the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: U.S. blacklists Chinese logistics firm over business with Iran airline
Description: Washington on Tuesday imposed sanctions on a China-based company it accused of acting on behalf of U.S.-blacklisted Mahan Air, the Treasury Department said, and denounced the Iranian airline's flights to Venezuela.

Headlines: UK will look at helping Rolls Royce employees and the sector: minister
Description: Britain will look at how it can help the employees of Rolls-Royce  after the engine maker said it would cut at least 9,000 jobs from its global staff of 52,000 and what options the government has to support the sector, the justice minister said.

Headlines: Rolls Royce could shut some factories with job cuts programme: CEO
Description: Rolls Royce  could close some of its factories as part of a programme to cut 9,000 jobs in response to the crisis in the global aviation industry, its chief executive said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Did hedge funds score on masks and sanitizer? Not so much
Description: What would seem like a sure win for elite investors - early bets on companies racing to make face masks, hand sanitizer and other coronavirus-related protective products - turned out to be a relatively unpopular strategy and one with surprisingly mixed results.

Headlines: Outlook for European corporate profits worsens further
Description: Expectations for second- and third-quarter corporate profits are deteriorating further in Europe, despite a gradual easing across the continent of lockdowns aimed at curbing the coronavirus pandemic, Refinitiv data showed on Wednesday.

Headlines: Fujifilm shares fall after report Avigan not showing clear efficacy in some coronavirus trials
Description: Shares of Fujifilm Holdings Corp  fell on Wednesday after Kyodo news reported that so far there has been no clear evidence of efficacy for its drug Avigan in treating the novel coronavirus in some clinical trials.

Headlines: Luckin scandal ripple effect prompts chairman-backed firm to seek cash: sources
Description: A company linked to China's scandal-hit Luckin Coffee Inc  is seeking fresh capital, sources said, highlighting the ripple effect of Luckin's fabricated transactions as the chairman of both firms scrambles to avoid a cash crunch.

Headlines: Global green energy growth to fall for first time in 20 years: IEA
Description: Global growth in new renewable energy capacity will experience its first annual decline in 20 years this year amid the coronavirus pandemic but is expected to pick up next year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.

Headlines: HSBC sees double-digit wealth asset growth in Asia by 2023
Description: HSBC Holdings PLC  expects to achieve double-digit asset growth in its newly combined wealth business in Asia Pacific in the next three years, as it looks to grab a bigger share of the growing rich population, the unit's regional head told Reuters.

Headlines: Exclusive: Exxon revives sale of stake in giant Azeri oilfield
Description: Exxon Mobil  has relaunched the sale of its stake in Azerbaijan's largest oilfield, the company said on Tuesday, as banking and industry sources said the move was drawing interest from large Asian oil and gas companies seeking to capitalize on the recent collapse in oil prices.

Headlines: Senate Democrats call for Trump administration to unveil details of TSMC plant deal
Description: Democratic lawmakers on Tuesday urged the Trump administration to answer "serious questions" about Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd's plans to build a U.S.-based $12 billion plant, flagging national security concerns and potentially undisclosed subsidies.

Headlines: Mnuchin defends U.S. fiscal response to pandemic, seeks payroll loan extension
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin on Tuesday defended the Trump administration's fiscal response to the coronavirus pandemic and told senators he was willing to consider extending and modifying a payroll loan program for small businesses.

Headlines: Trump wants payroll tax holiday to mitigate coronavirus economic pain: Kudlow
Description: White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said on Tuesday that President Donald Trump wants a payroll tax holiday for U.S. workers in the hopes of staunching economic pain caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Volkswagen pays 9 million euros to end proceedings against chairman, CEO
Description: Volkswagen AG  has agreed to pay 9 million euros ($9.9 million) in a deal with a German court to end legal proceedings against its chairman and chief executive, who were accused of holding back market-moving information on rigged emissions tests.

Headlines: U.S. to mandate new safety-management tools for aircraft makers
Description: The Federal Aviation Administration said Tuesday it would require Boeing Co and other aircraft manufacturers to adopt new safety-management tools following two fatal Boeing 737 MAX crashes that killed 346 people.

Headlines: U.S. workers hit McDonald's with class action over COVID-19 safety
Description: Five McDonald's workers in Chicago filed a class action lawsuit against the chain on Tuesday, accusing it of failing to adopt government safety guidance on COVID-19 and endangering employees and their families.

Headlines: Fiserv's First Data pays $40 million to settle FTC charges it aided merchants' fraud
Description: First Data Merchant Services LLC and a former executive will pay nearly $40.3 million to settle U.S. civil charges they knowingly processed payments and helped launder credit card transactions in four scams that harmed hundreds of thousands of consumers.

Headlines: Indigo Partners ties up with Oaktree for Virgin Australia bid: executive
Description: Indigo Partners is teaming up with Oaktree Capital Management in its offer for Virgin Australia Holdings Ltd  and will consider adding an Australian partner as the bidding process progresses, Indigo managing partner Bill Franke said.

Headlines: Spotify new home for Joe Rogan's podcast, shares jump
Description: Spotify Technology SA said on Tuesday comedian Joe Rogan's podcast will be available on the music streaming platform starting Sept. 1 and will become an exclusive later this year.

Headlines: S&P stumbles as Moderna sinks on report questioning trial results
Description: The S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday, as investors focused on a report questioning Moderna's recent coronavirus vaccine early-stage trial results, wiping out modest gains on the benchmark index in the last hour of trading.

Headlines: Urban Outfitters predicts 60% fall in same-store sales on slow recovery
Description: Apparel retailer Urban Outfitters Inc  on Tuesday projected a 60% decline in same-store sales in the second quarter due to tepid demand recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic disruptions, sending its shares down 6% in extended trading.

Headlines: Trump floats halt to U.S. cattle imports as pandemic hurts ranchers
Description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday the United States should consider terminating trade deals under which it imports cattle as he looks to help U.S. ranchers hit hard by the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: U.S. crude strengthens as certain stimulus measures to continue
Description: U.S. crude ended slightly higher on Tuesday, as U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said he supported extending certain measures intended to bolster the economy, while Brent ended lower on concerns that output cuts might not be sufficient.

Headlines: Exclusive: Third Point founder Daniel Loeb takes over as Munib Islam leaves firm
Description: Billionaire investor Daniel Loeb is taking back the reins as sole chief investment officer at his hedge fund Third Point LLC, less than one year after he appointed long-time colleague Munib Islam to be his co-chief investment officer, according to a letter the firm sent its investors.

Headlines: GM delays tentative restart for plant in Silao, Mexico to May 21
Description: General Motors Co signaled it has pushed back the tentative date for restarting operations at its auto assembly plant in the central Mexican city of Silao to May 21 from May 20, according to a message to workers seen by Reuters on Tuesday.

Headlines: MGM, Caesars and Boyd will participate in employee COVID-19 testing plan
Description: The Las Vegas gaming industry will offer COVID-19 tests to employees before they return to work, the Culinary Union announced Tuesday, moving the hard-hit sector a step closer to reopening.

Headlines: Business group cautions U.S. on 'reshoring' too much China supply
Description: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce on Tuesday warned the U.S. government against overdoing a major effort underway to rip U.S. supply chains out of China in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic, saying such moves could harm the economy.

Headlines: Lockheed may delay delivery of up to 24 F-35 jets as COVID-19 hits suppliers
Description: Lockheed Martin  said on Tuesday it will slow production of its stealthy F-35 fighter jets at its Texas facility, possibly delaying delivery of between 18 and 24 jets due to a parts shortage as the coronavirus hampers production across the jet's vast supply chain.

Headlines: Early data on Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine insufficient: Stat News
Description: Data from a small, early-stage safety trial testing Moderna Inc's  experimental COVID-19 vaccine does not provide the critical data needed to assess its effectiveness, health-focused Stat News reported on Tuesday, citing experts.

Headlines: Ford requires visitors to wear masks but unclear if Trump will comply
Description: Ford Motor Co  on Tuesday reiterated its policy that all visitors to its manufacturing plants must wear a mask but said the White House will ultimately decide if U.S. President Donald Trump will comply during a planned visit.

Headlines: Euro gains on EU recovery-fund plan, oil wavers
Description: The euro and European government debt rallied on Tuesday, lifted by a Franco-German proposal to fund grants for regions hit hardest by the coronavirus pandemic, while oil traded mostly higher on growing demand as countries eased business lockdowns.

Headlines: Early data on Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine insufficient: Stat News
Description: Data from a small, early-stage safety trial testing Moderna Inc's  experimental COVID-19 vaccine does not provide critical data to assess its effectiveness, Stat News reported on Tuesday, citing experts.

Headlines: Trump administration signs up new company to make COVID-19 drugs in U.S.
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration awarded a contract worth up to $812 million for a new U.S. company to manufacture drugs and drug ingredients to fight COVID-19 on American soil, aiming to end dependence on other countries.

Headlines: Visa extends work-from-home for majority of employees through 2020
Description: Visa Inc  will allow a majority of its workforce to work from home through 2020, according to Chief Executive Officer Alfred Kelly Jr., mirroring similar moves from other fintech companies earlier in the week.

Headlines: Elderly home turns to wearables for contact tracing, sidestepping Apple-Google limits
Description: When a senior living facility in Amarillo, Texas suspected a nurse may have caught the novel coronavirus this month, it had a list within five minutes of staff and residents the nurse could have infected.

Headlines: U.S. economy won't reclaim all of its lost ground until after 2021: CBO
Description: The U.S. economy should bounce back sharply in the third quarter after its deep coronavirus-related collapse, but it will not fully retake recover lost ground until sometime after next year, the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Coronavirus hammers U.S. homebuilding; permits tumble
Description: U.S. homebuilding dropped by the most on record in April and permits for future construction tumbled, underlining fears that the coronavirus crisis would lead to the deepest economic contraction in the second quarter since the Great Depression.

Headlines: Airlines say ticket cancellations slowing; business models may change
Description: Top U.S. airlines and Air Canada  on Tuesday reported slower ticket cancellations and an improvement in bookings on some routes, though executives said overall demand remained weak and changes to travel rules may force new business models.

Headlines: Nasdaq informs China's Luckin Coffee it plans to delist it
Description: Luckin Coffee Inc  said on Tuesday that Nasdaq Inc  has given it notice that it plans to delist it from the  U.S. stock exchange a month after the Chinese coffee chain disclosed that some of its employees fabricated sales accounts.

Headlines: Mnuchin says seeing large second quarter unemployment, negative economic data
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Tuesday that he is continuing to see large unemployment numbers and other negative economic indicators during the second quarter, but the situation is expected to improve as the U.S. economy starts to reopen.

Headlines: Facebook to launch new shopping feature across apps
Description: Facebook Inc  is launching Shops, a service that will allow businesses to display and sell products on the world's largest social network's platforms, Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said on Tuesday.

Headlines: As coronavirus crushes small restaurants, big chains see room to move in
Description: Prime storefronts left empty by failed businesses. Cheaper or even flexible rents. Landlords willing to add drive-thru lanes.

Headlines: White House panel: Build new tech infrastructure for future jobs
Description: A White House advisory panel on Tuesday urged the government and private industry to work together on new technological infrastructure to support future jobs and underpin a solid economic recovery from the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: U.S. energy secretary criticized by advocacy groups for 'redlining' comment
Description: Liberal groups criticized U.S. Energy Secretary Dan Brouillette on Tuesday for a comment they interpreted as comparing the reluctance of some banks to finance fossil fuels projects with discrimination against minorities.

Headlines: American Airlines may use loyalty program as collateral for U.S. debt: President
Description: American Airlines Group Inc  may use its Advantage loyalty program as collateral for a secured U.S. government loan, President Robert Isom said at a conference on Tuesday, noting that government talks are ongoing.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler's loan request raises doubts about 5.5 euro billion dividend
Description: Italy could look into Fiat Chrysler's  planned 5.5 billion euro ($6 billion) payout as part of its merger with Peugeot after the Italian-American carmaker asked for a 6.3 billion euro state-backed loan, a senior government source said.

Headlines: Lucky U.S. chickens fly the coop as pandemic hits egg demand
Description: About 1,000 lucky chickens flew on two chartered cargo planes to a California sanctuary from an Iowa farm that has been euthanizing its flock as the coronavirus outbreak slashes restaurant demand for eggs, an animal rights group said.

Headlines: Lufthansa expects hundreds of aircraft to be grounded until 2022
Description: Lufthansa is bracing for hundreds of aircraft to remain grounded due to the coronavirus pandemic well into 2022 and that further job cuts at its maintenance and catering businesses were inevitable.

Headlines: Walmart sales surge at stores and online on coronavirus-led demand
Description: Walmart Inc  emerged among the winners of the coronavirus lockdowns, beating Wall Street's quarterly revenue and profit forecasts and setting an online sales record as millions of consumers stocked up on food and cleaning supplies.

Headlines: GM says it is 'almost there' on million-mile electric vehicle battery
Description: General Motors Co is "almost there" on developing an electric vehicle battery that will last one million miles, a top executive said on Tuesday.

Headlines: France's Renault reaches deal on 5 billion euro state-backed loan: sources
Description: French carmaker Renault  has sealed a deal with banks on a 5 billion-euro ($5.47 billion) state-guaranteed loan to help the company to cope with the coronavirus outbreak, two sources close to the matter told Reuters on Tuesday.

Headlines: British retailer Asda's customers fear economic depression
Description: British supermarket group Asda got a sales boost in the first quarter from consumers stocking up before the coronavirus lockdown but it also highlighted that 90% of its shoppers now fear an economic depression.

Headlines: Asda CEO expects resumption of stake sale talks when Walmart ready
Description: Talks between Walmart  and possible buyers of a majority stake in its British supermarket Asda will likely resume when the industry settles into a "new norm" with the worst of the coronavirus crisis behind it, the boss of Asda said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Microsoft to adapt its cloud software for healthcare industry
Description: Microsoft Corp said on Tuesday it plans to roll out a version of its cloud-based software that will be modified to suit the needs of healthcare organizations.

Headlines: Home Depot misses profit estimates as coronavirus costs weigh
Description: Home Depot Inc  missed estimates for quarterly profit on Tuesday, as the home improvement chain spent about $850 million on benefits for employees keeping its stores and warehouses running through the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: Few U.S. oil and gas firms return small-business COVID-19 loans
Description: U.S. securities filings show that only four of 12 listed oil and gas companies that received emergency government aid made available for small businesses said they would return it ahead of a deadline for firms that do not need the funds to do so.

Headlines: S&P recovery will be far faster than 2008: Citigroup
Description: U.S. stock markets will deliver among the steepest recoveries in their history over the next year, returning to levels from before March's coronavirus lockdowns more than twice as fast as after the 2008 financial crisis, according to analysts from U.S. bank Citigroup.

Headlines: Citigroup launches new ESG investment banking group
Description: Citigroup Inc  said on Tuesday that is launching a new business unit within its corporate and investment bank dedicated to environmental sustainability to strengthen its commitment to an area that has grown increasingly important to corporate clients and investors.

Headlines: 'Nothing off-limits': Thyssenkrupp could sell steel business in historic shift
Description: Thyssenkrupp could sell most of its steelmaking division, its CEO said on Tuesday, marking a historic reversal in strategy for the German conglomerate which has built its 200-year-old legacy as an industrial champion on the business.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp CEO: Cannot put timeline on restructuring
Description: Thyssenkrupp's CEO on Tuesday said that she could not put a timeline on the group's fresh turnaround plans, saying that selling assets - a key part of its strategy - was difficult in the current environment.

Headlines: Renault to cut 400 jobs at its Slovenia unit
Description: French carmaker Renault  plans to cut about 400 out of some 3,200 jobs at its Slovenian unit Revoz after the coronavirus epidemic hit demand for its products, Revoz said on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. housing starts fall sharply in April
Description: U.S. homebuilding dropped to a five-year low in April, underlining fears that the novel coronavirus crisis would lead to the deepest economic contraction in the second quarter since the Great Depression.

Headlines: United Airlines says air travel demand improving
Description: United Airlines Holdings Inc  said on Tuesday it has seen a moderate improvement in demand for air travel so far in May in the United States and some international markets, as well as a reduction in cancellation rates.

Headlines: 'All my dreams are shattered': coronavirus crushes Asia’s garment industry
Description: Zarchi Lwin pawned her only two gold bangles for $140 when the owner of the Myanmar factory where she sewed winter coats for British retailer Next Plc shut it down after orders dried up due to the coronavirus.

Headlines: Factbox: Fashion brands cut orders with Asian garment makers
Description: As stores closed across Europe and the United States in March and April in response to the new coronavirus, many fashion brands and retailers cancelled orders for clothes, bags, and shoes worth billions of dollars from Asian garment factories, forcing them to close and lay off hundreds of thousands of workers.

Headlines: Empty middle seat? Depends on which country you are flying in
Description: In Thailand, you cannot have food or water in flight and must wear a mask. In Malaysia and Indonesia, the plane needs to be half-empty. In the United States and Europe, it's not mandatory for airlines to leave the middle seat open.

Headlines: Phlow gets $354 million U.S. funding to ensure drug supply amid COVID-19 pandemic
Description: U.S. drug manufacturer Phlow said on Tuesday it had received $354 million from the government to speed up the manufacturing of drugs being tested and used to fight the new coronavirus.

Headlines: Southwest says bookings outpace cancellations in May
Description: Southwest Airlines Co  said on Tuesday it recorded positive bookings on a net basis so far this month as passenger reservations outpaced trip cancellations, helping the company slow its cash burn rate.

Headlines: Factbox: New measures being put in place for air travel differ by country
Description: Governments, airlines and airports around the world are putting in place new measures to help protect travellers and allow for a return to the air during the global coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Past its peak? Battered oil demand faces threat from electric vehicles
Description: Oil companies may be facing uncertainty as the coronavirus pandemic triggers a collapse in demand for their products, but auto makers are betting the crisis will help accelerate an electric future.

Headlines: Mitsubishi Motors to cut costs after slump in annual profit
Description: Mitsubishi Motors Corp  will focus on cutting fixed costs by 20% or more in the next two years after reporting an 89% drop in annual profit, its weakest performance in three years, and skipping its year-end dividend.

Headlines: Exclusive: Delta will add flights to keep planes no more than 60% full as demand rises - sources
Description: Delta Air Lines Inc  will keep planes no more than 60% full through at least July, adding more flights to its schedule than demand would usually justify, people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Factbox: House cleaning at Thyssenkrupp could start M&A wave
Description: Steel-to-submarines conglomerate Thyssenkrupp has changed the structure of its sprawling empire, splitting operations into three categories as it seeks to simplify the business, stop cash burn and revive its battered share price.

Headlines: JPMorgan hands out $30 billion in loans to small businesses: memo
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  has given out more than $30 billion in loans to over 250,000 businesses as part of the United States' coronavirus aid program for small businesses, Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon said in a memo on Tuesday.

Headlines: Deutsche Boerse chief says plans to fulfil his term as CEO
Description: Deutsche Boerse  Chief Executive Theodor Weimer said on Tuesday that he planned to complete his term through the end of 2024 at the helm of the stock exchange operator.

Headlines: Disney's streaming chief Mayer to become TikTok CEO
Description: Walt Disney Co's   top streaming executive, Kevin Mayer, will leave the entertainment and theme parks giant to become the chief executive officer of TikTok, the popular video app owned by China's ByteDance Technology Co, the companies said on Monday.

Headlines: EU recovery fund should support aerospace sector: France's Le Maire
Description: The aerospace industry should be among the sectors that can tap a planned European recovery fund, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Nasdaq to tighten listing rules, restricting Chinese IPOs - sources
Description: Nasdaq Inc  is set to unveil new restrictions on initial public offerings (IPOs), a move that will make it harder for some Chinese companies to debut on its stock exchange, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: Abu Dhabi's Etihad cuts hundreds of jobs: sources
Description: Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways has laid off hundreds of employees this month, including cabin crew, after the coronavirus pandemic forced it to ground flights, according to industry and company sources.

Headlines: Tesla's China car registrations plunge 64% month-on-month in April
Description: U.S. electric vehicle maker Tesla Inc  suffered a slump of 64% in car registrations in China in April on the month, data from auto consultancy LMC Automotive showed.

Headlines: Fan-free sports and curbside retail as California loosens coronavirus rules
Description: Businesses in the San Francisco Bay Area may open for curbside retail and manufacturing, while fan-free professional sports events might be allowed as soon as June, as California continued to loosen coronavirus health restrictions on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. overtakes China as most attractive country for renewables investment: research
Description: The United States has overtaken China as the most attractive country in the world for renewables investment and the global clean energy sector is expected to bounce back quickly despite the coronavirus pandemic, research showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Electric car sales to fall, but not as much as other vehicles: research
Description: Worldwide electric car registrations are set to fall 18% this year, but those of combustion engine cars are set to drop even faster, analysts BloombergNEF (BNEF) said on Tuesday, as the automotive sector is hammered by the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: An easing of coronavirus prevention measures helps China's auto plants rev up
Description: In the eastern Chinese city of Yuyao, a group of five face-masked workers at a Geely auto plant, stood almost shoulder to shoulder behind an SUV as they conducted paint and other quality checks.

Headlines: Regulator asks for Credit Suisse directors' mobile data in spy inquiry: sources
Description: Swiss regulators have requested electronic messaging data from the mobile phones of several Credit Suisse managers and supervisory board directors as part of a probe into spying at the bank, three people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Long-lasting global recession likely due to COVID-19, says World Economic Forum report
Description: Risk managers expect a prolonged global recession as a result of the coronavirus pandemic, a report by the World Economic Forum showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Financial gain trumps espionage as top motivator in cyber attacks: report
Description: Money trumped spying as the top motivator for data breaches last year, according to Verizon's annual report on cyber crimes published on Tuesday.

Headlines: Coronavirus vaccine from Moderna appears safe, shows promise in data from eight people
Description: Moderna Inc's  experimental COVID-19 vaccine, the first to be tested in the United States, produced protective antibodies in a small group of healthy volunteers, according to very early data released by the biotech company on Monday.

Headlines: Australia's Qantas set to ramp up domestic flights without social distancing
Description: Qantas Airways Ltd could restart 40-50% of its domestic capacity in July if states relax border controls, and expects to offer low and flexible fares without social distancing measures to stimulate travel demand, its chief executive said on Tuesday.

Headlines: SEC settles charges against three former KPMG auditors
Description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Monday said it settled charges against three former KPMG LLP audit partners stemming from a cheating scandal at the firm.

Headlines: Starbucks says reopening many stores in Japan
Description: Starbucks Coffee Japan said it was reopening many of its stores in Japan, including Tokyo, starting on Tuesday, although many of them will be limited to take-out and drive-through services.

Headlines: SoftBank in talks to sell down T-Mobile U.S. stake to Deutsche Telekom: WSJ
Description: SoftBank Group Corp is in talks to sell "a significant portion" of its T-Mobile US stake to controlling shareholder Deutsche Telekom AG, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing unidentified sources.

Headlines: S&P 500 closes at 10-week high on vaccine hopes, stimulus pledge
Description: U.S. stocks jumped on Monday, and the S&P 500 closed at a 10-week high, on encouraging early-stage data for a potential coronavirus vaccine and on the promise of more stimulus to lift an economy beaten down by the pandemic.

Headlines: Uber to focus on core rides, delivery business as it cuts 23% of workforce
Description: Uber Technologies Inc  will concentrate on its core businesses in ride-hailing and food delivery and cut 23% of its workforce in an attempt to become profitable despite the coronavirus pandemic, Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi said in an email to employees on Monday.

Headlines: NIBC says it will pay 2019 dividend to Blackstone to ensure acquisition
Description: Dutch bank NIBC Holding NV  said late on Monday it has agreed to pay its 2019 dividend to its proposed buyer, U.S. equity firm Blackstone Group Inc , before the deal settles, in order to remove one hurdle to the proposed 1.36 billion-euro ($1.47 billion) takeover.

Headlines: Supplier restarts flow of critical truck parts to Detroit automakers
Description: Dana Inc , a key supplier of truck parts to Detroit automakers, restarted its Toledo plant Monday on a single shift, with one-third of its 750-person workforce and less than 1% absenteeism, according to plant manager Craig Zimmerly.

Headlines: As flying returns, jetmakers seek to quell fears over cabin air
Description: Jet manufacturers and airlines are launching an urgent initiative to convince nervous travelers that the air they breathe on planes is safe, believing this is critical to rebuilding a travel industry floored by the novel coronavirus.

Headlines: Delta to resume flying several major routes in June
Description: Delta Air Lines  said on Monday it would resume flying several major routes in June that were suspended due to the coronavirus pandemic, including some Trans-Atlantic and Caribbean destinations.

Headlines: Square joins Twitter in letting employees work from home permanently
Description: Jack Dorsey-led Square Inc said on Monday that most of its employees can continue to work from home permanently even after offices reopen, following a similar announcement from Twitter Inc, which is also headed by the billionaire.

Headlines: Global shares, oil rally on vaccine hopes, lockdown easing
Description: A gauge of global equity markets surged almost 3% on Monday and oil rallied to highs last seen in mid-April as data from an early-stage trial for a coronavirus vaccine lifted hopes of a faster recovery from the pandemic-driven economic slump.

Headlines: Trump says should be possible to allow PPP borrowers more time to use loans
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday extending the amount of time borrowers in the Paycheck Protection Program have to spend their funds to 24 weeks from the current eight weeks "should be easy."

Headlines: FCA has to strengthen investments in Italy to seek state-backed loan: Economy Minister
Description: Italy's Economy Minister Roberto Gualtieri on Monday said Fiat Chrysler [FCHA.MI] has to strengthen investments in Italy and avoid delocalizing its factories outside the national borders to apply for a state backed loan.

Headlines: Oil jumps to two-month high on easing lockdowns, positive vaccine results
Description: Oil prices on Monday jumped to their highest in over two months on positive early results on a potential coronavirus vaccine, optimism about a resumption in economic activity and signs producers were following through on planned output reductions.

Headlines: More than 8% of U.S. mortgages now in forbearance: MBA weekly survey
Description: Roughly 4.1 million U.S. mortgage borrowers have had their payments paused or reduced as the novel coronavirus outbreak hits household finances, but the increase in the number of people needing such help is slowing, the latest weekly survey from the Mortgage Bankers Association showed on Monday.

Headlines: Automated delivery cashes in on pandemic-driven demand
Description: The coronavirus crisis is accelerating a shift in the world of autonomous cars toward delivering packages instead of people, as big players open up a lead over startups in the race for funding.

Headlines: J.C. Penney to permanently shut about 242 stores as part of bankruptcy plan
Description: J.C. Penney Co Inc plans to trim its store count by 29% to about 604, as the U.S. department store chain looks to focus on those more profitable, a regulatory filing showed on Monday, two days after it filed for bankruptcy protection.

Headlines: Ailing icon Thyssenkrupp seeks partners for steel, warship units
Description: Thyssenkrupp  on Monday said it was looking for partners for its steel and warship divisions, singling out just three lines of businesses that will stay within the struggling German industrial icon.

Headlines: U.S. auto industry returns to life after lockdown
Description: The Detroit Three automakers and their suppliers began restarting assembly lines on Monday after a two-month coronavirus lockdown in a slow revival of a sector that employs nearly 1 million people in the United States.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. probes PerkinElmer's role in massive Medicare fraud - sources
Description: Medical diagnostic firm PerkinElmer Inc faces a federal investigation into its role in an alleged Medicare fraud involving tens of thousands of unnecessary genetic cancer tests, according to three sources with knowledge of the probe and documents reviewed by Reuters.

Headlines: U.S. Senator Klobuchar blasts Uber, Grubhub deal talks
Description: U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar on Sunday blasted merger talks between ride-hailing firm Uber Technologies Inc and online food delivery company Grubhub Inc, calling any deal bad for competition and consumers.

Headlines: JPMorgan fills senior leadership roles after February makeover
Description: JPMorgan  has made a number of changes in senior positions in its investment bank in the Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) region to support a February reshuffle of the top roles, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Total calls off plan to buy Occidental Petroleum's Ghana assets
Description: Total  has called off a plan to acquire Occidental Petroleum's  assets in Ghana, which was conditional on the completion of the acquisition of Occidental's other assets in Algeria, the French energy company said on Monday.

Headlines: IMF chief warns full global economic recovery unlikely in 2021
Description: The global economy will take much longer to recover fully from the shock caused by the new coronavirus than initially expected, the head of the International Monetary Fund said, and she stressed the danger of protectionism.

Headlines: Huawei calls U.S. move to curb chips supply 'arbitrary', expects business impact
Description: Huawei Technologies in its first official response to the Trump administration's move to curb its access to global chip supplies called it "arbitrary" and said its business would be impacted.

Headlines: Amazon's French warehouses to reopen with 30% staff: unions
Description: Amazon's French warehouses are set to reopen on Tuesday with about 30% of employees, three union officials said, ending a month-long dispute over whether the e-commerce giant was doing enough to protect workers from the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Walmart trailed supermarkets amid peak panic-buying: data
Description: Americans increased their visits to supermarkets far more than to Walmart Inc  stores as panic-buying peaked in mid-March, a Reuters analysis of foot traffic to retailers in the United States shows.

Headlines: SoftBank's Son hopes 'winged unicorns' can save crumbling tech empire
Description: SoftBank Group Corp  CEO Masayoshi Son on Monday pinned his hopes on a small group of "winged unicorns" to save the performance of his $100 billion Vision Fund - although he gave few clues on which ones they would be.

Headlines: U.S. homebuilder confidence rises in May
Description: Confidence among U.S. single-family homebuilders rose in May, potentially signaling that the worst of the economic downturn was probably over as the country gradually reopens after lockdowns to slow the spread of the novel coronavirus.

Headlines: Exclusive: Nissan's survival plan for Europe: SUVs and sharing with Renault
Description: Nissan Motor Co  is working on a plan to scale back its European business, focusing on sport utility and commercial vehicles as well as more effective sharing of products and investments with partner Renault, three sources told Reuters.

Headlines: Starbucks reopens in Italy but keeps Milan flagship closed
Description: Italians will be able to grab a cup of their favorite Starbucks coffee again after the group said on Monday it would reopen its Italian cafes, with the exception of its flagship location in central Milan.

Headlines: A California cafe reopens with a payroll loan, but the future unclear
Description: Chris and Amy Hillyard opened their Oakland, California restaurant late last month for the first time since mid-March, thanks in large part to a government loan aimed at tiding over small firms during the worst of the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Coronavirus widens climate rift between European and U.S. oil majors
Description: Europe's top oil and gas companies have diverted a larger share of their cash to green energy projects since the coronavirus outbreak in a bet the global health crisis will leave a long-term dent in fossil fuel demand, according to a Reuters review of company statements and interviews with executives.

Headlines: Ethiopian Airlines sees Boeing 737 MAX compensation deal by end-June
Description: Ethiopian Airlines expects a settlement with planemaker Boeing  by end of June over compensation related to the 737 MAX grounding in March 2019 following two fatal crashes, CEO Tewolde Gebremariam told Reuters on Friday.

Headlines: U.S. car rental firm Hertz names new CEO
Description: Hertz Global Holdings Inc  on Monday appointed Paul Stone as its chief executive officer days after the U.S. car rental company raised going-concern doubts following a bigger quarterly loss.

Headlines: U.S. mulls paying companies, tax breaks to pull supply chains from China
Description: U.S. lawmakers and officials are crafting proposals to push American companies to move operations or key suppliers out of China that include tax breaks, new rules, and carefully structured subsidies.

Headlines: Trump admin slaps solar, wind operators with retroactive rent bills
Description: The Trump administration has ended a two-year rent holiday for solar and wind projects operating on federal lands, handing them whopping retroactive bills at a time the industry is struggling with the fallout of the coronavirus outbreak, according to company officials.

Headlines: Factbox: Investors pour billions into automated delivery startups
Description: Since September, investors have pumped at least $6 billion into more than two dozen startups that are automating delivery of goods and food, from heavy trucks to sidewalk robots and drones.

Headlines: SoftBank's Vision Fund tumbles to $18 billion loss in 'valley of coronavirus'
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp reported a stunning $18 billion loss at its giant Vision Fund, pushing Masayoshi Son's conglomerate to a record loss and highlighting the deepening crisis at its portfolio companies from the global downturn.

Headlines: SoftBank to raise over $11 billion for buybacks using Alibaba shares
Description: Softbank Group will raise 1.25 trillion yen ($11.7 billion) using Alibaba stock to fund buybacks of its own shares, Chief Executive Masayoshi Son said on Monday.

Headlines: What did eight weeks and $3 trillion buy the U.S. in the fight against coronavirus?
Description: Unemployment checks are flowing, $490 billion has been shipped to small businesses, and the U.S. Federal Reserve has put about $2.5 trillion and counting behind domestic and global markets.

Headlines: Tech firms sweeten deals for U.S. banks cutting costs in crisis
Description: Top technology services firms are offering payment deferrals, discounts of up to 20% and other sweeteners to some U.S. banks to keep their business as the pandemic forces Wall Street to cut tech budgets, according to executives involved in the talks.

Headlines: Panasonic sees strong demand from Tesla, in talks to expand Nevada battery plant
Description: Panasonic Corp's  finance chief said the company is seeing strong demand for battery cells from U.S. partner Tesla  and they are in talks to expand their joint plant in Nevada, which is now profitable.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp steel workers open to consolidation talks - labor boss
Description: Thyssenkrupp's  powerful labor representatives are open to consolidation talks in the steel sector, a leading union official told Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: Fed's Powell: 'Medical metrics' most important data for U.S. economy now: CBS
Description: The most important data for the U.S. economy right now are the "medical metrics" around the coronavirus pandemic, Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell said Sunday night in broadcast remarks where he outlined the likely need for three to six more months of government financial help for firms and families.

Headlines: Britain, U.S. hopeful trade talks can proceed at pace: London
Description: Britain and the United States are hopeful that negotiations for a trade agreement can proceed at an accelerated pace, Britain's department for trade said on Monday in an update on the talks after the first round concluded last week.

Headlines: Japan braces for worst postwar slump as pandemic tips economy into recession
Description: Japan's economy slipped into recession for the first time in 4-1/2 years in the last quarter, putting the nation on course for its deepest postwar slump as the coronavirus crisis ravages businesses and consumers.

Headlines: Alibaba's Jack Ma resigns from SoftBank board
Description: SoftBank Group Corp said on Monday that Alibaba co-founder Jack Ma will resign from its board, in the latest departure by a high-profile ally of CEO Masayoshi Son.

Headlines: Apple reopening 25 more U.S. stores, will soon top 100 worldwide
Description: Apple Inc will this week reopen more than 25 of its branded stores in the United States, the company said on Sunday, continuing a gradual process that has unlocked doors at nearly a fifth of its worldwide retail outlets.

Headlines: TSMC stops new Huawei orders after U.S. restrictions: Nikkei
Description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd has stopped new orders from Huawei Technologies [HWT.UL] in response to Washington's move aimed at further limiting chip supplies to the Chinese company, the Nikkei reported on Monday, citing multiple sources.

Headlines: SoftBank in talks to sell down T-Mobile U.S. stake to Deutsche Telekom - WSJ
Description: SoftBank Group Corp is in talks to sell "a significant portion" of its T-Mobile US stake to controlling shareholder Deutsche Telekom AG, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday citing unidentified sources.

Headlines: Japan's economy to slump significantly due to pandemic: economy minister
Description: Japan's economy is expected to slump significantly due to sluggish overseas demand blamed on the coronavirus pandemic, Economy Minister Yasutoshi Nishimura said on Monday.

Description: General Motors Co is tentatively planning to restart operations at its auto assembly plant in the Mexican city of Silao on May 20, according to a message to workers seen by Reuters on Sunday, as the car industry prepares to exit the coronavirus lockdown.

Headlines: SK Hynix shares fall on demand worries after U.S. curbs on Huawei chip supply
Description: Shares of South Korea's SK Hynix , the world's No.2 memory chip maker and supplier to Huawei [HWT.UL], fell as much as 3.3% early on Monday after a U.S. move to curb semiconductor supplies to the Chinese company stoked fears about a demand hit.

Headlines: GM instructs Mexican suppliers to prepare to resume operations
Description: The president of General Motors Co's  Mexican unit advised suppliers to prepare to resume operations after the Mexican government said the automotive industry could exit the coronavirus lockdown before June 1 with adequate safety measures.

Description: A month after sellers had to pay nearly $40 a barrel to get rid of U.S. oil futures, the next watershed moment looms with the expiry of the June contract on Tuesday - and so far there is little sign of a repeat of the historic plunge.

Description: U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said on Sunday there will be negotiations on the new $3 trillion coronavirus relief legislation passed by the Democratic-controlled House of Representatives and that Democrats have "no red lines."

Headlines: Emirates plans to cut about 30,000 jobs amid virus outbreak: Bloomberg News

Headlines: Reliance in $870 million General Atlantic deal as Jio Platforms funding tops $8 billion
Description: India's Reliance Industries  on Sunday announced U.S. fund General Atlantic will invest 65.98 billion rupees ($870 million) in Jio Platforms, a fourth deal that takes investment in its digital unit to over $8 billion in less than a month.

Headlines: UK's Gove says EU trade deal can be done despite talks stalemate

Headlines: Temporary layoff schemes no cure-all in slow COVID recovery
Description: Temporary unemployment schemes operating across Europe could struggle to save the jobs of leisure and travel sector workers facing drawn-out or partial recoveries from the COVID-19 pandemic, even if they help industries that rebound quickly.

Description: Walt Disney Co  will partially reopen its Disney Springs entertainment and shopping complex at Walt Disney World Resort in Florida on May 20, it said late on Saturday.

Description: Investors are bracing for more turbulence in U.S. stocks, as some states prepare to reopen their economies and global trade tensions rise.

Description: South African Airways (SAA) has spent just under 10 billion rand ($540 million) since it entered a form of bankruptcy protection, business rescue practitioners said on Friday as they flagged a structured wind-down process as their preferred option for the carrier.

Description: Air France  is putting its grounded pilots through their paces in the flight simulator as the airline prepares to restore flights to dozens of destinations that had been suspended under coronavirus lockdown measures.

Description: United Airlines Holdings Inc  has told staff that it only has work for about 3,000 of its about 25,000 flight attendants in June, sources said, and warned of job losses if demand does not recover by the time government payroll aid expires in the fall.

Description: U.S. consumer sentiment rose unexpectedly in early May after a record plunge a month earlier as emergency assistance payments improved household finances hurt by mass layoffs from the coronavirus crisis, a survey released on Friday showed.
