Description: The U.S. Treasury Department said on Tuesday that major passenger airlines have agreed in principle to a $25 billion rescue package, ensuring airline workers have jobs until October while the industry battles its biggest-ever crisis.

Headlines: Amazon fires three critics of warehouse conditions in pandemic
Description: Amazon.com Inc said on Tuesday it had fired three critics of the company's pandemic response for workplace violations, dismissals that drew sharp words from U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders and a labor coalition.

Headlines: Texas oil hearing stirs hornet's nest, as regulators offer no clue to decision
Description: Texas energy regulators listened as top executives on Tuesday debated whether the state should cut oil output by 1 million barrels per day, but did not indicate how they might vote after more than 10 hours of sometimes dire testimony.

Headlines: Glade Brook pitches 'extraordinary opportunity' in tech debt amid coronavirus
Description: Glade Brook Capital Partners LLC, the venture capital firm led by Paul Hudson, is pitching a new fund to investors targeting the debt of private technology companies impacted by economic disruption from COVID-19.

Headlines: McDonald's and its U.S. franchisees at odds over financial relief as crisis weighed
Description: McDonald's Corp  rejected a request from its U.S. franchisees to delay collecting some March rent and royalty payments, prompting claims that the world's largest fast-food company is not providing enough support during the coronavirus crisis, according to several letters seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Delta working with Airbus on order book after deferring A350 orders linked to Latam
Description: Delta Air Lines Inc  confirmed on Tuesday it had taken over an order for 10 Airbus  A350 jets from Latam Airlines Group , but said it had deferred several of the near-term deliveries and was working with Airbus on options across its entire order book.

Headlines: Boeing 737 MAX cancellations pile up during production halt
Description: Boeing Co  on Tuesday reported another 75 cancellations for its 737 MAX jetliner in March, as the coronavirus crisis worsened disruptions from the grounding of its best-selling jet.

Headlines: Wall Street jumps as hopes for easing lockdown offset earnings worry
Description: U.S. stocks jumped on Tuesday as optimism that the Trump administration could move to ease lockdowns from the coronavirus outbreak overshadowed worrying earnings reports from JPMorgan and Wells Fargo.

Headlines: Virus-hit Princess Cruises to anchor all voyages till end of June
Description: Carnival Corp-owned  Princess Cruises, whose three ships had become hotbeds for coronavirus infections, said on Tuesday it would cancel all voyages until June-end, after a "no sail order" from U.S. health officials.

Headlines: General Motors says will make 1.5 million masks a month in Mexico
Description: General Motors Co will begin producing 1.5 million face masks a month at its plant in the Mexican city of Toluca at the end of April, it said on Tuesday, aiming for 9 million masks over six months to help curb the spread of the coronavirus.

Headlines: GM begins production of ventilators for U.S. government
Description: General Motors Co said on Tuesday it had started producing ventilators in the volume needed to treat severely ill coronavirus patients and would deliver the first batch of the medical equipment to the U.S. government this month.

Headlines: In hard-hit Florida, jobless workers struggle to get state aid
Description: With cruise ships idled and airplanes almost empty, Florida travel adviser Nick Pena has been out of work for nearly a month, spending his days trying to secure jobless benefits from a state seemingly unable to provide them.

Headlines: Global airlines' estimated coronavirus losses rise to $314 billion: IATA
Description: Estimated global airline losses from the coronavirus pandemic have climbed to $314 billion, 25% more than previously forecast, owing to the severity of the economic downturn and a slower than previously expected reopening of international routes.

Headlines: Fed officials see risks in reopening economy too soon, but acknowledge need to move
Description: U.S. Federal Reserve officials have begun grappling with the complexities of how to simultaneously reopen the country's economy and protect against a resurgence of coronavirus infections, goals they have argued cannot be successfully separated.

Headlines: Stocks gain on China trade data, easing pandemic worries
Description: Equity markets rallied globally on Tuesday as Chinese trade data defied expectations of a deep downturn as a result of the coronavirus pandemic, igniting hopes that world economies can soon recover and removing the safe-haven allure of the greenback.

Headlines: Oil slumps on worries that supply cuts are playing catch-up to falling demand
Description: Oil prices dropped sharply on Tuesday, with U.S. prices sliding back toward $20 a barrel, as investors bet that fuel demand destruction caused by the coronavirus pandemic would be too much for producers embarking on record global output cuts to offset.

Headlines: Credit Suisse investors should reject pay report after spy affair: advisor
Description: Credit Suisse  shareholders should reject its compensation report and deny its leadership a discharge in an upcoming vote, a proxy advisor said, the latest fallout from a spying scandal that cost ex-boss Tidjane Thiam his job.

Headlines: Trump oil deal raises question for Mexico: At what cost?
Description: Mexico's president has incurred a debt with his U.S. counterpart Donald Trump by accepting U.S. help to end a standoff over global oil cuts, triggering concern the American will in return make the country pay on issues like migration and security.

Headlines: Wells Fargo profit decimated as coronavirus-led loan defaults loom
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  eked out a first-quarter profit of one penny per share as the bank set aside nearly $4 billion to cover expected loan losses due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Apple launches site to show how coronavirus lockdowns affect movement
Description: Apple Inc  said on Tuesday it would release data that could help inform public health authorities on whether people are driving less during lockdown orders to slow the spread of the new coronavirus.

Headlines: Subaru extends U.S. assembly plant shutdown through May 8
Description: Japanese automaker Subaru Corp  said Tuesday it will extend a shutdown of its Indiana assembly plant through May 8 because of declining market demand and supply chain issues related to the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Republicans warn coronavirus aid program running out of cash
Description: Republicans in the U.S. Senate and the Trump administration on Tuesday warned that a key program to help small businesses survive the coronavirus pandemic was running out of money, pressuring Democrats to agree on an emergency infusion of aid.

Headlines: Strength of U.S. consumer staples stocks shows cracks as market recovers
Description: A broad rebound in U.S. stocks is leaving behind shares of some supermarkets, household product makers and other staples companies that provided a haven in last month's coronavirus-fueled selloff.

Headlines: Airlines mull empty seats and masks for coronavirus recovery
Description: Wizz Air is making plans to fly jets only two-thirds full to allow more space between passengers, it said on Tuesday, as airlines voiced concerns that anti-coronavirus measures could blight their profitability long after travel restrictions end.

Headlines: Rolex joins Baselworld defections that cast doubt on watch fair's future
Description: Rolex, Patek Philippe and Chanel will not exhibit at MCH Group's  Baselworld watch and jewellery trade show in 2021, they said on Tuesday, another blow to the flagging event that has already seen high-profile exits including Swatch Group .

Headlines: Global economy in 2020 on track for sharpest downturn since 1930s: IMF
Description: The global economy is expected to shrink by 3.0% during 2020 in a stunning coronavirus-driven collapse of activity that will mark the steepest downturn since the Great Depression of the 1930s, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.

Headlines: J&J sees medical devices business recovery at end of year after taking coronavirus hit
Description: Johnson & Johnson  on Tuesday said it expects its  medical device business to begin recovering in the fourth quarter as elective medical procedures delayed by the coronavirus pandemic start to resume.

Headlines: Two big U.S. banks offer glum outlook for coronavirus recession
Description: The main things investors wanted to learn from first-quarter results by JPMorgan Chase & Co  and Wells Fargo & Co  on Tuesday was just how bad the coronavirus recession is going to get and how long it will take to get back to normal.

Headlines: JPMorgan profit dives as banks brace for coronavirus-led loan defaults
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co's profit plunged by more than two-thirds in the first quarter as the largest U.S. bank put aside nearly $7 billion in reserves to protect it from a wave of potential loan defaults in the months ahead.

Headlines: Explainer: Trump has little power to restart U.S. economy
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday it was his decision when to reopen the U.S. economy, which has been largely shut down to slow the spread of the novel coronavirus.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler bolsters cash with $3.8 billion syndicated credit
Description: Fiat Chrysler  said on Tuesday it had successfully completed the syndication of a 3.5 billion euro ($3.8 billion)credit facility which it had agreed last month with two banks.

Headlines: Amazon ordered to limit French trade to essential goods
Description: Amazon  will have to limit its deliveries in France to essential goods like food and medical supplies while it carries out a more thorough assessment of the risk of coronavirus contagion at its warehouses, a French court ruled on Tuesday.

Headlines: Tesla surges 28% in two days as traders look beyond coronavirus disruption
Description: Shares of Tesla Inc  surged 12% on Tuesday after Credit Suisse upgraded its rating on the electric carmaker and as Wall Street rallied on optimism the coronavirus outbreak was reaching a plateau.

Headlines: Adidas gets 3 billion euro government backed loan, suspends dividend
Description: German sports retailer Adidas  on Tuesday said it received approval for a syndicated 3 billion-euro ($3.3 billion) government-backed loan to mitigate the financial impact on its business from the spread of the coronavirus.

Headlines: Spirit expects quarterly loss as coronavirus hits plane output
Description: Spirit AeroSystems Holdings Inc  said on Tuesday it would swing to a first-quarter loss and warned of a bigger blow in the current quarter, as customers Boeing Co  and Airbus SE  whittle down production due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: NMC Health board replaced by administrators
Description: The administrators of troubled hospital operator NMC Health  said on Tuesday they had replaced the company's board and asked its main lender, Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (ADCB), to lead a steering group to discuss cutting its debt pile.

Headlines: Spain denies requisitioning coronavirus tests bound for workers
Description: Spain's health minister denied on Tuesday that authorities had requisitioned 2,000 antibody tests which a workers union said Siemens Gamesa  had expected to receive to check whether its staff have been infected with the coronavirus.

Headlines: Fauci: May 1 target for reopening U.S. economy 'overly optimistic' - AP
Description: The top U.S. infectious disease expert, Anthony Fauci, said on Tuesday that a May 1 target date for reopening the economy was "a bit overly optimistic," citing a lack of critical testing and tracing procedures.

Headlines: U.S. funds that beat market plunge seek recession-proof stocks
Description: Beating the first quarter's market crash took some extreme strategies, such as moving nearly everything to cash, or going very short. Now, fund managers who prevailed during the worst start to a year for U.S. stocks are betting on recession-resilient companies to take them to the next leg.

Headlines: Honda extends Mexico plant suspensions to April 30 due to coronavirus
Description: The Mexican unit of Japanese automaker Honda Motor Co said on Tuesday it would extend a suspenion of operations at its plants in the states of Guanajuato and Jalisco until April 30 due to the impact of the novel coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Renault quits its main China venture after weak sales
Description: French automaker Renault SA  is ditching its main passenger car business in China following poor sales at the loss-making venture with Dongfeng Motor Group .

Headlines: Barclays delays incentive payments to CEO, CFO due to coronavirus
Description: Barclays  is delaying the release of portions of Chief Executive Jes Staley and Chief Financial Officer Tushar Morzaria's bonuses in light of the new coronavirus pandemic, it said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Norwegian Air shares plummet as survival hinges on creditors
Description: Norwegian Air  shares plummeted again on Tuesday, and are now trading down around 97% from their 2015 peak, with the airline's survival depending on creditors accepting a rescue plan proposed last week.

Headlines: U.S. awards airports $10 billion in grants amid travel falloff
Description: The U.S. Transportation Department on Tuesday awarded nearly $10 billion to U.S. airports struggling with a massive falloff in travel demand because of the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Exclusive: Saudi Aramco in talks with banks to borrow about $10 billion - sources
Description: Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil producer, is in early talks with banks for a loan of about $10 billion to help finance its acquisition of a 70% stake in Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), according to three banking sources.

Headlines: J.C. Penney to hire advisors as it mulls debt management options: Bloomberg News
Description: J.C. Penney Co Inc  has approached consulting firm AlixPartners LLP as the U.S. retailer looks at options for managing its debt, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Headlines: Qatar Airways signs $850 million financing deal with Standard Chartered
Description: Qatar Airways and Standard Chartered have signed an $850 million financing deal for seven Boeing 787-9 aircraft, a statement from the Qatari airline said on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. import prices post biggest decline in over five years; more to come
Description: U.S. import prices dropped by the most in more than five years in March amid declines in the costs of petroleum products and a range of other goods, pointing to import deflation that could deepen amid the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: G7 backs debt moratorium for poor countries if G20 creditors, Paris Club join
Description: Group of Seven (G7) finance officials on Tuesday vowed to continue to act as needed to combat the coronavirus pandemic and stabilize the global economy, and threw their support behind a push to provide temporary debt relief to the poorest countries.

Headlines: BOJ's Kuroda told G7 ready to ease policy to combat coronavirus fallout
Description: Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda said on Tuesday he explained to his G7 counterparts that the central bank would not hesitate easing monetary policy further depending on how the coronavirus pandemic affects the country's economy.

Headlines: G7 agreed on need to aid emerging economies battling with virus: Japan's Aso
Description: G7 finance leaders agreed on Tuesday on the need to provide financial and technical assistance to emerging economies battling with the fallout from the coronavirus pandemic, Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said.

Headlines: Hyundai first to restart Czech production, others still shut
Description: Hyundai Motor Co's  Czech car plant was the first in the central European country to get back to work on Tuesday after a three-week outage, potentially easing some of the strain on the hard-hit economy.

Headlines: Bombardier to resume some operations in UK
Description: Bombardier Inc  said on Tuesday it plans to resume production at some of its facilities in the United Kingdom, which had been halted in March due to government-mandated social distancing to battle the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Spain says IMF outlook confirms view of strong, short-lived crisis
Description: The Spanish government said on Tuesday the International Monetary Fund's forecast of an 8% economic slump this year due to the coronavirus pandemic, to be followed by a recovery in 2021, confirmed the view that the crisis would be intense, but short-lived.

Headlines: Debt levels expected to sharply increase in 2020, stabilize as economies recover: IMF
Description: Global debt is expected to increase significantly over the next year, the top economist of the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, while moratoriums on debt payments and debt restructuring may need to be continued as the world economy emerges from the coronavirus pandemic lockdown.

Headlines: Hyundai to provide COVID 19 tests, 'drive through' testing support in U.S.
Description: Hyundai Motor Co's North American unit will expand its support for "drive through" testing for the coronavirus and donate 65,000 tests to hospitals in the United States, the South Korean automaker said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Cisco offers big payment deferrals until 2021 as companies seek remote-work tools
Description: Cisco Systems Inc  on Tuesday launched a $2.5 billion financing program that lets its customers defer 95% of payments until 2021, giving companies additional leeway at time when some are facing a cash crunch but also need more remote-work tools.

Headlines: Alphabet soup: How will post-virus economic recovery shape up?
Description: (This story had been refiled to add missing words in paragraph 16 of story first published April 9.)

Headlines: Dash for cash as most investors expect drawn-out recovery: BofA survey
Description: Investors have been hoarding cash at a rate not seen since the immediate aftermath of the 9/11 attacks of 2001, BofA's April fund manager survey showed, as the coronavirus roiled global financial markets.

Headlines: Britain's Next re-opens online before maxing out daily limit
Description: British clothing retailer Next  hit a self-imposed daily limit within hours of re-opening its online business on Tuesday, indicating consumer demand during the coronavirus lockdown.

Headlines: Barclays halts new job cuts during coronavirus crisis: memo
Description: Barclays  has halted new job cuts while the coronavirus crisis is ongoing, the bank said in an internal memo seen by Reuters on Tuesday.

Headlines: Ten U.S. states developing 'reopening' plans account for 38% of U.S. economy
Description: The ten U.S. states coordinating plans separately from the White House to reopen businesses shut by the coronavirus are responsible for an outsized proportion of the U.S. economy.

Headlines: Pandemic survival plans: U.S. businesses scramble to conserve cash, boost liquidity
Description: Charlie Straface, president of Norwegian aluminum maker Norsk Hydro's North American extrusion operations, convenes a coronavirus task force every other day to draw up cost-cutting measures to offset declining revenues and protect the unit's cash balance during the economic slump related to the outbreak.

Headlines: SoftBank record loss estimate renews asset sale focus
Description: SoftBank Group Corp's  estimate it will post a record $13 billion full-year loss, dragged down by its spluttering $100 billion Vision Fund, has renewed attention on a planned asset sell-down aimed at raising cash and restoring confidence.

Headlines: Wizz Air not considering plane deferrals, sees growth returning in 2022: CEO
Description: European low cost airline Wizz Air  is not looking to defer any of the Airbus  narrowbody planes it has on order even though it does not expect the market to grow again until 2022, its chief executive said.

Headlines: Turkish Airlines extends flight cancellations until May 20
Description: Turkish Airlines  has extended the cancellation of international flights to May 20 from May 1 over the coronavirus outbreak, the airline said on Tuesday, adding that domestic flights would remain suspended until April 20.

Headlines: Tobacco giant BAT slides on report of U.S. criminal investigation
Description: British American Tobacco (BAT)  is the subject of a U.S. criminal investigation over suspected sanctions-busting, The Times reported https://bit.ly/2ydR5Wm on Tuesday, sending the company's shares down more than 5%.

Headlines: Toyota plans limited operations in France, Poland from April 22
Description: Toyota Motor Corp  on Monday said it plans to restart limited production at vehicle plants in France and Poland from April 22 after closing them due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Next's reopened website closed to new orders by 0730 GMT
Description: British clothing retailer Next  has closed its re-opened website to orders until Wednesday after reaching a self-imposed daily order limit.

Headlines: Pandemic shows investment fund vulnerabilities, G20 watchdog says
Description: Non-bank financial firms such as investment funds have exhibited  vulnerabilities during the coronavirus crisis that may need fixing to help economies recover, a global regulatory watchdog said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Brewer AB InBev halves final dividend and pushes back AGM
Description: Anheuser-Busch InBev , the world's largest brewer, proposes to halve its final dividend and has postponed its annual shareholder meeting owing to uncertainty around the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: Car parts group Valeo drops 2020 targets, gets 1 billion euros of new credit lines
Description: French car parts group Valeo  abandoned its 2020 financial targets on Tuesday because of the hit to its business from the coronavirus outbreak, although it got 1 billion euros  ($1.1 billion) in extra credit lines to shore up its finances.

Headlines: Julius Baer to postpone AGM, propose split dividend
Description: Swiss wealth manager Julius Baer  will propose splitting its 2019 dividend payment into two halves following a regulatory request, it said on Tuesday, postponing by a month its annual general meeting in order to meet notification requirements.

Headlines: Apple shipped 2.5 million iPhones in China in March following virus slump: government data
Description: Apple Inc  shipped roughly 2.5 million iPhones in China in March, a slight rebound after one of its worst months in the country ever, according to government data published on Friday.

Headlines: Trump says plan to re-open shuttered U.S. economy to be completed soon
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration was close to completing a plan to re-open the U.S. economy, which has been largely shut down to slow the spread of the novel coronavirus.

Headlines: Exxon raises $9.5 billion to load up on cash while debt market still open to new deals
Description: Exxon Mobil Corp on Monday raised $9.5 billion in new debt, with the largest U.S. oil producer seeking to bolster its finances while debt markets remain open to new deals.

Headlines: Disney enters $5 billion credit agreement
Description: Walt Disney Co said on Monday it has entered an unsecured credit agreement for $5 billion, at a time when companies across industries are scrambling to bolster their liquidity to weather the fallout from the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: U.S. airlines nearing acceptance of payroll aid plan: sources
Description: Some large U.S. passenger airlines are close to accepting the terms of a $25 billion offer for government coronavirus payroll aid, with announcements possible as early as Tuesday, people briefed on the matter said.

Headlines: Grubhub, DoorDash, Postmates, Uber Eats are sued over restaurant prices amid pandemic
Description: GrubHub, DoorDash, Postmates and Uber Eats were sued on Monday for allegedly exploiting their dominance in restaurant meal deliveries to impose fees that consumers ultimately bear through higher menu prices, including during the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Record oil output cuts fail to make waves in coronavirus-hit market
Description: The minimal impact on oil prices from a global deal for record output cuts showed that oil producers have a mountain to climb if they are to restore market balance as the coronavirus shreds demand and sends stockpiles soaring, industry watchers said.

Headlines: Factbox: Non OPEC+ crude oil supply cuts
Description: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, known as OPEC+, agreed on Sunday to reduce output by 9.7 million barrels per day (bpd) for May and June in an effort to prop up oil prices as the coronavirus outbreak slashes fuel demand.

Headlines: Smithfield shutting U.S. pork plant indefinitely, warns of meat shortages during pandemic
Description: Smithfield Foods, the world's biggest pork processor, said on Sunday it will shut a U.S. plant indefinitely due to a rash of coronavirus cases among employees and warned the country was  moving "perilously close to the edge" in supplies for grocers.

Headlines: Factbox: Spread of coronavirus closes North American meat plants
Description: Major meat companies in the United States and Canada have closed plants temporarily due to cases of the new coronavirus among employees and concerns about its spread.

Headlines: Trump says plan to re-open shuttered U.S. economy to be completed soon
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration was close to completing a plan to re-open the U.S. economy, which has been largely shut down to slow the spread of the novel coronavirus.

Headlines: Dow, S&P 500 slide as focus shifts to earnings; Nasdaq gains
Description: The Dow and S&P 500 fell on Monday as U.S. companies prepared to kick off a quarterly earnings season expected to be rough due to the coronavirus pandemic, while Amazon.com  gains helped the Nasdaq end higher.

Headlines: Telco shares are surprise losers as lockdown drives internet boom
Description: As lockdowns worldwide drive a surge in internet use, boosting online sales for businesses as varied as gaming and food delivery, the stocks of internet providers are an unlikely laggard on global markets.

Headlines: The list of U.S. Treasury questions for airlines seeking bailout cash
Description: U.S. Treasury officials have asked airlines seeking money from a $25 billion fund for payroll support to provide detailed information on their capital structure, liquidity and collateral, people briefed on the matter said.

Headlines: News Corp sees hit to ad revenue from coronavirus pandemic
Description: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp  said on Monday its newspaper advertising revenue would take a hit from widespread business closures caused by the coronavirus outbreak, although paid digital subscriptions for the Wall Street Journal are rising.

Headlines: 'Elbow to elbow:' North America meat plant workers fall ill, walk off jobs
Description: At a Wayne Farms chicken processing plant in Alabama, workers recently had to pay the company 10 cents a day to buy masks to protect themselves from the new coronavirus, according to a meat inspector.

Headlines: Reasons for hope: the drugs, tests and tactics that may conquer coronavirus
Description: With much of the world living in lockdown, the spread of the new coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, that was first detected in China late last year is beginning to slow in some places. As of April 12, 1.8 million had been infected and 115,000 killed  by COVID-19, the disease caused by the virus.

Headlines: Crude mixed on output deal, recession fears; shares slip
Description: Stocks on Wall Street mostly slid on Monday over concerns of what the coronavirus pandemic will do to corporate earnings, while crude prices were mixed as a global deal on record output cuts failed to quell doubts the pact would head off an oil glut.

Headlines: Amazon stops accepting new online grocery customers amid surging demand
Description: Amazon will begin to put new grocery delivery customers on a wait list and curtail shopping hours at some Whole Foods stores to prioritize orders from existing customers buying food online during the coronavirus outbreak, the company said on Sunday.

Headlines: Trump: It's my decision when to reopen U.S. economy
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday it was his decision when to reopen the U.S. economy, not that of state governors, but legal experts disagree and governors are going their own way.

Headlines: Oil mixed as demand worries offset gains from output cut deal
Description: Oil prices were mixed on Monday, as the historic production-cut deal inked by major global oil producers was not enough to assuage existing worries about the demand destruction brought on by the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. Treasury wants details on airline debt, liquidity, loyalty programs - sources
Description: U.S. Treasury officials have asked airlines seeking government payroll support to provide additional detailed information on capital structure, liquidity and loyalty programs, people briefed on the matter told Reuters.

Description: (This April 10 story has been refiled to fix typo in 'aid' in paragraph nineteen.)

Headlines: U.S. airlines ease loyalty programs in coronavirus travel slump
Description: U.S. airlines are extending loyalty program benefits and status into 2021 for members homebound because of the new coronavirus.

Headlines: Single passenger flights: The daily woes of airlines, and the crew still working
Description: When Reuters photographer Carlos Barria boarded American Airlines flight 4511 from Washington Reagan National Airport to New Orleans on Friday for an assignment, he was the only passenger on the 76-seat jet.

Headlines: U.S. GDP will contract 30% in second quarter, 5% in 2020: PIMCO
Description: (This April 8 story corrects to clarify that 30% contraction is the annualized rate)

Headlines: After pandemic, Fed policymakers see slow U.S. recovery
Description: The U.S. economy is set for a deep slide in coming months with the coronavirus forcing businesses to shut and putting millions out of work, but Federal Reserve policymakers are also warning of a slugging recovery once the pandemic subsides.

Headlines: Fashion giant Inditex working at reduced capacity despite loosened Spanish lockdown
Description: Employees at global fashion giant Inditex's 10 logistics centres in Spain - from where it sends garments to its stores worldwide - returned to work on Monday but only to less than half their normal levels of activity, workers said.

Headlines: Athene pays $45 million fine in first settlement of New York pension transfer probe
Description: Athene Holding Ltd agreed on Monday to pay a $45 million civil fine to settle charges it conducted insurance business in New York without a license, the first settlement in a probe into an industry where life insurers take over corporate pension plans.

Headlines: McDonald's faces class action over 'pervasive sexual harassment'
Description: McDonald's Corp has been hit with a class action lawsuit accusing it of subjecting female employees in its corporate-owned fast-food restaurants in Florida to widespread sexual harassment.

Headlines: Ford making masks to protect workers against COVID-19
Description: Ford Motor Co said on Monday it is producing face masks at a Michigan plant to protect its workers from the coronavirus pandemic and is seeking to have those masks certified for medical use.

Headlines: Russia hails oil deal it says will save millions of U.S.jobs
Description: The global oil production deal clinched at the weekend will help  establish a price floor and save millions of jobs in the United States, senior Russian officials said on Monday.

Headlines: GE offers to buy back at least $9 billion in debt, plans new longer-maturities issue
Description: General Electric Co  offered on Monday to buy back at least $9 billion in debt as part of a plan to cut its financial risk and manage liquidity in response to the downturn in business caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

Description: Worldwide oil producers, led by OPEC, are expected to cut production by roughly 20 million barrels per day (bpd), roughly equal to 20% of global daily supply, through a combination of mandated cuts, production falls due to poor economics, and purchases into oil reserves.

Headlines: Dish Network cuts jobs, re-evaluates business in coronavirus fallout
Description: Dish Network Corp  has cut staff and is re-evaluating  its business to cope better with the fallout from the coronavirus pandemic, the U.S. satellite TV provider told Reuters, without disclosing the number of employees laid off.

Headlines: Volkswagen offers cars for relief efforts in U.S. virus-hit regions
Description: Germany's Volkswagen AG  said on Monday its U.S. dealers would provide cars for free delivery of essential supplies to people in need during the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Aurora Cannabis falls on capital raise, reverse stock split
Description: Aurora Cannabis Inc's   U.S.-listed shares fell nearly 14% in morning trade on Monday after the Canadian pot producer renewed an at-the-market offering under which it can raise as much as $350 million in equity capital.

Headlines: Ford expects coronavirus shutdown to cause $600 million quarterly loss
Description: Ford Motor Co  said on Monday it expects to post a pre-tax loss of about $600 million for the first quarter as the coronavirus outbreak pummeled its sales and shuttered vehicle assembly plants, resulting in a 21% drop in vehicle sales to dealers versus the same quarter in 2019.

Description: Grocery distributor Performance Food Group Co  said on Monday it had furloughed about 3,000 employees and cut pay, while funneling 1,100 workers to help keep its retail clients' shelves stacked as it deals with the pressures exerted on supply chains and its business by the coronavirus crisis.

Description: OPEC and allies led by Russia agreed on Sunday to a record cut in output to prop up oil prices amid the coronavirus pandemic in  an unprecedented deal with fellow oil nations, including the United States, that could curb global oil supply by 20%.

Headlines: Trump says global oil production cut should help industry recover
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday the OPEC+ group of oil producers is looking to cut output by 20 million barrels per day (bpd), a figure that appeared to include a wider group of producers, including the United States.

Headlines: Saudi energy minister says effective global oil cuts above 19 million bpd
Description: Saudi Arabia's energy minister said on Monday that effective global oil supply cuts would amount to around 19.5 million barrels per day, taking into account the reduction pact agreed by OPEC+, pledges by other G20 nations and oil purchases into reserves.

Headlines: AutoNation CEO Cheryl Miller on leave for health reasons
Description: AutoNation Inc , the largest U.S. auto dealership chain, said on Monday Chief Executive Officer Cheryl Miller has been granted a leave of absence for health reasons.

Description: Toyota Motor Co  on Monday said it was suspending auto production in its Brazil plants until at least June 22, joining General Motors Co  which also expects to resume production in the same month.

Description: SoftBank expects its $100 billion Vision Fund to book a loss of 1.8 trillion yen due to the worsening performance of its tech bets, which will tip the group as a whole into its first loss for 15 years.

Headlines: GM plans to extend shutdown of Brazil auto production by 60 days
Description: (This April 9 story corrects start date of production shutdown to March 23, with furloughs starting on March 30.)

Description: Norway, Western Europe's largest oil producer, will announce its decision on whether to slash crude output soon, potentially adding its weight to a global push to shore up prices, the energy minister said on Monday.

Headlines: Russia fund says will continue to invest in Saudi Arabia: Al-Arabiya
Description: Russia's sovereign wealth fund will continue to invest in Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 development programme, the Saudi-owned Al-Arabiya channel on Monday cited the head of the fund as saying.

Headlines: Trading gains for big U.S. banks may not last past first quarter
Description: Big U.S. banks made a pretty penny in trading during the first quarter as the coronavirus pandemic caused wild market swings, analysts said, but those gains will likely be overshadowed by declines in other businesses and a bleak outlook for the rest of the year.

Description: Dubai's Emirates said on Monday it planned to operate limited passenger services to Algiers, Tunis, Jakarta, Manila, Taipei, Kabul and Chicago.

Description: Smithfield Foods Inc, the world's biggest pork processor, said on Thursday it is temporarily closing a plant in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, because of the new coronavirus, the latest disruption to the U.S. food supply chain from the outbreak.

Description: Global automakers reeling from the COVID-19 pandemic are accelerating efforts to restart factories from Wuhan to Maranello to Michigan, using safety protocols developed for China and U.S. ventilator production operations launched in recent weeks.

Headlines: Citigroup offers full-time positions to interns amid coronavirus crisis
Description: Citigroup Inc  said on Thursday it is offering full-time positions to its interns, but delaying the new class of summer intern program to July 6 amid the current coronavirus crisis.

Description: OPEC and other oil producers will debate on Thursday oil cuts as big as 20 million barrels per day, equivalent to about 20% of global supplies, one OPEC source and a Russian source told Reuters.

Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Thursday that aid for airlines will be the "next big thing" to be rolled out after the Federal Reserve announced new lending backstops for smaller and midsize companies and municipal bonds.

Headlines: IMF chief says engaged with all members including Turkey
Description: The International Monetary Fund remains engaged with all members, including Turkey, as they respond to the new coronavirus pandemic sweeping the globe, IMF Managing Director Kristalian Georgieva said on Thursday.

Description: Hyundai Motor Co's  Czech plant plans to restart on April 14 after a three-week production outage as part of efforts to fight the coronavirus, becoming the first of the three major carmakers in the central European country to resume work.

Description: JPMorgan  is seeking to sell at a discount loans raised by the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, according to two sources and a document, as banks brace for a borrowing spree in the Gulf due to low oil prices.

Headlines: Index Ventures raises $2 billion for early-stage, growth investments
Description: Venture capital firm Index Ventures said on Thursday it had raised $2 billion for early-stage and growth investments, backing entrepreneurs it reckons will lead the way out of the economic slump caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

Description: U.S. retail giant Costco  will open a new store in China's eastern city of Suzhou, near Shanghai, state media reported on Thursday.

Description: OPEC and its allies hold talks on Thursday to discuss plans for the biggest coordinated oil output cut in history but two hurdles remain: reaching a deal on the levels from which to make reductions and securing the participation of the United States.

Description: From Rupert Murdoch's News UK to McClatchy's chain of local newspapers across the United States, news publishers are attracting record numbers of readers as people in lockdown seek information about the coronavirus pandemic.

Description: A WeWork board committee that negotiated a $3 billion tender offer with SoftBank Group sued the Japanese conglomerate on Tuesday for abandoning the deal, accusing it of succumbing to "buyer's remorse" amid the novel coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Amazon testing disinfectant fog at New York warehouse after coronavirus protests
Description: Amazon.com Inc is testing the use of disinfectant fog at a warehouse in Staten Island, New York starting on Tuesday, the company told Reuters, following worker protests over the risk of coronavirus infection at the site.

Headlines: Mnuchin seeks additional $250 billion in small business relief from Congress by Friday
Description: Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Tuesday he wants Congress to approve an additional $250 billion for a small business relief program by Friday.

Headlines: Trump says $70 billion in coronavirus rescue loans authorized. But where's the cash?
Description: Roughly $70 billion of a $350 billion pot of loans to cover the payrolls of ailing small businesses have been originated by U.S. lenders in recent days, President Donald Trump said on Tuesday, adding that that money was "essentially loaned."

Headlines: Refunds row escalates as airlines warn millions of jobs at risk
Description: Global airlines warned that 25 million jobs across the world could be at risk from the coronavirus air travel downturn, and held out against offering refunds to passengers as cash runs out.

Headlines: Airlines cannot afford to refund cancelled tickets: IATA
Description: Global airlines cannot afford to refund cancelled flights because of the coronavirus crisis, said the head of the industry's representative body IATA, and carriers are issuing vouchers instead as they conserve cash to survive.

Headlines: U.S. SEC issues compliance focus areas for brokers before new rules take effect
Description: The head of the examination office at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Tuesday published details about the expected scope and content for compliance with a new rule requiring broker-dealers and investment advisers to disclose potential conflicts of interest.

Headlines: Oil drop saps gains as Wall Street fades late
Description: Wall Street fell on Tuesday, as a drop in oil prices steepened in the latter stages of the session and erased early gains built on tentative signs that coronavirus outbreaks in some of the biggest U.S. hot spots may be leveling.

Headlines: U.S. economy will eventually reopen but with big changes: Kudlow
Description: The Trump administration is aiming to reopen the U.S. economy when the nation's top health experts give the go-ahead, but Americans' lives will be drastically different, White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Former Fed chief Bernanke sees bad year, no quick recovery
Description: The U.S. economy could shrink 30% or more this quarter as stay-at-home orders aimed at slowing the coronavirus outbreak choke off business, and it could be a couple of years before the economy regains its footing, former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Wall Street volatility raises fears of another selloff
Description: The evaporation of a rally on Wall Street in the closing minutes of Tuesday's session shows that many investors fear the U.S. stock market is in danger of a renewed tumble due to uncertainty surrounding  the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Jobless Americans to see extra payments as soon as this week
Description: Americans who have lost their jobs due to the coronavirus outbreak will start getting enhanced jobless benefits as soon as this week as states deploy hundreds of billions of dollars in federal aid, state officials said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Oil drops on growing crude glut, doubts over output cuts
Description: Oil slumped on Tuesday in the face of swelling crude supplies and weak fuel demand due to the coronavirus pandemic, while investors also grew cautious over expectations that the world's biggest producers would quickly agree on output cuts.

Headlines: U.S. Treasury liquidity on the mend, but without Fed remains fragile
Description: Some measures of liquidity in the $17 trillion U.S. Treasury market are almost back to normal, thanks to the Federal Reserve's giant purchases, after drying up two weeks ago at the height of the coronavirus panic, but trading conditions remain challenging.

Headlines: Exxon lops 30% off 2020 spending, deeper and later than rivals
Description: Exxon Mobil Corp  on Tuesday throttled back investment in shale, natural gas and deep water production, cutting planned capital spending by 30% this year as the coronavirus pandemic saps energy demand and oil prices tumble.

Headlines: Exxon could delay third Guyana project as government review drags on
Description: Exxon Mobil Corp  said on Tuesday that production at the Payara project, its third development in Guyana, could be postponed due to delays in government approvals as the company scales back spending elsewhere due to the crude price crash.

Headlines: BlackRock's Aladdin investment management platform to be hosted on Microsoft's cloud
Description: BlackRock Inc, the world's largest asset manager, has partnered with Microsoft Corp to have its Aladdin investment and risk management system hosted on the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, the companies said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Investors await data on coronavirus drugs as market rally builds
Description: Clinical data on potential treatments for the new coronavirus could help sustain a market bounce that has buoyed stocks after last month's plunge, as investors look for signs that authorities may be able to stabilize the pandemic.

Headlines: Small U.S. businesses were already struggling. Then coronavirus hit
Description: Many small businesses were struggling with funding shortfalls and financial challenges even before the coronavirus pandemic hit, leaving them with little cash on hand to weather the slowdown caused by the virus, according to data released by the Federal Reserve on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. banking regulators encourage 'prudent efforts' by banks to help borrowers
Description: U.S. banks should feel welcome to pursue "prudent efforts" to help borrowers impacted by the coronavirus pandemic, according to a new joint statement issued by banking regulators Tuesday.

Headlines: Mexico asks U.S., Canada to grant automakers transition for USMCA rules
Description: Mexico's government on Tuesday asked the United States and Canada to grant its automotive industry extra time to adapt its supply chains as the deadline for implementing a new North American trade deal approaches.

Headlines: Hopes of progress against virus lift stocks; dollar falls
Description: World stock markets posted sharp gains on Tuesday as signs of progress in curbing the spread of the novel coronavirus in both Europe and the United States fueled investors' appetite for risk.

Headlines: Netflix rolls out more features for parental control globally
Description: Netflix Inc on Tuesday rolled out a number of features for parental control on its streaming platform, including options to filter out select titles and review what children are watching.

Headlines: United Airlines drastically cuts California flights to match demand
Description: United Airlines Holdings Inc said on Tuesday it was temporarily, but significantly, reducing daily flying in and out of Los Angeles and San Francisco airports to better match demand that has dropped due to the new coronavirus.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs must face class action over conflicts of interest, risky mortgages
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc must face a shareholder class action accusing the bank of hiding conflicts of interest, including behind-the-scenes dealings with a prominent hedge fund manager, when creating risky subprime securities before the 2008 financial crisis.

Headlines: Facebook launches new chat app for couples
Description: Facebook Inc on Tuesday launched a new messaging app for couples called "Tuned" that allows them to chat, share photos and music as well as have a timeline of shared memories.

Headlines: U.S. SEC's Clayton says companies seeking bailouts must disclose plans, communicate with investors
Description: The head of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Tuesday that companies in discussions about bailouts resulting from the economic impact of the coronavirus outbreak should disclose to investors where they stand.

Headlines: U.S. treasury secretary to seek additional $250 billion for small business
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Tuesday that he would seek an additional $250 billion to support small businesses hurt by the widespread economic slowdown.

Headlines: TJX to furlough most of about 286,000 staff as stores stay shut amid pandemic
Description: Off-price retailer TJX Companies Inc  said on Tuesday it would furlough most of the employees at its stores and distribution centers, as outlets remain closed to curb the spread of the coronavirus.

Headlines: Layoffs, closures to wipe out 6.7% of working hours worldwide in second quarter: ILO
Description: Workplace disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic are expected to wipe out labor equivalent to the effort of 195 million full-time workers, or 6.7% of hours clocked worldwide, in the second quarter of this year, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Colombian businesses call for more aid after quarantine extension
Description: Colombian businesses on Tuesday called on the government to expand measures to help companies weather coronavirus, after President Ivan Duque extended a nationwide lockdown by two weeks.

Headlines: OPEC+ needs to agree output numbers before meeting: Iran oil minister
Description: There needs to be an agreement on oil production numbers before any future meeting between OPEC and non-OPEC members, Iran's Oil Minister Bijan Zanganeh tweeted on Tuesday.

Headlines: Lufthansa to discontinue Germanwings in sweeping restructuring
Description: Lufthansa  will close its Germanwings low-cost airline as part of a broader overhaul including capacity cuts across the group, it said on Tuesday as it warned it could take years for the industry to recover from the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Online meal delivery firms knocked off course by coronavirus crisis
Description: The lockdown of millions of people at home across the globe due to the coronavirus should have been the perfect recipe for success for the burgeoning online meal delivery market.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. grants GE license to sell engines for China's new airplane
Description: The Trump administration on Tuesday granted a license to General Electric Co  to supply engines for China's new COMAC C919 passenger jet, a spokeswoman for the company said.

Headlines: AT&T takes on $5.5 billion loan to boost 'financial flexibility'
Description: AT&T Inc.  on Tuesday announced a $5.5 billion term-loan agreement, which it said would give the company "financial flexibility" during the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Side effects: Fuel demand crash shuts U.S. ethanol plants, meatpackers lack refrigerant
Description: A slew of U.S. ethanol plants have shut down as fuel demand has collapsed during the coronavirus outbreak, and meatpackers have been hit by a worrying side-effect: less carbon dioxide is now available to chill beef, poultry and pork.

Headlines: Huawei laments U.S. plans to crimp its global chip supply
Description: A Huawei Technologies Co Ltd [HWT.UL] executive on Tuesday described as "unfortunate" plans by the U.S. government to curb the Chinese telecom equipment maker's access to global chip supplies.

Headlines: Southwest building June flight schedule to reflect 'different phases of recovery'
Description: Southwest Airlines Co  said on Tuesday it would publish this week a new flight schedule for June 6 to June 27 with overall flight activity dropping by about 50% while taking into account "different phases of the recovery anticipated ahead."

Headlines: Honda, Nissan furlough U.S. workers as auto demand plummets
Description: Honda Motor Co  and Nissan Motor Co  on Tuesday said they had furloughed thousands of workers at their U.S. operations as the coronavirus pandemic slashes demand for cars in the country.

Headlines: Cineworld suspends dividend, defers pay to cushion virus hit; shares soar
Description: Cineworld's  shares soared 36% on Tuesday after it suspended its dividend and said it was in talks with landlords, film studios and major suppliers to offset the impact of the closure of all its 787 cinemas due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Japan's SoftBank to invest $48 million in Brazil pet products site Petlove
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp  reached an agreement to invest 250 million reais ($48 million) in pet products online retailer Petlove, the companies said in a statement on Tuesday.

Headlines: In a first, China knocks U.S. from top spot in global patent race
Description: China was the biggest source of applications for international patents in the world last year, pushing the United States out of the top spot it has held since the global system was set up more than 40 years ago, the U.N. patent agency said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Graphic: Oil majors cut 2020 spending by 22% after prices slump
Description: The world's biggest oil and gas companies are cutting spending this year following a collapse in oil prices driven by a slump in demand because of the coronavirus crisis and a price war between top exporters Saudi Arabia and Russia.

Headlines: Macy's finance chief Paula Price to step down in May
Description: Department store chain operator Macy's Inc  said on Tuesday Chief Financial Officer Paula Price would step down from the role next month after nearly two years on the job.

Headlines: Global health fund calls for $8 billion to begin COVID-19 exit strategy
Description: A leading global health fund has asked international businesses and governments to provide $8 billion to support development and production of COVID-19 tests, drugs and vaccines.

Headlines: Samsung first-quarter beats estimates; chips likely to prop up virus-hit second-quarter
Description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  said on Tuesday its first-quarter operating profit likely managed to rise slightly from a slump a year earlier, as solid chip sales helped cushion the blow from the coronavirus pandemic on smartphones and TVs.

Headlines: VW plans to partially reopen plant in Spain's Navarra on April 20
Description: German carmaker Volkswagen  hopes to partially reopen its plant in Spain's Navarra region on April 20 after its closure in mid-March due to the coronavirus outbreak, a spokesman for the plant said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Size of OPEC+ oil cuts will depend on how much others cut: source
Description: Any final agreement for how much OPEC and its allies, a group know as OPEC+, will cut during their talks on Thursday would depend on the volumes that other producers such as the United States, Canada and Brazil are willing to reduce, an OPEC source said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Demand for Luckin app surges as Chinese rush to drink up after admission of fraud
Description: Luckin Coffee's app has rocketed to become the second most popular in China as consumers rushed to claim a free drink that it has long offered for downloading, worried the chain might collapse after it said much of its sales last year were fabricated.

Headlines: As coronavirus hits tourism, Wizz Air finds new role
Description: Hungarian low-cost airline Wizz Air  is repatriating citizens and transporting medical equipment for east European governments, in a move coupling one-off charter traffic with savvy government relations amid the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: France's ADP loses 3 million euros a day in sales due to coronavirus - CEO
Description: French airports operator ADP is losing more than 3 million euros  ($3.25 million) in sales a day due to the coronavirus crisis, Chief Executive Augustin de Romanet said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Asian companies pose lower dividend risk due to stronger finances
Description: Asian firms appear better equipped to pay stable dividends compared with their western counterparts that are constrained by highly levered balance-sheets and a need to preserve cash during the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Employees worried about Valero response to virus cases at Texas refinery: sources
Description: Employees at Valero Energy Corp's Port Arthur, Texas, refinery expressed worries about the company's slow response to keep the coronavirus from spreading there after two workers tested positive, four people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Outbreak shows signs of leveling off in New York, New Jersey, but vigilance urged
Description: The governors of New York, New Jersey and Louisiana pointed to tentative signs on Monday that the coronavirus outbreak may be starting to plateau in their states but warned against complacency as the death toll nationwide approached 11,000.

Headlines: France's Thales withdraws final dividend, suspends outlook
Description: France's Thales  on Tuesday became the latest major company to slash its dividend, suspend profit guidance and top up liquidity in response to the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: China's Ucar, in which Luckin chairman is top shareholder, halts shares
Description: China's Ucar Inc, in which Luckin Coffee  Chairman Charles Zhengyao Lu is the biggest shareholder, suspended trading of its shares on Tuesday after regulators questioned the car service provider about how the alleged fraud at Luckin would impact it.

Headlines: Toshiba should sell stake in ex-chip unit at IPO, says HK activist fund in letter
Description: A Hong Kong-based activist investor in Toshiba Corp  has asked the Japanese conglomerate to sell its entire stake in Kioxia Holdings when the flash memory chip firm is listed in an IPO that could raise up to $32 billion, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters.

Headlines: Cemex resumes Mexico operations after brief pause due to coronavirus
Description: Mexican cement company Cemex said on Monday it would resume operations in the country, hours after announcing a pause, as fresh guidelines from the government permitted such a move.

Headlines: UPS employee dies of COVID-19 infection in Kentucky
Description: A United Parcel Service Inc worker employed in Kentucky died over the weekend from a COVID-19 infection, Gov. Andy Beshear said at a public health briefing on Monday.

Headlines: Hit by coronavirus, Fiat Chrysler, Peugeot seek to boost cash before merger
Description: With their sales hammered by the coronavirus outbreak, car makers Fiat Chrysler and Peugeot's owner PSA have postponed their shareholder meetings and are looking at ways to boost cash reserves ahead of their planned merger.

Headlines: NYSE in talks with SEC to ease listing rules during coronavirus volatility
Description: The New York Stock Exchange said on Monday it was in talks with regulators to temporarily ease its listing requirements to take the strain off companies that may have fallen out of compliance due to the market rout spurred by the coronavirus.

Headlines: Fed says it will provide financing against new U.S. 'payroll protection' loans
Description: The Federal Reserve on Monday moved to bolster a new small-business lending program by allowing banks to turn those loans over to the U.S. central bank for cash, easing concerns among banks about getting stuck holding the low interest loans.

Headlines: Wall Street soars on hopes of slowing coronavirus deaths
Description: U.S. stocks rocketed higher on Monday, with each of the major indexes rallying at least 7%, after a fall in the daily death toll in New York, the country's biggest coronavirus hot spot, fueled optimism a leveling off of the pandemic was on the horizon.

Headlines: Trump says OPEC has not asked him for a U.S. oil production cut
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday that OPEC had not pressed him to ask U.S. oil producers to reduce their output to support global prices, which have been hard-hit by the economic fallout of the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Alaska warned U.S. government its largest regional airline was on verge of collapse: letter
Description: Alaska's congressional delegation warned U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin last week that many of its airlines, including its largest regional carrier, RavnAir Group, were on the verge of collapse, according to a letter seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Airbnb secures $1 billion investment from Silver Lake, Sixth Street
Description: Airbnb said on Monday private equity firms Silver Lake and Sixth Street Partners will invest $1 billion in the U.S. home rental company, bolstering its finances at a time when the coronavirus outbreak has roiled the travel and leisure industry.

Headlines: Allstate to return $600 million in auto premiums as coronavirus cuts driving
Description: Allstate Corp , one of the largest U.S. auto insurers, said on Monday it would return more than $600 million in premiums to customers as many Americans drive less due to stay-at-home orders aimed at curbing the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Boeing suspending 787 production at South Carolina plant
Description: Boeing Co  said on Monday it would suspend production of its 787 airplane at its facilities in South Carolina amid the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: White House considering U.S. Treasury coronavirus bond: Kudlow
Description: White House advisers have been discussing the possibility of a coronavirus-related U.S. Treasury bond, President Donald Trump's economic adviser Larry Kudlow said on Monday.

Headlines: OPEC+ likely to agree to cut production if U.S. joins effort: sources
Description: Major oil producers including Saudi Arabia and Russia are likely to agree to cut production at a Thursday meeting but only if the United States joins the effort, aimed at coping with the disastrous effect of the coronavirus on fuel demand, three OPEC+ sources told Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: World stocks jump on less dire virus data, oil falls after OPEC+ delay
Description: World stock markets jumped on Monday, encouraged by slowdowns in coronavirus-related deaths and new cases in some global hot spots, while oil prices tumbled again due to a delay in talks between Saudi Arabia and Russia to cut supply.

Headlines: Honda, Fiat Chrysler aim to restart U.S., Canada auto production in May
Description: Honda Motor Co  and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV said on Monday they hope to restart U.S. and Canadian auto production in May amid the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Lufthansa to discuss permanently grounding Germanwings: sources
Description: Lufthansa  will discuss permanently grounding its Germanwings low-cost airline unit at a management board meeting on Tuesday, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Coronavirus muddies U.S. economic data as business closures push down response rates
Description: A near total closure of U.S. businesses as authorities try to control the spread of the novel coronavirus could make U.S. economic data unreliable in the coming months and harder to get a clearer picture of the severity of the recession caused by the virus.

Headlines: Oil falls after Saudi Arabia, Russia delay meeting, Cushing stockpiles soar
Description: Oil prices slumped on Monday, pulling back from last week's gains after Saudi Arabia and Russia delayed a meeting of oil producers aimed at resolving growing worldwide oversupply as the coronavirus pandemic pummels demand.

Headlines: CVS ramps up drive-through coronavirus testing sites with faster kits
Description: CVS Health Corp , called on by the Trump administration last month to help test Americans for infections from the new coronavirus, said it was launching two offsite testing locations with Abbott Laboratories'  faster diagnostic kit and would be able to handle 1,000 tests per day.

Headlines: Tiger at New York's Bronx Zoo tests positive for coronavirus
Description: A tiger at the Bronx Zoo in New York City has tested positive for the respiratory disease caused by the novel coronavirus, in the first known case of a human infecting an animal and making it sick, the zoo's chief veterinarian said on Sunday.

Headlines: Airbus announces additional production pauses
Description: Airbus  said on Monday it had decided additional production pauses, in Germany and in the United States, in response to an industry-wide slowdown triggered by the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Capri furloughs all North America retail staff, sees stores opening around June 1
Description: Capri Holdings Ltd  will furlough all its 7,000 retail staff in North America due to the coronavirus outbreak and expects to reopen stores around June 1, the owner of Michael Kors and Versace brands said on Monday.

Headlines: Zoom shares slip over security concerns, rising competition
Description: Shares of Zoom Video Communications Inc  fell 8% on Monday, adding to their sharp declines in the past few days, as the video conferencing app battles privacy concerns and increased competition from deep-pocketed rivals.

Headlines: Alaska Air expects to lower April and May capacity by 80%
Description: The U.S. carrier had earlier planned to reduce its April capacity by at least 10% and May capacity by at least 15%.

Headlines: Canada, U.S. farms face crop losses due to foreign worker delays
Description: Mandatory coronavirus quarantines of seasonal foreign workers in Canada could hurt that country's fruit and vegetable output this year, and travel problems related to the pandemic could also leave U.S. farmers with fewer workers than usual.

Headlines: Exclusive: Qatar Petroleum - coronavirus turmoil will not stop LNG expansion abroad
Description: Qatar Petroleum (QP) is pressing ahead with foreign as well as domestic expansion despite the global market turmoil caused by the coronavirus pandemic, its chief executive told Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: Luckin Coffee chairman defaults on loan, surrenders company shares
Description: Luckin Coffee  Chairman Charles Zhengyao Lu and Chief Executive Jenny Zhiya Qian have handed over shares in the embattled Chinese coffee chain to lenders after a company controlled by Lu's family defaulted on a $518 million margin loan, one of the banks said on Monday.

Headlines: GSK to partner with Vir for potential COVID-19 treatments, invest $250 million
Description: British drugmaker GlaxoSmithKline will invest $250 million in Vir Biotechnology Inc and collaborate to develop potential antibody treatments for COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus, the companies said on Monday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Qatar Petroleum not scaling down LNG expansion despite delay in bids - CEO
Description: Qatar Petroleum will postpone the start of production from its new gas facilities to 2025 due to a delay in the bidding process, but is not downsizing the world's largest liquefied natural gas project despite concerns of a mounting glut, its chief executive told Reuters.

Headlines: JPMorgan CEO Dimon calls 'bad recession', mulls suspending 2020 dividend
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co's top boss, Jamie Dimon , on Monday said he sees a "bad recession" in 2020, and that the largest U.S. bank could suspend its dividend if the coronavirus crisis deepens.

Headlines: Peugeot parent secures further 3 billion euros of loans
Description: Peugeot-owner PSA  said on Monday it had secured a further 3 billion euros ($3.3 billion) of loans, strengthening its financial position in the wake of the hit to the global automotive industry from the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: BMW sees demand falling further after first quarter sales plunge due to coronavirus
Description: BMW  is expecting a further decline in global demand as the coronavirus outbreak takes its toll, a spokesman said on Monday, after the German carmaker reported a 20.6% drop in first quarter sales to 477,111 vehicles.

Headlines: IBM taps former Bank of America CTO to oversee cloud business
Description: International Business Machines Corp  on Monday named former Bank of America Corp  top technology executive Howard Boville head of its cloud business, as Arvind Krishna takes over from long-time chief Ginni Rometty.

Headlines: Total among companies seeking force majeure on EDF contracts: sources
Description: Energy major Total  is among several power suppliers that tried to declare force majeure on buying nuclear power from EDF, sources said, as the coronavirus outbreak has pushed prices in the French electricity market far below existing contracts.

Headlines: As infections balloon, coronavirus squeezes Europe's armed forces
Description: Military forces across Europe have scaled back operations and imposed stricter rules on personnel to try to stem the spread of the coronavirus among staff who often live and work in close quarters, making them more vulnerable to infection.

Headlines: ILO annual gathering of labour ministers postponed for a year
Description: An annual gathering of the world's labour ministers will not take place this year because of the coronavirus pandemic, but will convene in June 2021, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said on Monday.

Headlines: Uber connects out-of-work U.S. ride-hail drivers to delivery, production jobs
Description: Uber Technologies Inc  said on Monday its app will list job openings in the delivery, food production and grocery industry that its U.S. drivers can access during a slump in ride-hailing demand due to the coronavirus.

Headlines: EasyJet founder steps up battle with management over Airbus order
Description: Stelios Haji-Ioannou, easyJet's  founder and biggest shareholder, on Monday intensified his battle with the airline's management over a huge aircraft order with Airbus  which he says it should cancel.

Headlines: EasyJet requests draw down of $500 million credit facility, explores more funding
Description: EasyJet  said on Monday it has requested to fully draw down its $500 million credit facility, secured against aircraft assets, and will continue to explore funding options due to a possibly prolonged grounding of its jets following the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Norwegian Air's March traffic tumbles 60% amid virus lockdown
Description: Norwegian Air's  passenger volume fell by 60% year-on-year in March as it grounded planes amid efforts to halt the spread of the new coronavirus, and will book a hedging loss of $102 million as the cost of fuel has plunged.

Headlines: BT boss gives salary to health workers, lifts pay for key staff
Description: The head of Britain's biggest telecoms firm BT  said he would donate his salary to health workers for at least six months and award a pay rise to his frontline staff who are maintaining broadband networks during the COVID-19 shutdown.

Headlines: SeaWorld CEO steps down after just five months on the job
Description: SeaWorld Entertainment Inc  said on Monday Sergio Rivera, the theme park operator's chief executive officer for just five months, has resigned due to disagreements with the board.

Headlines: HSBC Hong Kong shareholders mull legal action over dividend suspension
Description: HSBC  shareholders in Hong Kong are calling for an extraordinary meeting with the bank's management and considering legal action against its decision to scrap dividend payments.

Headlines: Safaricom, Vodacom finalise M-Pesa acquisition from Britain's Vodafone
Description: Kenya's leading telecom firm Safaricom  and South Africa's Vodacom  said on Monday that they had completed the acquisition of popular mobile money platform M-Pesa from Britain's Vodafone .

Headlines: American joins United, others in suspending more NYC flights on coronavirus spike
Description: American Airlines Group Inc  said late Sunday it would suspend more flights in and out of New York City's three main airports for about a month, joining other airlines that have cut flights to the area following a spike in coronavirus cases.

Headlines: Kia compact vehicles contractor suspends production
Description: A South Korean contract manufacturer for Kia Motors'  compact vehicles has suspended production, a company official said on Monday, citing a drop in overseas demand as the coronavirus outbreak has spread across Europe.

Headlines: Tesla engineers show ventilator prototype on YouTube
Description: Engineers at Tesla Inc  showed a prototype for a ventilator on Sunday evening in a video published on the company's YouTube channel, as hospitals around the country overwhelmed by coronavirus patients face device shortages.

Headlines: Solid chip sales unlikely to cushion Samsung's virus-hit first quarter profit
Description: The coronavirus-driven global shift to working from home is set to have boosted demand for Samsung Electronics' memory chips from laptop makers and data centres, but first-quarter profits are likely to remain flat as the outbreak weakened consumer electronics sales.

Headlines: Lufthansa's Belgian carrier suspends flights until mid-May
Description: Belgium's Brussels Airlines, a Lufthansa  subsidiary, has extended its suspension of flights until at least May 15, it said on Monday.

Headlines: Top Michelin executives agree to pay cuts to help with COVID-19 response
Description: French tyre company Michelin  said on Monday that its leading executives had agreed to take pay cuts as a gesture of solidarity to help deal with the negative effects of the hit to its business from the COVID-19 outbreak.

Headlines: As Germany reels from coronavirus, some officials debate impact on banks
Description: As Germany rolls out a 750 billion-euro economic stimulus package, officials and experts are discussing whether German lenders, including Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG, will be able to weather the economic fallout of coronavirus without state help.

Headlines: Dubai's Emaar suspends construction projects due to virus - sources
Description: Emaar Properties , the largest listed developer in the United Arab Emirates, has suspended work on major projects in Dubai, sources familiar with the matter said, as the coronavirus pandemic exacerbates a real estate slowdown in the business hub.

Headlines: Take Five: Life in the time of corona
Description: The world's biggest economy won't be open for business by Easter, as U.S. President Donald Trump had hoped, but the second biggest economy may come close. How China fares offers a guide to other countries when their coronavirus lockdowns lift.

Headlines: Rolls-Royce scraps targets, dividend on pandemic hit
Description: Rolls-Royce  is scrapping its targets and final dividend to shore up its finances as the British aero-engine maker's customers around the world ground planes due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: NMC in talks with lenders to avoid administration
Description: Troubled hospital group NMC Health  said on Monday it is in talks with Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank , seeking to convince it to withdraw an application that the lender had filed proposing that NMC be placed under administration.

Headlines: Wall St. looks for light at end of tunnel, sees risk stocks will re-test lows
Description: Wall Street analysts and investors see a risk that stocks could retest recent lows in the coming days or weeks as they worry about the spread of the virus and its impact on the economy, although some spot glimmers of light at the end of the tunnel.

Headlines: Rolls-Royce to ditch targets and suspend dividend due to coronavirus: FT
Description: British aero-engine maker Rolls-Royce  will abandon its targets on profits, cash and deliveries, and suspend its dividend, as airlines around the world ground planes due to the coronavirus outbreak, the Financial Times reported late on Sunday.

Headlines: Oil prices decline $3 a barrel as market remains uncertain on supply outlook
Description: Global benchmark oil prices traded as much as $3 a barrel lower as the market opened for Monday's trading session, reflecting fears of oversupply after Saudi Arabia and Russia postponed to Thursday a meeting about a potential pact to cut production.

Headlines: Exclusive: Silver Lake to seek more than $16 billion for buyout fund - sources
Description: Private equity firm Silver Lake Partners is preparing to seek at least $16 billion from investors for its sixth flagship buyout fund, braving the economic uncertainty of the coronavirus outbreak, according to people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Boeing extends Washington state production shutdown indefinitely
Description: Boeing Co  said on Sunday it would extend the suspension of production operations at its Washington state facilities until further notice amid the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: U.S. banks to defend dividend payments in stress tests: FT
Description: U.S. banks are expected to defend their dividend payments when they submit their annual capital plans to the Federal Reserve on Monday for the upcoming stress tests, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the situation.

Headlines: Fed's Bullard says another coronavirus economic relief bill may not be needed
Description: A top official at the U.S. Federal Reserve said on Sunday the $2.3 trillion economic relief bill approved by Congress was appropriately sized and that a further relief effort may not be needed if support efforts are well executed.

Headlines: How one Silicon Valley factory keeps running in the age of coronavirus
Description: The managers at Green Circuits — a small Silicon Valley electronics factory — thought they would have to close when the San Francisco Bay Area directed non-essential businesses to shut almost three weeks ago.

Headlines: United slashes New York-area flights due to coronavirus
Description: United Airlines  said late Saturday it will drastically reduce flights to two New York City airports amid the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: JPMorgan Chase probably unable to accept small business loan applications Friday: memo

Headlines: U.S. Air Force to release $882 million to Boeing: official
Description: The U.S. Air Force will release $882 million in payments to Boeing that were held back due to flaws in the KC-46 air refueling tanker, a Pentagon official said on Thursday.

Headlines: General Motors, Honda to jointly develop two new electric vehicles
Description: General Motors Co  and Honda Motor Co Ltd  said on Thursday they would jointly develop two new electric vehicles for Honda and are exploring more ways to expand their alliance.

Headlines: Stocks climb on oil price surge despite grim U.S. jobs data
Description: World equity markets climbed on Thursday on a surge in risky assets like oil, offsetting concerns over an increasing death toll from the coronavirus pandemic that is expected to push the global economy into recession.

Headlines: Dollar gains for second day; U.S. non-farm payrolls loom
Description: The dollar rose against a basket of currencies for a second straight day on Thursday as investors, worried about the prospect of a global recession, continued to take shelter in the greenback.

Headlines: Oil crash poses severe test for OPEC+ after Moscow, Riyadh miscalculate
