Description: The U.S. telehealth industry, including market leader Teladoc Health Inc, is preparing for a surge in demand as public health officials aiming to contain the fast-spreading new coronavirus encourage use of alternatives to clinic visits and patients seek to avoid public spaces.

Description: A three-year pact between OPEC and Russia ended in acrimony on Friday after Moscow refused to support deeper oil cuts to cope with the outbreak of coronavirus and OPEC responded by removing all limits on its own production.

Headlines: Another victim of coronavirus: Spain's religious statue-kissing
Description: A Spanish pre-Easter tradition, where Catholics flock in droves to kiss statues of Jesus and Mary, fell victim to the coronavirus epidemic this week as churches with some of the most sought-after statues told worshippers not to touch or kiss them.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp shares hit record low as investor faith dwindles
Description: Thyssenkrupp  shares hit a record low on Friday, prompting its finance chief to come out and defend the ailing conglomerate which must convince investors that it can earn cash following the sale of its elevator division.

Description: A Florida toymaker plans layoffs. A Wisconsin construction gear manufacturer has frozen hiring. And a California cosmetics company has idled some production, leaving 20 temporary workers with no paycheck.

Description: Futures traders are betting the Federal Reserve will slash U.S. interest rates in coming months to blunt damage to the world's largest economy, as governments and companies move to control the spread of the new coronavirus by limiting travel and public gatherings.

Headlines: Take Five: Credit crunch at time of rock-bottom rates?
Description: Is it possible we may see a wave of corporate defaults at a time when interest rates are at record lows and falling? In Europe, where many rates are below 0%, signs of stress are emerging as the coronavirus outbreak hits companies' bottom lines. An index of credit default swaps on 75 high-risk European companies compiled by IHS Markit -- the iTraxx Europe Crossover - has surged to the highest in almost four years. The list is pretty diverse: airlines, retailers, carmakers and others all feature.

Headlines: Fund managers change tack as Fed reacts to virus
Description: Fund managers are changing their allocations after the U.S. Federal Reserve stunned investors with a half-point rate cut this week to contain the economic fallout from the coronavirus epidemic.

Headlines: UBS hardens energy lending as 'sustainable' investments rise
Description: Switzerland's UBS  said the value of its 'sustainable' investments rose by more than 50% to nearly $500 billion in 2019, while lending to the energy and utilities sectors fell by 40% as it tightened its rules.

Headlines: Apple, Netflix pull out of South by Southwest festival amid coronavirus outbreak
Description: Apple Inc and Netflix Inc said they were pulling out of the South by Southwest music and tech festival to be held later this month, amid the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Exclusive: Mexican private sector pitches $92 billion in energy investment - document
Description: Mexico's private sector has drawn up a broad package of proposed energy investments for the government worth almost $92 billion, according to a document seen by Reuters on Wednesday, providing a potential lift to the country's misfiring economy.

Headlines: Wells Fargo to raise minimum pay in most of its U.S. markets
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Wednesday it plans to increase minimum wage to between $15 and $20 per hour for most of its U.S. markets, joining other Wall Street banks that have raised hourly pay in recent years.

Headlines: U.S. senator's trade advice to EU: Keep calm and put agriculture on the table
Description: The Trump administration would face resistance from the U.S. Congress if it tried to push through a mini trade deal with the European Union that did not include agriculture, U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley said on Wednesday.

Headlines: United Airlines, JetBlue cut flights, spending as coronavirus hits demand
Description: United Airlines Holdings Inc  and JetBlue Airways Corp  are cutting flights and implementing cost controls in the most drastic actions by U.S. airlines to get ahead of depressed travel demand due to the spreading coronavirus.

Headlines: U.S. lawmakers seek to step up pressure on UK to reverse Huawei 5G decision
Description: Members of the U.S. Congress on Wednesday took another step to try to prod Britain to reverse its decision to allow China's Huawei Technologies Co to build portions of the UK's next generation 5G networks.

Headlines: Wall Street surges on Biden bounce
Description: Wall Street roared back to life on Wednesday, with both the Dow and the S&P 500 surging more than 4%, after former Vice President Joe Biden's strong showing in the Super Tuesday Democratic primary contests injected a dose of confidence.

Headlines: IMF chief says coronavirus erases hopes for stronger growth in 2020
Description: The global spread of the novel coronavirus has crushed hopes for stronger growth this year and will hold 2020 global output gains to their slowest pace since the 2008-2009 financial crisis, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Canopy Growth to close two greenhouses, cut about 500 positions
Description: Pot producer Canopy Growth Corp  said on Wednesday it plans to close two of its greenhouses in Aldergrove and Delta, British Columbia, cutting about 500 positions.

Description: The dollar and global equities rose on Wednesday as a strong showing by Joe Biden in the U.S. Democratic presidential primaries cheered the markets, though the economy-slowing coronavirus outbreak kept investors on tenterhooks.

Headlines: EU executive seeks to crack down on gender pay gap
Description: The European Union's executive aims to introduce laws to combat gender pay gap across the bloc for the first time ever in a bid to fight inequality and boost the economy, according to a document seen by Reuters ahead of official publication.

Headlines: Oil gives up gains even as OPEC works on big output cut
Description: Crude oil prices ended lower, giving up early gains as major oil producers, including Saudi Arabia, struggled to bring Russia on board for deeper supply cuts to try to offset a slump in demand caused by the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Huawei pleads not guilty to new U.S. criminal charges in 2018 case
Description: China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd, the world's largest telecommunications equipment maker, on Wednesday pleaded not guilty in a New York federal court to new charges in a 2018 case against the company.

Headlines: GM takes aim at Tesla with 'Ultium' batteries and fleet of electric vehicles
Description: General Motors Co  Chief Executive Mary Barra said Wednesday the Detroit automaker will invest $20 billion by 2025 in electric and automated vehicles as it races to catch up with Elon Musk's Tesla Inc  as vehicles go electric.

Headlines: Uber open to using self-driving tech from competition: CEO
Description: Uber Technologies Inc's self-driving unit is open to using technology from competitors in the industry, the company's chief executive said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Data show U.S. economy on solid footing as coronavirus fears mount
Description: U.S. services sector activity jumped to a one-year high in February, suggesting strength in the economy before a recent escalation of recession fears ignited by the coronavirus epidemic that prompted an emergency interest rate cut from the Federal Reserve.

Headlines: U.S. businesses show growing concern over impact of coronavirus, Fed survey shows
Description: There are signs the escalating coronavirus outbreak has begun to weigh on business sentiment in the United States, a report by the Federal Reserve released on Wednesday showed, even as the U.S. economy expanded at a modest to moderate pace over the past several weeks.

Headlines: Factbox: From shadow banking to coronavirus, U.S. regulators eye lurking risks
Description: U.S. regulators will gather Wednesday at a scheduled meeting of the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) to discuss risks to the United States and beyond. With fears around coronavirus driving market turmoil not seen since the 2007-2009 financial crisis, here are some of the top risks in their sights.

Headlines: New BoE boss Bailey does not back immediate virus rate cut
Description: The Bank of England should wait until it has more clarity about the economic hit from the coronavirus outbreak before making any decision to cut interest rates, its next governor Andrew Bailey said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Family clan members back Volkswagen CEO's electric strategy: Bild
Description: Wolfgang Porsche and Hans-Michel Piech, members of the family which controls German carmaker Volkswagen , fully support the shift towards electric cars being driven by Chief Executive Herbert Diess, they told the Bild newspaper.

Headlines: Follow the Fed? Why central banks will not be rushed on coronavirus response
Description: Will the world's big central banks leave U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell hanging? They are certainly going to try.

Description: Campbell Soup Co  on Wednesday raised its fiscal full-year earnings forecast and posted better-than-expected quarterly profit and sales due to strong demand for soups and snacks, and its shares rose 5% in early trade.

Headlines: As Americans hoard food, Campbell Soup speeds up ingredients orders
Description: Campbell Soup  said it is ordering more ingredients to ensure it can keep enough soups, sauces and snacks on hand to meet growing demand from retailers as U.S. consumers hoard food in preparation for potential coronavirus quarantines.

Headlines: Keep calm and work from home during coronavirus, European banks tell workers
Description: Global banks and small investment firms in Europe are urging staff to work from home and curb travel as the financial industry braces for disruption from the rapidly spreading coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: GM CEO: North American plants secure 'quite far into this month'
Description: General Motors Co  Chief Executive Mary Barra said on Wednesday the automaker's North American vehicle production should be secure from parts shortages caused by the coronavirus outbreak "quite far into this month."

Headlines: GM launches advanced electric batteries to power its EVs
Description: U.S. automaker General Motors Co  on Wednesday launched Ultium, a battery with higher capacity and fast charging capabilities, to power its upcoming line of electric vehicles.

Headlines: Next BoE boss Bailey wants clearer view on coronavirus hit before rate decision
Description: Andrew Bailey, the next governor of the Bank of England, said on Wednesday that he wanted to see more evidence about the economic impact of the coronavirus outbreak before deciding whether to cut interest rates.

Headlines: GE says coronavirus will hit first-quarter cash flow, sticks to full-year forecast
Description: General Electric Co  predicted on Wednesday that the coronavirus would wipe out a substantial chunk of industrial free cash flow in the first quarter, but stuck to full-year financial targets the company set in January.GE predicted that the outbreak would erase $300 million to $500 million from industrial free cash flow and cause a hit of $200 million to $300 million to its first-quarter operating profit. Headlines: Fiat Chrysler's U.S. sales chief Reid Bigland who sued company steps down
Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles  said on Wednesday its U.S. sales chief, Reid Bigland, is leaving the company to pursue other interests.

Headlines: U.S. service sector races to one-year high in February
Description: U.S. services sector activity accelerated to a one-year high in February, suggesting underlying strength in the economy despite the coronavirus outbreak, which has triggered financial market fears of a recession and led to an emergency interest rate cut from the Federal Reserve.

Headlines: Johnson & Johnson ordered to pay $1.7 million to three Australian women in pelvic mesh class action
Description: An Australian court on Tuesday ordered Johnson & Johnson  to pay three women a total of A$2.6 million ($1.7 million) plus legal costs as compensation for misleading patients and surgeons about the risks of its pelvic mesh implants.

Headlines: Bayer's top seed faces U.S. soybean challenge from Corteva
Description: Bayer AG's takeover of Monsanto has been beset by problems, and now a decades-long dominance of the $4 billion U.S. soybean seed market is under threat from rival Corteva Inc.

Headlines: Facebook gives WHO free ads in battle with coronavirus misinformation
Description: Facebook Inc  will provide free advertisements to the World Health Organization (WHO) as it seeks to ensure users are not misinformed about the virus, its risks and how to react to it, Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Investor Stroll eyes sharing Formula One tech with Aston Martin road cars
Description: Canadian billionaire Lawrence Stroll, who is investing in carmaker Aston Martin , sees the opportunity to share Formula One technology with the firm's range of road cars, he said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Lego classics build growth for Danish toymaker in shrinking market
Description: Model fire stations and garbage trucks helped Lego defy a shrinking toy market with a rise in sales last year, as the plastic brick maker outpaced rivals with the latest versions of its classic kits, as well as new stores and a revamped website.

Headlines: Factbox: Airlines' steps to revive bookings hit by global coronavirus outbreak
Description: In an effort to win over passengers hesitant about traveling in the midst of a spreading coronavirus outbreak, some airlines are offering free rebooking options.

Headlines: How an ill-timed bet on a U.S. oil refinery cost ICBCS millions
Description: A team of ICBC Standard bankers celebrated in London last June after closing its first major U.S. refinery deal and gaining a foothold in the biggest energy market in the world.

Headlines: Resiliency test: How well can Chinese firms cope financially from a virus hit?
Description: As companies in China gradually restart business following the extended Lunar New Year break, investors are fretting over the  financial impact of the coronavirus outbreak that has squeezed cash flow and hammered revenues in many sectors.

Headlines: Amazon confirms first coronavirus case among U.S. employees
Description: Online retailer Amazon.com Inc  said on Tuesday an employee in the United States tested positive for the coronavirus.

Headlines: Exclusive: SoftBank-backed CloudMinds blocked from exporting U.S. tech to China
Description: SoftBank-backed startup CloudMinds has been blocked from sharing U.S.-origin technology with its China business, documents showed, illustrating how increased U.S. government restrictions are creating new headaches for tech firms and their investors.

Headlines: HK's Bank of East Asia to review assets with Elliott Management
Description: Hong Kong-based Bank of East Asia  said on Wednesday it would carry out a comprehensive review of its portfolio of businesses and assets with the support of activist investor Elliott Management.

Headlines: U.S. Supreme Court leans toward SEC's power to recover ill-gotten gains
Description: U.S. Supreme Court justices on Tuesday appeared inclined to back the Securities and Exchange Commission's power to use federal courts to force defendants to surrender profits obtained through fraud as part of enforcement of investor-protection laws.

Headlines: SoftBank CEO hosts 'pre-IPO summit' in New York as he courts investors
Description: SoftBank Group Corp Chief Executive Masayoshi Son held his first "pre-IPO summit" for the Japanese conglomerate's portfolio companies on Tuesday, introducing them to Wall Street investors who could be backing their stock market debuts.

Headlines: Fed cuts rates to blunt coronavirus impact, markets drop
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve cut interest rates on Tuesday in a bid to shield the world's largest economy from the impact of the coronavirus, but the emergency move failed to comfort U.S. financial markets roiled by worries about a deeper, lasting slowdown.

Headlines: Fed's Evans expects virus impacts on economy to be short-lived
Description: The coronavirus outbreak will likely have only a "short-lived imprint" on the U.S. economy, Chicago Federal Reserve bank President Charles Evans said on Tuesday night.

Description: Wall Street tumbled in a volatile session on Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve surprised investors with a half percentage-point cut in interest rates, amplifying fears about the magnitude of the coronavirus' impact on the economy.

Description: Wall Street stepped up preparations to deal with the impact of the coronavirus on Tuesday, testing backup plans and asking employees to work from home, as a New Yorker tested positive for the virus, bringing the prospect of the spread of the infection closer to home.

Headlines: Hewlett Packard Enterprise cuts cash flow outlook on coronavirus impact, shares down
Description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise  on Tuesday cut its free cash flow forecast for the year citing supply constraints due to the coronavirus outbreak, and reported a lower-than-expected quarterly revenue.

Headlines: Ackman hedges to protect against coronavirus' 'negative' impact
Description: Billionaire hedge fund investor William Ackman on Tuesday said he has moved to protect the firm's $6.6 billion portfolio, which includes restaurant chain and hotel stocks, as the spread of the coronavirus has sparked prolonged panic selling in markets.

Headlines: NBCUniversal sells record $1.25 billion in Tokyo Olympic ads
Description: Comcast Corp's  NBCUniversal said on Tuesday it had sold more than $1.25 billion in national advertising for the Tokyo Olympics, a new record for any broadcaster for the games.

Description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc , the conglomerate run Warren Buffett, said it will hold its annual shareholder meeting on May 2 despite the coronavirus outbreak, but may curtail some of the surrounding events.

Headlines: Fed's Mester sees possible economic impact from coronavirus outbreak
Description: The coronavirus outbreak has muddied the outlook for the U.S. economy and could weigh on growth in the first half of this year, Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank President Loretta Mester said in London on Tuesday.

Headlines: JPMorgan to test emergency coronavirus plans with some employees working from home: sources
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  is asking thousands of U.S. employees to spend a day working from home in the coming weeks to test its contingency plans should the coronavirus spread, sources familiar with the plan told Reuters.

Description: Bank of England Governor Mark Carney said policymakers around the world are working on a "powerful and timely" response to the economic hit from coronavirus which has raised fears of a new global recession.

Description: The global oil benchmark ended Tuesday slightly lower under pressure from falling equities, but the losses were contained slightly as top producers considered more output cuts to support prices and the Federal Reserve cut U.S. interest rates to support the economy.

Headlines: Fed virus-driven cut may test new approach to inflation
Description: U.S. Federal Reserve officials have slashed interest rates half a percentage point because of the coronavirus.

Headlines: OPEC, Russia moving closer to big oil cut as coronavirus hits demand
Description: A panel of OPEC and its allies recommended cutting oil output by an extra 1 million barrels per day (bpd) on Tuesday signaling that Russia and Saudi Arabia were moving closer to a deal to prop up prices which have been hit by the coronavirus outbreak.

Description: U.S. package delivery companies United Parcel Service Inc  and FedEx Corp  warned on Tuesday that the coronavirus outbreak could disrupt shipment of goods in affected countries and possibly weigh on their first-quarter results.

Description: Finnish network equipment maker Nokia will cut up to 148 jobs in Finland in 2020 excluding its 5G development operations, it said on Tuesday evening.

Description: Germany's Lufthansa  threw its weight behind a proposed $4.2 billion takeover of Embraer's commercial aircraft activities by Boeing , saying it would preserve a level playing field.

Description: A technical committee of OPEC and its allies considered a cut in oil production of 600,000 to 1 million barrels per day (bpd), and recommended a reduction in output of at least 600,000 bpd, two sources said.

Description: The European Central Bank is ready to support the economy in the face of the coronavirus outbreak, but governments with budget leeway also need to help, ECB policymaker Francois Villeroy de Galhau said in a Dutch newspaper interview released on Tuesday.

Headlines: Exxon Mobil calls for tighter methane regulations
Description: Exxon Mobil on Tuesday called for tighter regulation of the greenhouse gas methane and offered up its own in-house rules as a model for companies and lawmakers worldwide.

Description: OPEC and its allies will consider making substantial oil production cuts to lift prices that have been battered by the coronavirus outbreak, Algeria's oil minister said on Tuesday, as ministers began arriving for talks in Vienna this week.

Description: The World Bank said it would announce a package of financial and technical support later on Tuesday to assist with the health and economic impacts of the global coronavirus outbreak.

Description: The U.S. dollar's strength will remain in place and for longer than expected just a month ago, despite Federal Reserve interest rate cuts intended to limit the economic damage from the spreading coronavirus, a Reuters poll showed.

Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin on Tuesday said the United States was not considering lowering tariffs on goods from China in response to the fast-spreading coronavirus, but would look at all options as the situation evolved.

Description: Traders of futures contracts tied to the Federal Reserve's policy rate reacted to a sooner-than-expected reduction in borrowing costs Tuesday with bets on more to come as the central bank moves to try to shield the U.S. economy from the effects of the new coronavirus.

Description: Urged to restore economic activity by President Xi Jinping, large parts of China relaxed curbs on transport and travel on Monday as reported new cases of coronavirus outside the worst-hit province fell to the lowest in a month.

Description: PepsiCo Inc  has agreed to buy Chinese snack brand Be & Cheery from local jujube maker Haoxiangni Health Food Co Ltd  for $705 million, the companies said.

Headlines: Ex-Facebook executive starts group to help employees push companies on climate
Description: Facebook's former sustainability chief has launched an organization to help employees at big companies press their bosses for more aggressive policies to fight climate change.

Description: Canadian miner Teck Resources Ltd has withdrawn an application to build its C$20.6 billion ($15.7 billion) Frontier oil sands mine in Alberta, days before the federal government was to decide on whether to approve a project opposed by environmentalists and indigenous groups.

Headlines: Rising stocks fuel record profit for Buffett's Berkshire; operating profit disappoints
Description: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc  on Saturday posted a 23% decrease in quarterly operating profit, while soaring prices in stock holdings such as Apple Inc  enabled the conglomerate to smash its old record for full-year earnings.

Headlines: Buffett calls for more accountability for corporate directors
Description: Warren Buffett on Saturday called on corporate America to make their boards of directors more accountable to shareholders and less beholden to chief executive officers, perhaps by reducing their pay and requiring that they buy more stock.

Headlines: Buffett defends Berkshire stock push, reassures on future as profit smashes record
Description: Warren Buffett on Saturday forcefully defended Berkshire Hathaway Inc's  decision to invest heavily in stocks of companies such as Apple Inc  as he labors through a four-year drought since his last major acquisition of a company.

Headlines: Exclusive: If Lebanon needs financial aid, France will be there, finmin says
Description: France is ready to support Lebanon financially - bilaterally or multilaterally - its finance minister said on Sunday, warning against mixing economic recovery in the small Mediterranean state with U.S.-led efforts to counter Iran in the region.

Headlines: UniCredit CEO Mustier ruled out of HSBC role: source
Description: UniCredit Chief Executive Jean Pierre Mustier has ruled himself out of a switch to European rival HSBC , a source with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Sunday.

Headlines: No global digital tax by end-2020 would mean chaos: France
Description: Failure to reach a global deal on where and how much to tax digital giants such as Google , Amazon  or Facebook  would result in many digital tax regimes emerging all over the world, France's Finance Minister said on Sunday.

Headlines: G20 finance heads eye impact of coronavirus outbreak on growth, see modest pickup
Description: Finance chiefs of the world's top 20 economies vowed to monitor the impact of the coronavirus outbreak on global growth and act if needed, as they said loose monetary policy and easing trade tensions would prompt a pick-up in 2020 and 2021.

Headlines: As Teck oil sands mine hopes for okay from Canada's Trudeau, 20 other projects on hold
Description: As Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau considers whether to approve Teck Resources' Frontier oil sands project, roughly 20 others sit on the shelf as companies delay investment decisions hoping for new pipelines and higher prices.

Headlines: Japan criticizes U.S. digital tax proposal at G20
Description: Japanese finance minister Taro Aso criticized on Sunday a U.S. tax reform proposal that he said could undermine global efforts to agree new rules on taxing big tech companies.

Headlines: Banned Thai opposition party says junta helped 1MDB cover-up
Description: A banned Thai opposition party on Sunday accused the former military junta of helping cover up Malaysia's multi-billion-dollar 1MDB scandal, urging Thais to demand the truth ahead of a censure debate against Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha.

Headlines: Shifting sands of inflation unsettle top bankers at Riyadh G20 meeting
Description: Central bankers from the United States, Japan and the euro zone meeting in the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia this weekend had their own shifting sands to cross – those of elusive inflation.

Headlines: Hughes fears Indian closure, bank disruptions over unpaid fees
Description: U.S. satellite broadband provider Hughes Network Systems may have to shut its Indian operations due to unpaid levies owed to the government, which could put thousands of banking services at risk, a company letter seen by Reuters showed.

Headlines: TurboTax maker Intuit nears agreement to buy Credit Karma for $7 billion: WSJ
Description: Intuit Inc is nearing an agreement to buy financial technology portal Credit Karma Inc for about $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Headlines: Samsung Electronics confirms coronavirus case at phone factory complex in South Korea
Description: Samsung Electronics  said on Saturday that one coronavirus case had been confirmed at its mobile device factory complex in the southeastern city of Gumi, causing a shutdown of its entire facility there until Monday morning.

Headlines: Let's come together to tax tech giants, say G20 officials eyeing $100 billion boost
Description: Leading world economies must show unity in dealing with aggressive "tax optimization" by global digital giants like Google , Amazon  and Facebook , G20 officials said on Saturday.

Headlines: G20 sees need to coordinate coronavirus response as IMF trims growth forecasts
Description: The world's top economies called on Saturday for a coordinated response to the coronavirus outbreak, which the IMF predicted would lower China's growth this year to 5.6% and shave 0.1 percentage points from global growth.

Headlines: Honda's Philippine unit to close auto production plant
Description: The Philippine unit of Honda Motor Co Ltd  said on Saturday its production facility will shut down next month, as the Japanese automaker struggles to shore up global automobile operations.

Headlines: Japan urges G20 members with fiscal scope to boost spending
Description: Japan called on G20 countries with fiscal space to ramp up spending to help the global economy weather risks, including the fallout from the coronavirus outbreak, Finance Minister Taro Aso said on Saturday.

Headlines: The ECB wants to talk to you about inflation. But will it listen?
Description: For many people, the language of European Central Bank policymakers is so impenetrable, it could be beamed from another planet.

Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Saturday it was very important to have tax certainty on a global basis and that the OECD was very close to consensus on a framework for minimum corporate tax.

Description: Federal prosecutors investigating Boeing Co  are examining whether the U.S. planemaker knowingly misled the Federal Aviation Administration while it was seeking approval for its 737 MAX jet, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.

Description: Blocked highways. Stranded workers. Dwindling supplies. Shipping and air freight companies also hamstrung.

Headlines: U.S. meeting on Huawei, China policy still on for Thursday despite Trump tweets: sources
Description: A meeting of U.S. government officials to discuss further curbs on exports to Huawei and China is still on for Thursday, two sources said, despite pushback from President Donald Trump against the restrictions.

Headlines: Fed policymakers cautiously optimistic on U.S. economy despite new risks, minutes show
Description: Federal Reserve policymakers were cautiously optimistic about their ability to hold interest rates steady this year, minutes of the central bank's last policy meeting showed, even as they acknowledged new risks caused by the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Fed staff float plan to end term-repo after April, minutes show
Description: Senior Federal Reserve staff proposed ending longer-term loans to banks after April as part of a broader blueprint laying out how the central bank could scale back the support provided to money markets, the minutes from the January policy meeting showed.

Headlines: Lofty stocks, hefty debt sow seeds of worry for some at Fed
Description: Rock-bottom corporate bond yields, high levels of business debt and one of the fastest expansions of stock market valuations on record are worrying some Federal Reserve officials who fret such financial imbalances could aggravate any negative shocks to the U.S. economy.

Headlines: S&P 500, Nasdaq hit record closing highs, lifted by China stimulus hopes
Description: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose to record closing highs on Wednesday as optimism that China would take more measures to prop up its economy eased concerns about the economic impact of the coronavirus epidemic.

Headlines: Fresenius Medical says fourth-quarter operating profit up 3%
Description: Germany's Fresenius Medical Care  on Wednesday said quarterly adjusted operating income edged 3% higher as growth in dialysis services and products was partly offset by a negative adjustment for accounts receivable in a legal dispute in North America.

Headlines: Boeing, crash victims' lawyers negotiate over access to 737 MAX documents
Description: Boeing Co and lawyers representing families of victims of a 737 MAX crash agreed in court on Wednesday to hold a conference call with U.S. government crash probe authorities over access to documents related to the now-grounded aircraft's design, development and two fatal disasters involving it.

Headlines: China's HNA emerges as recent buyer of A330neo jets amid revamp: sources
Description: Debt-laden HNA Group has restructured jet orders with Europe's Airbus in a compromise deal that includes an order for dozens of A330neo jets, two people familiar with the matter said, amid reports of a wider shake-up at the Chinese conglomerate.

Headlines: Virgin Galactic looks like newest cult stock as short sellers dig in
Description: Wall Street's newest cult stock appears to be Richard Branson's Virgin Galactic Holdings Inc , as investors drive shares of the space tourism company to sky-high levels and short sellers dig in their heels.

Headlines: French judges step up Ghosn probe over palace party, Oman dealings
Description: French prosecutors have stepped up their investigation into alleged misappropriation of funds at Renault by former boss Carlos Ghosn, saying a judge had now been assigned to the case to launch a formal investigation.

Headlines: Stocks scale fresh peaks on slowing virus, dollar gains
Description: The dollar gained while several U.S. and European equity indexes scaled fresh peaks on Wednesday after China reported another decline in new coronavirus cases and on expectations of Chinese stimulus to counter a slowdown in growth.

Headlines: Exclusive: Google users in UK to lose EU data protection - sources
Description: Google is planning to move its British users' accounts out of the control of European Union privacy regulators, placing them under U.S. jurisdiction instead, sources said.

Headlines: Should Facebook, Google be liable for user posts? asks U.S. Attorney General Barr
Description: U.S. Attorney General William Barr on Wednesday questioned whether Facebook, Google and other major online platforms still need the immunity from legal liability that has prevented them from being sued over material their users post.

Headlines: Oil up more than 2% on slowing coronavirus cases, U.S. move on Venezuela
Description: Oil prices gained more than 2% on Wednesday as worries eased about demand declining due to the spread of coronavirus cases in China, while supplies tightened as the United States moved to cut off more Venezuelan crude from the market.

Headlines: Business jet deliveries hit decade high in 2019, helped by new models
Description: Business jet deliveries across the globe hit a decade high in 2019, the General Aviation Manufacturers Association (GAMA) said on Wednesday, helped by strong market demand for new models.

Headlines: U.S. housing starts fall, building permits near 13-year high
Description: U.S. homebuilding fell less than expected in January while permits surged to a near 13-year high, pointing to sustained housing market strength that could help keep the longest economic expansion in history on track.

Headlines: Exclusive: 'Made in Russia' passenger jet finds a single buyer, Aeroflot
Description: Russia's main home-grown passenger jet, the Sukhoi Superjet 100,  conceived as a rival to Airbus, Bombardier and Embraer, has no confirmed orders this year beyond a long-standing deal with state carrier Aeroflot , two sources told Reuters.

Headlines: This revamp will be different, says HSBC boss; staff not so sure
Description: Noel Quinn, the interim chief executive of HSBC , says this time things are going to be different.

Headlines: Airbus defense division plans to cut more than 2,300 jobs
Description: The defense business of Airbus  on Wednesday laid out plans to cut more than 2,300 jobs, citing a flat space market and postponed defense contracts.

Headlines: T-Mobile owner sets sights on becoming U.S. number one
Description: Deutsche Telekom  is aiming to become market leader in the United States, CEO Tim Hoettges said on Wednesday, now that a deal for its T-Mobile US  unit to take over Sprint  is within reach.

Headlines: We can live with German, EU ideas on vendor regulation: Deutsche Telekom
Description: It looks as though German and European policy makers are working towards rules governing vendors of telecoms network equipment that Deutsche Telekom  can live with,

Headlines: Lyft resumes shared electric bike rentals in NYC
Description: Lyft Inc  will roll out a fleet of several hundred electric bikes for rent across New York City, the company said on Wednesday, 10 months after it pulled them following complaints and injury reports.

Headlines: Regulators need to get up to speed on digital currencies
Description: Global financial regulators risk falling behind on rapid innovation in the digital payments industry and need to work more quickly to devise rules for crypto-currencies or "stablecoins", the chair of a global finance watchdog said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Boeing finds debris in 737 MAX jetliners: company memo
Description: Boeing Co  found debris that could pose potential safety risks in the fuel tanks of several 737 MAX aircraft that are in storage and waiting to be delivered to airlines, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Tuesday.

Headlines: Nokia to acquire optical networking tech firm Elenion
Description: Finnish telecom networks maker Nokia Oyj said on Wednesday it has agreed to acquire privately-held U.S.-based company Elenion Technologies to boost its optical networking business and broaden its offering to telecoms operators.

Headlines: Kuwaiti parliament to investigate Airbus aircraft orders
Description: Kuwaiti lawmakers agreed on Wednesday to set up a committee to look into whether Airbus's  aircraft orders from the Gulf Arab state involved alleged corruption, the state news agency reported.

Headlines: U.S. urges EU to use 5G by Ericsson, Nokia, Samsung, seen on par with Huawei
Description: EU countries have no reason to use 5G mobile technology from Huawei because Sweden's Ericsson , Finland's Nokia  and South Korea's Samsung  are on par with the Chinese group in the field, a senior U.S. diplomat said.

Headlines: Air France faces new strikes over domestic network cuts
Description: Air France  unions have called for strikes at its domestic carrier Hop as pilots seek improved pay and conditions and ground staff press for job guarantees, union officials said.

Headlines: Exclusive: Vodafone, Telecom Italia offer rivals access to some sites to ease EU concerns - EU paper
Description: Vodafone  and Telekom Italia  have offered to allow rivals access to sites in some cities for up to nine years, a proposal aimed at allaying EU antitrust concerns over the creation of Italy’s largest mobile tower company, according to an EU document seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Qatar Airways spends $600 million to lift stake in BA owner to 25%
Description: Qatar Airways has bought a $600 million stake in British Airways-owner IAG  to increase its holding to 25.1%, strengthening its position ahead of a change in IAG management.

Headlines: Their market shut, traders in China's Silicon Valley do business from bags
Description: While coronavirus fears curtail much of China's bustle, traders are getting back to business at the world's largest electronics market, buying and selling from bags and suitcases on the streets outside their shut premises.

Headlines: Adidas, Puma warn of coronavirus hit to China business
Description: German sportswear makers Adidas  and Puma  have both warned that the coronavirus outbreak was hurting their business in China due to store closures and fewer Chinese tourists travelling and shopping in other markets.

Headlines: UniCredit CEO says no M&A deal after Intesa's surprise UBI bid
Description: The head of UniCredit  repeated in a letter to staff on Wednesday that Italy's biggest bank had no intention of engaging in merger and acquisition deals following Intesa's  blitz move to buy rival UBI Banca .

Headlines: General Motors to lay off all 1,500 plant workers in Thailand following sale
Description: General Motors will begin laying off around 1,500 employees in Thailand in June, after announcing the sale of its production plants in the country, a government official said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Citi, Deutsche start talks to sell $9 billion Dubai port company debt: sources
Description: Citi  and Deutsche Bank  have started talks with other banks to sell roughly $9 billion in debt Dubai raised to take full control of DP World  and refinance borrowings of Dubai World, sources familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Renault shares fall after Moody's cuts its debt to 'junk' status
Description: Renault's  shares fell on Wednesday after Moody's cut its rating on the French carmaker's debt to "junk" status, citing weaker profitability as the company restructures and grapples with falling demand.

Headlines: BlackRock bolsters European management as part of regional expansion: memo
Description: BlackRock , the world's biggest asset manager, has appointed two executives to oversee its operations in continental Europe as part of efforts to expand in the region, a memo to staff on Wednesday seen by Reuters showed.

Headlines: Merged T-Mobile U.S. to close valuation gap on Big Two: Deutsche Telekom CEO
Description: The merger between T-Mobile US  and Sprint  is within reach, the head of its main owner Deutsche Telekom said, forecasting that the combined business would quickly close a valuation gap on market leaders AT&T  and Verizon .

Headlines: Puma warns of hit to sales and profits from coronavirus
Description: German sportswear group Puma  on Wednesday said it expected China's coronavirus outbreak to hit its sales and profits in the first quarter but it still hopes to reach its targets for 2020.

Headlines: Hyundai Motor chairman to give up board seat as succession looms
Description: Hyundai Motor Group  Chairman Mong-Koo Chung plans to give up his board seat, in the latest sign that the octogenarian patriarch of South Korea's second-largest conglomerate is preparing to hand the reins over to his son.

Description: Shanghai has compiled a list of firms, including local units of multi-nationals Unilever PLC  and 3M Co , as eligible for millions of dollars in subsidized loans to ease any blow from the coronavirus outbreak, according to bankers and documents seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Exclusive: India antitrust investigators see no evidence of collusion by IndiGo, SpiceJet and others - sources
Description: Investigators with India's antitrust watchdog have found no evidence that the country's biggest airline, IndiGo , and four rival carriers colluded to fix ticket prices, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Metro Bank names interim boss Dan Frumkin CEO
Description: Metro Bank  on Wednesday named interim Chief Executive Dan Frumkin to the role permanently, tasking him with leading the British lender past an accounting scandal that plunged it into crisis last year.

Headlines: Uber closing office in downtown Los Angeles
Description: Uber Technologies Inc  is closing its office in downtown Los Angeles, where the ride-hailing company employs customer support staff, to focus on its bigger locations.

Description: Spam-maker Hormel Foods Corp  is eliminating a growth drug banned by China from its hog supply, the company said on Tuesday, joining rivals that are seeking to increase meat sales to Chinese buyers grappling with a pork shortage.

Description: A federal judge in Texas on Tuesday rejected Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's constitutional challenge to a U.S. law that restricted its ability to do business with federal agencies and their contractors.

Description: When cameraman Mark Xia returned to his job this month after holidays, the Shanghai video production house where he worked told him to take three months of leave with no pay, as a coronavirus epidemic takes a toll of China's businesses.

Description: Oil prices were near flat on Tuesday, pressured by concerns over the impact on crude demand from the coronavirus outbreak in China, but prices drew support from a reduction in supply from Libya.

Description: A group of unions and consumer groups wrote to U.S. antitrust enforcers on Tuesday to oppose a proposed remedy that could lead to U.S. approval for AbbVie Inc's  planned purchase of Allergan Plc .

Description: Virgin Galactic Holdings Inc  shares surged 24% on Tuesday, extending a rally since early December to over 400% and evoking a warning from an analyst who likes the space tourism company but warns it has become overbought.

Description: InterContinental Hotels (IHG) warned on Tuesday that fewer travellers are booking its rooms in China because of the coronavirus outbreak.

Description: Vodafone  and Telecom Italia (TIM)  have offered to give rivals access to some of their infrastructure for up to nine years to allay EU antitrust concerns over plans to merge their tower units, according to a document seen by Reuters.

Description: As investors crunch numbers to determine how the coronavirus will hit China’s economy, hedge fund manager Nathaniel Polachek has tied much of his outlook to the fate of a ship anchored near Weihai, China.

Description: When Kristin and Thomas Schmitt took out a mortgage and bought a house last summer, the German couple's dream looked as if it was coming true. Two months later, they learned that the tire factory where both work would be shut down early next year.

Description: JPMorgan  has shifted some of its top dealmakers to a newly-created executive committee of global chairs of investment banking to deepen ties with major clients and mentor the next generation of star bankers, two sources told Reuters.

Description: DuPont  has brought back management veteran Edward Breen as its chief executive officer, in a move that the industrial materials maker is hoping will help lift sluggish sales since its split from DowDuPont Inc.

Description: (This 17th Feb. story corrects final paragraph to "raised" not "valued")

Description: The French government will make sure the acquisition of Bombardier's train business by Alstom creates value for the European rail industry and the staff of both companies, Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Monday.

Description: By Christoph Steitz, Tom Käckenhoff, Arno Schuetze and Edward Taylor

Headlines: Chinese support measures buoy world stocks

Headlines: Mobile World Congress in Barcelona called off over coronavirus fears
Description: The Mobile World Congress (MWC), the annual telecoms industry gathering that draws more than 100,000 visitors to Barcelona, was canceled on Wednesday after a mass exodus by exhibitors due to fears over the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Hyundai bet big on China. Now coronavirus is twisting its supply chain
Description: South Korean car giant Hyundai Motor  has increasingly relied on China to supply auto parts to its manufacturing hub at home in recent years. As the coronavirus spreads, its strategy could be backfiring.

Headlines: UK's Domino's finds buyers for Norway business
Description: Britain's biggest pizza delivery company Domino's Pizza Group  said on Thursday it would sell its Norwegian business to existing minority shareholders of the business, kicking off the sale of its loss-making overseas operations.

Headlines: Qantas raises the stakes in pilot pay dispute
Description: Australia's Qantas Airways  has urged its pilots to reach agreement on a pay deal for the world's longest commercial flights or face being replaced for those routes.

Headlines: Turkey's Atlasglobal suspends flight operations: news websites
Description: Turkish airline Atlasglobal has decided to suspend all its operations and told its personnel not to come to work on Thursday, the aviation sector news website AirportHaber and other media reported.

Headlines: Elevator sale in focus in competitive process: Thyssenkrupp CFO
Description: A sale of Thyssenkrupp's  elevator division is currently in focus, the group's finance chief said on Thursday, adding an ongoing auction was "very competitive".

Headlines: Factbox: Nestle CEO Schneider's top deals
Description: Nestle Chief Executive Mark Schneider has made great strides in positioning the world's largest food company for the future with his aggressive deal-making since taking over in January 2017.

Headlines: Akzo Nobel targets rival-beating growth
Description: Dutch paints and coatings maker Akzo Nobel  aims to outpace its competitors' revenue growth in the coming years while lifting profitability, it said on Thursday.

Headlines: Japan's Asahi says Korean boycott cost it 3 billion yen last year
Description: Japanese beer and beverage maker Asahi Group Holdings  said a South Korean consumer boycott of Japanese goods cost it around 3 billion yen ($27.32 million) last year.

Headlines: Credit Suisse director Alexander Gut not to stand for re-election
Description: Credit Suisse supervisory board member Alexander Gut will not stand for re-election at the group's annual general meeting on April 30, the bank said alongside its annual results on Thursday.

Headlines: Airbus negotiating to win large preliminary order for A220 jets
Description: Airbus is negotiating a preliminary order for up to 100 A220 jets as it prepares to buy out Bombardier's  minority stake in the Canadian-designed jet, industry sources said.

Headlines: Mad cow fright keeps EU cautious on food rules
Description: The specter of the 1990s BSE crisis means the European Union is likely to reject U.S. demands it ease strict food safety rules, even with President Donald Trump threatening car tariffs if EU countries do not start importing more U.S. farm products.

Headlines: Hong Kong banks compare pandemic stress test with epidemic reality
Description: Last October, nearly four dozen banks in Hong Kong confronted a nightmare "stress test" scenario: a pandemic that swept through the city, followed by a major cyberattack and a telecoms breakdown.

Headlines: Wells Fargo ends forced arbitration for sexual harassment claims
Description: Wells Fargo & Co on Wednesday ended its forced arbitration policy for employee sexual harassment claims, opening the lender to potential lawsuits in the future.

Headlines: Australia court approves $10 billion Vodafone-TPG merger, overrules regulator
Description: An Australian court approved a A$15 billion ($10.1 billion) merger between a unit of Britain's Vodafone Group  and internet provider TPG Telecom  on Thursday, overruling a regulator and enabling a huge rival to the country's top telcos.

Headlines: Factbox: Vodafone-TPG merger advances in Australia after hiccups
Description: An Australian court on Thursday backed the A$15 billion ($10.1 billion) merger between TPG Telecom  and Vodafone's Australian joint venture   despite opposition from the country's competition regulator.

Headlines: Interest in private jets surges as coronavirus keeps airlines away from China
Description: A drop in airline flights from China and Hong Kong due to the coronavirus is increasing demand for private jets as wealthy passengers try to get out, executives say, but travel bans and nervous crew have kept that from translating to more business.

Headlines: Tesla seeks approval to build longer range Model 3s in China
Description: Tesla Inc is seeking approval from Chinese regulators to offer a new China-made Model 3 variant, a government document shows.

Headlines: Bezos buys Warner Estate in Beverly Hills for record $165 million
Description: Amazon Chief Executive Jeff Bezos, the world's wealthiest person, has purchased a Beverly Hills mansion known as the Warner Estate from media mogul David Geffen for $165 million, a source familiar with the deal said on Wednesday.

Headlines: SoftBank profit wiped out by Vision Fund losses, second fund scaled back
Description: Quarterly profit at SoftBank Group Corp  was almost wiped out as the Japanese technology giant was hit for a second straight quarter by losses at its $100 billion Vision Fund.

Headlines: Raytheon discloses SEC subpoena related to payments by Thales JV in Middle East
Description: Raytheon has received a subpoena from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission related to an investigation into the possibility of improper payments made for contracts in certain Middle East countries since 2014, the U.S. weapons maker disclosed in a filing https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1047122/000104712220000009/rtn-12312019x10k.htm on Wednesday.

Headlines: U.S. lawmaker calls for ouster of CalPERS CIO over China ties: letter
Description: A U.S. Republican lawmaker on Wednesday urged California to fire the chief investment officer of its public pension fund, the nation's largest, citing what he called the CIO's "long and cozy" relationship with Beijing, and assailed the fund's investments in Chinese companies.

Headlines: Juul bought ad space on kids' websites, including Cartoon Network: lawsuit
Description: E-cigarette maker Juul Labs Inc bought online advertisements on teen-focused websites for Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network and Seventeen magazine after it launched its product in 2015, according to a lawsuit filed on Wednesday by the Massachusetts attorney general's office.

Headlines: Despite $1 trillion deficits, Trump tax cuts will still 'pay for themselves': Mnuchin
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin insisted on Wednesday that President Donald Trump's tax cuts will still pay for themselves over 10 years, even as the administration forecasts near-term deficits close to $1 trillion.

Headlines: Pentagon expected to back additional Huawei restrictions: source
Description: The Pentagon is likely to back new U.S. restrictions on Huawei Technologies, reversing earlier opposition to a proposal meant to further crack down on exports to the blacklisted Chinese company, a person briefed on the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Thyssenkrupp-Kone elevator merger would trigger legal war - Schindler
Description: Swiss elevator maker Schindler  would embark on an all-out antitrust offensive in the courts to stall any deal to combine Thyssenkrupp's  lift division with rival Kone , board member Alfred Schindler told Reuters.

Headlines: MGM Resorts CEO Jim Murren to step down before contract ends
Description: MGM Resorts International's  Chief Executive Officer Jim Murren will step down before completing his contract, the U.S. casino operator said on Wednesday.

Headlines: MGM Resorts withdraws 2020 financial targets on coronavirus hit
Description: MGM Resorts International  withdrew its forecast for 2020 on Wednesday, as it assesses the fallout of the coronavirus epidemic on its business.

Headlines: Fed Chair Powell: 'no reason' rising wages, job gains can't continue
Description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Wednesday reiterated his confidence in the U.S. economic outlook, even as he said he expected some drag "soon" from China's new coronavirus epidemic and called out the threat from income inequality and an expanding federal debt.

Headlines: Stocks gain as China says fewer new coronavirus cases
Description: Global equity markets scaled fresh highs on Wednesday after China reported the lowest number of new coronavirus cases in two weeks, boosting hopes the epidemic will be contained and driving up the price of commodities sensitive to Chinese demand.

Headlines: Oil rises over 3% as demand worries ease amid fewer new coronavirus cases
Description: Oil prices rose over 3% on Wednesday as China reported its lowest daily number of new coronavirus cases since late January, stoking investor hopes that fuel demand in the world's second-largest oil consumer may begin to recover.

Headlines: Nestle bets on shark tank, startups and students to boost innovation
Description: Food giant Nestle  has set up new structures to turn innovative ideas from outside and inside the company into new products, its technology head told journalists on Wednesday ahead of the publication of the group's full-year results.

Headlines: U.S. judge drops some charges against Theranos's Holmes, leaves wire fraud
Description: A federal judge late on Tuesday dismissed some charges against Theranos Inc founder Elizabeth Holmes, but let stand wire fraud charges accusing her and an associate of misleading patients about the abilities of her company's blood tests.

Headlines: Insurance comparison firm SelectQuote taps banks for IPO: sources
Description: SelectQuote has hired investment banks for an initial public offering (IPO) that could value the owner of the eponymous insurance policy comparison website at more than $2 billion, including debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Alstom board to discuss buying Bombardier rail unit: sources
Description: Alstom's  board will meet late on Wednesday to discuss buying Bombardier's  rail unit, sources familiar with the matter said, and a media report said the French train maker had valued the business at just under $7 billion.

Headlines: Boeing unlikely to hit pre-grounding output targets for 737 MAX before 2022
Description: Boeing Co  is unlikely, for several years, to hit the monthly 57-unit production rate it had targeted for the 737 MAX preceding the grounding of the jet due to delays in regulatory approval, Chief Financial Officer Greg Smith said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Softbank's Vision Fund 2 stalls as key backers opt out
Description: Big investors who are critical to SoftBank Group's plans for a second massive technology investment fund are refusing to take part unless the first $100 billion Vision Fund can turn around its performance, sources familiar with the talks told Reuters.

Headlines: SoftBank executive flags some 50 'winners' in $100 billion Vision Fund
Description: SoftBank Vision Fund has around 50 winners in its $100 billion portfolio and a dozen or more companies could pursue listings over the next 18 months, Rajeev Misra, chief executive of SoftBank Investment Advisers, said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Mexico's America Movil to focus on bringing 5G to Latin America
Description: America Movil, Mexico's largest telecommunications provider, shed light on its plans to roll out 5G technology in Latin America on Wednesday as the company's shares surged on a strong earnings report.

Headlines: Fed's Powell reinforces regulation and defends repo support in letter to Congress
Description: U.S. central bank officials are considering options that would make it easier for banks to treat Treasury holdings similar to reserves when meeting liquidity requirements, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said this week in a letter to a top Senate Democrat.

Headlines: Bed Bath & Beyond's gloomy sales indicate tough turnaround ahead
Description: Shares of Bed Bath & Beyond Inc  were on pace for their worst day ever on Wednesday, as disappointing sales numbers  raised concerns on Wall Street that the retailer's turnaround would take longer and be much tougher than anticipated.

Headlines: BP boss Looney sets out to 'reinvent' oil giant with zero carbon goal
Description: BP set one of the oil sector's most ambitious targets for curbing carbon emissions on Wednesday as new chief executive Bernard Looney began the biggest revamp in its 111-year history.

Headlines: Shopify hits record high on better-than-expected 2020 sales forecast
Description: Canadian e-commerce company Shopify Inc's     full-year revenue forecast above analysts' estimates and  better-than-expected quarterly earnings on higher holiday sales, pushed its shares to a record high on Wednesday.

Headlines: Boeing sees airline profits hit, stagnant freight due to virus
Description: Airlines are facing a fall in profits as the coronavirus crisis hits passenger demand and prolongs weakness in economically sensitive air freight, planemaker Boeing  warned on Wednesday.

Headlines: New coronavirus: what markets should watch now
Description: World markets started shrugging off the worst of the coronavirus impact last week and stock markets have since reached record highs. China's announcement that new cases of the so-called COVID-19 detected on Tuesday were at their lowest since Jan 30 has only consolidated those gains.

Headlines: A stock and a hard place: SoftBank's $150 billion Alibaba warchest in spotlight
Description: SoftBank  CEO Masayoshi Son threw cold water on Wednesday on the idea of cutting his firm's $150 billion stake in e-commerce giant Alibaba , after prominent activist investor Elliott Management called for big buybacks.

Headlines: Shareholder activists test JPMorgan's Dimon on climate proposals
Description: Shareholder activists focused on climate issues vowed to press proxy battles with JPMorgan Chase & Co  after getting a cold reception from the top Wall Street bank, even though Chief Executive Jamie Dimon has vowed to protect the environment.

Headlines: Spanish health authorities say no reason to cancel Mobile World Congress
Description: Spanish health officials said on Wednesday there was no reason to cancel the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona over coronavirus fears, despite major companies pulling out of the event.

Headlines: Airbus unveils 'blended wing body' plane design after secret flight tests
Description: Airbus  on Tuesday unveiled a curvaceous aircraft design that blends wing and body, designed to slash carbon emissions by some 20%.

Description: Airbus SE  is confident of selling more than 1,000 A321XLR aircraft, a longer-range version of the single-aisle A321neo jetliner, over the next 10 years, a senior executive at the manufacturer said on Tuesday.

Description: Chemicals giant BASF  on Wednesday picked a site in the eastern German state of Brandenburg for its second European battery materials factory, part of a 400 million euro investment plan to tap into the growing electric vehicle market.

Description: Gucci-owner Kering has temporarily shut half of its stores in China, and shelved new openings and advertising campaigns there,  as the coronavirus outbreak throws luxury brands into turmoil.

Description: Nissan Motor Co  could be heading for its first quarterly loss in more than a decade, three company sources said on Wednesday, as news emerged the Japanese carmaker is seeking $91 million in damages from ousted former boss Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: Telecoms group Orange to also pull out from Mobile World Congress: source
Description: French telecoms group Orange  has also decided to pull out of the Mobile World Congress telecoms event in Barcelona due to concerns over the coronavirus, said a source close to the matter on Wednesday.

Headlines: Britain's BT pulls out of Mobile World Congress
Description: Britain's biggest telecoms group BT  said on Wednesday it was pulling out of the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona because of the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Telecoms lobby to discuss Barcelona congress on Wednesday: source
Description: Telecoms industry lobby GSMA will hold a virtual board meeting on Wednesday to discuss a major conference later this month which is looking increasingly threatened by fears of coronavirus, a person with knowledge of the matter said.

Headlines: We're monitoring coronavirus, say organizers of Barcelona telecoms meet

Headlines: Kering frustrated with slow progress in cosmetics development

Headlines: Airbus Helicopters signs order from Royal Thai Air Force

Description: Food retailer Ahold Delhaize  met forecasts with a 3% rise in fourth-quarter core earnings on Wednesday helped by its Food Lion and Hannaford U.S. grocery chains and strong online sales.

Headlines: Heineken sees more profit growth in final year for long-serving CEO
Description: Heineken , the world's second largest brewer, forecast lower barley and aluminum costs would help to boost profits this year, when its long-serving chief executive will step down.

Description: Nissan Motor Co  may report its first quarterly loss in more than a decade on Thursday because of slumping sales, sources familiar with the company said, adding more pressure on efforts to rebuild the company after Carlos Ghosn's ouster.

Headlines: JPMorgan appoints new heads of Australia and NZ investment banking

Headlines: Sainsbury's Bank chairman Davis to step down

Description: JPMorgan  has been picked as an adviser for the sale of a stake in a $7.3 billion motorway in Turkey, four sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: 'Everyone is guessing' about coronavirus economic impacts, say experts

Description: Clariant  Chief Financial Officer Patrick Jany is exiting for a post at Maersk , the world's biggest shipping company, marking the latest management change at the Swiss speciality chemicals maker after its CEO jumped ship last year.

Headlines: SoftBank stock surges to seven-month high after judge OKs Sprint-T-Mobile merger
Description: SoftBank Group Corp  stock surged to its highest price in over half a year in Tokyo on Wednesday, after a U.S. federal judge rejected an antitrust challenge to the proposed takeover of subsidiary Sprint Corp  by T-Mobile US Inc .

Headlines: FAA agrees it must boost safety oversight for Southwest Airlines
Description: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it should have done a better job of ensuring Southwest Airlines Co  had certified completion of maintenance on 88 used Boeing 737 jets, as noted in a report by the U.S. Transportation Department's Inspector General released on Tuesday.

Headlines: Bankers in Asia brace for a virus-related deal drought
Description: Bankers in Asia are bracing for a deal drought as efforts to limit the spread of the coronavirus epidemic have put key meetings and roadshows on hold.

Headlines: S&P 500, Nasdaq eke out new closing highs
Description: S&P 500 and the Nasdaq inched to their second consecutive record closing highs on Tuesday as Chinese officials said the deadly coronavirus epidemic could be contained by April.

Headlines: Hyundai signs development deal with another electric vehicle startup
Description: Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Co broadened its future transportation portfolio with an agreement to jointly develop electric vehicles with California startup Canoo, the companies said on Tuesday.

Headlines: NY attorney general considers appealing ruling OK'ing Sprint T-Mobile merger
Description: New York Attorney General Letitia James said Tuesday the state may appeal a court ruling approving a merger between No.3 and No.4 wireless carriers T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp.

Headlines: Exclusive: JPMorgan in talks to merge blockchain unit Quorum with startup ConsenSys - sources
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co is in talks to merge its marquee blockchain unit Quorum with Brooklyn-based startup ConsenSys, according to people familiar with the plans.

Headlines: China c.bank gives green light to Mastercard's China JV for clearing business
Description: China's central bank said on Tuesday it has approved an application by Mastercard's China joint venture to conduct bank card clearing operations in the country.

Headlines: Airbnb swings to a loss as costs climb: WSJ
Description: Home rentals giant Airbnb Inc swung to a loss for the first nine months of last year as costs climbed sharply, The Wall Street Journal reported https://www.wsj.com/articles/airbnb-swings-to-a-loss-as-costs-climb-ahead-of-ipo-11581443123?mod=searchresults&page=1&pos=1 on Tuesday, citing people close to the company.

Description: PayPal Holdings Inc  is teaming up with criminologists and experts at several universities to probe the payment systems used in the trafficking of illegal firearms in the United States, the company said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Merkel's conservatives stop short of Huawei 5G ban in Germany

Headlines: Exclusive: Argentina's Aerolineas to add new flights to New York and Madrid - chairman
Description: Aerolineas Argentinas will add new flights to New York and Madrid as the government-controlled carrier seeks to ramp up sales outside its home country and boost income in an effort to beat back persistent operating losses.

Headlines: Tesla driver in fatal crash had reported problems before with 'Autopilot' feature

Description: President Donald Trump reiterated his criticism that the Federal Reserve has kept interest rates too high and seemed to say the U.S. central bank's chair, Jerome Powell, had hurt stock prices during his testimony to Congress on Tuesday.

Headlines: German conservative lawmakers back compromise on 5G: sources
Description: Lawmakers from German Chancellor Angela Merkel's ruling conservatives have backed a position paper on 5G mobile networks that recommends tougher rules on foreign vendors while stopping short of banning China's Huawei, sources said.

Headlines: Finland's Supercell reports sales up 2% while core earnings slip

Headlines: IKEA new CEO targets 'even more affordable' furniture as habits shift
Description: IKEA named insider Jon Abrahamsson Ring to succeed Torbjorn Loof as chief executive of the world's biggest furniture brand on Tuesday as it adapts to seismic shifts in shopping.

Headlines: U.S. federal judge allows merger between T-Mobile and Sprint

Headlines: Exclusive: Deutsche Bank taps U.S. tech companies for makeover - sources
Description: Deutsche Bank has invited bids from Microsoft, Google and Amazon to overhaul the German bank's outdated and fragmented technology networks, people with knowledge of the matter said.

Headlines: FAA says approaching 737 MAX test flight, awaits Boeing proposals

Headlines: Lloyd's of London sets up independent group to improve culture
