Description: Shares of Beyond Meat rose as much as 16% on Wednesday after Canada's Restaurant Brands International Inc's coffee chain Tim Hortons said it will introduce three new sandwiches using the vegan burger marker's plant-based sausages

Headlines: French fashion group Kering pledges to hire only over-18 models
Description: Kering, the French fashion group whose brands include Gucci and Saint Laurent, said it would only work with models aged over 18, as the fashion industry aims to tighten up its ethical guidelines.

Headlines: U.S. tariffs against Airbus would harm Delta: airline official
Description: U.S. imposition of tariffs against the European Union over aircraft subsidies would cause "serious harm" to Delta Air Lines since the U.S. carrier is already under contract to buy several billion dollars worth of Airbus aircraft, a senior airline official said on Wednesday.

Headlines: No easy options for China as trade war, U.S. pressure bite
Description: China is running out of options to hit back at the United States without hurting its own interests, as Washington intensifies pressure on Beijing to correct trade imbalances in a challenge to China's state-led economic model.

Headlines: Mnuchin says China trade talks likely to continue in Beijing
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Wednesday he will likely travel to Beijing soon to continue negotiations with Chinese counterparts as the world's two biggest economies try to salvage talks aimed at ending their months-long trade war.

Headlines: Ubisoft's fourth quarter misses company's expectations
Description: French video game producer Ubisoft on Wednesday reported fourth-quarter net bookings of 676.7 million euros, below company's expectations of approximately 698.0 million euros.

Headlines: Exclusive: Tesla's solar factory is exporting most of its cells - document
Description: The "great majority" of solar cells being produced at Tesla Inc's factory in upstate New York are being sold overseas instead of being used in the company's trademark "Solar Roof" as originally intended, according to documents reviewed by Reuters.

Headlines: Brazil's Embraer posts quarterly loss due to fewer plane deliveries
Description: Embraer SA reported a $42.5 million loss for the first quarter on Wednesday, its fifth straight quarter of losses, as revenue fell amid fewer plane deliveries and as the Brazilian planemaker spent heavily ahead of a deal with Boeing Co.

Headlines: U.S. close to resolving steel, aluminum tariffs with Canada, Mexico: reports
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin on Wednesday said the United States is close to resolving steel and aluminum tariffs with Canada and Mexico, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Headlines: Tencent profit tops forecast as fintech and cloud revenues surge
Description: Tencent Holdings Ltd posted record quarterly profit on Wednesday, smashing market expectations, as the social media and gaming giant booked a rise in the value of its investments while fintech and cloud revenues helped make up for declines in games.

Headlines: Ford to build more Lincolns for Chinese market locally: CFO
Description: Ford Motor Co plans to start production of new luxury Lincoln models in China for that market as they are launched, starting with the new Corsair later this year, to benefit from lower costs and avoid the risk of tariffs, a top executive said on Monday.

Headlines: Russia says it may sell contaminated oil at a discount: Ifx
Description: Russia may sell contaminated oil at a discount, Energy Minister Alexander Novak was quoted as saying on Wednesday by Interfax news agency.

Headlines: U.S. business inventories unchanged; sales surge
Description: U.S. business inventories were unchanged in March as sales increased by the most in more than two years, which could ease concerns of a broad build-up in inventories in the economy.

Headlines: Macy's CEO says recent tariffs to impact furniture business
Description: Macy's Inc said on Wednesday the recent hike in U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods will hurt its furniture business of the department store operator.

Headlines: U.S. factory output drops for third time in four months
Description: Declining output of cars and machinery led U.S. factory production to fall unexpectedly in April, a sign the economy is losing a step as a trade war with China intensifies.

Headlines: Fears of flying Boeing’s 737 MAX won’t get in way of price conscious ticket shoppers: Reuters/IPSOS poll
Description: U.S. fliers still consider ticket prices the most important factor when choosing a flight, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll, suggesting two fatal crashes of Boeing Co 737 MAX jets have had little impact on consumer sentiment.

Headlines: JPMorgan Chase will invest $125 million in programs to encourage people to save money
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co will provide $125 million over the next five years to nonprofit groups in the United States and abroad that help people save, pay down debt and improve their credit scores, the bank said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Nissan set for weakest profit in 11 years as Ghosn woes, bleak sales weigh
Description: Nissan Motor Co forecast a 28% plunge in its annual operating profit, putting it on course for the weakest earnings in 11 years and underscoring its struggle to turn the page after former Chairman Carlos Ghosn was ousted.

Headlines: Exclusive: Trump expected to sign order paving way for U.S. telecoms ban on Huawei
Description: President Donald Trump is expected to sign an executive order this week barring U.S. companies from using telecommunications equipment made by firms posing a national security risk, paving the way for a ban on doing business with China's Huawei, three U.S. officials familiar with the plan told Reuters.

Headlines: China's retail sales growth slumps to 16-year low as trade war risks rise
Description: China reported surprisingly weaker growth in retail sales and industrial output for April on Wednesday, adding pressure on Beijing to roll out more stimulus as the trade war with the United States escalates.

Headlines: China says it will support firms in boosting R&D spending
Description: China will support firms in boosting their spending on research and development, state television cited the cabinet as saying on Wednesday.

Headlines: Walmart mulls stock market listing for UK arm Asda
Description: Walmart, the world's biggest retailer, said it is considering a stock market listing for its British supermarket arm Asda, whose attempt to combine with rival Sainsbury's was blocked by the UK regulator last month.

Headlines: IKEA says in final stages of talks to invest in Northvolt
Description: IKEA is in the final stages of talks with Northvolt about participating in the battery startup's fundraising for a factory, the world's biggest furniture retailer said on Wednesday.

Headlines: SoftBank leads $200 million investment in India's Grofers
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp has led an investment round of more than $200 million in online grocery startup Grofers India through its Vision Fund, the New Delhi-based company said on Wednesday, upping competition in a hotly chased market in the country.

Headlines: Rising U.S. oil output helps fill gap left by Iran, Venezuela: IEA
Description: The world will require very little extra oil from OPEC this year as booming U.S. output will offset falling exports from Iran and Venezuela, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.

Headlines: China says it is only taking actions in self defense in U.S. trade dispute
Description: China's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday the United States was defining the two countries' dispute over trade as a trade war, and China was only taking action in self-defense.

Headlines: Trump calls trade war with China 'little squabble,' says talks ongoing
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday called the trade war with China "a little squabble" and insisted talks between the world's two largest economies had not collapsed, as investors remained on guard for a further escalation of tit-for-tat tariffs.

Headlines: WhatsApp security breach may have targeted human rights groups
Description: WhatsApp said on Tuesday that a security breach on its messaging app had signs of coming from a government using surveillance technology developed by a private company, and it may have targeted human rights groups.

Headlines: WhatsApp informs Irish regulator of 'serious security vulnerability'
Description: Facebook's WhatsApp has informed its lead regulator in the European Union, Ireland's Data Protection Commissioner (DPC), of a serious security vulnerability on its platform, the DPC said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Startups target banks' small business customers in FX payments drive
Description: Revolut and TransferWise are signing up thousands of small businesses a month for foreign exchange payments, touting slicker service and lower fees as they try to take on banks in a sector with flows of $7 trillion a year.

Headlines: Uber drivers are contractors, not employees, U.S. labor agency says
Description: Drivers for ride-hailing company Uber Technologies Inc are independent contractors and not employees, the general counsel of a U.S. labor agency has concluded, in an advisory memo that is likely to carry significant weight in a pending case against the company and could prevent drivers from joining a union.

Headlines: Nissan faces long, rocky road to cut U.S. discounts, rental sales
Description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had hit "rock bottom" with a 45% drop in annual operating profit. The automaker's troubles in the United States, including a failure to deliver on a slew of promises to dealers, are a major reason why.

Headlines: U.S. growth would have contracted without trillions in government, consumer debt: Gundlach
Description: U.S. growth appears to be based "exclusively" on government, corporate and mortgage debt and the economy would have contracted if the United States had not added trillions in debt, Jeffrey Gundlach, chief executive of DoubleLine Capital, said in an investor webcast on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. to take 'fresh look' at opening automakers' key spectrum band
Description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission plans to vote in June on launching a new review of a key spectrum band reserved for automakers that could boost Wi-Fi use, a person briefed on the matter said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Google to push new ads on its apps to snare shoppers
Description: Whether you are Googling on the couch, fiddling with Maps in the car or swiping through the Discover feed on the toilet, expect Alphabet Inc's Google to put ads in several new spots this year.

Headlines: Stocks bounce back as trade rhetoric cools
Description: U.S. stocks on Tuesday reclaimed some of the ground lost in the prior day's steep sell-off, with tariff-sensitive technology stocks leading the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq higher as investors were heartened by a tonal shift in U.S.-China trade rhetoric.

Headlines: Global stocks bounce back as Trump downplays U.S.-China trade fight
Description: U.S. and European stocks regained ground on Tuesday after President Donald Trump downplayed the U.S.-China trade war as "a little squabble" a day after a spike in tensions between the world's two largest economies rattled financial markets.

Headlines: Disney takes control of Hulu to challenge Netflix, Amazon
Description: Walt Disney Co said it will take full control of the Hulu service in a deal with Comcast Corp, as it vies for a bigger piece of the global video streaming market dominated by companies such as Netflix Inc.

Headlines: U.S. Treasury chief to plan for trade meeting in China soon: spokesman
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin will plan for another trade meeting in China at some point soon, a Treasury spokesman said on Tuesday, adding to President Donald Trump's earlier statements that U.S. dialogue with Beijing was continuing.

Headlines: U.S. Senate moves forward on plan to develop electric vehicle supply chain
Description: U.S. lawmakers on Tuesday moved closer to developing a national electric vehicle supply chain policy, with senators voicing bipartisan support for legislation designed to parry China's dominance in metals production and battery manufacturing.

Headlines: Bayer nears seven-year low after $2 billion award in Roundup trial
Description: Bayer shares fell by as much as 5 percent on Tuesday after a California couple were awarded more than $2 billion in the largest U.S. jury penalty over allegations its Roundup weed killer causes cancer.

Headlines: Factbox: More Roundup trials, appeals in store for Bayer after $2 billion verdict
Description: Bayer shares continued to fall on Tuesday after a California jury on Monday awarded more than $2 billion in damages to a couple who alleged that the company's glyphosate-based weed killer Roundup caused their cancers.

Headlines: Nissan earnings slide fuels Renault deal pressure
Description: Renault is quietly pushing for a change of Nissan leadership as a prelude to merger talks, sources at both companies said, after the Japanese carmaker warned of a further earnings slide in the wake of the Carlos Ghosn scandal.

Headlines: Oil prices rise over 1% on drone attack on Saudi Aramco facilities
Description: Oil prices rose over 1% on Tuesday after top exporter Saudi Arabia said explosive-laden drones launched by a Yemeni-armed movement aligned to Iran had attacked facilities belonging to state oil company Aramco.

Headlines: Senate Majority Leader McConnell says 'nobody wins a trade war'
Description: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said on Tuesday that "nobody wins a trade war" but he hoped President Donald Trump's tactics in negotiations China would put the United States in a better position to move trade talks forward with Beijing.

Headlines: Exclusive: UniCredit advances toward bid for Germany's Commerzbank – sources
Description: UniCredit has stepped up preparations for a potential bid for Germany's Commerzbank by drafting in investment bankers including a former top German official, three people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Rapid bitcoin rally cheers crypto market investors, others wary
Description: Bitcoin hit its highest level in 10 months on Tuesday, raising hopes among cryptocurrency enthusiasts of greater mainstream acceptance as an escalating U.S.-China trade war roiled global markets, but others urged investor caution.

Headlines: Walmart fights back against Amazon with one-day shipping in some U.S. markets
Description: Walmart Inc is stepping up its battle with Amazon.com Inc by offering one-day delivery without a shipping fee, weeks after Amazon announced a similar offer - a move that will intensify the race to deliver orders to shoppers faster.

Headlines: Carrefour and TerraCycle launch 'Loop' test in Paris to tackle waste
Description: French retailer Carrefour and U.S. waste recycling company TerraCycle launched on Tuesday the test for their 'Loop' initiative which they hope will tackle the problems of plastic waste threatening to destroy the environment.

Headlines: OPEC sees more 2019 demand for its oil as it keeps cutting output
Description: OPEC said on Tuesday that world demand for its oil would be higher than expected this year as supply growth from rivals including U.S. shale producers slows, pointing to a tighter market if the exporter group refrains from raising output.

Headlines: GE books more power plant orders, beats Mitsubishi, Siemens: sources
Description: General Electric Co won the most orders in the sharply contracting market for new gas-fired power plants in the first quarter, according to people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Huawei willing to sign 'no-spy' pacts with governments: chairman
Description: Huawei  is willing to sign no-spy agreements with governments, including Britain, the Chinese telco company's chairman said on Tuesday, amid U.S. pressure on European countries to shun the firm over espionage concerns.

Headlines: Britain downplays Huawei threat to U.S. intelligence sharing
Description: Britain would never take a decision on Huawei and 5G that would threaten its intelligence sharing alliance with the United States but it also does not want a new Cold War with China, Foreign Secretary Jeremy Hunt said on Tuesday.

Headlines: ChargePoint sounds alarm on electric vehicle charging standards
Description: A leading operator of charging stations has sounded the alarm on a proposed technical standard that it says could hamper mass adoption of electric vehicles by making it harder to charge them at home or at work.

Headlines: ConocoPhillips will not chase expensive Permian deals, CEO says
Description: ConocoPhillips Chief Executive Officer Ryan Lance on Tuesday repeated a pledge to restrain spending, saying the U.S. oil producer would not be drawn into pricey mergers and acquisitions.

Headlines: VOI makes European push in crowded electric scooter-sharing market
Description: Sweden's VOI Technology plans to put a new fleet of thousands of electric scooters on European streets this summer to fend off competition in an increasingly crowded market.

Headlines: Volkswagen wins worker backing for restructuring with $1.1 billion battery plan
Description: Volkswagen workers backed a restructuring of the world's largest carmaker on Tuesday after Chief Executive Herbert Diess pledged to spend 1 billion euros ($1.1 billion) on a new battery cell production plant near its headquarters in Lower Saxony.

Headlines: Boeing deliveries hammered by 737 MAX groundings
Description: Boeing Co handed over 24 percent fewer jet airplanes in the first four months of 2019 compared with the same period a year earlier as the grounding of its top-selling 737 MAX aircraft halted deliveries for a second month.

Headlines: Ralph Lauren's North America woes cloud profit beat, shares down nearly 8%
Description: Luxury apparel maker Ralph Lauren Corp beat Wall Street estimates for quarterly profit on Tuesday, benefiting from higher demand in international markets, but weak sales in its biggest market, North America, disappointed investors.

Headlines: Trump says U.S.-China trade talks have not collapsed
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said trade talks with China had not collapsed, characterizing the trade war between the world's two largest economies as "a little squabble."

Headlines: No sign that Beijing will offer a no-spy deal: Germany
Description: There is no sign that China is offering a "no-spy" agreement of the kind that would help telecommunications equipment maker Huawei in its bid for contracts to build Germany's next-generation mobile networks, a German Interior Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Cash-rich Canadian oil firms favor buybacks as other options narrow
Description: Canadian oil producers are raking in the highest revenues in five years thanks to strong global oil prices and Alberta's production cuts, but government intervention has hamstrung their spending abilities, encouraging many to buy back shares and pay down debt.

Headlines: Mexico's rising oil nationalism faces debt-rating crisis
Description: Mexican President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador took office in December vowing to revive state-owned energy company Pemex and put the brakes on foreign investment to give the public a bigger cut of the country's oil wealth.

Headlines: India's Jet Airways sees management exodus as rescue hopes dim
Description: The chief executive and two other senior figures at Jet Airways have quit, the Indian company said on Tuesday, further eroding any hopes of a rescue of the debt-laden carrier that grounded operations last month.

Headlines: U.S. leaves rare earths, critical minerals off China tariff list
Description: The United States has again decided not to impose tariffs on rare earths and other critical minerals from China, underscoring its reliance on the Asian nation for a group of materials used in everything from consumer electronics to military equipment.

Headlines: Oil prices jump on drone attack on Saudi Aramco facilities
Description: Oil prices rose on Tuesday after top exporter Saudi Arabia said explosive-laden drones launched by a Yemeni armed movement aligned to Iran had attacked facilities belonging to state oil company Aramco.

Headlines: JPMorgan says UK PM May unlikely to survive beyond the end of June
Description: U.S. investment bank JPMorgan said on Tuesday it was difficult to see British Prime Minister Theresa May surviving beyond the end of June.

Headlines: Trump defends China trade battle, vows deal will happen
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday defended his trade war with China as tensions escalated and markets extended their losses, promising a deal with Chinese President Xi Jinping soon, even as fears escalated about a protracted battle.

Headlines: India delays levying retaliatory tariff on U.S. goods to June 16
Description: India delayed on Tuesday the implementation of higher tariffs on some goods imported from the United States to June 16, according to a government statement.

Headlines: PG&E proposes court order for CEO, board to tour town destroyed by wildfire
Description: PG&E Corp on Monday submitted a proposed order to a U.S. District Court judge that would require the power provider's chief executive and board to visit the California town of Paradise by July 15, to see the destruction caused by a wildfire in November that may be linked to the company's equipment.

Headlines: Factbox: Tariff wars - duties imposed by Trump and U.S. trading partners
Description: China on Monday raised tariffs on $60 billion of U.S. goods in retaliation for President Donald Trump's decision to increase tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese imports last week, escalating the trade war between the world's two largest economies.

Headlines: China says it hopes U.S. does not underestimate its determination
Description: China's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that it hopes the United States does not underestimate its determination to protect its interests, even as Washington threatened to extend tariffs to virtually all Chinese imports.

Headlines: U.S. LNG companies Cheniere and Tellurian see U.S.-China trade spat as short term
Description: Executives from U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG) companies Cheniere Energy and Tellurian on Tuesday said they view the trade dispute between China and the United States as temporary, with no major impact on their ability to sell LNG.

Headlines: Saudi Aramco bets on oil supply to Europe, trading expansion
Description: Saudi Aramco aims to boost its oil supply to Europe by 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) within the next two years as it expands its trading operations there with an office opening this summer in London, a senior company executive said.

Headlines: Iran insists on ramping up oil sales to stay in nuclear pact: sources
Description: Iran insists on exporting at least 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil, triple May's expected levels under U.S. sanctions, as a condition for staying in an international nuclear deal, sources with knowledge of Iran-EU talks said.

Headlines: Record level of funds hedge against stocks fall: BAML survey
Description: Global investors' equity allocations fell 6 percentage points in May and over a third of fund managers have taken out protection against sharp stock market falls in coming months, Bank of America Merrill Lynch's latest monthly survey found on Tuesday.

Headlines: Fed's Williams says policymakers need to better prepare for lower interest rate world
Description: Torturously slow recoveries from recessions and low inflation are here to stay unless policymakers can get a better grip on how to stabilize the global economy in an era of lower interest rates, a top Federal Reserve policymaker said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Fed's Williams says tariffs boost U.S. inflation, weigh on growth
Description: Tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on Chinese goods in the escalating trade war between the two countries will boost U.S. inflation and could dampen economic growth, a top Federal Reserve policymaker said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs bought Commerzbank's claim in Saudi's biggest debt saga: sources
Description: Goldman Sachs has bought a claim against The International Bank Corporation (TIBC), a Bahraini bank whose default 10 years ago triggered the biggest financial crisis in Saudi Arabia, three sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: EU regulators to investigate Insurance Ireland data pooling system
Description: EU antitrust regulators opened an investigation on Tuesday into Insurance Ireland's data pooling system, concerned that conditions set by the association to access the system may block rivals in violation of EU competition rules.

Headlines: Huawei is not controlled by China, executive says
Description: Huawei is a private company that is not controlled by the Chinese government and would refuse to hand over information to Beijing although no such request has been made, the firm's Vice President of Western Europe said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Volkswagen will use Traton proceeds to internationalize truck business: CEO
Description: Volkswagen will use proceeds of an initial public offering of its Traton trucks unit to invest in the "internationalization" of the division, Chief Executive Officer Herbert Diess said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Starbucks, Mercon announce separate sustainability loans
Description: Starbucks and Mercon Coffee Group separately announced sustainability-focused loan facilities on Monday, signaling the coffee sector's growing emphasis on sustainability as climate change and low global prices threaten the future of the crop.

Headlines: Members only: U.S. retailers revamp loyalty schemes for Amazon era
Description: With private fitting rooms, members-only stores and clever apps, U.S. department stores are reinventing their old and tested loyalty programs to fend off the challenge from e-commerce giant Amazon.com Inc and other online rivals.

Headlines: Trump and Xi to meet after defiant China hits U.S. with new tariffs
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he would meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next month as the trade war between the world's two largest economies intensified, sending shivers through global markets.

Headlines: Trump says U.S. farmers to get $15 billion in aid amid China trade war
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration was planning to provide about $15 billion in aid to help U.S. farmers whose products may be targeted with tariffs by China in a deepening trade war.

Headlines: British telco giant Vodafone offloads NZ business to Brookfield, Infratil
Description: Vodafone Group Plc on Monday agreed to sell its New Zealand business for NZ$3.4 billion ($2.23 billion) to a consortium comprising of New Zealand-based Infratil Ltd and Canada's Brookfield Asset Management, in a deal the telecom giant says would help reduce its debt.

Headlines: Tokyo prosecutors detail Ghosn's alleged cash transfer in revised indictment: Kyodo
Description: Tokyo prosecutors have filed a request to revise the content of their indictment of Carlos Ghosn for aggravated breach of trust, providing further details on alleged cash transfers involving the former Nissan boss and a Saudi friend, Kyodo news reported.

Headlines: Japan Finmin Aso: Sino-U.S. trade war won't trigger economic crisis
Description: Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said on Tuesday the Sino-U.S. trade war would not immediately trigger an economic shock on the scale of the "Lehman shock", though the friction between the world's two largest economies is unlikely to be resolved easily.

Headlines: Trump says he feels U.S.-China trade talks 'going to be very successful'
Description: President Donald Trump said on Monday he was optimistic about resolving the U.S. trade dispute with China.

Headlines: What's at stake for Europe Inc in a trade spat with Washington
Description: Europe's listed companies are expected to generate 1.2 trillion euros (£1.04 trillion) in revenue from the United States this year, highlighting what's at stake as global trade tensions grow and earnings and economic growth stall.

Headlines: Cellphones and laptops on latest USTR China tariff list, drugs excluded
Description: A list of products subject to possible U.S. tariffs on about $300 billion of Chinese imports will include cellphones and laptop computers but not pharmaceuticals and rare earth materials, the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said on Monday.

Headlines: Long fight over error in JPMorgan loan to GM settles for $231 million
Description: Lenders and hundreds of investors agreed on Monday to pay $231 million to end their decade-long legal fight over a clerical error in a $1.5 billion loan to General Motors that was administered by JPMorgan Chase & Co , according to court documents.

Headlines: Amazon extends lead as top retail brand in Kantar/WPP survey
Description: Amazon has almost doubled its brand value to $316 billion as it expands in areas like entertainment and smart speakers, while China's Alibaba is now the world's second most valuable retail brand, a survey showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Investors brace portfolios for longer U.S.-China trade war
Description: Investors are losing faith that a U.S.-China trade deal could happen soon and are bracing their portfolios for a more prolonged battle that could hamper global growth.

Headlines: Bitcoin tops $8,000 as it hits highest since July 2018
Description: Bitcoin surged to more than $8,000 late on Monday, its highest level since July last year, as the cryptocurrency's rally gained further momentum.

Headlines: Uber CEO expects further pressure as shares add to losses, down 12%
Description: Uber Technologies Inc's shares fell 12% on Monday, more than doubling their losses since the ride-hailing giant's poorly received market debut, and its chief executive officer said he expected the stock to remain under pressure in the coming months.

Headlines: Wall Street hit hard by escalation of tariff war
Description: Wall Street's main indexes tumbled on Monday after Beijing announced plans to retaliate with higher tariffs on U.S. goods, raising fears that another round of tit-for-tat measures could push the U.S. economy toward recession.

Headlines: U.S. liquefied natural gas shipments to China face mounting tariffs
Description: China said on Monday it would raise tariffs on liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports from the United States amid a series of additional levies, a move that could further reduce U.S. LNG shipments to the world's fastest growing importer of the fuel.

Headlines: U.S. exempts water filters, camera parts from China tariffs
Description: The Trump administration on Monday announced that it will  exempt a broad range of additional Chinese-made products from 25 percent U.S. tariffs, including industrial equipment, water filtering equipment, small electric motors, remote control devices and stereoscopic microscopes.

Headlines: In setback for Apple, U.S. Supreme Court lets App Store antitrust suit proceed
Description: A divided U.S. Supreme Court on Monday gave the go-ahead to an antitrust lawsuit accusing Apple Inc of forcing consumers to overpay for iPhone software applications, a decision that could lead to billions of dollars in damages and put at risk the company's lucrative way of selling apps.

Headlines: Wall Street shudders as U.S.-China trade war intensifies
Description: Wall Street sank on Monday after China defied Washington by announcing retaliatory tariffs, the latest salvo in the two countries' increasingly belligerent trade war, sending investors fleeing equities for less risky assets.

Headlines: Billionaire Schwartz makes $2.6 billion bet on Canada's WestJet Airlines
Description: Billionaire Gerry Schwartz pounced on Canada's WestJet Airlines on Monday as his private equity firm Onex Corp offered to buy the struggling airline for C$3.5 billion ($2.6 billion), betting it can turn around its recent decline by taking the company private.

Headlines: Stocks dive, yuan weakens as U.S.-China trade fight intensifies
Description: Global stock markets tumbled on Monday and the Chinese yuan weakened to its lowest level since December as the trade war between the United States and China escalated.

Headlines: Fed officials see risks in weaker inflation expectations, trade row
Description: A drop in the consumer outlook for inflation and intensifying trade tensions drew caution from Federal Reserve officials on Monday as policymakers faced fresh market volatility and a renewed set of risks.

Headlines: Fed can lower rates if U.S.-China trade spat causes slowdown: Rosengren
Description: The Federal Reserve has the tools it needs, including lowering interest rates, to respond to any slowdown resulting from the U.S.-China trade spat, a top Fed policymaker told Reuters on Monday, adding that he is not necessarily expecting such a need now.

Headlines: Exclusive: Amazon rolls out machines that pack orders and replace jobs
Description: Amazon.com Inc is rolling out machines to automate a job held by thousands of its workers: boxing up customer orders.

Headlines: Volkswagen to make batteries in Germany, slim down
Description: Volkswagen will invest almost 1 billion euros ($1.1 billion) in battery cell production at a facility in western Germany and is seeking to simplify the group by spinning off or selling units, the automaker said on Monday.

Headlines: Trump says no decision yet on levying tariffs on more Chinese goods
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he was has not made a decision to go ahead with tariffs on another $325 billion in goods from China and said he plans to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the G20 summit next month.

Headlines: Fed's Kaplan says interest rates are about where they should be
Description: Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Kaplan on Monday said that the Fed should neither be cutting nor raising interest rates but should "move off to the side and be patient."

Headlines: Fed's Kaplan says he's vigilant but patient on U.S.-China tensions
Description: Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Kaplan on Monday said he is "extremely vigilant" on the escalating trade tensions between the United States and China, though it could take months before there is more clarity on how the talks are shaping up.

Headlines: Facebook raises minimum wage for U.S. contract workers to $20/hour
Description: Facebook Inc said on Monday it was raising its minimum wage for all U.S. contract workers, reacting to rising costs of living as it faces intense scrutiny over the treatment of ordinary employees and their pay.

Headlines: China says U.S. policies are causing existential damage to the WTO
Description: China said on Monday U.S. policies are threatening the existence of the World Trade Organization, setting out a string of grievances in a WTO "reform proposal" published by the WTO on its website.

Headlines: U.S. drops plan to require vehicle brake-throttle override system
Description: The Trump administration said Monday it will drop rules first proposed in 2012 that would have required automakers to install brake-throttle override systems to prevent runaway vehicles.

Headlines: Apple revamps its TV app ahead of streaming service launch
Description: Apple Inc on Monday rolled out a new television-watching app for its devices and some Internet-connected TVs, an effort to gain more revenue from reselling other companies' programming and, later this year, its own original shows.

Headlines: Exclusive: Truckmaker Scania signs Northvolt battery deal, in talks on equity
Description: Volkswagen truck brand Scania has signed a battery supply deal with Sweden's Northvolt and is in talks about making an equity investment as part of the startup's efforts to raise 1.5 billion euros ($1.68 billion), Scania's head said on Monday.

Headlines: Wells Fargo CEO search hobbled by pay limitations: sources
Description: (This May 10th story corrects paragraph 7 to say Wells Fargo may need to match stock-based compensation a candidate has at a current employer, not that company may need to match vested shares.)

Headlines: Bayer says Monsanto likely kept files on influential people across Europe
Description: Bayer said on Monday its Monsanto unit, which is being investigated by French prosecutors for compiling files of influential people such as journalists in France, likely did the same across Europe, suggesting a potentially wider problem.

Headlines: Ray-ban owner EssilorLuxottica draws line under Franco-Italian feud
Description: EssilorLuxottica declared an end to a feud between its French and Italian partners on Monday, saying it would drop all legal proceedings and focus on integrating the eyewear group formed by last year's 54 billion euro ($61 billion) merger.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank talks with UBS on asset management deal stall: sources
Description: Talks have stalled between Deutsche Bank and UBS on a tie up of their asset management businesses due to differences over who would control the combined entity, people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Trump warns China not to retaliate against tariff hike

Description: The decision of U.S. asset manager BlackRock to pull out of the rescue of Italian troubled bank Carige makes state intervention more plausible, Moody's Investors Service said on Monday.

Description: The latest U.S. and Chinese round of planned tariffs on each other's imports may reduce global economic growth by 0.15% and lower China's gross domestic product by 0.5% and U.S. GDP by 0.25%, Societe Generale's U.S. chief economist said on Monday.

Description: Ford Motor Co said on Tuesday it partnered with Amazon.com Inc to allow members of the ecommerce company's loyalty club Prime to deliver packages to their cars when they are not at home.

Headlines: Former Abraaj executive gets bail in New York in fraud case
Description: A U.S. district court has granted bail to a former managing partner of collapsed private equity firm Abraaj, Mustafa Abdel-Wadood, on condition that he sign a $10 million bond and remain confined to a New York apartment, court documents showed.

Headlines: Trade war and sagging prices push U.S. family farmers to leave the field
Description: Shuffling across his frozen fields, farmer Jim Taphorn hunched his shoulders against the wind and squinted at the auctioneer standing next to his tractors.After a fifth harvest with low grain prices, made worse last fall by the U.S.-China trade war, the 68-year-old and his family were calling it quits. Farming also was taking a physical toll on him, he said; he'd suffered a heart attack 15 months before.

Headlines: Ford reaches agreement with workers at Brazilian plant it plans to shut down
Description: Ford Motor Co said on Tuesday it had reached an agreement with the workers' union at a historic Brazil plant it plans to shutter by the end of the year, paving the way for a friendly shutdown or potential takeover by a local buyer.

Headlines: Wall Street queries Google ad changes after rare revenue miss
Description: Wall Street punished Google on Tuesday for managers' refusal to give details of changes made to its ad platform in first-quarter results, following a rare miss of expectations for revenue due to a cleanup of YouTube content.

Headlines: How to train your machine: JPMorgan FX algos learn to trade better
Description: JPMorgan Chase, a top player in the $5.1 trillion-a-day global currency market has started applying a new technology that enables machine-trading programs to learn from previous trades and search for the most profitable way to execute them.

Headlines: U.S. Upper Midwest factory growth rebounds in April
Description: A gauge of manufacturing activity in the U.S. Upper Midwest rose in April, bolstered by increases in stronger production and hiring activities, according to a private-sector survey released on Tuesday.

Headlines: Why Airbus isn't pouncing on Boeing's 737 MAX turmoil
Description: When Boeing launched its 737 MAX jetliner in response to Airbus's record-selling A320neo, a wave of poker-faced satisfaction spread through Airbus headquarters in France.

Headlines: Trump sues Deutsche Bank and Capital One to block House subpoenas
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump, three of his children and seven of his companies filed a federal lawsuit Monday against Deutsche Bank and Capital One Financial Corp to block the banks from complying with federal subpoenas investigating his financial dealings.

Headlines: Supervisors ignored Russian warnings over money laundering at Danske: document
Description: Russia's Central Bank sent warnings in 2007 and 2013 to Estonian and Danish financial supervisors over suspect transactions worth billion of dollars at the Estonian branch of Danske Bank but they were largely ignored, a confidential EU document shows.

Headlines: As trade talks reach endgame, U.S.-China ties could hinge on enforcement
Description: U.S. negotiators head to China on Tuesday to try to hammer out details to end the two countries' trade war, including the shape of an enforcement mechanism, the success or failure of which could set the trajectory of ties for years to come.

Headlines: SAS cancels more Scandinavian flights as pilots strike for fifth day
Description: Scandinavian airline SAS canceled more than 500 flights scheduled for Wednesday, which will ground some 47,000 passengers, as a strike by pilots entered a fifth day with no sign of talks between management and unions.

Headlines: Cable operator Charter edges past quarterly revenue estimates
Description: Cable operator Charter Communications Inc edged past analysts' estimates for first-quarter revenue on Tuesday, as the company attracted more customers for its internet services, offsetting a drop in video subscribers.

Headlines: Iran says it will keep exporting oil despite U.S. pressure
Description: Iran will continue to export oil despite U.S. pressure aimed at reducing the country's crude shipments to zero, Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Samsung Electronics bets on better second-half after first-quarter profit slumps
Description: South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co Ltd flagged improved second-half results on expectations of a pick up in memory chip and smartphone sales, after posting its weakest profit in more than two years in the first quarter.

Headlines: OPEC supply squeeze seen supporting higher oil prices: Reuters survey
Description: Oil prices are likely to stay buoyant this year as the U.S. decision to end waivers on Iranian oil and OPEC output curbs are expected to keep supply tight, a Reuters survey showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Senior China diplomat says trade talks with U.S. have made 'much positive progress'
Description: Trade talks between China and the United States to date have achieved "much positive progress," a senior Chinese diplomat said on Tuesday, as senior U.S. officials have arrived in Beijing for the latest round of talks.

Headlines: Strike-hit airline SAS cancels 504 flights on Wednesday
Description: SAS said it was cancelling 504 flights scheduled for Wednesday, affecting about 47,000 passengers, as much of its fleet remained grounded for a fifth day on Tuesday due to a pilot strike at the Scandinavian airline.

Headlines: Southwest Airlines loses top spot in passenger satisfaction, even as others gain
Description: Southwest Airlines Co, the biggest user of Boeing Co's 737 MAX jets that were grounded worldwide following two fatal crashes, dropped two places from the top in terms of passenger satisfaction in 2019, a survey by the American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI) showed.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler picks Google, Samsung for global connected car system
Description: Fiat Chrysler  said on Tuesday it will use technology from Alphabet Inc's Google and Samsung to connect all its vehicles by 2022, providing music and video and facilitating future car-sharing and self-driving capabilities.

Headlines: Pariah no more? Greece needs big bond investors to seal its comeback
Description: By Dhara Ranasinghe, Abhinav Ramnarayan and Lefteris Papadimas

Headlines: Danske Bank cuts outlook as money laundering scandal weighs
Description: Danske Bank lowered its outlook for 2019 after a disappointing first quarter, due in part to the effects of a massive money laundering scandal at its Estonian branch that has sent ripples across the Nordic banking sector.

Headlines: Boxed in: $1 billion of Iranian crude sits at China's Dalian port
Description: Some 20 million barrels of Iranian oil sitting on China's shores in the northeast port of Dalian for the past six months now appears stranded as the United States hardens its stance on importing crude from Tehran.

Headlines: Google parent's shares dive as YouTube changes, competition hurt revenue
Description: Alphabet Inc's Google on Monday saw its slowest revenue growth in three years from increased competition in advertising, stumbles in its smartphone business and disruptive changes at YouTube that left the leading internet ad company lagging rivals.

Headlines: Indebted Chinese seek wisdom of credit card 'goddesses' as retail lending surges
Description: In a ballroom at the Vienna International Hotel in Shanghai, Mei Liangming was giving a lecture on the ins and outs of getting credit cards, rolling over debts with multiple cards, and cleaning up one's bad credit history.

Headlines: Virgin Australia to delay taking Boeing 737 MAX jets to cut spending
Description: Virgin Australia Holdings said on Tuesday it would delay taking the first deliveries of Boeing Co 737 MAX jets for nearly two years to reduce capital spending and give it time to be satisfied with the model's safety.

Headlines: Strong U.S. growth, weak inflation leave Fed stuck happily on hold
Description: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady at its policy meeting this week as policymakers balance recent stronger-than-expected U.S. economic growth against sluggish inflation.

Headlines: White House says Stephen Moore still has Trump's support for Fed seat
Description: The White House still backs Stephen Moore for a seat on the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, President Donald Trump's top economic adviser said on Monday, despite concerns among some Democratic lawmakers about his competence and past remarks.

Headlines: Anadarko to negotiate sale to Occidental 'superior' to Chevron deal
Description: Anadarko Petroleum Corp said on Monday it would negotiate with Occidental Petroleum Corp over its $38 billion cash-and-stock bid, after determining it could get a better deal than its agreed $33 billion sale to Chevron Corp.

Headlines: U.S. SEC freezes assets over suspected insider trading in Anadarko
Description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday obtained an asset freeze in connection with suspected insider trading in Anadarko Petroleum Corp before the oil company agreed to be acquired by rival Chevron Corp.

Headlines: Anadarko's weak performance in U.S. Permian made it a takeover target
Description: Anadarko Petroleum Corp has become the biggest prize in the energy industry in part because of lagging oil production despite large land holdings in the top U.S. shale field.

Headlines: S&P 500 posts high, extends 2019 rally; Alphabet falls late
Description: The S&P 500 set an intraday record high on Monday, bolstering the view that the decade-long bull market has further to run, after consumer spending rose in March and inflation data was benign.

Headlines: Uber quizzed on growth at IPO roadshow in London
Description: Uber Technologies Inc Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi sought to persuade money managers in London that the loss-making ride hailing firm's growth plans justified a valuation of up to $91.5 billion in an initial public offering (IPO).

Headlines: Uber drivers plan protest over pay ahead of IPO
Description: Uber Technologies Inc's drivers in six U.S. cities are planning to shut their apps for 12 hours on May 8 to protest against low wages and working conditions, two days ahead of the company's expected market debut.

Headlines: Daimler will pull Smart mini-cars out of United States, Canada
Description: The tiny, two-person Smart cars once pitched as the next big thing in urban mobility will be discontinued in the United States and Canada at the end of the current model year, German automaker Daimler AG said on Monday.

Headlines: Amazon starts recruiting and leases office for Virginia 'HQ2'
Description: Amazon.com Inc on Monday said it had leased office space and posted several jobs for its second headquarters outside Washington, D.C., the start of more than a decade of investment and hiring that cities across North America had sought.

Headlines: Boeing wins $5.7 billion U.S. defense contract - Pentagon
Description: Boeing Co has been awarded a $5.7 billion U.S. defense contract for post-production requirements for the KC-46 Pegasus aircraft, the Pentagon said on Monday.

Headlines: Toyota to produce Lexus NX for North America at Canada plant
Description: Toyota Motor Corp will build its Lexus NX luxury crossover vehicle at a Canadian plant starting in 2022, the company said on Monday, a decision that Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said demonstrated the value of the country's international trade agreements.

Headlines: Global stocks climb as S&P 500 hits record, oil steadies after selloff
Description: A jump in U.S. consumer spending propelled U.S. shares to a record high on Monday and global equities edged upwards, helping offset a weak euro zone sentiment survey and political uncertainty over Spain's elections.

Headlines: The obscure advisory committees at the heart of the U.S. drug pricing debate
Description: Expectations were high last year for three new migraine drugs hitting the market from Amgen Inc, Eli Lilly and Co and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries.

Headlines: Oil climbs, shaking off Trump calls for OPEC to offset Iran sanctions
Description: Oil prices edged higher on Monday, as the market attempted to resume a weeks-long rally that was halted on Friday when U.S. President Donald Trump demanded that producer club OPEC raise output to soften the impact of U.S. sanctions against Iran.

Headlines: Canadian farm exports hit new Chinese obstacles amid diplomatic dispute
Description: An expanding list of Canadian farm exports is hitting obstacles at Chinese ports, leaving sellers of soybeans, peas and pork scrambling amid a bitter diplomatic dispute.

Description: Tesla Inc said on Monday it could seek alternative sources of financing, days after Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk reached a deal with U.S. securities regulators to settle a dispute over his Twitter use, removing an overhang on the stock.

Headlines: Colombia's Avianca says bankruptcy of Avianca Brasil causing 'reputational harm'
Description: Colombia's Avianca Holdings SA said on Monday it is experiencing "reputational harm" from its association with Avianca Brasil, an air carrier that licenses its name and has canceled over 1,000 flights amid a bankruptcy restructuring.

Headlines: Analyst View: Wall Street teases out records above 2018 highs
Description: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq edged up to their highest intraday levels ever on Monday after data showed U.S. consumer spending surged in March, but gains in shares remained muted as investors waited for a fresh batch of earnings reports.

Headlines: Alibaba to pay $250 million to settle lawsuit over pre-IPO warning on counterfeiting
Description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd said on Monday it will pay $250 million to settle a U.S. lawsuit faulting the Chinese e-commerce company for concealing a regulatory warning about its ability to stop counterfeiting before it went public in 2014.

Headlines: Is Buffett still a buy? Wall Street splits on Berkshire Hathaway as annual meeting looms
Description: Two longtime analysts of Berkshire Hathaway Inc appear deeply divided over prospects for the company led since 1965 by billionaire Warren Buffett, in reports issued on Monday ahead of this weekend's shareholder extravaganza.

Headlines: Sprint, T-Mobile push back deadline to complete merger
Description: T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp on Monday extended the deadline for completing their proposed $26 billion deal to July 29 as the U.S. Justice Department's Antitrust Division chief said he had not decided whether to approve the transaction.

Headlines: Slowing inflation may lead Fed to cut interest rates: Kudlow
Description: Slowing inflation may lead the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates, White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said in a television interview on Monday.

Headlines: Airbnb CEO says company will be ready for IPO later this year: CNBC
Description: Airbnb will be ready for an initial public offering later this year, the home-renting company's chief executive officer told CNBC on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. consumer spending roars back, but inflation tame
Description: U.S. consumer spending increased by the most in more than 9-1/2 years in March as households stepped up purchases of motor vehicles, but price pressures remained muted, with a key inflation measure posting its smallest annual gain in 14 months.

Headlines: Jaguar Land Rover planning to allow helpful car drivers to earn cryptocurrency
Description: Jaguar Land Rover, Britain's largest auto manufacturer, said on Monday it is testing software that will allow drivers of its cars to earn the IOTA cryptocurrency as a reward for sharing data.

Headlines: Amazon speeds up shipping, but rivals' stores buck its challenge
Description: Amazon's promise of one-day shipping threatens to upend the retail sector, but its rivals' physical stores give the likes of Walmart and Target powerful assets that Amazon itself is scrambling to match.

Headlines: Spotify hits 100 million subscribers, reports revenue jump
Description: Spotify Technology SA, the world's leading streaming platform, said on Monday it had hit 100 million paid subscribers as it reported a better-than-expected rise in first-quarter revenue.

Headlines: U.S. Supreme Court seeks Trump administration views on Google-Oracle copyright feud
Description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday asked the Trump administration to offer its views on whether it should hear Google's bid to end Oracle Corp's copyright infringement lawsuit involving the Android operating system that runs most of the world's smartphones.

Headlines: Swiss group files criminal complaint against Credit Suisse over Mozambique loans
Description: A Swiss anti-corruption lobby group has filed a criminal complaint against Credit Suisse over alleged fraud in the arrangement of $2 billion of loans to Mozambique, the group said on Monday.

Description: Boeing Co said on Monday it was making steady progress to certify its grounded 737 MAX jets with a software update and completed a final flight test prior to the certification flight.

Description: The CEO of Scandinavian airline SAS has told negotiators to thrash out what concessions the company could make to end a pilots strike that has disrupted travel plans for hundreds of thousands of passengers.

Description: Tighter U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil planned for May are adding to a wealth of factors curbing global supply of heavy-medium crude, driving up prices for scarcer barrels and setting up a stand-off between buyers and sellers.

Headlines: ZTE Corp swings to first-quarter profit of 862.6 million yuan
Description: China's ZTE Corp reported on Monday a first-quarter profit of 862.6 million yuan ($128.2 million), as expected, up from 276 million yuan in the preceding three months, as it recovered from last year's U.S. sanctions.

Headlines: Iran says U.S. sanctions on its oil industry will damage market stability
Description: U.S. sanctions against Iran's oil industry will damage the stability of global oil markets, a senior Iranian official was quoted as saying on Monday.

Description: Fines for violations of air, water and waste regulations by U.S. petroleum storage facilities so far this year have exceeded all of last year - even without including two major Houston-area disasters in the last month still under investigation - according to a Reuters analysis of federal data.

Headlines: Emirates says full-year results will not be as good as in previous years
Description: Dubai state-owned airline Emirates will report "positive" full-year results next month but they will not be as good as in previous years due to higher fuel costs and unfavourable currency moves, the company's president said on Monday.

Headlines: Exclusive: GAM whistle blower concerns focused on bonds sold by metals tycoon
Description: A whistle blower at Swiss asset manager GAM Holding AG who alerted UK financial regulators last year did so over concerns about the purchase of more than half a billion pounds of bonds from commodities tycoon Sanjeev Gupta, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Description: The European Union has accepted an offer by Visa and Mastercard to cut fees on payments made by tourists using cards issued outside the bloc to stave off fines and end an EU antitrust investigation.

Headlines: Global tightening cycle over, slower ride for growth ahead: Reuters Poll
Description: Major central banks are done tightening policy, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters, with the growth outlook wilting across developed and emerging economies along with scant prospects for a surge in inflation.

Headlines: Emirates president confident Boeing will resolve issues with 737 MAX
Description: Emirates Airline President Tim Clark said on Monday he believes Boeing Co will resolve issues with its 737 MAX aircraft, saying the U.S. company has an outstanding track record.

Description: Engine maker Rolls-Royce said on Monday that it had been suspended from the UK government's Prompt Payment Code (PPC) after failing to pay suppliers in time.

Headlines: DBS posts record profit on lending gains, raises bar for Singapore banks
Description: Southeast Asia's biggest lender DBS Group Holdings Ltd beat market estimates to post a record quarterly profit, as strong lending income offset weakness in wealth management, brokerage and investment banking fees.

Headlines: Exclusive: Anadarko to pursue deal talks with Occidental Petroleum - sources
Description: Anadarko Petroleum Corp, the U.S. oil and gas exploration and production company that agreed this month to sell itself to Chevron Corp for $33 billion, decided on Sunday to begin negotiations to sell itself to Occidental Petroleum Corp instead, according to people familiar with the matter.

Description: Royal Bank of Scotland is searching for a new chief executive after Ross McEwan resigned, signaling a fresh start  as it heads for full private ownership after a state bailout.

Headlines: Airline SAS cancels 1,200 more flights as pilot strike drags on
Description: Scandinavian airline SAS canceled more than 1,200 flights scheduled for Monday and Tuesday as a pilot strike that has disrupted the travel plans of hundreds of thousands of passengers entered its third day on Sunday.

Headlines: U.S. opens criminal probe into Ford emissions certification
Description: The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into Ford Motor Co's emissions certification process in the United States, the automaker disclosed on Friday, saying it was cooperating fully with the probe and still conducting its own internal review.

Headlines: UK regulator blocks Sainsbury's $9.4 billion takeover of Walmart's ASDA
Description: Britain's competition regulator on Thursday blocked Sainsbury's proposed 7.3 billion pound ($9.4 billion) takeover of Walmart-owned Asda - a huge blow to the supermarket groups who wanted to combine to overtake market leader Tesco.

Headlines: Tesla's Musk agrees to new vetting rules for tweets in SEC deal
Description: Tesla Inc Chief Executive Elon Musk has reached a deal with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to settle a dispute over his use of Twitter, agreeing to submit his public statements about the company's finances and other topics to vetting by its legal counsel, according to a court filing on Friday.

Headlines: Gardner Denver to merge with Ingersoll-Rand division: WSJ
Description: Industrial machinery maker Gardner Denver Holdings Inc is nearing a deal to merge with a division of Ingersoll-Rand Plc, creating a business that would have an enterprise value, including debt, of about $15 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

Headlines: Vale shareholders push to loosen company control over board elections
Description: Minority shareholders of Brazilian iron ore miner Vale SA have enough votes to request that board members be elected independently using a cumulative voting system and not in a single vote approving all names proposed by controlling shareholders, the company said in a filing.

Headlines: Italy's deputy PM says Alitalia bid deadline is Tuesday
Description: The deadline for bids to take part in a plan to rescue Italian flagship carrier Alitalia is next Tuesday, Italy's Deputy Prime Minister Luigi Di Maio said on Sunday.

Headlines: Pilots demand better training if Boeing wants to rebuild trust in 737 MAX
Description: American Airlines pilots have warned that Boeing Co's  draft training proposals for the troubled 737 MAX do not go far enough to address their concerns, according to written comments submitted to the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and seen by Reuters.

Description: Saudi Arabian budget airline Flyadeal's decision on whether it goes ahead with an order for 30 Boeing 737 MAX jets is "imminent", its chief executive said on Sunday.

Description: China sought to put a gentler face on its massive plan to recreate the old Silk Road at a summit that ended on Saturday, saying it must do more to explain the program and boost sustainability even as state media hit back at critics.

Description: Renault will propose a plan to create a joint holding company that would give the French carmaker and Japanese partner Nissan equal footing, a person with knowledge of the issue told Reuters.

Headlines: China's Xi says Belt and Road must be green, sustainable
Description: China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) must be green and sustainable, President Xi Jinping said in opening a summit on his grand strategy, adding that the massive infrastructure and trade plan would deliver "high-quality" growth for all.

Description: Nearly 40 world leaders and scores of finance officials, including International Monetary Fund Managing Director Christine Lagarde, are gathered in Beijing for China's second Belt and Road infrastructure summit, but the World Bank's new president is not among them.

Description: Major European Union countries want to deal with China as a group rather than sign bilateral agreements as individual states, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Friday, attending a summit in Beijing on China's Belt and Road plan.

Headlines: Take Five: Dollar darling. World markets themes for the week ahead

Description: Even as the lift from optimism over prospects for U.S.-China trade detente shows signs of wearing off for the wider U.S. stock market, upbeat sentiment around China's economy could bolster shares of materials companies.

Description: Brazil's state-controlled oil company Petrobras on Friday for the first time detailed long-awaited plans to sell a series of refineries and other assets as the company focuses on its core oil and gas exploration business.

Description: A surprisingly strong report card on the U.S. economy helped power the benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indexes to record high closes on Friday, capping a week of gains for stocks that came largely on the back of resilient corporate profits.

Description: Exxon Mobil Corp and Chevron Corp on Friday reported lower profits, citing lower margins and refining weaknesses, areas that have plagued the two oil companies off and on for more than a year.

Description: White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said on Friday that "ample progress" is being made in the U.S.-China trade talks.
