Headlines: JD Sports raises its stake in Footasylum to more than 18 percent
Description: Footasylum Plc said on Tuesday its larger rival JD Sports Fashion Plc has increased its stake in the company to more than 18 percent.

Headlines: Honda to close British car plant as Brexit looms
Description: Honda will close its only British car plant in 2021 with the loss of up to 3,500 jobs, a major departure of Japanese investment announced just over a month before the United Kingdom is due to leave the European Union.

Headlines: Medtronic quarterly profit beats on strength in surgical products
Description: Medtronic Plc beat analysts' estimates for quarterly profit on Tuesday, boosted by sales of its surgical products, and the largest U.S. standalone medical device maker raised the upper end of its full-year earnings forecast.

Headlines: BAE Systems wins funding from U.S. Army to start production of new armored vehicles
Description: Britain's defense company BAE Systems on Tuesday said it had won additional funding up to $575 million from the U.S. Army to begin production of its new armored vehicles that would replace the Vietnam War-era M113 fleet of personnel carriers.

Headlines: Aviva, NatWest to join 'Brexodus' of business to EU
Description: England's High Court on Tuesday gave Aviva, Britain’s second largest insurer, approval to transfer around 9 billion pounds ($11.69 billion) in assets to a new Irish company just before the starting gun is fired on Brexit.

Headlines: German government unlikely to make quick decision on Huawei: source
Description: The German government will probably not take a quick decision on whether to allow China's Huawei to build Germany's 5G network, a government source said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Germany still in talks on Huawei 5G network role, minister says
Description: Germany's government is still in talks on whether China's Huawei will be allowed to participate in building the country's high-speed internet infrastructure, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. consumers forecast more spending than a year ago: NY Fed
Description: U.S. consumers expect to spend more money in 2019 than they did a year ago, data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Mexico pushes mobile payments to help unbanked consumers ditch cash
Description: Mexico's new leftist government is betting on financial technology to help lift people out of poverty.

Headlines: BHP CEO staying around to deal with tailings and transformation
Description: The chief executive of mining group BHP has no plans to quit and will focus on the "nuclear level of safety" needed to avoid any repeat of the Vale dam collapse in Brazil, as well as on transforming his own company.

Headlines: HSBC warns on China, UK slowdowns as 2018 profit disappoints
Description: HSBC warned it may have to delay some investments this year as Europe's biggest bank missed 2018 profit forecasts due to slowing growth in its two home markets of China and Britain.

Headlines: Glencore to cut output, jobs at copper, cobalt mine in Congo: WSJ
Description: Glencore Plc is planning to cut production at one of its largest copper and cobalt mining operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources on Tuesday.

Headlines: UK PM May told Honda president she was disappointed by plant closure: spokesman
Description: British Prime Minister Theresa May spoke to the president of Honda to express her disappointment after the car manufacturer's decision to shut a plant in England, May's spokesman said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Huawei founder says will not share data with China: CBS News
Description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's founder and chief executive pledged not to share any customer information with the Chinese government and said the company had never done so, in an interview with CBS News that aired on Tuesday.

Headlines: Get Brexit sorted out, UK business minister says after Honda plant decision
Description: The United Kingdom must urgently end the uncertainty over its exit from the European Union so that businesses can have clarity about the future, business minister Greg Clark said just hours after Honda said it would close its car plant in Britain.

Headlines: Activist Bramson's unlikely Barclays board seat bid sharpens scrutiny of bank
Description: Activist investor Edward Bramson's bid to join the Barclays board is destined to fail, shareholders told Reuters, though he has sharpened scrutiny of its investment banking strategy that Bramson argues has depressed profitability.

Headlines: Saab proposes to make 96 Gripen jets in India to win Air Force deal
Description: Swedish defense firm Saab AB, which is seeking to sell its Gripen fighter jets to the Indian Air Force, said on Tuesday it could offer to make most of them in a production facility likely to be set up in one of the southern cities.

Headlines: VW's Audi mulls cutting night shifts at Ingolstadt plant: Handelsblatt
Description: Volkswagen's Audi is considering cutting night shifts at its Ingolstadt plant, Handelsblatt reported on Tuesday, citing the head of the luxury carmaker's works council.

Headlines: Alibaba boosts stake in investment bank CICC for $231 million
Description: China's e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd has raised its stake in top domestic investment bank China International Capital Corp's Hong Kong-listed shares to nearly 12 percent, an exchange disclosure showed on Monday.

Headlines: Nestle says it is now well positioned in confectionery
Description: Nestle's success with its KitKat brand means its does not need to add new businesses after selling its candy unit to Italy's Ferrero last year, the Swiss food group's global head of confectionery said.

Headlines: UK business secretary skips conference to update lawmakers on Honda
Description: British business secretary Greg Clark will not speak at Tuesday's EEF manufacturing conference as billed and his deputy Richard Harrington will appear instead, the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy said.

Headlines: Volkswagen customer plans to take diesel case to Germany's highest court
Description: A German court on Tuesday ruled in favor of Volkswagen in a case brought by a customer seeking compensation for having bought a diesel car affected by emissions cheating, but the plaintiff's lawyer plans to appeal.

Headlines: British supermarkets battle to secure stocks as chaotic Brexit looms
Description: Britons could face shortages of fresh food, price rises and less variety if the country leaves the European Union next month without agreeing on trade terms, food industry officials say.

Headlines: Payless ShoeSource seeks bankruptcy protection again
Description: U.S. discount retailer Payless ShoeSource Inc on Monday filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection for the second time, along with its North American subsidiaries, and said it would wind down all North American stores by the end of May.

Headlines: China's JD.com to lay off 10 percent of senior executives this year: report
Description: JD.com Inc, one of China's largest e-commerce sites, will lay off 10 percent of its senior executives this year, Chinese online media outlet Sina Tech reported on Tuesday, citing unnamed sources.

Headlines: China's Fosun makes bid for German fashion chain Tom Tailor
Description: Chinese conglomerate Fosun International announced a takeover bid for troubled German clothing retailer Tom Tailor on Tuesday, further expanding its reach into Europe's fashion sector.

Headlines: Germany sees 'most difficult part' in EU-U.S. trade talks ahead
Description: The most difficult part in trade negotiations between Europe and the United States is starting now and talks should focus on reducing tariffs on industrial goods to increase the chances of a deal, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Chinese government doesn't get involved in Huawei's business: German boss
Description: The head of China's Huawei Technologies in Germany told a German newspaper that the Chinese government does not get involved in the company's business, adding the firm would work on being open and transparent in the debate about security of mobile networks.

Headlines: Mongolia to suspend KFC outlets for inquiry after food poisoning reports
Description: A Mongolian regulator said it will suspend operations at KFC restaurants temporarily to conduct inquiries, as 42 people were hospitalized and hundreds showed food poisoning symptoms after eating at one of the outlets of the fast-food chain.

Headlines: Honda to shut UK car plant in 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs
Description: Japanese car maker Honda is set to announce it's closing its only British car plant in 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs, a lawmaker told Reuters, in the latest blow to the UK car industry as Brexit approaches.

Headlines: UK deeply disappointed by Honda's decision to close plant
Description: Britain said on Tuesday it was deeply disappointed by Honda's decision to close its only British car plant.

Headlines: Honda UK plant closure not related to Brexit: Europe boss
Description: Honda's decision to close its only British car plant is not related to Brexit and is a product of global changes in the industry, the firm's Europe's boss said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Honda CEO says decision to end production in UK not Brexit related
Description: Honda Motor Co's decision to end production in Britain was not related to Brexit, its chief executive said on Tuesday, after announcing the closure of its only British car plant.

Headlines: Britain's Cobham takes $206 million charge to settle Boeing dispute
Description: British engineer Cobham will take an additional exceptional charge of 160 million pounds ($206 million) to settle a dispute with Boeing over its delayed KC-46 aerial refuelling programme, it said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Elliott takes 6.1 percent stake in Dutch Intertrust
Description: Paul Elliott Singer, the hedge fund manager behind activist investor Elliott, has taken a 6.1 percent stake in Dutch trust and business administration company Intertrust, according to a filing published by the Dutch Authority for Financial Markets (AFM).

Headlines: Goldman Sachs Asia Pacific CEO to retire: Bloomberg
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc's Chairman and Chief Executive for the Asia-Pacific region excluding Japan, Ken Hitchner, is retiring from the company, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Headlines: Huawei founder says Huawei CFO arrest was politically motivated: BBC
Description: Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei said on Monday that the arrest of his daughter, Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou, was politically motivated.

Headlines: Britain does not support total Huawei network ban: sources
Description: British security officials do not support a full ban of Huawei from national telecoms networks despite U.S. allegations the Chinese firm and its products could be used by Beijing for spying, people with knowledge of the matter said.

Headlines: U.S. FAA investigates Southwest over baggage weight discrepancies: WSJ
Description: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is investigating Southwest Airlines Co for widespread failure to accurately track the combined weight of checked bags loaded onto its jets, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

Headlines: Auto industry lines up against possible U.S. tariffs
Description: The U.S. auto industry urged President Donald Trump's administration on Monday not to saddle imported cars and auto parts with steep tariffs, after the U.S. Commerce Department sent a confidential report to the White House late on Sunday with its recommendations for how to proceed.

Headlines: U.S. agency submits auto tariff probe report to White House
Description: The U.S. Commerce Department sent a report on Sunday to U.S. President Donald Trump that could unleash steep tariffs on imported cars and auto parts, provoking a sharp backlash from the industry even before it is unveiled, the agency confirmed.

Headlines: EU's Juncker expects Trump to refrain from imposing higher tariffs on cars
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump has promised European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker that he will not impose additional import tariffs on European cars for the time being, Juncker was quoted in a published interview as saying on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. tariffs on EU cars could mean EU buying less U.S. soya beans and gas: Juncker
Description: United States tariffs on imports of European cars could mean that Europe would buy less soya beans and liquid gas from the U.S., the head of the European Commission Jean-Claude Juncker said on Monday.

Headlines: Papa John's founder Schnatter says he welcomes hedge fund Starboard
Description: Papa John's International Inc founder John Schnatter welcomes hedge fund Starboard Value LP's investment in the pizza restaurant chain, his lawyer said, even as he filed an updated lawsuit on Monday against the company.

Headlines: Germany bans Wirecard 'shorting' as prosecutors probe FT journalist
Description: Germany's financial watchdog has banned "short" selling of Wirecard shares due to volatility in the payments firm's stock following reports in the Financial Times which are now the subject of an investigation by German authorities.

Headlines: Honda plan to close UK plant is not due to Brexit:  lawmaker
Description: Japan's Honda plans to shut its British car plant in Swindon by 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs but the decision is not related to Brexit, a local lawmaker told Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: Citi expects privatization to bolster revenue in Brazil
Description: Citigroup Inc expects to boost annual revenue in Brazil over the next years by advising potential public asset sales and through a revival in capital markets, its chief executive officer in Brazil told journalists on Monday.

Headlines: Russia's Rusal is in talks to resume reinsurance with Western companies
Description: Russia's Rusal, the world's second-largest aluminum producer, is in talks to resume reinsuring its risks with Western companies after Washington lifted sanctions on it, officials with Russian National Reinsurance Co (RNRC) said.

Headlines: World stocks lifted to 2 1/2-month highs by trade optimism
Description: Hopes for progress in Sino-U.S. trade talks and expectations of policy stimulus from central banks lifted world stocks to 2 1/2- month highs on Monday, though European gains were held back by concern over the outlook for auto makers.

Headlines: Britain's FT says allegations over Wirecard reporting are false
Description: Britain's Financial Times rejected as "baseless and false" any allegations accusing the newspaper or its reporters of market manipulation or unethical reporting in relation to German payments company Wirecard.

Headlines: Citi in talks to buy Canary Wharf office building: source
Description: Citigroup is in talks to buy the tower housing its European headquarters in London's Canary Wharf district, which is on the market with a price tag of around 1.2 billion pounds ($1.55 billion), a source familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: SoftBank invests in Mubadala's new $400 million European tech fund: source
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group has provided nearly half of the cash for Abu Dhabi's state investor Mubadala Investment Co's new $400 million fund investing in European start-ups, a source familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: New Zealand will conduct own assessment of Huawei equipment risk: PM
Description: New Zealand will independently assess the risk of using China's Huawei Technologies in 5G networks, Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said on Monday after a report suggested that British precautions could be used by other nations.

Headlines: New Zealand to target online giants with digital tax
Description: New Zealand said on Monday that it plans to update its laws so it can tax revenue earned by multinational digital firms such as Google, Facebook and Amazon, extending a global effort to bring global tech giants into the tax net.

Headlines: Famed Cullinan mine banks on big diamonds to drive down debt
Description: The owner of one of the world's most famous diamond mines could be about a decade away from clearing its multi-million-dollar debts, in a sign of the struggles facing an industry assailed by synthetic rivals and uncertain demand.

Headlines: Alabama jury awards $152 million in Ford Explorer rollover case
Description: An Alabama jury awarded $151.8 million to a young man paralyzed in 2015 rollover accident involving a Ford Explorer sport utility vehicle, Ford and lawyers in the case said on Sunday.

Headlines: Russia's Gazprombank freezes accounts of Venezuela's PDVSA: source
Description: Russian lender Gazprombank  has decided to freeze the accounts of Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA and halted transactions with the firm to reduce the risk of the bank falling under U.S. sanctions, a Gazprombank source told Reuters on Sunday.

Headlines: Qatar aims to build $20 billion sports sector ahead of World Cup
Description: Qatar wants to attract more sports companies to the Gulf state, aiming to develop a $20 billion sports sector ahead of the 2022 World Cup, a senior official said on Sunday.

Headlines: Airbus warns of no-deal Brexit, says has spent tens of millions preparing
Description: Airbus said on Sunday it would have to make "difficult decisions" about future investment if Britain crashes out of the European Union without a deal, adding it had already spent tens of millions of euros in preparations.

Headlines: Qatar's real estate market faces reality check ahead of World Cup
Description: Qatar's Doha Tower, a spike-tipped cylinder that glows orange at night, won an award when finished in 2012 amid a Gulf-wide real estate boom, but today about half of its 46 floors are empty.

Headlines: Nissan panel to recommend outside director to chair board: Nikkei
Description: A Nissan Motor governance committee will recommend the appointment of an external director as board chairman, a role distinct from company chairman, in a move to decentralize power at the top level, the Nikkei business daily reported on Sunday.

Headlines: Canada's Freeland pushes end of steel, aluminum tariffs in meeting with Pelosi
Description: Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland said on Saturday she had made clear in a meeting with U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Nancy Pelosi at the Munich Security Conference the importance of the U.S. lifting tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from Canada.

Headlines: Russian court extends custody of Baring Vostok's Calvey until April
Description: A Russian court on Saturday ordered Michael Calvey, the U.S. founder of one of Russia's biggest private equity firms accused of fraud, to be kept in custody until April 13.

Headlines: Russian court orders Baring Vostok's Calvey to be kept in custody until April 13
Description: A Moscow court has ordered Baring Vostok's founder Michael Calvey to be kept in custody until April 13.

Headlines: Exclusive: China ride-hailing giant Didi plans Chile, Peru launches to take on Uber
Description: Chinese ride-hailing giant Didi Chuxing is planning to take on U.S. rival Uber in some of Latin America's fastest-growing markets, recruiting managers in Chile, Peru and Colombia, according to job postings and a company official.

Headlines: HNA cuts stake in Deutsche Bank to 6.3 percent: SEC filing
Description: Chinese conglomerate HNA has cut its stake in Deutsche Bank to 6.3 percent, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Headlines: U.S.-China trade talks to resume next week, Trump hints at extension
Description: The United States and China will resume trade talks next week in Washington with time running short to ease their bruising trade war, but U.S. President Donald Trump repeated on Friday that he may extend a March 1 deadline for a deal and keep tariffs on Chinese goods from rising.

Headlines: China-U.S. trade talks 'making a final sprint': state media
Description: Chinese state media on Saturday expressed cautious optimism over trade talks between the United States and China, a day after President Xi Jinping said a week of discussions had produced "step-by-step" progress.

Headlines: Automakers brace for U.S. government report on import tariffs
Description: A confidential Commerce Department report due to be sent to Donald Trump on Sunday is widely expected to clear the way for the U.S. president to threaten tariffs on imported autos and auto parts by designating the imports a national security threat, auto industry officials said on Friday.

Headlines: Payless ShoeSource to start liquidation sales at stores
Description: U.S. discount retailer Payless ShoeSource Inc said on Friday it would begin going-out-of-business sales at its U.S. and Puerto Rico stores on Feb. 17 and wind down its e-commerce operations.

Headlines: Big U.S. exchanges to sue SEC over 'overreaching' fee experiment
Description: The three largest U.S. stock exchange operators said they will sue the Securities and Exchange Commission for overstepping its authority by ordering a pilot program to test banning lucrative payments exchanges make to brokers for resting stock orders.

Headlines: Starboard gauges Bristol-Myers shareholder support for Celgene deal
Description: Activist hedge fund Starboard Value LP has asked a proxy solicitor to probe the level of support among Bristol-Myers Squibb Co shareholders for the U.S. drug maker's $74 billion deal to buy Celgene Corp, people familiar with the matter said on Friday.

Headlines: Mexico to inject $3.9 billion in Pemex, seeks to prevent credit downgrade
Description: Mexico will inject $3.9 billion into ailing state oil company Pemex, officials said on Friday, promising to strengthen its finances and prevent a further credit downgrade, although investors saw the plan as only a short-term fix.

Headlines: Analyst View: Investors divided over Mexico's bailout of state oil company
Description: The Mexican government promised on Friday to do what it takes to strengthen the finances of ailing state oil company Petroleos Mexicanos with an injection of at least $3.6 billion to prevent a further credit downgrade.

Headlines: Mattel warns of weak 2019, shares drop most in 20 years
Description: Mattel Inc on Friday issued a disappointing 2019 forecast and said demand for its iconic Barbie doll was slowing, triggering an 18 percent drop in its shares, their worst day in nearly two decades.

Headlines: Wall Street Week Ahead: Profit estimates may be adding in too much cost risk
Description: As Wall Street braces for the first quarterly decline in earnings in nearly three years, some investors are wondering if the market is factoring in a bigger erosion in profit margins than will actually come to pass.

Headlines: Fed policymakers see one U.S. rate hike, or none, as growth slows
Description: When the Federal Reserve last month adopted a new "patient" approach to monetary policy, it gave no specific guidance about how long its policy pause would last, or how many more interest-rate increases, if any, were in the offing.

Headlines: Amazon invites Ocasio-Cortez for tour, calls worker claims untrue
Description: A senior Amazon.com Inc executive on Friday disputed claims raised by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez that Amazon workers face "dehumanizing conditions" as being untrue and invited her to take a tour of company facilities.

Headlines: Take Five: The R-word - World markets themes for the week ahead
Description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

Headlines: Venezuela opposition to leave Citgo funds, management untouched: envoy
Description: Venezuela's opposition has no plans to use funds belonging to U.S. refiner Citgo, which is owned by state oil company PDVSA, despite having named a new board for the company this week, the self-declared interim government's U.S. envoy said on Friday.

Headlines: Lyft to woo investors with fast U.S. growth in IPO race with Uber
Description: Lyft Inc will pitch investors on its fast growth in the United States as it seeks to beat out Uber Technologies Inc to become the first publicly listed ride-hailing company, according to people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Wall Street rallies on trade optimism
Description: Wall Street rallied on Friday, with the Dow and the Nasdaq posting their eighth consecutive weekly gains as investors grew hopeful that the United States and China would hammer out an agreement resolving their protracted trade war.

Headlines: How Amazon scrapped its plans for a New York headquarters
Description: More than a year of work to bring Amazon.com Inc's headquarters and tens of thousands of jobs to New York City ended on Thursday with a couple of phone calls.

Headlines: TSX rises 0.91 percent
Description: * The Toronto Stock Exchange's  S&P/TSX rose 142.26 points, or 0.91 percent, to 15,838.24.

Headlines: Citigroup CEO gets $24 million as compensation in 2018
Description: Citigroup Inc said on Friday its Chief Executive Michael Corbat will get a 4.35 percent raise, bringing his total compensation for 2018 to $24 million.

Headlines: Amazon places big bet on aspiring Tesla rival Rivian
Description: Amazon.com Inc said on Friday it would lead a $700 million investment in U.S. electric pickup truck startup Rivian Automotive LLC, in the e-commerce giant's biggest bet on technologies with potential to reshape the automotive sector.

Headlines: Progress in U.S.-China trade talks sparks world stock rally
Description: Progress in the U.S.-China trade talks helped send world stock markets broadly higher on Friday and pulled investors out of the safety of government bonds.

Headlines: Oil rises over 2 percent to 2019 highs on tightening supplies
Description: Oil prices rose more than 2 percent to their highest this year on Friday after an outage at Saudi Arabia's offshore oilfield boosted expectations for tightening supply, while progressing U.S.-Sino trade talks strengthened demand sentiment.

Headlines: After strong 2019 start for U.S. stocks, trade verdict looms
Description: Optimism about a U.S.-China trade agreement has helped drive U.S. stocks to more than two-month highs, creating a make-or-break moment for Wall Street as a year-long clash between the world's two largest economies comes to a head.

Headlines: Alphabet unit seeks share of property taxes for Toronto smart city
Description: Alphabet Inc's  Sidewalk Labs unit is proposing it get a share of property taxes, development fees, and the rising value of Toronto city land as part of a deal to build a smart city, according to the company's slide presentation made public on Friday.

Headlines: Hundreds of Chinese protest against BBVA in Madrid
Description: Hundreds of Chinese citizens waving Spanish and Chinese flags took to the streets of Madrid on Friday to protest against BBVA, saying the bank had blocked their accounts.

Headlines: Visa, Mastercard mull increasing fees for processing transactions: WSJ
Description: Visa Inc and Mastercard Inc, the two biggest U.S. card networks, are preparing to raise certain fees levied on U.S. merchants for processing transactions from this April, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Uber posts $50 billion in annual bookings as profit remains elusive ahead of IPO
Description: Uber Technologies Inc had $50 billion in total bookings for its ride-service and food-delivery businesses last year, a testament to the size and global reach of the company as it prepares to woo investors in one of the biggest public stock listings to date.

Headlines: U.S. drafts WTO reform to halt handouts for big and rich states
Description: The United States proposed a reform of the World Trade Organization on Friday that would slash the number of countries that are eligible for "special and differential treatment", a plan likely to be resisted by China, India and other countries.

Headlines: Citgo Petroleum to dismiss workers in Aruba over U.S. sanctions: prime minister
Description: A Citgo Petroleum Corp refining unit in Aruba plans to dismiss workers following sanctions imposed by the United States on Venezuela's state-run PDVSA, the parent company of the U.S. refining firm, the island's prime minister said on Friday.

Headlines: Trust in tailings? Vale dam disaster spurs investors into action
Description: Seeking assurances from Brazilian miner Vale by phone after a second deadly dam disaster in three years is not enough for Sasja Beslik. He plans to fly there himself to get answers.

Headlines: Sputtering auto production sinks U.S. manufacturing output
Description: U.S. manufacturing fell sharply in January, led by the biggest drop in motor vehicle production since the recession, the latest indication that the economy was losing momentum.

Headlines: Risk of U.S. corporate recession rises as earnings outlook dims
Description: The outlook for Wall Street earnings has deteriorated significantly in recent months, data shows, raising the risk that companies in the United States may slip into recession before its economy does - with Europe close behind.

Headlines: London bankers will need 'chaperones' for EU clients under no-deal Brexit: sources
Description: Investment banks have warned M&A teams in Britain they cannot pitch business to clients in the European Union if there is a no-deal Brexit without an EU "chaperone" sitting in on their meeting, sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Trump says may extend March 1 deadline for China trade deal
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday he may extend a March 1 deadline for reaching a trade deal with China while keeping current tariffs in place, adding that the negotiations are "very complicated."

Headlines: Wells Fargo's Tim Sloan set to appear twice before House panel: WSJ
Description: Wells Fargo & Co's Chief Executive Officer Tim Sloan is expected appear before the House Financial Services Committee alone in March this year, and then in April with several other banking heads, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: PepsiCo says investments to drive sales will dent profit this year
Description: PepsiCo Inc said on Friday increased investments in advertising and products aimed at boosting sales growth would lead to a fall in profit this year.

Headlines: U.S. factory output drops, autos fall the most since recession
Description: U.S. manufacturing output fell steeply in January as motor vehicle production posted its biggest fall since 2009, with declines in a broad range of goods likely to fuel fears of a sharp slowdown in factory activity.

Headlines: Nvidia forecasts demand rebound, Wall Street not so sure
Description: Nvidia Corp's forecast of a demand rebound by the end of the year calmed investor nerves and pushed its shares up 5 percent on Friday, but several Wall Street analysts said the outlook was "aggressive" given weak demand and the ongoing U.S.-China trade war.

Headlines: Air France CEO meets Dutch politicians on KLM unrest
Description: Air France-KLM chief executive Ben Smith on Friday met the Dutch finance and transport ministers, amid growing unrest at the company's vital KLM subsidiary over plans for tighter integration with its French parent.

Headlines: Factories to test world's 'delicate equilibrium'
Description: The world economy is caught in a "delicate equilibrium" between stabilization and a further downturn, according to Bank of England Governor Mark Carney, and that balance could look even shakier over the next few days.

Headlines: China says reached consensus on some key issues during U.S. trade talks
Description: China and the United States reached a consensus in principle on some key issues during trade talks in Beijing, state news agency Xinhua reported on Friday.

Headlines: U.S., Chinese officials to meet next week in Washington on trade: White House
Description: Officials from the United States and China will meet next week in Washington to continue working on a trade deal after having made progress in talks in Beijing this week, White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders said in a statement on Friday.

Headlines: Seizing on Huawei's troubles, Samsung bets big on network gear
Description: Samsung Electronics is pouring resources into its telecom network equipment business, aiming to capitalize on the security fears hobbling China's Huawei, according to company officials and other industry executives.

Headlines: Exclusive: Trafigura halts oil trade with Venezuela - source
Description: Global commodities firm Trafigura has decided to stop trading oil with Venezuela due to U.S. sanctions on the OPEC nation's energy sector, a source with direct knowledge of the matter said.

Headlines: China's President Xi meets top U.S. trade delegation officials
Description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin on Friday, following high-level negotiations aimed at striking a trade deal ahead of a March 1 deadline.

Headlines: China's Xi: trade talks with U.S. to continue in Washington next week
Description: Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday trade talks with the United States will continue in Washington next week and that he hopes the two sides will be able to reach a mutually beneficial deal in the upcoming negotiations, state media reported.

Headlines: Euronext confident 'dual-listed' trading to continue after Brexit
Description: The trading of dual-listed shares in Britain by European investors is expected to continue after Brexit, a senior official at pan-European exchange Euronext has said.

Headlines: European shares recover after weak data wobble
Description: European shares recovered on Friday after weak U.S. and Chinese economic data earlier sent global equity markets into a dive.

Headlines: German watchdog widens Deutsche monitor mandate over Danske
Description: German financial watchdog Bafin has extended the mandate of its monitor at Deutsche Bank over the bank's role in a money laundering scandal involving Danske Bank.

Headlines: Lloyds Bank hires Morgan Stanley banker Chalmers as CFO
Description: Britain's biggest mortgage lender Lloyds Banking Group has hired senior Morgan Stanley banker William Chalmers as its new chief financial officer.

Headlines: Hong Kong company sorry after 'vacuum cleaner for her' HSBC Valentine offer
Description: Hong Kong telecoms company HKT apologized after a Valentine's day deal it sent to HSBC staff offering discounted laptops "for him" but vacuum cleaners and kitchen appliances "for her" angered employees over its sexist implications.

Headlines: Exclusive: China offers to end market-distorting subsidies but won't say how
Description: China has pledged to end market-distorting subsidies for its domestic industries but offered no details on how it would achieve that goal, according to three people familiar with the U.S.-China trade talks in Beijing this week.

Headlines: Exclusive: Alibaba in talks on stake in China operations of Germany's Metro - sources
Description: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd is in talks with Germany's Metro about taking a stake in the German wholesaler's China operations, three sources told Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: Malaysian court allows ex-Goldman banker to return to U.S. to face 1MDB charges
Description: Roger Ng, a former Goldman Sachs Group Inc banker caught up in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) fraud scandal, will be allowed to return to the United States to face criminal charges against him there, a Malaysian court ruled on Friday.

Headlines: As Amazon drops New York City project, progressives claim a major coup
Description: U.S. Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez wasted no time on Thursday in calling Amazon's decision to scrap plans to build a major New York outpost with nearly $3 billion in city and state incentives a big victory for progressive politicians.

Headlines: Starbucks launches all-day dining cafe in China
Description: Starbucks Corp said on Friday it would launch a new all-day dining cafe in China which will serve a brunch menu and cocktails, as the world's largest coffee chain seeks to expand its retail offering in the increasingly competitive market.

Headlines: Feeling unwelcome, Amazon ditches plans for New York hub
Description: Amazon.com Inc abruptly scrapped plans to build a major outpost in New York that could have created 25,000 jobs, blaming opposition from local leaders upset by the nearly $3 billion in incentives promised by state and city politicians.

Headlines: Amazon's NY exit spurs reactions on money saved and jobs lost
Description: Amazon.com Inc's decision on Thursday to scrap its proposal to locate a second headquarters in the Queens borough of New York City ignited a sea of dueling reactions on Twitter, with some calling it a victory for working people while others said it meant that fewer people would work.

Headlines: Airbus A380 production halt to fuel transatlantic trade spat
Description: Airbus's decision to shut production of the A380 looks set to reignite a translatlantic trade row over mutual claims of illegal aircraft subsidies, even as Airbus implements a two-year plan to stop making the world's largest airliner.

Headlines: Mexico's Pemex, after downgrade, will make all debt payments: Lopez Obrador
Description: Mexican state oil firm Pemex will make all its debt payments, President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador said on Thursday, promising to shore up its finances after Moody's and Fitch downgraded its credit rating to one notch above junk.

Headlines: Prominent investors stock up on eBay, then activists flex muscle
Description: EBay Inc.'s stock price slumped for most of last year but a number of prominent hedge funds were so convinced that change is on the horizon for the e-commerce company that they established new or added to existing positions in the last months of 2018.

Headlines: Nvidia full-year sales outlook tops analyst views; shares rise
Description: Chip maker Nvidia Corp on Thursday forecast sales for its current fiscal year that topped Wall Street expectations, sending its shares up 8 percent in late trading.

Headlines: Chance of a U.S. recession up, number of Fed rate hikes down: Reuters poll
Description: There is a one-in-four chance of a U.S. recession in the next 12 months, a scenario that should keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates next month, according to a Reuters poll of economists who now expect only one rate hike this year.

Headlines: Big hedge funds dumped China stocks, Apple as market tumbled
Description: Prominent hedge fund managers sold out of Chinese technology stocks and dumped Silicon Valley majors such as Apple Inc and Facebook Inc while global stock markets cratered during the fourth quarter, according to securities filings released on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. shale executives predict oil production constraints to remain
Description: Drilling curbs by oil producers in the largest U.S. shale field will continue until transport bottlenecks ease and investors stop punishing companies for increasing capital spending, executives at an energy conference said on Thursday.

Headlines: CBS misses on profit, revenue but network hits streaming subscribers milestone
Description: CBS Corp generated less quarterly profit and revenue than Wall Street expected, but the network announced plans on Thursday to have 25 million streaming subscribers by 2022.

Headlines: U.S. trade envoys to meet China's Xi, no decision on deadline extension
Description: The Trump administration's top two negotiators in trade talks with China will meet on Friday with Chinese President Xi Jinping, but there has been no decision to extend a March 1 U.S. deadline for a deal, White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said on Thursday.

Headlines: Explainer: What's at stake in U.S.-China trade talks
Description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin are in Beijing this week as Chinese and American negotiators try to hammer out a trade deal to ease a trade war and avert an increase in U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods scheduled for March 2.

Headlines: Icahn to lobby Caesars Entertainment management for sale: WSJ
Description: Activist investor Carl Icahn plans to push management of casino operator Caesars Entertainment Corp to sell the company after it received at least two offers, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people it said were familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Berkshire trims Apple stake, adds Suncor and Red Hat, exits Oracle
Description: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc said it has trimmed its stake in iPhone maker Apple Inc, though none of the selling was Buffett's, and added positions in Canada's Suncor Energy Inc and software company Red Hat Inc.

Headlines: U.S. negotiating multibillion-dollar fine with Facebook: report
Description: The U.S. government and Facebook Inc are negotiating a settlement over the company's privacy lapses that could require the online social network to pay a multibillion-dollar fine, the Washington Post reported on Thursday.

Headlines: Eddie Lampert steps down as chairman of Sears' board
Description: Eddie Lampert will step down as chairman of Sears Holdings Corp's board, effective immediately, a company filing showed https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1310067/000119312519041193/d704657d8k.htm on Thursday.

Description: The U.S. Commerce Department is set to meet a Sunday deadline to deliver its recommendations to President Donald Trump on whether imported vehicles and parts pose a national security risk and to outline options on how to address the issue, officials said Thursday.

Description: The S&P 500 and the Dow slipped while the Nasdaq posted a slim gain on Thursday as investors struggled to square grim retail sales data with hopes that high-level talks in Beijing could resolve the ongoing U.S.-China trade dispute.

Headlines: U.S.-owned utility to close two coal plants, in blow to Trump
Description: The Tennessee Valley Authority voted on Thursday to close two aging coal-fired power plants, including one supplied by a company led by a major supporter of President Donald Trump, who had urged the U.S.-owned utility to keep it open.

Description: General Electric Co scrapped plans for a 12-story headquarters office tower on Boston's waterfront on Thursday, choosing instead to lease smaller buildings nearby and return $87 million in incentives to the state of Massachusetts.

Headlines: #FedValentines is back; roses, rates and job market slack
Description: In January, the Federal Reserve delivered what investors took as a kind of love letter, a rate-hike pause that sent stock markets soaring. On Valentine's Day, U.S. central bankers offered tender missives of a different sort.

Description: Charlie Munger, the longtime business partner of Warren Buffett at Berkshire Hathaway Inc, on Thursday criticized active fund managers, bankers and even Elon Musk as he urged investors to court simplicity and temper expectations for future returns.

Headlines: Ford CFO to retire: CNBC
Description: Ford Motor Co Chief Financial Officer Bob Shanks plans to  retire and is expected to stay through the end of the year, CNBC reported on Thursday, citing sources.

Description: Jeff Leonard slides behind the wheel of his burgundy Honda Accord and heads to a nearby Walmart Inc store, where he picks up the package of groceries waiting for him.

Description: A senior administration official said on Friday that U.S. national security depends on affordable energy, and slammed cartels when asked if President Donald Trump would support a bill targeting the OPEC production group's oil supply cuts.

Headlines: Boeing's tanker program records $2.31 billion in losses over 3 years
Description: Boeing Co said on Friday it had recorded reach-forward losses of $2.31 billion related to the U.S. Air Force KC-46A aerial refueling tanker over 2016, 2017 and 2018, bringing the total pre-tax cost of the program to $3.6 billion.

Headlines: Tesla cuts Model 3 price for second time this year
Description: Tesla Inc said on Wednesday it was lowering the price of its Model 3 sedan for the second time this year, moves that come in the wake of Tesla losing a tax credit that made its cars more affordable for U.S. buyers.

Headlines: U.S. prosecutors weigh if American Media violated immunity deal: Bloomberg
Description: U.S. prosecutors are reviewing whether National Enquirer parent company American Media Inc violated an earlier agreement granting it legal immunity in exchange for cooperation given the tabloid's handling of a story about Amazon.com Inc Chief Executive Jeff Bezos, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

Headlines: Ryanair CEO's new share option scheme targets doubling profit in 5 years
Description: Ryanair's Chief Executive Michael O'Leary could earn almost 100 million euros ($113 million) if he doubles either the profitability or share price of the carrier within five years, under a new share option scheme announced on Friday.

Headlines: GM Canada says Oshawa production stopped due to supplier strike
Description: Production at General Motors' plant in Oshawa, Ontario, stopped at approximately 12:30 p.m. EST on Friday, a spokesman said, after the U.S. automaker exhausted its on-hand supply of seats from Lear Corp, where workers are striking.

Headlines: German banks maneuver in Washington to temper Russia sanction risk
Description: German banks are seeking to blunt any fresh U.S. sanctions against Russia so they can continue existing business with Russian clients, according to an internal briefing paper prepared by a financial industry lobby group.

Headlines: Staff wanted: pensioners welcome, but anyone, really
Description: Zsuzsanna Czeizel told herself she'd never work again after she retired in 2012. But since October, she's held a job -- scanning boxes of sweets in a large warehouse near Budapest.

Headlines: Barclays to shift some credit and equity derivatives sales jobs to Paris: sources
Description: Barclays is shifting some jobs in its London-based credit and equity derivatives sales teams to Paris as it reorganizes its operations ahead of Brexit, two sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Exclusive: Russia's Sechin raises pressure on Putin to end OPEC deal
Description: Igor Sechin, head of Russian oil giant Rosneft and one of Vladimir Putin's closest allies, has written to the Russian president saying Moscow's deal with OPEC to cut oil output is a strategic threat and plays into the hands of the United States.

Headlines: German prosecutors mull dieselgate fine for auto supplier Bosch
Description: Prosecutors in the German city of Stuttgart are looking into a possible fine for auto supplier Robert Bosch for providing Volkswagen with engine management software that the carmaker used to cheat vehicle emissions tests in 2015.

Headlines: Short seller Carson Block targets medical device company Inogen
Description: Prominent short seller Carson Block is saying that medical device company Inogen Inc has inflated the size of its markets and expects the stock price to fall.

Headlines: Sprint sues AT&T over 5G branding
Description: Sprint Corp sued AT&T Inc late on Thursday, saying it was misleading consumers into believing that they were using fifth generation or 5G wireless network, a technology that has not yet been widely deployed.

Headlines: Explainer: Germany, France face hurdles in push to rewrite EU antitrust rules
Description: Germany and France want to overhaul EU mergers rules following the European Commission's veto of efforts by Siemens and Alstom to create a European rail champion to compete with larger foreign rivals.

Headlines: To guide or not to guide? Fed 'dots' complicate message
Description: U.S. central bankers say clear communication is important, with economic research showing that if the public understands what the Federal Reserve is doing, monetary policy works better and the economy does better.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. considers withdrawal of zero tariffs for India - sources
Description: India could lose a vital U.S. trade concession, under which it enjoys zero tariffs on $5.6 billion of exports to the United States, amid a widening dispute over its trade and investment policies, people with close knowledge of the matter said.

Headlines: Activist Elliott tells Pernod there is still work to do
Description: Activist investor Elliott kept up the pressure on French spirits group Pernod Ricard, welcoming this week's first-half results but calling for boardroom changes and better margins.

Headlines: Shell leads cash race but Exxon catching up
Description: Royal Dutch Shell widened its lead over Exxon Mobil as king of cash among the world's top oil and gas companies last year but its U.S. rival could catch up with its investment drive in new production.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank merger talk 'speculation': German finance minister
Description: German Finance Minister Olaf Scholz said on Friday he was in talks with banks about their future and called reports of a merger of Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank "speculation".

Headlines: Crypto bear market threatens to last as potential token supply weighs
Description: Cryptocurrencies may be facing a prolonged bear market.

Headlines: Fifty years on, Boeing's 747 clings to life as cargo carrier
Description: Boeing's 747 jumbo jet, an aircraft that democratized global air travel in the 1970s but fell behind modern twin-engine passenger jets, has bounced back from near death to mark its 50-year flying anniversary on Saturday, thanks to a cargo market boom fueled by online shopping.

Headlines: Brookfield in talks with India's Reliance Industries to buy tower, fibre assets: report
Description: Canadian private equity firm Brookfield Asset Management is in preliminary talks with India's Reliance Industries to buy a stake in its optical fibre and telecom tower assets, The Times of India newspaper reported on Friday.

Headlines: Bank of America appoints head of new EU unit in Brexit move
Description: Bank of America Merrill Lynch has named Sanaz Zaimi as head of its new Paris-based European Union broker-dealer unit BofA Securities Europe, the U.S. bank said on Friday.

Headlines: Sony stock jumps after first-ever share buyback announcement
Description: Sony Corp announced its first-ever major share buyback on Friday, worth 100 billion yen ($910 million), helping its stock recover from a hammering days earlier when investors freaked over lackluster earnings.

Headlines: Amazon's Bezos says National Enquirer owner tried to blackmail him
Description: Jeff Bezos, chief executive of Amazon.com Inc, has accused the owner of the National Enquirer of trying to blackmail him with the threat of publishing "intimate photos" he allegedly sent to his girlfriend unless he said in public that the supermarket tabloid's reporting on him was not politically motivated.

Headlines: No talks between Trump and China's Xi before trade deadline
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday he did not plan to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping before a March 1 deadline set by the two countries to achieve a trade deal.

Headlines: Pernod defends its performance in light of new Elliott criticism
Description: Drinks group Pernod Ricard defended its performance and strategy on Friday, in the light of renewed criticism of the company from activist fund Elliott.

Headlines: Explainer: Why Shanghai's new Nasdaq-style tech board may be a game-changer
Description: The detailed rules for a Nasdaq-style start-up board in Shanghai have fueled hopes among early-stage companies the new regime could bring about positive changes in China's stance towards raising equity that investors have been seeking.

Headlines: Starbucks 'unlikely' to be overtaken in China by Luckin in 2019: CEO
Description: Starbucks Corp is unlikely to cede its leading position in China, the company's fastest-growing major market, to Chinese startup Luckin in 2019, Starbucks CEO Kevin Johnson said in an interview on Thursday.

Headlines: Australia's bruised big banks offered respite in inquiry wash-up
Description: After a year of bruising interrogation, Australia's oligopoly banking system has emerged from a government-appointed inquiry with reputations tarnished and some top executives removed - but also an unexpected opportunity to rebuild.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler paid $77 million in U.S. fuel economy penalties in 2018
Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV told Reuters on Thursday it paid $77 million in U.S. civil penalties late last year for failing to meet 2016 model year fuel economy requirements, the first significant sign the industry is facing hurdles meeting rising emissions rules.

Headlines: U.S. bankruptcy judge approves sale of Sears to Chairman Lampert
Description: A U.S. bankruptcy judge on Thursday approved Sears Holdings Corp Chairman Edward Lampert's $5.2 billion takeover of the beleaguered retailer, allowing the department store chain to avert liquidation and preserve tens of thousands of jobs.

Headlines: Fed's Bullard: 'Restrictive' U.S. policy likely curbing inflation
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve's interest rate increase in December likely tipped monetary policy into a restrictive setting that may be pushing the economy farther from one of the Fed's key goals, James Bullard, president of the St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank, said on Thursday.

Headlines: Fed's Bullard considers current U.S. rate setting 'slightly restrictive'
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve's interest rate increase in December likely tipped monetary policy into slightly restrictive territory, a step beyond the neutral level policymakers had hoped to hit, St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank President James Bullard said on Thursday.

Headlines: Renault to alert prosecutors over ex-CEO Ghosn's wedding costs
Description: Renault has found evidence that it paid part of Carlos Ghosn's wedding costs and is preparing to turn the investigation over to prosecutors, two weeks after the French carmaker's scandal-hit chairman and chief executive was forced out.

Headlines: J&J becomes first drugmaker to add prices to television ads
Description: Johnson & Johnson said on Thursday it will start adding the price of its medicines to television commercials by next month, becoming the first drugmaker to heed a call by U.S. President Donald Trump for price transparency of drugs advertised directly to consumers on TV.

Headlines: Mattel posts surprise profit as Barbie makeover lifts sales
Description: Mattel Inc posted a surprise fourth-quarter profit on Thursday, as the toymaker benefited from a makeover of its iconic Barbie doll, while keeping a tight lid on costs, sending its shares soaring 19 percent in extended trading.

Headlines: Chevron ties executive pay to methane and flaring reduction targets
Description: Chevron Corp plans to set greenhouse gas emissions targets and tie executive compensation and rank-and-file bonuses to the reductions, the oil major said in its latest climate report released on Thursday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Dell explores sale of cybersecurity company SecureWorks - sources
Description: Computer maker Dell Technologies Inc is exploring a sale of SecureWorks Corp, a U.S. provider of cybersecurity services with a market value of close to $2 billion, people familiar with the matter said on Thursday.

Headlines: BB&T to buy SunTrust in biggest U.S. bank deal in a decade
Description: A more permissive regulatory environment culminated on Thursday in the biggest bank merger since the 2007-2009 financial crisis, and more deals are likely, analysts and investors said.

Headlines: Wall Street slides on renewed U.S.-China trade fears
Description: Wall Street stocks sank on Thursday as worries that the United States and China would not be able to reach a trade deal increased concerns about slowing global economic growth.

Headlines: Barclays hires internet banker from Deutsche Bank
Description: Barclays Plc said on Thursday it hired Riaz Ladhabhoy, an investment banker from Deutsche Bank to be the co-head of internet banking in the Americas, a move that comes ahead of a wave of IPOs expected in the sector this year.

Headlines: Ford investing $1 billion, adding 500 jobs in Chicago
Description: Ford Motor Co said on Thursday it is investing more than $1 billion in its Chicago operations and adding 500 jobs as it prepares to launch three new SUVs this year and end production of the Taurus.

Headlines: Shares stumble on fresh fears about global growth, trade
Description: Stocks pulled back sharply around the world on Thursday on fears of a global growth slowdown spreading to Europe and worry about the chances for a resolution of U.S.-China trade tensions anytime soon, while the U.S. dollar strengthened for a sixth session against a basket of currencies.

Headlines: New Zealand PM says exporters could suffer due to U.S.-China trade tensions
Description: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said on Friday that trade tensions between the U.S. and China, which is New Zealand's top trading partner, could affect exporters in the country and hurt its economy.

Headlines: Trump confirms he won't meet with China's Xi before March 1 trade deadline
Description: President Donald Trump confirmed on Thursday that he did not plan to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping before a March 1 deadline set by the two countries to achieve a trade deal.

Headlines: Apple to contribute to U.S. teen's education for spotting FaceTime bug
Description: Apple Inc on Thursday rolled out software updates to iPhones to fix a privacy issue in its FaceTime video calling service, and said it would contribute toward the education of the Arizona teenager who discovered the problem.

Headlines: Airbus hit by jet cancellations as A380 shutdown looms
Description: Airbus on Thursday reported the cancellation of orders worth $4 billion, dominated by 8 A380 aircraft, highlighting an increasingly bleak picture for the world's largest airliner as preparations to close production gather pace amid weak demand.

Headlines: Huawei open to European supervision: executive in speech
Description: Chinese telecoms giant Huawei wants cybersecurity to be viewed as a technical rather than ideological issue and is open to supervision by European governments to prove the point, a senior company executive is expected to say on Thursday evening.

Headlines: France 'categorically denies' Nikkei report on Renault-Nissan stakes
Description: France's finance ministry denied on Thursday a report from Japanese news outlet Nikkei that the French government had informed Tokyo it was open to considering reducing Renault's stake in Nissan Motor.

Description: Twitter Inc forecast that revenue in the first quarter would be weaker than expected while full-year operating costs would rise, sending shares down more than 10 percent in midday trading on Thursday.

Description: Fiat Chrysler (FCA) shares fell 12 percent on Thursday after weaker-than-expected guidance for profits and industrial free cash flow this year raised doubts about the Italian-American carmaker's longer-term targets.

Headlines: Volvo Cars feels margin pressure from U.S.-China tariff war
Description: Chinese-owned Volvo Cars reported a fall in 2018 profit margins as a prolonged trade war between Washington and Beijing pushed up costs and resulted in pricing pressure in its main market China.

Description: Volvo Cars is talking to Chinese and U.S. tech investors as the company seeks external finance for its Polestar performance electric car brand, the Swedish company's chief said on Thursday.

Headlines: Italy denies it will ban Huawei, ZTE from its 5G plans
Description: Italy has denied a report it will ban China's Huawei Technologies and ZTE Corp from playing a role in building its fifth-generation mobile phone network.

Description: Denmark's ATP pension fund, which handles the retirement savings of most Danes, has increased its stake in Danske Bank, which is mired in a money laundering scandal, saying it wants to be an active owner.

Description: Thomas Cook said it was willing to sell its profitable airline business to raise cash to fund its fight back from losses racked up in 2018 and to cope with a tough year ahead, sending the travel group's shares 12 percent higher.

Description: Facebook's reported plans to merge the infrastructure of its Messenger, WhatsApp and Instagram services would, if implemented, face antitrust scrutiny in Germany, the head of the Federal Cartel Office said on Thursday.

Description: Uncertainty caused by the expansion of U.S. sanctions on Russia last year has pushed companies' share prices lower, prompting investment bankers to suggest their clients should delist from local and international exchanges.

Description: Two Democratic U.S. Senators - one of whom is a presidential candidate - renewed their calls on Thursday for a probe by the Senate banking committee into Deutsche Bank laundering allegations, according to a letter seen by Reuters.

Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV and Robert Bosch have agreed to pay lawyers representing owners of U.S. diesel vehicles $66 million in fees and costs, according to court filing on Wednesday and people briefed on the matter.

Description: French carmaker Renault needs to show "total transparency" as it probes its business practices, including a sponsorship deal stuck with the Chateau de Versailles, finance minister Bruno Le Maire said on Thursday.

Description: U.S. shared workspace provider WeWork plans to launch in South African later this year, it said on Thursday, a move that would mark the first African expansion for the $47 billion New York-based company.

Headlines: Pernod CEO hopes new strategy plan will please all its shareholders
Description: The boss of Pernod Ricard said on Thursday that the priority of the French spirits group, which is under pressure from activist investor Elliott, was to create long-term value and added he had no plans to sell its champagne assets.

Headlines: Qantas cancels order for 8 Airbus A380s amid doubts on jet's future
Description: Australia's Qantas Airways Ltd said on Thursday it formally canceled a longstanding order for eight Airbus SE  A380 superjumbo jets.

Headlines: Long, strange trip: How U.S. ethanol reaches China tariff-free
Description: In June, the High Seas tanker ship loaded up on ethanol in Texas and set off for Asia.

Headlines: California utility PG&E vows more power shutdowns to prevent wildfire
Description: California utility PG&E Corp plans to increase the controversial practice of shutting off the power to communities at risk of wildfire when dangerous conditions such as high winds and dry heat are present.

Headlines: Amazon changes business structures in India to bring big seller back: sources
Description: One of the biggest sellers on Amazon.com Inc's India website has returned after the online retail giant changed its business structures to comply with new federal e-commerce curbs that took effect last week, two sources told Reuters.

Headlines: Novartis CEO lauds Trump administration plan to overhaul rebates
Description: Novartis AG Chief Executive Vas Narasimhan said his company's prescription drug prices have been "flat to negative" over the last three years, and directed blame for high costs for U.S. patients on industry middlemen that manage drug benefits.

Headlines: Bank branches lose influence in battle for U.S. market share: study
Description: In a world with fewer branches, banks will need to rely more heavily on advertising to win market share, according to a study released on Thursday by McKinsey.

Headlines: SoftBank Group adds $14 billion to market value as shares soar on buyback, third-quarter profit
Description: SoftBank Group Corp shares jumped 17 percent on Thursday, adding $14 billion to the Japanese tech investment giant's market value, after it unveiled a record share buyback and a surge in quarterly operating profit.

Headlines: GM's incentive plan for Cruise chief points to IPO: SEC filing
Description: General Motors Co on Wednesday outlined an incentive plan for the head of its self-driving car unit that points the way toward a possible initial public offering for the business.

Headlines: Weak U.S. profit picture may not be so bad: Credit Suisse
Description: As some market watchers brace for a potential U.S. earnings recession this year, one prominent equity strategist says the picture is not as bad as feared.

Headlines: Spotify posts first ever operating profit, but cautious outlook for 2019
Description: Spotify posted its first ever quarterly operating profit on Wednesday driven by a strong gross margin and slower-than-expected headcount growth, but it warned of a loss in 2019 and issued modest forecasts which disappointed investors.

Headlines: Chipotle's fresh food campaign drives profit beat, shares surge
Description: Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc topped Wall Street forecasts for quarterly earnings as aggressive marketing helped lure more diners and boost online orders, sending its shares up 10 percent in after-hours trading on Wednesday.

Headlines: GoPro tops revenue estimates, posts first profit in five quarters
Description: GoPro Inc reported its first profit in five quarters on Wednesday and topped Wall Street estimates for revenue, as it cut costs and saw strong demand for the latest action cameras from its flagship HERO line.

Headlines: At least four pharma CEOs to testify at Senate drug pricing hearing
Description: Drugmakers Pfizer Inc, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co and Sanofi SA said on Wednesday that their chief executives plan to testify at a Senate hearing on rising prescription drug prices later this month.

Headlines: Wall Street rally pauses after underwhelming revenue forecasts
Description: U.S. stocks edged lower on Wednesday as videogame makers gave disappointing revenue forecasts and investors awaited developments on U.S.-China trade relations.

Headlines: Scoot over Microsoft: Apple again the most valuable U.S. company
Description: Apple won back its crown as the most valuable publicly listed U.S. company on Wednesday, ending the session with a market capitalization above recent leaders Microsoft and Amazon.com.

Headlines: Stocks recede from two-month highs; Aussie dollar tanks
Description: The Australian dollar tumbled on Wednesday after the country's central bank signaled a possible interest-rate cut in the latest indication that a global economic slowdown is tilting policymakers toward looser monetary policy, while a gauge of world equity markets edged off two-month highs.

Headlines: High-margin pickup trucks drive GM profit, shares rise
Description: General Motors Co on Wednesday reported a quarterly profit that exceeded Wall Street expectations, thanks to high-margin pickup trucks and small SUVs in the U.S. market and cost cutting.

Headlines: Zynga bookings beat estimates as turnaround takes hold
Description: Zynga Inc on Wednesday forecast quarterly bookings above analysts' estimates after beating expectations for the fourth quarter, suggesting that the game developer was benefiting from its mobile push.

Description: The European Commission's decision to block a tie-up between Alstom and Germany's Siemens is fueling speculation over possible merger talks between the French rail business and Canada's Bombardier, lifting both companies' shares on Wednesday.

Headlines: Germany to seek antitrust reform in 2020 EU presidency: source
Description: Germany will seek to reform competition law during its European Union presidency in 2020, a government source told Reuters on Wednesday, hours after antitrust regulators blocked a rail deal between Siemens and Alstom.

Headlines: U.S. trade deficit narrows in November as imports decline
Description: The U.S. trade deficit fell for the first time in six months in November as cheaper oil and higher domestic petroleum production helped to curb the country's import bill, leading economists to boost their economic growth estimates for the fourth quarter.

Headlines: French Senate rejects tougher telecoms controls despite U.S. Huawei warning
Description: The French Senate rejected on Wednesday proposed legislation aimed at toughening checks on telecoms equipment, following a U.S. warning about Chinese telecoms giant Huawei.

Headlines: Factbox: Franco-German mergers: a difficult history
Description: Berlin and Paris are working to change European competition rules to facilitate large cross-border mergers, after the European Union blocked Siemens and Alstom from merging their rail businesses on Wednesday.

Headlines: Winter storms, U.S. shutdown boost demand for private jets
Description: Harsh winter weather and the partial U.S. government shutdown boosted demand for private jets in January, according to three business aviation companies that recently reported an uptick last month in deep-pocketed travelers seeking alternatives to commercial flying.

Headlines: United to add premium seats on regional and mainline jets
Description: United Airlines said on Wednesday it was adding 1,600 premium seats to nearly 250 international and domestic aircraft, including the introduction of a first-class cabin on 50 Bombardier Inc regional jets.

Headlines: Daimler cuts dividend as downturn, R&D costs hit Mercedes
Description: Daimler cut its dividend on Wednesday after fourth-quarter operating profit plunged by 22 percent, hit by trade wars, rising costs for developing electric cars and an industry downturn that has dented even the most profitable carmakers.

Headlines: Exclusive: Facing crackdown in Canada, drugmakers offered billions in price cuts
Description: Canadian pharmaceutical industry lobby groups, in an effort to head off a planned crackdown on prescription drug prices, offered to give up C$8.6 billion ($6.6 billion) in revenue over 10 years, freeze prices or reduce the cost of treating rare diseases, according to interviews and documents seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Carlyle expects 26 percent jump in 2019 fee earnings
Description: Private equity firm Carlyle Group LP said on Wednesday it expects to grow the amount it earns from management fees by more than a quarter in 2019, as it wraps up a $100 billion fundraising push.

Headlines: Eli Lilly backs U.S. proposal on drug rebates to lower costs
Description: Eli Lilly and Co on Wednesday embraced a U.S. government proposal to end a decades-old system of rebates drugmakers make to industry middlemen, saying it could lower the cost of insulin and other prescription drugs for patients.

Headlines: Boeing says aircraft demand supports even faster 737 production
Description: A top Boeing Co executive said on Wednesday market demand was strong enough to support an even higher production rate of 63 single-aisle 737 aircraft per month but such an increase depends more on suppliers being able to keep up.

Headlines: UBS gets approval to shift 32 billion euros of assets from Britain
Description: UBS has received approval from a London court to move up to 32 billion euros ($36.44 billion) in assets from Britain to Germany as part of plans to keep business in the European Union after Brexit.

Headlines: Snap shares soar as Android app shows promise
Description: Shares of Snap Inc rose 26 percent on Wednesday, after the maker of Snapchat messaging app arrested a fall in users on Apple devices and drew a series of favorable reviews from analysts for its progress with a new Android app.

Headlines: China sales buoy Toyota's profit, but U.S. weakness persists
Description: Toyota Motor Corp's quarterly profit edged up as demand for its bread-and-butter car models from cost-conscious Chinese buyers helped offset bleak North American sales, although the firm's shares slipped as it cut its annual net income outlook.

Headlines: Return of French farmer's case keeps Monsanto in legal spotlight
Description: A decade-old lawsuit in which a French farmer with neurological problems accuses Monsanto of not providing adequate safety warnings for a weedkiller returns to court on Wednesday, adding to health claims faced by the Bayer-owned firm.

Headlines: German ministers meet as U.S. urges Huawei exclusion: sources
Description: German ministers discussed on Wednesday how to safeguard security in future 5G mobile networks, government sources said, amid intense debate over whether to shut China's Huawei Technologies out of the market.

Headlines: SoftBank's Son unveils $5.5 billion buyback, laments share price
Description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp announced a $5.5 billion share buyback on Wednesday as it reported a 60 percent increase in quarterly operating profit buoyed by rising valuations for its technology investments.

Headlines: Etihad approaches banks for over $500 million for Boeing deliveries: sources
Description: Abu Dhabi’s Etihad Airways has approached banks to raise over $500 million to finance four Boeing 787 Dreamliners it previously ordered, two sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Brazil's Azul to replace more E-Jets with Airbus planes in 2019
Description: Brazilian airline Azul SA will replace more of its aging E-Jet fleet, made by local manufacturer Embraer SA, with larger planes from Airbus SE this year, the carrier said in a securities filing on Wednesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Huawei needs 3-5 years to resolve British security fears - letter
Description: A $2 billion effort by China's Huawei to address security issues raised in a British government report last year will take between three and five years to produce results, according to a company letter to British lawmakers seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Germany presses for changes in EU competition rules after Siemens/Alstom deal blocked
Description: Europe should change its competition rules to facilitate cross-border mergers and create European champions which can compete with rivals from China and the United States, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Bouygues confident about Alstom prospects despite EU ruling
Description: French conglomerate Bouygues, which has a 28 percent stake in Alstom, said it regretted the European Union's decision to veto a merger between Alstom and Siemens but added it was confident over Alstom's prospects.

Headlines: Volvo to recall 167,000 cars due to possible tailgate fault
Description: Volvo Cars said on Wednesday it would recall 167,000 of its XC60 model vehicles due to a possible fault with the electric tailgate mechanism.

Headlines: Reviving M&A hopes, Uniper starts open-minded talks with Fortum
Description: Uniper said on Wednesday nothing was off limits in fresh talks with Finland's Fortum, its top shareholder, renewing investor hopes for a full takeover of the 9.7 billion euro ($11.1 billion) German energy group.

Headlines: Siemens regrets European decision to block rail merger with Alstom
Description: Siemens said it regretted the European Commission's decision to block the merger of its rail business with France's Alstom and would now assess "all options" for the future of its own train operations.

Headlines: Nippon Steel cuts full-year profit forecast by 6 percent on lower output

Headlines: Daimler, Geely in talks to expand cooperation into a 'bigger dimension'

Headlines: Roche, joining rivals, donates hemophilia drug to boost access
Description: Switzerland's Roche will donate its new hemophilia A drug Hemlibra to a World Hemophilia Federation program, it said on Wednesday, joining rivals who also back the effort to help patients in developing countries who face treatment hurdles.

Headlines: Credit Suisse warns of higher tax rate under new U.S. rules
Description: Credit Suisse expects a higher tax rate for 2018 than previously forecast, it said on Wednesday, citing U.S. tax changes aimed at preventing companies from shifting profits abroad.

Description: The United States sees the European Union as its top priority in a global effort to convince allies not to buy Huawei equipment for next-generation mobile networks, a U.S. State Department Official said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Sunshine and soccer helped Carlsberg return to growth in 2018
Description: Danish brewer Carlsberg's sales rose last year for the first time in three years, helped by strength in China and the long, hot summer in Northern Europe and Russia, but it warned it expects slower growth in 2019.

Headlines: Bet everything on electric: Inside Volkswagen's radical strategy shift

Headlines: German ministers meeting to discuss how to deal with Huawei in 5G auction: source
Description: German ministers are meeting on Wednesday to discuss how to deal with China's Huawei Technologies in building Germany's 5G network, a government source told Reuters.

Headlines: Judge pauses lawsuits against cryptocurrency company Quadriga
Description: A cryptocurrency platform that lost access to millions of dollars when its founder died with sole knowledge of company passwords has been granted a temporary reprieve from creditor lawsuits.

Headlines: 1970s-era musicians sue Sony, UMG to reclaim song rights

Description: (This February 4 story corrects headline and paragraphs 1, 4 to show Wirth is eligible to earn $19 million, not "more than $28 million".)

Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV said on Tuesday it would recall 882,000 pickup trucks worldwide in two new recalls to address steering and pedal issues.

Description: A dimming economic outlook and massive street protests against President Emmanuel Macron have made France less attractive for U.S. companies with investments in the country, a survey showed.

Description: U.S. grains trader Archer Daniels Midland Co on Tuesday  reported lower-than-expected fourth-quarter 2018 earnings as the U.S.-China trade war roiled global agriculture, sending its shares down more than 6 percent.

Headlines: Appaloosa steps up pressure on Allergan to split chairman, CEO roles
Description: Hedge fund Appaloosa LP on Tuesday urged pharmaceutical company Allergan Plc  to split its chairman and chief executive roles, arguing that an independent chair could help CEO Brent Saunders boost the company's sagging share price.

Description: A marketing blitz involving supermodels and Instagram helped Ralph Lauren woo more customers and report another quarter of better-than-expected sales and earnings, sending its shares up over 12 percent on Tuesday.

Description: The unlikely combination of freshwater fish and cannabis is producing outsized medical marijuana crops that Green Relief Inc aims to capitalize on, as the Canadian company plots a stock market listing and global expansion.

Description: Mickey McMaster is on his 12th pickup truck.

Description: More investors who typically make passive bets flexed their muscles last year and helped push a total of 922 companies to perform better by improving operations and capital allocation, data from research group Activist Insight show.

Description: HMV, the British music retailer that collapsed after Christmas, has been sold to the owner of Canada's Sunrise Records in a deal that will save 100 stores and 1,487 jobs, its joint administrators said on Tuesday.
