Description: GlaxoSmithKline bolstered its cancer drug development pipeline on Tuesday, agreeing to pay up to 3.7 billion euros ($4.2 billion) to Germany's Merck KGaA for the rights to a next-generation immunotherapy.

Description: The Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi alliance will tie up with Alphabet Inc's Google to develop autonomous taxis and other services using self-driving vehicles, the Nikkei reported on Tuesday.

Headlines: General Electric to pay $57 million for missing French job target: ministry
Description: General Electric is to pay 50 million euros ($57 million) for failing to meet a job creation target agreed when it took over French group Alstom's energy business, the French Finance Ministry said on Tuesday.

Headlines: German state ready to buy company stakes to protect core industry
Description: Germany's government could take stakes in key domestic companies to prevent foreign takeovers, its Economy Minister said on Tuesday, presenting a marked shift in industrial strategy he said was needed to safeguard the country's prosperity.

Description: Amazon.com Inc's grocery service is slowly returning on its India website after the online retail giant faced disruption from revised e-commerce curbs which kicked in on Feb. 1.

Description: Banks, insurers and other financial firms in Britain may have to come up with tougher targets for getting women into top jobs, UK financial services minister John Glen said on Tuesday.

Description: Volkswagen is in talks with Swedish institutional investors AMF, AP Fund 1 and 4, Investor AB and Folksam about being cornerstone shareholders in the dual listing of its trucks unit Traton in Stockholm and Frankfurt, people familiar with the talks said.

Description: Indian steel firms are putting pressure on the nation's government to impose higher duties on imports as trade disputes and a global economic slowdown divert surplus Asian steel stocks to India, industry executives and government sources said.

Headlines: Exclusive: Fed could raise rates as much as twice this year - BlackRock's Rieder
Description: The Federal Reserve wants to raise interest rates one to two more times this year and will do so if inflation gathers steam, BlackRock Inc's Rick Rieder told Reuters this week.

Description: German Chancellor Angela Merkel said on Tuesday Germany needs guarantees that China's Huawei Technologies will not hand over data to the Chinese state before the telecoms equipment supplier can participate in building its 5G network.

Description: German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday that only secure technology could be installed to build Germany's 5G network, adding that clear rules applied to all providers.

Description: Nissan Motor said on Tuesday it will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on April 8 to formally discharge its ex-chairman Carlos Ghosn following his arrest on  financial misconduct charges.

One is a telecom equipment seller that operated in Tehran; the other is that firm's owner, a holding company registered in Mauritius.

Headlines: Move aside, backseat driver! New tech at CES monitors you inside car
Description: As vehicles get smarter, your car will be keeping eyes on you.

Headlines: HNA sells majority stake in Manhattan building in $422 million deal
Description: Chinese conglomerate HNA Group [HNAIRC.UL] on Wednesday said it had sold a majority stake in a Manhattan building in a $422 million deal, the latest in a slew of asset disposals undertaken by the group to ease an intensifying cash crunch.

Headlines: China's approval of DowDuPont soy poses challenge to Bayer
Description: China's approval of imports of a DowDuPont Inc  genetically modified soybean puts rival Bayer AG  on the defensive, investors and analysts said, as U.S. farmers will have a new choice when planting their most valuable agricultural export.

Headlines: Factbox: What can the state of California do about PG&E?
Description: California utility PG&E Corp  is exploring filing some or all of its business for bankruptcy protection as it could face billions of dollars in potential liabilities if it is held responsible for fatal wildfires in 2018 and 2017, people familiar with the matter have told Reuters.

Headlines: World Bank's Kim to join Global Infrastructure Partners
Description: World Bank Group President Jim Yong Kim will join Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), a private equity fund that invests in projects in wealthy and developing countries, the firm said on Tuesday, a day after Kim's shock resignation from the bank.

Headlines: U.S. government official says trade talks with China continuing Wednesday
Description: Trade talks between China and the United States will continue on Wednesday, a U.S. government official told reporters.

Headlines: U.S.-China trade talks extended amid some signs of progress
Description: The United States and China will continue trade talks in Beijing for an unscheduled third day, U.S. officials said on Tuesday amid signs of progress on issues including purchases of U.S. farm and energy commodities and increased access to China's markets.

Headlines: Venezuela congress slams oil deals with U.S., French companies
Description: Venezuela's opposition-run congress on Tuesday issued a resolution calling deals between state-run oil company PDVSA [PDVSA.UL] and U.S. and French companies announced this week illegal, since they had not been sent to lawmakers for approval.

Headlines: LG Electronics sees 80 percent drop in fourth-quarter profit; analysts point to thinning TV margins
Description: South Korea's LG Electronics Inc  said on Tuesday its fourth-quarter operating profit likely plummeted 80 percent from the same period a year earlier, falling well below analyst expectations.

Headlines: China gives long-awaited GM crop approvals amid U.S. trade talks
Description: China approved five genetically modified (GM) crops for import on Tuesday, the first in about 18 months in a move that could boost its overseas grains purchases and ease pressure from the United States to open its markets to more farm goods.

Headlines: Factbox: China approves new GMO soybean, corn and canola traits
Description: China approved five genetically modified crops for import on Tuesday, the first in about 18 months, as representatives from the Asian country and the United States met in face-to-face talks to try to resolve trade disagreements.

Headlines: Apple, Facebook propel Wall Street to three-week peak
Description: The S&P 500 jumped to a three-week high on Tuesday, led by Apple, Amazon, Facebook and industrial shares on bets that the United States and China would strike a deal to end their trade war.

Headlines: On brink of demise, Sears to reconsider billionaire chairman's bid
Description: Sears Holdings Corp agreed on Tuesday to consider a revised takeover bid from billionaire Chairman Edward Lampert, temporarily staving off a liquidation that would have spelled the end of the 126-year-old U.S. department-store chain.

Headlines: Kroger plans $1.2 billion debt offering
Description: U.S. supermarket chain Kroger Co  said on Tuesday it plans to raise $1.2 billion through a debt offering, according to a U.S. regulatory filing https://bit.ly/2QxmZAN.

Headlines: U.S. retail imports level off after China tariff avoidance rush
Description: Imports at major U.S. container ports are leveling off after retailers' months-long rush to bring in Chinese merchandise before higher tariffs hit, according to a retail trade report issued on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. delegation member says trade talks with China to continue Wednesday
Description: Trade talks between the United States and China will continue on Wednesday, U.S. delegation member Steven Winberg said on Tuesday, as the world's two largest economies seek to resolve a bitter trade dispute.

Headlines: Sears workers demand hardship fund after Toys 'R' Us success
Description: As Sears Holdings Corp teeters on the brink of liquidation, its employees are pushing for a hardship fund they hope can replicate the success of bankrupt retailer Toys 'R' Us, whose workers collected $20 million in severance pay from its former owners.

Headlines: Mercedes claims luxury car crown as analysts eye challenger Tesla
Description: Mercedes-Benz sold 2.31 million passenger cars last year, likely enough to make it the top-selling premium automotive brand in 2018, although some analysts are questioning how much longer German manufacturers can dominate the luxury car industry.

Headlines: GM did not heed call to keep Oshawa, Ontario plant open: union boss
Description: The head of Canada's auto union blasted General Motors Co on Tuesday for pushing ahead with plans to phase out work at its Oshawa, Ontario, assembly plant despite calls by workers and politicians in Canada to find a new vehicle to build there.

Headlines: PG&E falls further after S&P cuts credit rating to junk
Description: PG&E Corp's shares fell 14 percent on Tuesday, after S&P Global stripped the California power company of its investment-grade credit rating in the face of massive claims stemming from deadly wildfires.

Headlines: Prospect of U.S. profit drop rises for investors
Description: Investors are growing more fearful that U.S. companies' profits could shrink this year following Apple's warning of soft demand in China, coupled with mounting evidence of a drag from tariffs, a global slowdown and fading tailwinds from tax cuts.

Headlines: Nissan's Ghosn claims innocence in first appearance since November arrest
Description: Ousted Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn declared his innocence in his first public appearance since his November arrest, telling a Tokyo court on Tuesday that he had been wrongly accused of financial misconduct.

Headlines: Boeing delivers record 806 aircraft in 2018, shares jump 4 percent
Description: Boeing Co delivered a record 806 aircraft in 2018 as it overcame supplier woes, retaining the title of the world's biggest planemaker for the seventh straight year.

Headlines: World stocks rise on U.S.-China trade talk hopes
Description: An index of world stocks rose for the third straight session on Tuesday, with investors hopeful that the United States and China would strike a deal to end their months-long trade war that has hurt sentiment in financial markets.

Headlines: Verizon adds more phone subscribers than expected in fourth quarter
Description: Verizon Communications Inc on Tuesday beat Wall Street estimates for net new phone subscribers who pay a monthly bill, adding 650,000 customers in the fourth quarter.

Headlines: Airbus delivered 800 jets in 2018, pushing shares higher
Description: Airbus  delivered 800 aircraft last year, provisionally hitting a key industrial target that only weeks ago had seemed beyond its reach as its battles to overcome supply chain problems and factory snags to meet record demand for jetliners.

Headlines: U.S. job openings drop, but still at lofty levels
Description: U.S. job openings fell in November, pulled down by sharp declines in construction and other services, but did little to change views that the economy is facing a shortage of workers.

Headlines: U.S. initiative warns firms of hacking by China, other countries
Description: The Trump administration on Monday launched a drive to push  U.S. firms to better protect their trade secrets from foreign hackers, following a slew of cases accusing individuals and companies of economic espionage for China.

Headlines: Latest trial in J&J talc litigations gets under way in California
Description: A California jury on Monday heard opening statements in the latest trial over allegations that Johnson & Johnson's  talc-based products, including the company's baby powder, were contaminated with asbestos and cause cancer.

Headlines: American Express suspends a director in foreign-exchange pricing probe: WSJ
Description: American Express Co  suspended a director in its foreign-exchange department as part of an ongoing investigation into pricing practices in the division, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Scant relief for U.S. aluminum users from removal of Rusal sanctions
Description: U.S. plans to remove sanctions on Russian aluminum giant Rusal  will be of limited benefit to consumers in the United States where tariffs on aluminum imports mean producers still need much higher prices to incentivize shipments.

Headlines: India to issue new safety rules for A320neos with Pratt & Whitney engines
Description: India's civil aviation watchdog will issue an advanced safety management protocol in one week for airlines operating Airbus A320neo aircraft fitted with the troubled Pratt & Whitney engines, the civil aviation secretary told Reuters on Tuesday.

Headlines: Eli Lilly to cut 250 jobs at France plant, through voluntary redundancy
Description: Pharmaceutical group Eli Lilly  said on Tuesday it will cut 250 jobs at its factory located near Strasbourg in Eastern France.

Headlines: Monsanto patent victory seen as a boost for biotech investment in India
Description: India's Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday that Monsanto can claim patents on its genetically modified (GM) cotton seeds, a victory for the U.S. company that is expected to encourage   biotechnology firms to step up investment in the country.

Headlines: MetLife names Khalaf CEO, Kandarian to retire
Description: MetLife Inc  on Tuesday named insider Michel Khalaf as its new chief executive officer to succeed Steven Kandarian, who held the position for eight years and helped the company ride through intense regulatory oversight in the wake of the financial crisis.

Headlines: Forest fire insurance costs soar
Description: Forest fires are becoming increasingly likely because of climate change and costing insurers more than ever, with the deadly fire that ravaged northern California the single most expensive natural disaster in 2018, Munich Re  said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Union Pacific jumps 8 percent after company picks turnaround expert as COO
Description: Shares of Union Pacific Corp  rose 8 percent in early trading on Tuesday after the No.1 U.S. railroad named https://www.up.com/media/releases/190107-jim-vena.htm industry veteran Jim Vena as chief operating officer, prompting upgrades by several brokerages.

Headlines: 'We are down, but not out': Sears gets feisty on social media
Description: The clock may be fast running out on Sears Holdings Corp, but you wouldn't know it from the company's feisty posts on Twitter.

Headlines: Trump renews dig at Fed, expresses longing for lower interest rates
Description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday expressed longing for the lower interest rates that the Federal Reserve put in place during the 2007-09 recession, saying he could boost the economy if the central bank brought interest rates to zero.

Headlines: Samsung Electronics says weak chip demand sent fourth-quarter profit well below market estimates
Description: Samsung Electronics surprised the market on Tuesday with an estimated 29 percent drop in quarterly profit, blaming weak chip demand in a rare commentary issued to "ease confusion" among investors already fretting about a global tech slowdown.

Headlines: Ryanair's Spanish cabin crew unions call off Tuesday strike
Description: Unions representing Ryanair  cabin crew in Spain called off plans to strike on Tuesday to allow time for further talks, the SITCPLA and USO unions said in a statement.

Headlines: More U.S. regions see job openings outnumbering jobless
Description: Job openings are outnumbering unemployed workers across increasingly wide swaths of the United States, forcing businesses to rethink how they find workers, which could keep pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates despite a global economic slowdown.

Headlines: BMW says sold 2.49 million BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce vehicles in 2018
Description: German carmaker BMW  on Tuesday said it achieved record sales of 2.49 million BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce vehicles last year.

Headlines: Exclusive: China's HNA touts assets for sale as funding crunch intensifies
Description: China's indebted HNA Group met bankers on Tuesday to tout the latest assets that the sprawling conglomerate is putting on the block as it looks to raise funds and stave off an intensifying cash crunch.

Headlines: Group close to India's ruling party seeks change in patent act after pro-Monsanto court verdict
Description: A nationalist group close to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party said on Tuesday it would seek a legislative amendment to the rules governing patents, after the country's top court ruled in favor of Monsanto's cotton seed patent.

Headlines: Ghosn's lawyer: Nissan agreed on transfer of currency contracts
Description: Nissan Motor Co had agreed with former chairman Carlos Ghosn to take on his personal foreign exchange contracts, his lawyer said, disputing allegations of financial misconduct.

Headlines: Lilly makes $8 billion bet on drugs for rare cancers with Loxo Oncology buy
Description: Eli Lilly said on Monday it will buy Loxo Oncology Inc for $8 billion, an expensive bet on a pipeline of cancer drugs that target rare genetic mutations and the biggest acquisition in the drugmaker's 143-year history.     The price represents a 68 percent premium to Loxo's Friday share price close, which some Wall Street analysts said was high for a company with only one drug on the market that it shares with a partner.

Headlines: Statement by ex-Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn in Tokyo court
Description: The following are prepared remarks by Carlos Ghosn, ex-chairman of Nissan Motor Co, for his court appearance in Tokyo on Tuesday regarding allegations against him of aggravated breach of trust. The statement was released by Ghosn's lawyers in the United States.

Headlines: SoftBank to invest additional $2 billion in WeWork: sources
Description: SoftBank Group Corp  will inject another $2 billion in WeWork Cos Inc this year, bringing the Japanese conglomerate's total investment in the office space provider to more than $10 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Venezuela's PDVSA in oil deal with firm part-owned by Florida Republican
Description: Venezuelan state oil firm PDVSA [PDVSA.UL] has signed a deal with little-known U.S. energy firm Erepla, partly owned by a prominent Florida Republican, to help increase the socialist-run country's plummeting crude oil output, the company said.

Headlines: Activist Starboard seeks Dollar Tree board changes, disposal
Description: Activist hedge fund Starboard Value LP on Monday called on Dollar Tree Inc  to sell its underperforming Family Dollar business and proposed replacing a majority of the board after revealing a stake in the U.S. discount retailer.

Headlines: Major Wall Street players plan exchange to challenge NYSE, Nasdaq
Description: Morgan Stanley, Fidelity Investments, Citadel Securities LLC and a host of other financial companies plan to launch a  low-cost bourse that will compete with the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.

Headlines: Nvidia says new self-driving platform to hit streets next year
Description: Nvidia Corp on Monday announced its Drive AutoPilot platform, with artificial intelligence technologies, that can enable the next level of self-driving cars by 2020, further strengthening its position in the industry.

Headlines: U.S., China can reach trade deal 'we can live with': U.S. Commerce secretary
Description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross predicted on Monday that Beijing and Washington could reach a trade deal that "we can live with" as dozens of officials from the world's two largest economies resumed talks in a bid to end their trade dispute.

Headlines: PG&E shares and bonds plunge on bankruptcy worries
Description: PG&E Corp's  shares dived more than 22 percent on Monday after sources said the California utility is exploring filing for bankruptcy protection as it fears a massive charge in the fourth quarter related to potential liabilities from wildfires.

Headlines: Amazon and Netflix push Wall Street higher
Description: Amazon.com Inc  and Netflix  fueled a second straight session of gains on Wall Street on Monday, as the resumption of U.S.-China trade talks helped ease concerns that have pummeled the market in recent months.

Headlines: Karen Peetz to retire from Wells Fargo board
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Monday board member Karen Peetz has decided not to stand for reelection after roughly two years on the board.

Headlines: Stocks rise on trade talk optimism; rate outlook hits dollar
Description: An index of world stocks rose on Monday, adding to Friday's strong gains, on optimism about the outcome of trade talks between Washington and Beijing.

Headlines: Sears picks liquidator should rescue talks fall through: sources
Description: A long-standing liquidator is now first in line for one of the U.S. retail sector's most daunting assignments: shutting down 126-year-old department store chain Sears Holdings Corp , people familiar with the matter said on Sunday.

Headlines: Oil rises; lifted by OPEC cuts, steadying stock market
Description: Oil prices edged higher on Monday, rebounding further from 1-1/2-year lows reached in December, on support from OPEC production cuts and steadying equities markets.

Headlines: Canada auto union head to meet with GM on Tuesday
Description: The head of Canada's auto union said on Monday he was set to meet with General Motors Co  executives in Detroit on Tuesday to discuss the automaker's Oshawa, Ontario, assembly plant, scheduled to shut down in December 2019.

Headlines: ICBC leads Asian jet lessor buying spree: sources
Description: Asian-controlled leasing companies splashed out on passenger jets worth $25 billion at list prices to pick out bargains as planemakers Airbus  and Boeing  raced to end a relatively quiet year with fresh orders.

Headlines: U.S. top court rejects Amgen over cholesterol medication patent fight
Description: Amgen Inc on Monday lost its bid at the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that kept the Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc and Sanofi SA cholesterol-lowering drug Praluent on the market, but the patent dispute among the rival drugmakers will continue in another trial.

Headlines: U.S. top court declines to take up Fiat Chrysler hacking case
Description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear Fiat Chrysler's appeal in a class action lawsuit over allegations that its Jeeps and other trucks are vulnerable to hacking, one of the first legal cases involving automotive cyber security risks.

Headlines: Dassault business jet deliveries down, Rafale higher
Description: Dassault Aviation  business jet deliveries fell last year while deliveries of the Rafale warplane rose and new orders for both categories were also higher, the French jetmaker said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S., China could settle immediate trade issues: Ross on CNBC
Description: The United States and China are likely to reach a good settlement over immediate trade issues while agreement on structural trade issues and enforcement will be harder, U.S. Secretary of Commerce Wilbur Ross said on Monday as U.S.-China trade talks resumed.

Headlines: Nucor to set up plate mill in U.S. Midwest for $1.35 billion
Description: Steel producer Nucor Corp  said on Monday it would spend about $1.35 billion to build a plate mill in the U.S. Midwest, taking advantage of federal tax cuts that has resulted in windfall gains for several companies.

Headlines: Daimler to invest $573 million in autonomous trucks
Description: German luxury carmaker Daimler  will invest 500 million euros ($573 million) in the coming years to develop highly autonomous trucks, it said on Monday, a move that will create more than 200 jobs.

Headlines: Merck loses bid to revive $200 million Gilead verdict at U.S. high court
Description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday handed a defeat to Merck & Co  by refusing to hear its appeal of a ruling that it had dishonestly obtained patent rights and could not collect a $200 million verdict against rival drugmaker Gilead Sciences Inc  in a dispute involving blockbuster hepatitis C drugs.

Headlines: Brazil studying if Boeing-Embraer deal is in its 'ideal form'
Description: Brazil national security adviser Augusto Heleno said on Monday that the government is studying whether the deal between planemakers Embraer  and Boeing  is in its "ideal form" or in need of changes.

Headlines: Credit Suisse settles New York state RMBS lawsuit
Description: Credit Suisse has settled a 2012 New York state lawsuit alleging misconduct over residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS), with a source familiar with the deal saying the bank would pay much less than prosecutors had originally sought.

Headlines: Ex-Goldman Sachs banker denied bail in Malaysia pending extradition to U.S.
Description: A Malaysian court on Monday refused bail to former Goldman Sachs banker Roger Ng, pending his extradition to the United States where he faces charges related to suspected money laundering of funds siphoned off from state fund 1MDB.

Headlines: Ford plans new wireless tech for cars starting 2022
Description: Ford Motor Co  said on Monday it plans to roll out a wireless technology for its new vehicle models in the United States, starting 2022, that will allow direct communication between connected devices.

Headlines: Exclusive: Aston Martin triggers contingency plans for no deal Brexit
Description: British carmaker Aston Martin  has triggered contingency plans to cope with a potentially disorderly Brexit, including hiring a new supply chain chief and preparing to fly in components as well as use ports other than Dover.

Headlines: Huawei sues U.S. firm InterDigital in China over patent practices
Description: InterDigital Inc on Monday said Huawei Technologies Co Ltd filed a lawsuit against it in China, alleging the U.S. technology firm had not licensed its intellectual property on fair terms.

Headlines: Tesla CEO Musk breaks ground at Shanghai Gigafactory to launch China push
Description: Tesla Inc  broke ground on Monday for its Shanghai Gigafactory where it plans to begin making its Model 3 electric vehicles (EV) by year-end, a first step in localizing production in the world's largest auto market.

Headlines: China's Geely sees sales growth evaporating as car market struggles
Description: China's most globally high-profile and successful carmaker, Geely, is forecasting flat sales this year, a sharp slowdown from 2018 as the country's giant auto market struggles with slowing economic growth and more cautious consumers.

Headlines: Chinese tech investors flee Silicon Valley as Trump tightens scrutiny
Description: New Trump administration policies aimed at curbing China's access to American innovation have all but halted Chinese investment in U.S. technology startups, as both investors and startup founders abandon deals amid scrutiny from Washington.

Headlines: Trump: Weakness in China economy gives Beijing incentive for trade deal
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday that trade talks with China were going very well and that weakness in the Chinese economy gave Beijing a reason to work toward a deal.

Headlines: Assets worth $1 trillion to shift from UK to EU due to Brexit: EY
Description: Assets worth nearly 800 billion pounds ($1 trillion) are being moved from Britain to new financial hubs in the European Union ahead of Brexit, consultancy EY said on Monday.

Headlines: Ex-Nissan chairman Ghosn's lawyers to give news conference Tuesday: FCCJ
Description: Lawyers of ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd  chairman Carlos Ghosn are scheduled to give a news conference on Tuesday, the Foreign Correspondents' Club of Japan (FCCJ) said on its website on Monday, their first such public appearance.

Headlines: Huawei launches server chipset as China pushes to cut reliance on imports
Description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd [HWT.UL] on Monday launched a new chipset for use in servers, at a time when China is pushing to enhance its chip-making capabilities and reduce its heavy reliance on imports, especially from the United States.

Headlines: Starboard buys stake in Dollar Tree, seeks sale of Family Dollar: WSJ
Description: Activist investor Starboard Value LP has acquired a stake in discount store operator Dollar Tree Inc  and is asking the company to sell its Family Dollar business, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

Headlines: Apple inks deal with Samsung to distribute iTunes shows on TVs
Description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  said Sunday that it will add an app to its smart televisions in the coming months to let owners watch content bought on Apple Inc's  iTunes service, a possible first sign Apple is looking to distribute its forthcoming television service on devices made by others.

Headlines: Samsung Electronics braces for profit drop as China slowdown chips away at demand
Description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd is set to post its first drop in quarterly operating profit in two years as slowing economic growth in China, a key market for the South Korean tech giant, erodes demand for its products.

Headlines: Fund managers hoping for stock rally look to emerging markets
Description: After emerging market stocks led global equity markets lower in a brutal 2018, some U.S.-based fund managers are betting that the asset class may have the largest rebound in the new year.

Headlines: Southeast Asia wary of China's Belt and Road project, skeptical of U.S.: survey
Description: Southeast Asian countries should be cautious in negotiating with China on its flagship Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) to avoid being trapped in unsustainable debt, 70 percent of respondents said in a policy survey released on Monday.

Headlines: France presses Renault over executive compensation paid via Dutch holding company
Description: The French government has told Renault  to provide more details on compensation paid to senior executives via a Dutch holding company jointly owned with alliance partner Nissan, Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Sunday.

Headlines: Mercedes aims to be among top two players to scale autonomous tech: paper
Description: Mercedes-Benz's is not aiming to be the first manufacturer to develop a self-driving car but it wants to be among the first two players able to scale up the technology, Mercedes-Benz executive Christoph Schroeder told German paper Welt am Sonntag.

Headlines: South Korea's Celltrion aims to set up China JV within first half of 2019: chairman
Description: South Korean drugmaker Celltrion Inc  aims to set up a joint venture in China within the first half of this year, and begin selling products in the country next year, its chairman said on Sunday.

Headlines: Japanese prosecutors want Ghosn to sign confession, says son: paper
Description: Japanese prosecutors want Carlos Ghosn, the detained auto executive who oversaw an alliance that sold 10 million vehicles a year, to confess to financial misconduct, his son told France's weekly Journal du Dimanche (JDD).

Headlines: German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg sues VW for damages: FAZ
Description: The German Federal State of Baden-Wuerttemberg is seeking damages from Volkswagen  after local authorities purchased VW diesel vehicles which now face bans in cities like Stuttgart, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said on Saturday.

Headlines: Take Five: Be careful out there! World markets themes for the week ahead
Description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

Headlines: Nissan's executive Munoz takes leave of absence in wake of Ghosn arrest
Description: A senior executive of Nissan Motor Co Ltd , Jose Munoz, has taken a leave of absence in a sudden management shake-up as the Japanese automaker deals with the aftermath of the arrest of former chairman Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: Wall St. rebounds on robust jobs report, dovish Powell remarks
Description: Wall Street rebounded on Friday to close at its highest in two weeks after a strong jobs report and assurances from Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell that the central bank would be patient and flexible in steering the course of interest rates.

Headlines: Trump says China woes help U.S. in trade talks, downplays Apple warning
Description: President Donald Trump on Friday downplayed a revenue warning from Apple Inc that cited slowing sales in China and said China's weakening economic growth puts the United States in a strong position as negotiators from the world's two largest economies prepare for trade talks next week.

Headlines: Tesla urges tariff exemption for Chinese-made car computer 'brain'
Description: Tesla Inc has asked the Trump administration to exempt the Chinese-made car computer "brain" of its new Model 3 sedan from 25 percent tariffs imposed in August, saying they threaten the electric carmaker's bottom line.

Headlines: Samsung, Huawei supply majority of own modem chips, Qualcomm says
Description: The two largest smart phone makers in the world supply a majority of their own modem chips to help their devices connect to wireless data networks, according to evidence presented at an antitrust trial for chip supplier Qualcomm Inc .

Headlines: Upbeat employment report underscores U.S. economic strength
Description: U.S. employers hired the most workers in 10 months in December while boosting wages, pointing to sustained strength in the economy that could ease fears of a sharp slowdown in growth.

Headlines: China warnings signal Trump's trade war finally hitting home
Description: Weak sales at Apple and Cargill, U.S. giants of technology and agriculture, may be the clearest sign yet that President Donald Trump's quest to reset world trade carries costs at home and could isolate the United States as the increasingly fragile engine for global economic growth.

Headlines: PG&E seeks to make changes to its board
Description: PG&E Corp , the electricity provider in the northern California region ravaged by a deadly wildfire, said it was searching for new directors at its holding company and its utility subsidiary Pacific Gas and Electric Co.

Headlines: UK pay gap between CEOs and staff widens -lobby group
Description: The earnings of Britain's top bosses will match a typical worker's entire annual salary even faster than last year, hitting the mark by Friday lunchtime, a report by the Chartered Institute of Personnel & Development and High Pay Centre said.

Headlines: U.S. jobs data, dovish Fed comments boost equities
Description: Equities around the globe rallied on Friday while bond yields rose after sharply declining earlier in the week as U.S. employment data pointed to economic strength and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the U.S. central bank would be patient with monetary policy.

Headlines: Powell tells markets Fed is flexible and aware of risks
Description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday sought to ease market concerns that the U.S. central bank was ignoring signs of an economic slowdown, saying he was aware of the risks and would be patient and flexible in policy decisions this year.

Headlines: Instant View: Powell pledges patience; says won't quit if Trump asks
Description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday moved to mollify financial markets concerned about a U.S. economic slowdown, saying that while momentum is solid, the U.S. central bank will be sensitive to the downside risks the market is pricing in.

Headlines: Supreme Court to weigh Broadcom bid to end shareholder suit
Description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear an appeal filed by a subsidiary of chipmaker Broadcom Inc  seeking to put an end to a shareholder lawsuit concerning its 2015 acquisition of Emulex Corp.

Headlines: Marriott cuts estimate on size of massive Starwood hack
Description: Marriott International Inc  said on Friday that fewer than 383 million customer records were stolen in a massive cyber attack disclosed last month, down from its initial estimate that up to 500 million guests were affected.

Headlines: Court battle, trade war and 5G spell tough 2019 for Apple in China
Description: Apple Inc's chief executive Tim Cook has his work cut out in China this year: the iPhone maker faces the looming threat of a court-ordered sales ban, the uncertain outcome of trade war talks and the roll-out of a new 5G network, where it finds itself behind rivals like Huawei and Samsung.

Headlines: Oil rises on China-U.S. talks, gains capped by U.S. fuel build
Description: Oil rose nearly 2 percent on Friday after proposed trade talks between the United States and China eased some fears about a global economic slowdown, but gains were capped after the United States reported a sharp build in refined product inventories.

Headlines: U.S. judge stands by ruling to limit evidence in Roundup cancer trials
Description: A federal judge overseeing lawsuits alleging Bayer AG's glyphosate-based Roundup weed killer causes cancer on Friday declined to reconsider a ruling that limits evidence the plaintiffs in the litigation consider crucial to their cases.

Headlines: Fed Chair Powell says he would not resign if Trump asked
Description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday said he would not resign even if President Donald Trump asked him to do so, a clear assertion of the U.S. central bank's independence in the face of Trump's strident criticism of the Fed's rate hikes.

Headlines: Qualcomm kicks off crucial fight with U.S. antitrust regulator
Description: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission's antitrust case accusing Qualcomm Inc  of abusing a monopoly on mobile chip technology kicked off in a California courtroom on Friday in a trial whose outcome could have a major impact on the smartphone industry.

Headlines: Nissan's Ghosn to make first public appearance in seven weeks in court on Tuesday
Description: Ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd  chairman Carlos Ghosn is set to make his first public appearance in seven weeks at a Tokyo court on Tuesday after he requested an open hearing to hear the reason for his continued detention.

Headlines: Brazil's Bolsonaro: worried Boeing could own all of Embraer's commercial division
Description: Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro said on Friday he is concerned that a proposed sale of 80 percent of Embraer's  commercial aviation business to Boeing  could lead to the U.S. planemaker taking over all of the division.

Headlines: Tesla to start delivering Model 3 to China buyers in March
Description: Tesla Inc said on Friday it plans to start delivering Model 3 cars to customers in China in March, cementing a time frame that the U.S. electric vehicle (EV) maker's chief executive, Elon Musk, tweeted about late last year.

Headlines: Airbus chases aircraft lessors as order race tightens
Description: Airbus  has been chasing deals with leasing companies in recent weeks to try to narrow a gap in orders against rival Boeing , while industry experts took a somewhat more sanguine view on 2018 deliveries after shares took a beating.

Headlines: Instant View: U.S. December payrolls surprise big to the upside
Description: U.S. employers hired the most workers in 10 months in December while boosting wages, which could help to allay a recent upsurge in fears about the economy's health that has roiled financial markets.

Headlines: Ex-Credit Suisse bankers arrested on U.S. charges over Mozambique loans
Description: Three former Credit Suisse Group AG  bankers were arrested in London on Thursday on U.S. charges of involvement in a fraud involving $2 billion in loans to state-owned companies in Mozambique, U.S. prosecutors and British police said.

Headlines: Celgene, Bristol-Myers set $2.2 billion termination fee for their mega deal
Description: Celgene Corp  and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  will have to pay $2.2 billion if either of the drugmakers walks away from their $74 billion merger announced on Thursday, according to a regulatory filing.

Headlines: Chinese phone maker Huawei punishes employees for iPhone tweet blunder
Description: China's Huawei Technologies [HWT.UL] has punished two employees for New Year greetings sent on the smartphone maker's official Twitter account using an iPhone, an internal memo showed.

Headlines: Qualcomm enforces ban to halt some Apple iPhone sales in Germany
Description: U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm Inc  took steps to enforce a court order banning the sale of some iPhone models in Germany following a patent dispute, a move that will likely see Apple Inc  pull those models from its German stores.

Headlines: China slashes banks' reserve requirements again as growth slows
Description: China's central bank said on Friday it was cutting the amount of cash that banks have to hold as reserves for the fifth time in a year, freeing up $116 billion for new lending as it tries to reduce the risk of a sharp economic slowdown.

Headlines: Audits reveal Deutsche Bank's links to tax trade scandal
Description: There are "lots of indications" that some managers discussed "the reputational risks" of Deutsche Bank's involvement in a share-trading scheme that is the subject of Germany's biggest  post-war fraud investigation, according to a conclusion in one of five internal audits seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Pioneering Southwest Airlines co-founder Herb Kelleher dies at 87
Description: Herb Kelleher, who co-founded pioneering low-cost carrier Southwest Airlines Co and built it into an industry powerhouse stamped with his colorful, unconventional personality, died on Thursday at age 87, the U.S. carrier said.

Headlines: UK consumer lending growth slows to near four-year low as Brexit approaches
Description: Lending to British consumers grew at its slowest pace in nearly four years in November and the number of mortgage approvals fell, Bank of England data showed, adding to signs of a pre-Brexit slowdown in the economy.

Headlines: German Apple reseller Gravis says still selling iPhones 7, 8
Description: German Apple  retailer Gravis said it was still selling iPhone 7 and 8 models at its stores and online after Qualcomm  posted security bonds to enforce a court order that will ban sales of some Apple iPhones in Germany.

Headlines: Yen's surge is a red flag for world markets
Description: A gradual rise by the Japanese yen in recent weeks culminated in a dramatic overnight surge -- firing a warning shot for world markets and the global economy in 2019.

Headlines: Bristol-Myers to buy Celgene for $74 billion in largest biopharma deal
Description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  said on Thursday it would buy Celgene Corp  for about $74 billion, combining two of the world's largest cancer drug businesses in the biggest pharmaceutical deal ever.

Headlines: Offices grow 'brains' as companies seek to attract smarter workers
Description: Employees will not need a key to get into the office of the future when it opens in Berlin this year, featuring ample meeting space, plenty of copy machines always stocked with paper along with high-quality air processed to maximize worker health and minimize sick time.

Headlines: U.S. retail vacancies rise marginally in fourth quarter: Reis
Description: U.S. retail vacancies inched higher in the fourth quarter, underscoring how the retail sector has withstood many store closures across the country, real estate research firm Reis Inc said in a report.

Headlines: Apple plunge deepens Warren Buffett's book value woes
Description: The plunge in Apple Inc's share price will likely cause new pain for Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc, after the conglomerate suffered a big quarterly decline in its net worth that will hit its bottom line.

Headlines: U.S. judge limits evidence in trial over Roundup cancer claims
Description: A federal judge overseeing lawsuits alleging Bayer AG's glyphosate-based weed killer causes cancer has issued a ruling that could severely restrict evidence that the plaintiffs consider crucial to their cases.

Headlines: Detroit Three ready for 2019 rumble over lucrative pickup trucks
Description: The battle for profits from sales of large pickup trucks is intensifying among the Detroit Three automakers as sales of small cars in the United States shrivel.

Headlines: Wall Street plunges as factory data, Apple warning fuel slowdown fears
Description: Wall Street plunged on Thursday after slowing U.S. factory activity on the heels of a dire revenue warning from Apple Inc  fueled fears of a global economic slowdown.

Headlines: Instant view: Stocks slammed, Treasury yields fall, yen surges
Description: U.S. stocks plunged on Thursday and 2-year U.S. Treasury yields dropped below the Federal Reserve's policy rate for the first time in more than a decade, delivering a signal the U.S. central bank could begin reversing its tightening regime before long.

Headlines: Delta shares fall 10 percent on lowered outlook; drags down rivals
Description: Shares of Delta Air Lines Inc fell about 9 percent on Thursday, after the U.S. carrier warned fourth-quarter unit revenue would be slightly below its prior forecast due to the lower-than-expected improvement in last-minute fares booked by travelers.

Headlines: At Brazil's Petrobras, a 'Chicago Boy' takes the reins
Description: Depending on who you ask, Roberto Castello Branco, the new chief executive of Brazil's Petroleo Brasileiro SA , will either save the indebted oil major - or strip it to the bone.

Headlines: Oil rises in choppy trade as OPEC supply cuts vie with demand worry
Description: Oil prices rose more than 1 percent on Thursday in volatile trade, drawing support from signs that Saudi Arabia is cutting crude output but pressured by concerns that slowing global economic growth could dent demand.

Headlines: Apple shares dive; rare revenue warning drags global markets
Description: Apple Inc shares plunged 10 percent on Thursday after the iPhone maker blamed weak China demand for a holiday-quarter revenue shortfall, with many investors worried the rare stumble was a harbinger for slowing global growth.

Headlines: Petrobras, Brazil government expect to resolve dispute within 100 days: minister
Description: Brazil's government and state-run oil firm Petroleo Brasileiro SA  expect to resolve a dispute over the oil producing zone known as the 'transfer-of-rights' area within 100 days, a minister said on Thursday.

Headlines: Father and son advised on opposite sides of Bristol-Celgene deal
Description: For most U.S. families, the holidays are all about gathering around the fireplace, overeating at festive dinners, and playing the occasional board game. But this year, a father and son were also working on the biggest pharmaceutical acquisition of all time.

Headlines: Reuss, 35-year GM veteran, to succeed Ammann as president
Description: General Motors Co  said on Thursday that Mark Reuss would succeed Dan Ammann as president, effective immediately, as part of the automaker's ongoing shift to electric and self-driving vehicles in North America and China.

Headlines: FDIC chair says no concerns about U.S. bank health amid market turmoil
Description: A top U.S. bank regulator said on Thursday she had no concerns that volatility in the equities and futures markets posed a threat to the banking system, telling Reuters the country's lenders have plenty of capital to weather further market swings.

Headlines: Truckmaker Volvo to take $778 million emissions hit
Description: Sweden's Volvo is setting aside 7 billion Swedish crowns ($778 million) to cover costs related to its admission in October that its truck and bus engines could be exceeding limits for nitrogen oxide emissions.

Headlines: Cost to insure Bristol-Myers debt jumps as leverage balloons
Description: The cost to insure Bristol-Myers Squibb  debt hit its highest point since May 2010 on Thursday, following the announcement that the U.S. pharmaceutical company would acquire rival Celgene Corp  in a deal worth about $74 billion.

Headlines: UAW sues GM over temporary workers, escalating fight over job cuts
Description: The United Auto Workers said on Thursday it was suing General Motors Co over labor contract violations stemming from its alleged use of temporary workers at an Indiana assembly plant, escalating the union's fight against GM's plans to possibly close U.S. factories.

Headlines: Google shifted $23 billion to tax haven Bermuda in 2017: filing

Headlines: U.S. factory activity hits two-year low, casts shadow over economy
Description: U.S. manufacturing activity slowed sharply to a two-year low in December amid a plunge in new orders and hiring at factories, suggesting the economy was probably not immune to slowing growth in China and Europe.

Headlines: Major automakers bullish on U.S. market despite rising interest rates
Description: Major automakers on Thursday shrugged off declines in U.S. new vehicle sales in December and said they were bullish about 2019 even as economists warned that rising interest rates will discourage consumers from buying cars in the year ahead.

Headlines: Apple sales should pick up when U.S.-China strike trade deal: Trump adviser
Description: A sharp drop in Chinese economic growth will hit the profits of U.S. firms but sales by Apple Inc and other American companies should recover once Washington strikes a trade deal with Beijing, a senior White House adviser said on Thursday.

Headlines: Apple's warning a bad omen for Wall Street bulls
Description: Apple's  warning on Wednesday about weak iPhone demand in the holiday quarter is a gloomy omen for Wall Street bulls hoping for an early gift in 2019 following December's steep selloff.

Description: Apple's first sales warning in nearly 12 years sent European shares sliding on Thursday, with the tech sector particularly badly bruised as chipmakers that supply the iPhone maker fell sharply.

Headlines: OPEC oil output posts biggest drop since 2017 on Saudi move

Headlines: Cargill net drops 20 percent, revenues fall as trade fight bites

Headlines: Nordstrom heir Blake Nordstrom dies at 58

Headlines: Nestle welcomes Indian court ruling in Maggi case

Headlines: GM sold 200,000 electric vehicles in U.S. by 2018, triggering tax-credit phaseout: source

Now Smith's estate is suing Sunrise, saying that aides did not properly watch her.

Description: Amazon.com Inc  is planning to expand its Whole Foods Market portfolio by adding more stores to put more customers within its two-hour delivery service range, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing sources.

Description: Perceived safe havens like utilities and consumer staples, often an afterthought in Wall Street's cascade of year-ahead investment recommendations each December, are emerging as top picks as stocks limp into 2019.

Description: China is willing to work with the United States to implement the consensus reached during talks between the two countries' leaders in Argentina, the Chinese foreign ministry said in a statement on Sunday.

Headlines: Pacific trade pact takes off with tariffs cut in six nations
Description: A landmark 11-country trade deal, a revamped version of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), came into force on Sunday with New Zealand's trade minister hailing the opportunities it presented for exporters.
