Headlines: Thyssenkrupp to propose Merz as chairwoman as year of turmoil ends
Description: Thyssenkrupp  will propose as chairwoman Martina Merz, whose background includes roles at Volvo , Bosch [ROBG.UL] and Lufthansa , the German company said, as it prepares to spin off its capital goods units.

Headlines: German auto supplier to plead guilty, pay $35 million fine in VW emissions case
Description: German auto supplier IAV Gmbh has agreed to plead guilty and pay a $35 million fine for conspiring to assist Volkswagen AG  in its effort to evade U.S. diesel emissions standards, the U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Exxon Mobil opposes weakening Obama-era emissions rules: letter to EPA
Description: Exxon Mobil Corp  sent a letter to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in support of methane gas emission rules put in place under the Obama administration, according to a copy of the letter seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Renault-Nissan leaders to meet amid alliance crisis
Description: The head of Nissan and acting CEO of Renault will hold talks during a two day meeting of their carmaking partnership starting on Tuesday, sources said, amid a crisis in relations sparked by the arrest of long-time alliance supremo Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: BP launches $3 billion sale of U.S. onshore assets to fund BHP deal: sources
Description: Britain's BP has launched the sale of U.S. oil and gas onshore assets that could raise more than $3 billion to help pay for other fields in the United States it bought in October from BHP , industry and banking sources said.

Headlines: J&J says Indian drug regulators visited facilities, company provided talc samples
Description: Johnson & Johnson said on Wednesday that Indian drugs authorities visited some of its facilities and it provided them with "tests and samples" of its talcum powder.

Headlines: Bristol-Myers gets $1.6 billion offer for French consumer health unit
Description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  received an offer from Japanese healthcare firm Taisho Pharmaceutical Holdings Co Ltd  to buy the company's French over-the-counter drugs business UPSA for $1.6 billion, the companies said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Boeing says Indian airfares unsustainably low; lifts country's 20-year order forecast
Description: Airfares in the fast-growing Indian market are 10 to 15 percent lower than breakeven levels for airlines, a Boeing Co  executive said, as the planemaker raised its long-term jet order forecast for the nation to a record despite market challenges.

Headlines: Asian business confidence wallows near three-year low on trade worries: Thomson Reuters/INSEAD
Description: A very cautious optimism remains among Asian companies in the fourth quarter as they wait to see whether there will be any breakthrough in a trade dispute between the United States and China, a Thomson Reuters/INSEAD survey showed.

Headlines: Italy's transport minister says he would like to revoke Autostrade concession
Description: Italy's Transport Minister Danilo Toninelli said on Wednesday that he would like to revoke motorway concessions held by Autostrade per l'Italia  after the collapse of a bridge in Genoa last August.

Headlines: Indian regulator to test samples of Johnson & Johnson baby powder: media
Description: India's federal drug regulator will on Wednesday seize samples of Johnson & Johnson's  baby powder for testing, local media said, following a Reuters report that the company knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in the product.

Headlines: Investors revolt against executive pay plans at tarnished Australian banks
Description: Shareholders voted against the executive remuneration plans of two of Australia's biggest banks on Wednesday following misconduct revelations that have swept through the country's financial sector.

Headlines: Micron sales, profit miss estimates as chip glut hurts prices
Description: U.S. chipmaker Micron Technology Inc  gave on Tuesday quarterly sales and profit forecasts well below Wall Street estimates, citing a market glut of memory chips as consumer and business demand for phones and computers is weakening.

Headlines: Sears to take $443 million in charges arising from store closures
Description: Bankrupt U.S. retailer Sears Holdings Corp will take a charge of about $443 million arising from store closures, a regulatory filing showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Oil drops over 5 percent on economic slowdown fears, supply glut
Description: Oil prices tumbled more than 5 percent on Tuesday in heavy trade due to fears of oversupply and deteriorating demand, extending a selloff that has taken major crude benchmarks down more than 30 percent from an October peak.

Headlines: FedEx sees global trade slowdown, says U.S. economy still 'solid'
Description: FedEx Corp  on Tuesday slashed its 2019 forecast after Europe's economy weakened and the U.S. trade row exacerbated a slowdown in China, sending shares in the package delivery company tumbling more than 6 percent after the closing bell.

Headlines: High taxes could hasten bank moves from Britain after Brexit
Description: Britain risks driving banks overseas if current high levels of taxation on the industry are maintained after Brexit, a bank lobby group said on Wednesday.

Headlines: S&P flat as government shutdown threat, Fed decision loom
Description: The benchmark S&P 500 stock index ended little changed in a choppy trading session on Tuesday as the possibility of a partial U.S. government shutdown raised investor jitters ahead of a highly anticipated meeting of the Federal Reserve.

Headlines: J&J moves to limit impact of Reuters report on asbestos in Baby Powder
Description: Johnson & Johnson on Monday scrambled to contain fallout from a Reuters report that the healthcare conglomerate knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in its Baby Powder, taking out full-page newspaper ads defending its product and practices, and readying its chief executive for his first television interview since investors erased tens of billions of dollars from the company’s market value.

Headlines: Lockheed Martin wins $585 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
Description: Lockheed Martin Corp  has been awarded a $585 million U.S. defense contract for a Homeland Defense Radar in Hawaii, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Judge mulls using monitor to oversee CVS during court process
Description: A federal judge said on Tuesday that he was considering using a court-appointed monitor to make sure CVS Health Corp refrains from fully integrating with insurer Aetna while he examines the companies' settlement with the government.

Headlines: Yelp, Consumer Watchdog lose Google intervention bid
Description: Search company Yelp and lobby group Consumer Watchdog lost their joint bid to intervene in Google's challenge of a 2.4 billion euro ($2.7 billion) EU antitrust fine after a court said they had no direct interest in the case.

Headlines: Uber gets approval from Pennsylvania to resume self-driving testing
Description: Uber Technologies Inc received approval from Pennsylvania to resume self-driving car testing on public roads this week, state records show, nine months after it suspended the program following a deadly accident in Arizona.

Headlines: Trump pressures Fed before meeting, warns against 'another mistake'
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday further sought to pressure the Federal Reserve as the central bank prepared to start its two-day policy meeting, warning the Fed's board not to "make yet another mistake" ahead of an expected interest rate hike.

Headlines: Stocks dip ahead of Fed news; oil prices drop
Description: Global equity markets dipped on Tuesday as nervous investors awaited indications whether the Federal Reserve will be able to raise interest rates much further amid turbulent markets and a weakening outlook for the global economy.

Headlines: Glencore's Katanga pays $22 million to settle Canada regulator probe
Description: Glencore-controlled  Katanga Mining Ltd  said on Tuesday it agreed to pay more than $22 million to settle Canadian allegations of inadequate historical disclosures of its finances and activities in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Headlines: China embarks on second round of soy buying post Trump-Xi truce
Description: Chinese importers returned to the U.S. soy market on Tuesday for their second round of purchases since the two countries agreed to a truce in their trade war, four traders with knowledge of the deals and the U.S. Soybean Export Council said.

Headlines: Kinder Morgan faces proposed class action lawsuit on pipeline
Description: Kinder Morgan is facing a proposed class action lawsuit, claiming that a division of the pipeline operator has emitted chemicals and toxic gas that caused damage to property and killed animals.

Headlines: CBS fires CEO Leslie Moonves and denies $120 million severance
Description: CBS Corp said on Monday it has fired Leslie Moonves for cause and has denied a $120 million severance package as it girds for a potential legal battle with its former chief executive who has been accused of sexual harassment and assault that allegedly took place before and after he joined the company.

Headlines: Citi reorganizes prime brokerage unit
Description: Citigroup Inc  is shuffling its prime brokerage business, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, amid reports that the unit could lose millions on a bad loan to an Asian hedge fund.

Headlines: IPO activity next year could dampen if markets do not rebound: report
Description: The excitement of proposed initial public offerings by ride-hailing rivals Uber and Lyft next year may not be enough to encourage other firms to follow suit, as they fear that slowing global growth and rocky stock markets dragging into next year could threaten market debut valuations.

Headlines: Treasury's Mnuchin says expects January trade talks with China: Bloomberg
Description: The United States and China are planning to hold meetings in January to "document an agreement" on trade, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told Bloomberg in an interview on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. agency to speed reviews of automaker self-driving petitions
Description: The U.S. auto safety regulator said on Tuesday it is speeding up the process for reviewing whether automakers can deploy self-driving vehicles without devices such as brakes and steering wheels.

Headlines: Musk's SpaceX to raise $500 million in funding: WSJ
Description: Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX Corp is set to raise $500 million at a $30.5 billion valuation, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the fundraising plan.

Headlines: GM cutting 50 jobs at U.S. battery plant tied to Chevy Volt
Description: General Motors Co  said on Tuesday it plans to cut 50 jobs at a suburban Detroit lithium-ion battery assembly plant after the largest U.S. automaker announced last month it will end production of its plug-in hybrid Chevrolet Volt in 2019.

Headlines: Facebook's Sandberg cites need to do more after reports of Russia meddling
Description: Facebook Inc's Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg said on Tuesday the company needs to step up its efforts to curb misinformation after research revealed that Russia-backed organizations targeted African-Americans, who favored Hillary Clinton, to suppress voter turnout during the 2016 election.

Headlines: Burnout, stress lead more companies to try a four-day work week
Description: (Corrects paragraph 4 to identify Perpetual Guardian as a trust company instead of an insurance company; corrects paragraph 13 to reflect that the study was conducted by Kronos and Future Workplace)

Headlines: Volkswagen may have to step up electric car plans to meet EU CO2 targets
Description: Volkswagen  may have to step up its plans for mass production of electric vehicles in order to meet tougher-than-expected European targets to cut greenhouse emissions from cars, its chief executive said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Twitter tumbles on concerns about hacking activity
Description: Twitter Inc  shares fell almost 7 percent on Monday after the company said it was investigating unusual traffic that might be from state-sponsored hackers and, in what appeared to be an unrelated issue, a security firm said hackers used the platform to try to steal user data.

Headlines: Kroger starts use of unmanned vehicles for delivery in Arizona
Description: U.S. supermarket chain Kroger Co  said on Tuesday it has started using unmanned autonomous vehicles to deliver groceries Scottsdale, Arizona in partnership with Silicon Valley startup Nuro.

Headlines: Indian regulator says Reuters report on J&J baby powder 'under consideration'
Description: India's federal drug regulator said on Tuesday a Reuters report that Johnson & Johnson  knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in its baby powder was "under consideration".

Headlines: Malaysia says Goldman Sachs failed to disclose key facts in 1MDB bond sales
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  made untrue statements and omitted key facts in offering circulars for the bonds it sold for Malaysian state fund 1MDB, the Malaysian government said in criminal charges against the U.S. bank.

Headlines: Cash-strapped South African Airways expands Emirates code sharing
Description: South African Airways (SAA) said on Tuesday that it had signed a deal with Emirates [EMIRA.UL] to expand an existing codeshare agreement, in a rare bright spot for the cash-strapped airline.

Headlines: Italy's UniCredit settles dispute with Caius
Description: British hedge fund Caius has made a payment to UniCredit  to settle a dispute over complex financial instruments which Italy's biggest bank counts toward its core capital, the two companies said.

Headlines: T-Mobile, Sprint win U.S. security approvals for merger
Description: T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp have won backing for their $26 billion merger from two national security reviews on Monday, clearing key hurdles in their tie-up bid.

Headlines: South Korea to provide $3 billion in financial support for troubled auto suppliers
Description: South Korea unveiled a policy package to support its embattled car parts makers industry that includes providing financial support worth over 3.5 trillion won ($3.10 billion) and encouraging the use of electric cars.

Headlines: T-Mobile, Sprint get CFIUS approval for proposed merger
Description: T-Mobile US  and Sprint Corp  have received approval from the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) for their proposed merger, the companies said on Monday.

Headlines: Qualcomm says Apple violating Chinese court order, despite new software
Description: Qualcomm Inc said it believes Apple Inc remains in violation of a Chinese court's orders to stop selling iPhones despite a software update that Apple pushed on Monday.

Headlines: S&P 500 hits 14-month low on economic jitters ahead of Fed meeting
Description: Wall Street's major indexes all slid more than 2 percent on Monday, with the benchmark S&P 500 closing at its lowest in 14 months, on concerns about slowing economic growth ahead of a highly anticipated decision from the Federal Reserve this week on the course of U.S. interest-rate hikes.

Headlines: Oracle sees strong third quarter on cloud strength, share rise
Description: Oracle Corp on Monday forecast current-quarter profit above estimates after growth in its cloud services and license support unit helped the business software maker surpass Wall Street expectations for the second quarter.

Headlines: Google to spend $1 billion on new campus in New York
Description: Alphabet Inc's  Google is investing more than $1 billion on a new campus in New York, becoming the second major technology company after Amazon to pick America's financial capital to expand and create thousands of jobs.

Headlines: Embraer's net proceeds from Boeing deal the same, despite higher price
Description: Brazil's Embraer SA will receive the same net proceeds from a deal to sell 80 percent of its commercial jet unit to Boeing Co, even though the U.S. aircraft maker increased the enterprise value which includes debt by 11 percent.

Headlines: DoubleLine's Gundlach says U.S. equities are in long-term bear market
Description: Jeffrey Gundlach, chief executive of DoubleLine Capital, on Monday said the S&P 500 stock index is headed to new lows and that U.S. equities are in a long-term bear market.

Headlines: J&J announces $5 billion share buyback after shares extend losses
Description: Johnson & Johnson said on Monday it plans to buy back up to $5 billion of its stock, after a Reuters report on Friday that the company knew for decades that its Baby Powder contained cancer-causing asbestos wiped about $40 billion from its market value.

Headlines: Oil falls, U.S. crude dips below $50 on oversupply fears
Description: Oil prices fell more than 2 percent on Monday, with U.S. crude tumbling below $50 a barrel, on signs of oversupply in the United States and as investor concern over global economic growth and fuel demand grows.

Headlines: J&J announces $5 billion share repurchase plan
Description: Johnson & Johnson  on Monday announced a share repurchase of up to $5 billion of its common stock.  The repurchase plan has no time limit and may be suspended for periods or discontinued at any time, the company said in a statement.

Headlines: General Dynamics warns Canada: Canceling Saudi deal would cost billions
Description: General Dynamics Corp  on Monday put pressure on Ottawa over the sale of armored vehicles to Saudi Arabia, warning that the federal government would incur "billions of dollars of liability" by unilaterally scrapping the deal.

Headlines: Global stocks drop, where is 'Santa Claus rally'?
Description: Broad stock declines in Europe and the United States dragged world equity markets lower on Monday, adding to a sell-off that has sent global stocks near 17-month lows.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs fires back after Malaysia charges bank in 1MDB probe
Description: Malaysia on Monday filed criminal charges against Goldman Sachs Group Inc related to its dealings with the sovereign wealth fund 1MDB, and Goldman Sachs fired back that the previous Malaysian government had lied to the investment bank.

Headlines: U.S. healthcare stocks drop after judge rules Obamacare unconstitutional
Description: Shares of U.S. health insurers, hospitals and healthcare companies fell on Monday in the aftermath of a ruling by a federal judge in Texas that the Affordable Care Act (ACA), commonly called Obamacare, was unconstitutional.

Headlines: Carlyle nearing deal to buy StandardAero for more than $5 billion: sources
Description: Private equity firm Carlyle Group LP  is nearing a deal to acquire aviation services company StandardAero from Veritas Capital, another buyout firm, for more than $5 billion, including debt, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: Siemens, Alstom offer to sell high-speed train technology: sources
Description: Siemens  and Alstom  have offered to sell either one of their high-speed train technology to address EU antitrust concerns about their plan to create a Franco-German rail champion, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. ethanol producers seek pricing reform as markets plunge, ADM sells
Description: U.S. ethanol producers stung by collapsing prices are seeking changes to the way benchmark values for the biofuel are established, arguing the current system used by exchanges is vulnerable to manipulation, according to sources.

Headlines: BNY Mellon to pay more than $54 million for improper handling of ADRs: SEC
Description: The top U.S. securities regulator on Monday said that Bank of New York Mellon  will pay more than $54 million to settle charges of improper handling of "pre-released" American Depositary Receipts, U.S. securities representing foreign shares of a foreign company.

Headlines: Czech cyber watchdog calls Huawei, ZTE products a security threat
Description: The Czech cyber watchdog warned network operators on Monday against using software or hardware made by Chinese telecom equipment suppliers Huawei and ZTE , saying they posed a security threat.

Headlines: Goldman, Morgan Stanley gain clout in Brazil as NY IPOs grow
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc , Morgan Stanley and Bank of America Merrill Lynch are regaining clout in Latin America's largest economy as Brazilian companies opt to list shares in New York instead of on their local exchanges, Refinitiv data shows.

Headlines: Nissan CEO calls on Renault to listen to detail of Ghosn allegations
Description: Nissan Motor's CEO called on directors at alliance partner Renault to heed its reasons for sacking former Chairman Carlos Ghosn over alleged financial misconduct amid tensions over how to handle the fallout from his arrest.

Headlines: China, EU lambast United States for miring WTO in crisis
Description: The United States came under fire from China and the European Union on Monday, accused by both major trading partners of taking protectionist measures and bringing the World Trade Organization (WTO) to its knees.

Headlines: China says U.S. has brought back 'the ghost of unilateralism' to WTO
Description: China said on Monday that the Trump administration's trade measures on items from steel to intellectual property taken under the guise national security were "bringing back to life the ghost of unilateralism".

Headlines: Eni, Shell knew of 'sharks' in Nigeria graft case: judge
Description: An Italian judge said on Monday oil majors Eni  and Royal Dutch Shell  were fully aware their 2011 purchase of a Nigerian oilfield would result in corrupt payments to Nigerian politicians and officials.

Headlines: German union calls strike at Amazon warehouses
Description: German trade union Verdi called on workers at two Amazon  logistic centers to strike on Monday, part of a long-running campaign for better pay and conditions.

Headlines: ABB to sell Power Grids to Hitachi, revamp business structure
Description: ABB  reached a deal with Japan's Hitachi  to sell its Power Grids division, with the Swiss engineering group adding it plans to return net cash proceeds of $7.6-7.8 billion from selling the 80.1 percent stake in the unit to shareholders.

Headlines: Foxconn not in settlement talks with Qualcomm in Apple battle: attorney
Description: The lead attorney for the group of Apple Inc device assemblers seeking at least $9 billion in damages from Qualcomm Inc said on Sunday the contract manufacturers are not in settlement talks with the mobile chip supplier and are "gearing up and heading toward the trial" in April.

Headlines: As bitcoin trading shifts shape, big money stays away
Description: (This version of the December 7th story corrects spelling of first name to Erik (not Eric) in paragraph 21)

Headlines: Ten years on, Fed's long, strange, trip to zero redefined central banking
Description: Whatever the acronym, when the U.S. Federal Reserve dropped its policy rate to near zero on Dec. 16, 2008, to counter a full-scale economic crisis, it ushered in what the central bank's chairman at the time, Ben Bernanke, called "the end of the old regime."

Headlines: Mercedes-Benz cuts China prices after tariff on U.S.-made cars suspended
Description: German luxury carmaker Mercedes-Benz on Monday said it would offer discounts on cars imported into China from the United States until March 31 after Beijing suspended additional tariffs on U.S.-made cars.

Headlines: Nissan hopes Renault will listen about Ghosn misconduct
Description: Nissan's  Chief Executive said on Monday he hoped alliance partner Renault SA  will listen to its explanation of financial misconduct by former Chairman Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: German regional state to sue VW over diesel scandal: FAZ
Description: The German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg plans to sue Volkswagen over the carmaker's cheating of emissions tests, newspaper Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) reported on Monday.

Headlines: Nestle to cut about 380 jobs at four locations in Germany
Description: Swiss food giant Nestle  is cutting around 380 jobs in Germany by closing two locations and reducing the workforce at two others as it reacts to lower demand and shifts some production elsewhere, the company said on Monday.

Headlines: Canadian regulator to fine Glencore-controlled miner over Congo - WSJ
Description: A Glencore-controlled  mining company and some of its current and former executives have agreed to pay more than $22 million to settle Canadian allegations they hid the risks of doing business with an Israeli close to Congolese President Joseph Kabila, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Headlines: Uber welcomes, unions criticize UK plan to maintain flexible gig economy
Description: Uber Technologies Inc welcomed on Monday the British government's response to a review into workplace rights, which looks set to preserve the business models of gig economy companies, but unions rubbished the business ministry's plans.

Headlines: ABB relents to activist shareholder and unloads Power Grids unit
Description: ABB  will sell a majority stake in its Power Grids division to Japan's Hitachi  and return the proceeds to shareholders, bowing to pressure from an activist investor to sell the business that makes transformers and converters.

Headlines: Canada gets consular access to second man detained in China
Description: Canadian diplomats gained consular access on Sunday to the second of two men detained by China over the past week, Canada's foreign ministry said in a statement that gave few details, as China said it was ensuring their rights were protected.

Headlines: Exclusive: Nissan probe into Ghosn trains lens on 'CEO Reserve' fund, Dutch unit
Description: (This December 15 story was refiled to correct paragraph 9 to show date Nissan fired Ghosn as chairman as Nov. 22, not Nov. 26)

Headlines: Australia bank NAB's CEO to take long holiday around inquiry report release
Description: National Australia Bank Ltd  said on Monday its CEO will take about two months leave around the scheduled release of a major report into the country's finance sector, prompting a rebuke from a shareholder group.

Headlines: Taisho said to near $1.6 billion deal for Bristol-Myers's UPSA: Bloomberg
Description: Japanese healthcare firm Taisho Pharmaceutical Holdings Co Ltd  is said to be close to a $1.6 billion deal for Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's  French over-the-counter drugs business UPSA, Bloomberg reported on Sunday, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Headlines: EQT's board to seek talks with Rice brothers: sources
Description: EQT Corp's board of directors will ask to meet Toby and Derek Rice for talks, people familiar with the matter said on Sunday, after the two brothers threatened the largest producer of natural gas in the United States with a board challenge.

Headlines: Pemex aims for splash in shallow waters, retreats from the deeps
Description: Mexican state-run oil giant Petroleos Mexicanos will focus on existing shallow water assets and refining next year at the expense of riskier, deepwater projects under a new government that has vowed to turn around the ailing company.

Headlines: Renault seeks Nissan shareholder meeting as Ghosn crisis deepens
Description: Renault  requested a full Nissan shareholder meeting, a source close to the company said - appearing to escalate the carmaker's standoff with its Japanese alliance partner in the wake of the pay scandal engulfing Chairman and CEO Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: Shareholders call on ExxonMobil to set greenhouse gas reduction targets
Description: A number of institutional investors in ExxonMobil Corp  have said they will file a shareholder resolution which calls on the world's largest oil company to set targets for lowering its greenhouse gas emissions.

Headlines: Recent market 'jolt' will be first of many as easy money era ends, says BIS
Description: Recent sharp selloffs across global financial markets are probably the first of many, as investors adjust to a world of tighter monetary conditions and the threat of economic downturn, the Bank of International Settlements said on Sunday.

Headlines: Regulators need joined up thinking to spot derivatives risks: BIS
Description: Regulators should scrutinize clearing houses and banks together to spot financial stability threats from the world's multi-trillion dollar derivatives market, the Bank for International Settlements said on Sunday.

Headlines: Nord Stream 2 can be justified if Ukraine's interests safeguarded
Description: Germany's economy minister said he believed the Russian-backed Nord Stream 2 pipeline can go ahead while preserving Ukraine's vital interests, but that Berlin is also in talks to diversify its energy supply with liquefied natural gas.

Headlines: French government may back Michelin CEO for Renault chairman: paper
Description: The French government is considering backing Michelin  chief executive Jean-Dominique Senard for the chairmanship of Renault , replacing embattled CEO Carlos Ghosn, Le Figaro reported on Sunday, citing several sources.

Headlines: Will landing be soft or 'chaotic' as Fed begins to stop rate hike cycle
Description: In June 2006, the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for a 17th consecutive time but cushioned the increase with a strong signal that officials were ready to stop the tightening cycle.

Headlines: Renault calls for Nissan shareholder meeting: WSJ
Description: Renault SA  has sent a letter to its alliance partner Nissan Motor Co Ltd , urging the Japanese carmaker to call a meeting of its shareholders "as promptly as practicable", the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

Headlines: Qatar considering increasing its stake in Deutsche Bank: Handelsblatt
Description: Qatar is considering increasing its stake in Deutsche Bank , newspaper Handelsblatt reported on Sunday.

Headlines: Wall Street looks to Fed outlook Wednesday for early Christmas gift
Description: Investors are eager for a touch of Christmas cheer from the U.S. Federal Reserve next week, hoping for signs the central bank may ease up on interest rate hikes next year and spark a Santa Claus rally.

Headlines: Qatar Petroleum to invest $20 billion in U.S. in major expansion
Description: Qatar Petroleum (QP) is looking to invest at least $20 billion in the United States over the coming few years, its chief executive told Reuters, after the Gulf Arab state unexpectedly quit OPEC this month.

Headlines: Indonesia, EFTA sign long delayed free trade deal
Description: Indonesia on Sunday signed an economic agreement with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) aimed at increasing trade and investment, concluding almost eight years of negotiations.

Headlines: Germany plans to lower threshold for probes of foreign takeovers: Handelsblatt
Description: Berlin plans to cut to 10 percent the threshold at which it can  launch national security probes of stake purchases by non-European companies in German firms, business newspaper Handelsblatt reported on Sunday.

Headlines: 2018: The year volatility came home to roost
Description: U.S. stocks are down only slightly for 2018, but that masks a volatile year for investors.

Headlines: Boeing opens first 737 plant in China amid U.S.-Sino trade war
Description: Boeing Co  opened its first 737 completion plant in China on Saturday, a strategic investment aimed at building a sales lead over arch-rival Airbus  in one of the world's top travel markets that has been overshadowed by the U.S-China trade war.

Headlines: Motiva preliminarily picked to run Curacao refinery: report
Description: Motiva Enterprises has preliminarily been chosen by the government of Curacao to operate the 335,000-barrel-per-day Isla refinery, replacing Venezuela's state-run PDVSA, local media said on Saturday.

Headlines: OPEC has shown it can reach deal despite splits: Iran oil minister
Description: Iranian Oil Minister Bijan Zanganeh praised OPEC on Saturday for what he said was the producer group's ability to reach agreement despite intense internal political differences.

Headlines: Exclusive: T-Mobile, Sprint see Huawei shun clinching U.S. deal - sources
Description: (This story corrects paragraph 8 to show Wanzhou was arrested in Canada, not China)

Headlines: China should free Canadians held after Huawei arrest, U.S.'s Pompeo says
Description: U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Friday China should free two Canadian citizens who were detained this week after authorities in Canada arrested a senior Chinese technology executive on a U.S. extradition warrant.

Headlines: China to halt added tariffs on U.S.-made cars in easing of trade tensions
Description: China will temporarily suspend additional 25 percent tariffs on U.S.-made vehicles and auto parts starting Jan. 1, 2019, the  finance ministry said on Friday, following a truce in a trade war between the world's two largest economies.

Headlines: Tesla cuts China prices after tariff drop on U.S.-made cars
Description: Tesla Inc  has cut prices on its Model S and Model X vehicles in China after Beijing suspended additional tariffs on U.S.-made cars.

Headlines: California regulator opens case against PG&E for falsifying pipeline safety records
Description: The California Public Utilities Commission has opened a proceeding to consider penalties against Pacific Gas and Electric Company, ordering immediate action against the utility for falsifying safety documents for natural gas pipelines, the regulator said in a statement on Friday.

Headlines: Global growth worry hits stocks, but U.S. data lifts dollar
Description: A gauge of global stocks tumbled on Friday after weak economic data from China and Europe intensified global growth worries as investors weighed the broader impact of the trade dispute between the United States and China.

Headlines: CVS defends settlement that allowed Aetna merger as judge assesses
Description: CVS Health Corp  defended on Friday an agreement with the U.S. Justice Department which allowed it to purchase health insurer Aetna for $69 billion, a settlement that a federal judge is still assessing.

Headlines: U.S. sets new March 2 date for China tariff increases amid talks
Description: The U.S. Trade Representative's office on Friday officially changed the scheduled date of a tariff rate increase on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods to 12:01 a.m. EST (0501 GMT) on March 2, 2019 as the United States and China pursue talks on trade and intellectual property.

Headlines: Anti-harassment groups share $20 million CBS handout after Moonves exit
Description: CBS Corp  on Friday named the Time's Up anti-sexual harassment group and 17 other organizations that will share a $20 million donation stemming from the exit of its chief executive Les Moonves following allegations of sexual misconduct.

Headlines: Wall St. tumbles on global growth worries, J&J decline
Description: Wall Street's three major indexes tumbled on Friday and the Dow confirmed a correction as weak data from China and Europe stoked fears of a global economic slowdown, while Johnson & Johnson shares were the biggest drag after Reuters reported the company knew for decades that its Baby Powder contained asbestos.

Headlines: Intel, TPG in early talks to sell McAfee to Thoma Bravo: source
Description: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo LLC is in early talks to buy security software company McAfee from TPG Capital and Intel Corp, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday.

Headlines: Small-cap S&P 600 index confirms bear market
Description: As U.S. stocks have been rocked by trade tensions and monetary policy worries, shares of small-cap companies, by one measure, have now confirmed that they are in their first bear market in three years.

Headlines: J&J shares nosedive on report it knew of asbestos in Baby Powder
Description: Shares of Johnson & Johnson  fell 10 percent on Friday and were on track to post their biggest percentage drop in more than 16 years, after Reuters reported that the pharma major knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in its Baby Powder.

Headlines: Irish regulator investigates Facebook over private photo glitch
Description: An Irish regulator said on Friday it was investigating Facebook Inc  following the company's disclosure that a bug may have exposed private photos of up to 6.8 million users, the latest in a series of Facebook privacy glitches.

Headlines: Air Berlin's administrator sues Etihad for up to 2 billion euros
Description: German airline Air Berlin's insolvency administrator is suing Abu Dhabi's Etihad, its former owner, for damages of up 2 billion euros ($2.26 billion), a Berlin court said on Friday.

Headlines: PG&E seeks 6.4 percent rate hike in 2020
Description: (This Dec. 13 story corrects the rate-hike percentage to 6.4 from 12 in the headline and the first paragraph)

Headlines: Canada says it agrees with U.S. on need to keep politics out of Huawei case
Description: Canada and the United States agreed on Friday that politics should be kept out of the process to extradite senior Huawei Technologies Co [HWT.UL] executive Meng Wanzhou, who is being held on a U.S. extradition warrant, Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland said.

Headlines: Colombia court fines Odebrecht consortium $250 million for graft
Description: A Colombian tribunal fined a consortium led by Brazilian construction firm Odebrecht [ODBES.UL] $250 million and banned it from government contracts for 10 years, saying the group used corrupt tactics to win infrastructure contracts.

Headlines: Starbucks sales growth to be steady despite UberEats deal, plans for China expansion
Description: Starbucks Corp  said on Thursday it was partnering with UberEats for delivery from about 3,500 U.S. stores and would nearly double its outlets in China over the next four years, but forecast that same-store sales would remain steady, sending shares down 3 percent.

Headlines: LVMH splashes out on luxury hotels with $3.2 billion Belmond deal
Description: Luxury goods maker LVMH  has agreed to buy Belmond , the owner of hotels including Venice's landmark Cipriani, for a total of $3.2 billion to raise its profile in upmarket hospitality.

Headlines: Volkswagen says talks on cooperation with Ford progressing
Description: Volkswagen's  talks with Ford on the two companies cooperating are progressing, though a few details still need to be worked out, the German carmaker said on Friday.

Headlines: Facebook's lead EU regulator opens probe into data breach
Description: Facebook's  lead regulator in the European Union, the Irish Data Protection Commissioner (DPC), on Friday began an investigation into a number of breach notifications received from the social networking site.

Headlines: U.S. consumer spending strengthening in boost to economy
Description: U.S. consumer spending gathered momentum in November as households bought furniture, electronics and a range of other goods, which could further allay fears of a significant slowdown in the American economy even as the outlook overseas continued to darken.

Headlines: Ousted Nissan boss' daughter takes documents, cash from apartment
Description: The daughter of ousted Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn early on Friday retrieved documents and cash from a corporate apartment in Rio de Janeiro, capping a legal battle over the items, which the carmaker maintains may contain evidence of wrongdoing.

Headlines: N.Y. Fed's U.S. fourth-quarter GDP growth holds near 2.4 percent
Description: The U.S. economy is growing at a 2.42 percent pace in the fourth quarter as stronger-than-expected November data on industrial output offset the steepest drop in import prices in over three years last month, the New York Federal Reserve's Nowcast model showed on Friday.

Headlines: Atlanta Fed raises U.S. fourth-quarter GDP growth view to 3 percent
Description: The U.S. economy is expanding at a 3.0 percent annualized rate in the fourth quarter based on steady retail sales growth and stronger-than-forecast industrial output in November, the Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow forecast model showed on Friday.

Headlines: Trump praises China move on autos, says trade deal could happen soon
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed China's move on Friday to suspend additional tariffs on U.S.-made vehicles, saying it could help push forward a larger trade deal with Beijing.

Headlines: Macron calls Ford's decision over Bordeaux plant 'hostile'
Description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Friday that Ford's  decision to end production at its plant in Blanquefort, southern France next year was "hostile" and said his government was actively seeking a buyer for the site.

Headlines: Deutsche Telekom reviews Huawei ties; Orange says no on 5G
Description: Huawei [HWT.UL] faces fresh challenges in Europe after Germany's Deutsche Telekom  announced it would review its vendor strategy and Orange  said it would not hire the Chinese firm to build its next-generation network in France.

Headlines: Scale of theft at Shell's Singapore refinery much greater, court documents show
Description: Around $150 millions' worth of oil was stolen from Shell's biggest global refinery over several years, Singapore court documents reviewed by Reuters show, far more than reported when police first revealed the heist earlier this year.

Headlines: GM to begin U.S. layoff notices as it offers job transfers
Description: General Motors Co  on Friday said it is beginning to send formal notices to U.S. government agencies of its plan to end production at auto plants and cut thousands of jobs as it shrinks passenger car production in North America.

Headlines: LSE names Experian's Donald Robert as next chairman
Description: London Stock Exchange Group Plc  said on Friday Chairman Donald Brydon would be replaced by Donald Robert, chairman of the world's biggest credit data firm Experian Plc .

Headlines: U.S. business inventories increase strongly in October
Description: - U.S. business inventories rose solidly in October as stocks at retailers increased by the most in more than a year, suggesting inventory investment could contribute to economic growth in the fourth quarter.

Headlines: U.S. industrial output up 0.6 percent in November, manufacturing flat
Description: U.S. industrial output rose in November as a jump in mining and utilities production was offset by drops in other sectors including business equipment and construction.

Headlines: Apple to push software update in China as Qualcomm case threatens sales ban
Description: Apple Inc, facing a court ban in China on some of its iPhone models over alleged infringement of Qualcomm Inc patents, said on Friday it will push software updates to users in a bid to resolve potential issues.

Headlines: Exclusive: France plans Renault CEO hunt as board frays over Ghosn - sources
Description: The French government is seeking candidates to replace Renault's  embattled boss Carlos Ghosn, as some board members began to voice doubts about keeping him in office after his indictment in Japan for suspected misconduct, several sources told Reuters.

Headlines: Merck bolsters animal health unit with $2.4 billion Antelliq purchase
Description: Merck and Co  said on Friday it will buy privately held French company Antelliq Group, which makes digital identification products for livestock, for about 2.1 billion euros ($2.37 billion) to bolster its fast-growing animal health business.

Headlines: Renault board did not consider replacing Ghosn: interim chairman
Description: Renault's board did not consider replacing Chief Executive Carlos Ghosn when it met on Thursday, interim chairman Philippe Lagayette said in a statement issued by the carmaker.

Headlines: Exclusive: China Development Bank supervising HNA asset sales - sources
Description: China Development Bank (CDB) is leading a team to supervise HNA Group's asset disposals as the heavily indebted conglomerate scales back operations to a point that will leave it holding only core assets, people familiar with the situation said.

Headlines: SoftBank telco IPO sees strong demand despite Huawei, network disruption
Description: Domestic investors have sought nearly double the number of shares offered by SoftBank Group Corp's  soon-to-list wireless unit, two sources from a lead IPO underwriter said, underscoring strong demand for Japan's third-largest telco.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp fills key management posts after year of turmoil
Description: Thyssenkrupp  moved on Friday to fill key management positions, preparing for the spin off its capital goods business after a tumultuous year that saw the resignation of the conglomerate's top leadership.

Headlines: Exclusive: Chinese battery firm halts purchases of cobalt from Glencore - sources
Description: Chinese battery firm GEM has stopped buying cobalt from Glencore as the price of the battery material crashed below that agreed in a three-year deal between the two companies, sources close to the matter said.

Headlines: Jet Airways' survival may rest on founder Goyal leaving the cockpit
Description: Jet Airways Ltd's  69-year-old founder Naresh Goyal, who started out as an assistant in a travel agency, wove together charm, persistence and consummate dealmaking to build India's biggest full-service carrier.

Headlines: Exclusive: India's Motherson Sumi in early-stage merger talks with Leoni - sources
Description: Indian car wiring maker Motherson Sumi Systems Ltd  is in early talks with German peer Leoni AG  over a possible merger of the pair, two people close to the matter said.

Headlines: Barclays promotes 85 in investment bank to managing director
Description: Barclays has promoted 85 executives in the international division that houses its investment bank to the rank of managing director, the British lender said on Friday.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp appoints Walker as new boss of elevator unit
Description: Industrials conglomerate Thyssenkrupp  on Friday appointed Peter Walker as the new chief executive of its prized elevators unit, the group said.

Headlines: Airbus names Mhun as next programs chief
Description: Airbus  on Friday named services boss Philippe Mhun as its next head of programs, succeeding defense and commercial aerospace veteran Didier Evrard, who is scheduled to retire.

Headlines: U.S. recession risks jump, Fed rate hike expectations slump - Reuters poll
Description: The risk of a U.S. recession in the next two years has risen to 40 percent, according to a Reuters poll of economists who also found a significant shift in expectations toward fewer Federal Reserve interest rate rises next year.

Headlines: Nissan files claim against Ghosn's sister in Brazil court
Description: Nissan Motor Co  has filed a court claim against Carlos Ghosn's sister that references alleged "unjust enrichment", escalating a battle being waged in Brazilian courts between the car maker and its once-celebrated former chairman.

Headlines: Nissan board unlikely to select new chairman on Monday: source
Description: Nissan Motor Co's board is unlikely to select a chairman to succeed Carlos Ghosn as had been expected on Dec. 17 after a panel tasked to choose a candidate did not agree on a nominee in a meeting held Thursday, a source said.

Headlines: Explainer: Ex-Nissan chief Ghosn affair raises issues beyond one man, one company
Description: How big should executive pay packets be? How widespread is lax corporate governance in Japan? And what's the future of the alliance between Nissan and France's Renault?

Headlines: Ahead of China anniversary, trade war fans calls for faster market reforms
Description: China's trade war with the United States is spurring some Chinese entrepreneurs, government advisers and think-tanks to call for faster reforms in the world's second-largest economy and the freeing of a private sector stifled by state controls.

Headlines: Japan's business mood, capex steady but outlook sours: BOJ tankan
Description: Japanese business confidence and capital expenditure plans held steady from three months ago, a closely-watched central bank survey showed, a sign companies weren't significantly worried about escalating trade frictions and global growth concerns.

Headlines: Oil prices edge up on hopes global supplies will tighten
Description: Oil prices climbed more than 2 percent on Thursday, after data showed inventory declines in the United States and as investors began to expect that the global oil market could have a deficit sooner than they had previously thought.

Headlines: New York sues Target, Walmart over lead-contaminated toys
Description: Target Corp , Walmart Inc  and toy importer LaRose Industries were sued on Thursday over the sale of lead-contaminated children's toys, New York Attorney General Barbara Underwood said.

Headlines: GE's digital unit to sell majority stake in ServiceMax
Description: General Electric Co  on Thursday said its digital unit would sell a majority stake in ServiceMax, a cloud-based provider of software used in inventory and workforce management, to technology-focused private equity firm Silver Lake.

Headlines: Costco margin dip overshadows sales beat, shares slide
Description: Costco Wholesale Corp's  gross margins fell in the first quarter, as the warehouse operator paid higher wages, ramped up investments in its online business and cut prices amid intense competition in the grocery industry.

Headlines: Evidence of Apple switch ruled inadmissible in Qualcomm antitrust case
Description: A federal judge on Thursday ruled that evidence provided by chip supplier Qualcomm Inc  that major phone makers like Apple Inc  have moved to competing suppliers like Intel Corp  cannot be used to fight allegations Qualcomm acted to preserve a monopoly on some mobile phone chips.

Headlines: Instacart, Amazon's Whole Foods relationship to end next year
Description: Instacart said on Thursday it will stop delivering groceries for Whole Foods next year, ending a partnership that has been under stress since Amazon.com Inc  bought the upmarket grocer last year.

Headlines: Wall Street ends flat as nervous investors flock to defensive shares
Description: The S&P 500 finished little changed after a volatile session on Thursday, as investors continued to be spooked by uncertainty on both domestic and international issues, driving up bids for defensive shares while financials and consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest drags.

Headlines: Long-time GE bear ditches negative view, shares jump
Description: A JP Morgan analyst who has long held a negative outlook on General Electric Co  shares as they have tumbled upgraded his view on the conglomerate's stock on Thursday.

Headlines: Apple plans new $1 billion campus for Austin, Texas
Description: Apple Inc  said on Thursday it would spend $1 billion to build a second campus in Austin, Texas, that will house up to 15,000 workers as part of a broader push by U.S. companies to create more domestic jobs.

Headlines: Renault finds no irregularities in Ghosn pay audit
Description: Renault  said on Thursday an audit launched in the wake of Chairman and CEO Carlos Ghosn's arrest in Japan had so far found no irregularities with his pay at the French carmaker.

Headlines: Japan Post to invest $2.6 billion in U.S. insurer Aflac: source
Description: Japan Post Holdings Co  is planning to invest about $2.6 billion in Aflac Inc , aiming to become the largest shareholder in the U.S. insurer, a person familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Trump says GM shift to electric vehicles is 'not going to work'
Description: President Donald Trump on Thursday said General Motors Co's  decision to shift much of its focus to electric vehicles will not succeed, and he asserted a new trade deal will make it harder for the company to move work to other countries.

Headlines: Caterpillar CEO Jim Umpleby adds chairman role
Description: Caterpillar Inc  said on Thursday Chief Executive Officer Jim Umpleby would take on the additional role of chairman, effective immediately.

Headlines: Global stocks lose steam as nerves persist, euro dips after ECB
Description: A gauge of world equities was little changed after giving up early gains on Thursday, continuing a pattern seen for the past several sessions, while the euro eased after the European Central Bank formally ended its bond purchasing scheme.

Headlines: Adobe's quarterly revenue surges 23 percent
Description: Adobe Systems Inc on Thursday reported a 22.8 percent rise in quarterly revenue, helped by higher subscriptions for its flagship Creative Cloud suite of software that includes Photoshop.

Headlines: Brazil judge allows ousted Nissan chairman access to Rio apartment
Description: A Brazilian appellate judge on Thursday granted ousted Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn access to a Rio de Janeiro apartment, whose contents have become subject of an intense legal battle in local courts.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and others back risk management startup AccessFintech
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc , JP Morgan Chase & Co , Citigroup Inc  and Credit Suisse Group AG  have invested $17.5 million in AccessFintech, a startup that sells technology to help financial firms better handle business errors, the companies said on Thursday.

Headlines: Enel-BYD say Chile electric bus roll-out heralds more for region
Description: Europe's biggest utility Enel and Chinese electric vehicle giant BYD on Thursday marked the arrival of 100 electric buses in Chile and said they would work together on similar plans for three other Latin American nations.

Headlines: U.S. auto sales expected to dip in 2019, says NADA
Description: New vehicle sales in the United States are expected to drop next year as higher interest rates and rising prices could prompt customers to hold off their car-buying plans, the National Automobile Dealers Association (NADA) said on Thursday.

Headlines: WPP hires Publicis executive as chief marketing officer
Description: WPP  said it had hired Laurent Ezekiel from its French rival Publicis  to be its chief marketing and growth officer, tasked with helping new boss Mark Read steer the world's biggest advertising group back to growth.

Headlines: YouTube, under pressure for problem content, takes down 58 million videos in quarter
Description: YouTube took down more than 58 million videos and 224 million comments during the third quarter based on violations of its policies, the unit of Alphabet Inc's  Google said on Thursday in an effort to demonstrate progress in suppressing problem content.

Headlines: U.S. confirms China soybean sale, but size disappoints
Description: China's meager first purchase of U.S. soybeans since its trade war with the United States began in July disappointed farmers, grain traders and a U.S. government official hoping for larger sales to lift slumping prices and absorb a huge surplus across the U.S. farm belt, they said on Thursday.

Headlines: Standard Chartered axes over 200 jobs in India: source
Description: Standard Chartered Plc has laid off over 200 employees in India in its retail banking division, as more customers move to digital services, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: Qualcomm to file suits in Chinese courts to ban iPhone XS, XR sales
Description: Chipmaker Qualcomm Inc  is asking courts in China to ban sales of Apple Inc's  latest iPhone models XS and XR after winning a preliminary injunction against older models, the company confirmed on Thursday.

Headlines: ECB ends crisis-fighting bond buys but eyes increasing risks
Description: The European Central Bank formally ended its 2.6 trillion euro crisis-fighting bond purchase scheme on Thursday but promised to keep feeding stimulus for years into an economy struggling with an unexpected slowdown and political turmoil.

Headlines: Vitol, rival oil traders in spotlight of Brazil bribery probe
Description: Brazil's epic "Car Wash" corruption investigation has taken down presidents and elite businessmen, and led to the largest corporate leniency deal ever signed.

Headlines: Factbox: The trading firms under investigation in Brazil graft probe
Description: Last week, Brazilian investigators accused four of the world's largest oil-trading firms of participating in a corruption scheme focused on Brazil's state-controlled oil company Petrobras.

Headlines: Delta Air Lines shares drop on weak revenue outlook
Description: Shares in U.S. carrier Delta Air Lines Inc  dropped 4 percent in Thursday morning trading on concerns that slowing global economies would limit the No. 2 U.S. airline's revenue growth in 2019 despite strong travel demand.

Headlines: U.S. labor market tightening; inflation pressures muted
Description: The number of Americans filing applications for jobless benefits tumbled to near a 49-year low last week, which could ease concerns about a slowdown in the labor market and economy.

Headlines: Exclusive: Carlsberg, United Breweries plead leniency in India beer cartel probe - sources
Description: Denmark's Carlsberg  and India's United Breweries  have filed pleas with Indian authorities, seeking leniency in a probe into alleged collusion to fix beer prices, five sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Group forms to oppose tie-up of U.S. telecom firms T-Mobile, Sprint
Description: An array of companies and groups that have opposed T-Mobile US Inc's  plan to buy Sprint Corp  announced on Thursday that they had banded together, saying the deal would lead to higher prices for wireless customers and hurt rural consumers.

Headlines: Ford set to end production at Blanquefort in France, jobs at risk
Description: Ford  will end production at its Blanquefort plant in France by late August next year after rejecting a rescue deal for the factory, in a move which drew the ire of France's finance minister due to the risk of large-scale job losses.

Headlines: Huawei $2 billion security pledge followed walkout by British official: sources
Description: Huawei's relations with British authorities hit a low last month when a top official walked out of a meeting with the Chinese company over its perceived failure to fix security holes in its products, sources familiar with the talks told Reuters.

Headlines: Ford's rejection of deal for Blanquefort was 'betrayal': French minister
Description: Ford's  rejection of a rescue deal for the Blanquefort site in France represented a "betrayal" by the U.S. carmaker, said French finance minister Bruno Le Maire on Thursday.

Headlines: Bombardier's venture in China gets $453 million state rail contract
Description: Canadian manufacturer Bombardier Inc's Chinese joint venture said on Thursday it had won a $453 million contract to supply 168 high-speed train cars to state-owned China Railway Corp (CRC), making it the second order win this year for China's growing high-speed network.

Headlines: Airbus strategy review augurs clean break under new CEO
Description: Airbus has launched a strategic review to outline changes under incoming chief executive Guillaume Faury as it faces   industrial challenges and prepares for overdue modernization, industry sources said.

Headlines: ECB still sees balanced economic outlook, but downside risk more prominent
Description: The European Central Bank maintained on Thursday its long-standing assessment that risks to growth remain "broadly balanced", but acknowledged that downside elements were becoming more prominent.

Headlines: Draghi comments at ECB press conference
Description: The European Central Bank decided on Thursday to end its lavish asset purchase scheme but otherwise kept policy broadly unchanged, promising protracted stimulus for an economy struggling with an unexpected slowdown and political turmoil.

Headlines: What comes after the ECB's money presses stop?
Description: The European Central Bank will formally end its 2.6 trillion euro money-printing scheme -- known as quantitative easing, or QE -- on Thursday but stimulus will continue for years and the central bank may even look at further measures of support.

Headlines: ECB formally ends QE, keeps reinvestments open-ended
Description: The European Central Bank decided on Thursday to formally end its 2.6 trillion euro ($2.95 trillion) bond purchase scheme but said it would keep reinvesting cash from maturing bonds for a long time after its first interest rate hike.

Headlines: UK's Nissan Brexit letter still too confidential to release two years on: FOI
Description: A British government letter to Nissan two years ago offering reassurances about Brexit, which helped secure a major investment from the Japanese carmaker, is still considered too sensitive to release, a Reuters freedom of information request revealed.

Headlines: Exclusive: China makes first big U.S. soybean purchase since Trump-Xi truce
Description: China on Wednesday made its first major purchases of U.S. soybeans since President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping struck a trade war truce earlier this month, providing some relief to U.S. farmers who have struggled to find buyers for their record-large harvest.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler may review $5.7 billion plan if Italy taxes diesel, petrol cars
Description: Fiat Chrysler (FCA) could review its 5 billion euro ($5.7 billion) Italian investment plan, which includes a shift to cleaner engines, if Rome raises taxes on petrol and diesel cars.

Headlines: China's auto sales in 2019 to roughly match 2018: industry association
Description: China, the world's biggest car market, expects to sell 28 million vehicles in 2019, roughly level with 2018, its Association of Automobile Manufacturers said on Thursday.

Headlines: Top German court rules Uber limousine service illegal
Description: Germany's highest court ruled on Thursday that a defunct limousine service offered by Uber [UBER.UL] was illegal, in a setback for the U.S. ride-hailing company that has struggled to comply with the law in Europe's largest economy.

Headlines: VW's Skoda deliveries drop in November on China, January-November shipments up
Description: Czech carmaker Skoda Auto, part of the Volkswagen Group, delivered 1.149 million vehicles in the January-November period, a 5.1 percent rise from a year ago, it said on Thursday.

Headlines: IEA sees global oil supply tightening more quickly in 2019
Description: The global oil market could move into deficit sooner than expected thanks to OPEC's output agreement with Russia and to Canada's decision to cut supply, the International Energy Agency said on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. solar takes hit from Trump tariffs but is cheaper than ever: report
Description: U.S. solar installations fell 15 percent in the third quarter as the Trump administration's tariffs on overseas-made panels forced developers to put off large projects, according to a report commissioned by the industry's primary trade group.

Headlines: OPEC exit frees Qatar from U.S. legal concerns
Description: Even before taking over Qatar's energy policy in a government reshuffle last month, Qatar Petroleum (QP) CEO Saad al-Kaabi had long wanted the Gulf state to leave OPEC.

Headlines: Autostrade could challenge government decree over Genoa bridge: source
Description: Autostrade per l'Italia will decide on Thursday whether to appeal against a government decree that excludes the operator of the collapsed Genoa bridge from works to rebuild it, a source familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Japan's SoftBank to shun Huawei in favor of Ericsson, Nokia equipment: Nikkei
Description: SoftBank Group Corp plans to replace 4G network equipment from China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd with hardware from Nokia and Ericsson, Nikkei reported on Thursday, without citing sources.

Headlines: Canada warns U.S. not to politicize extradition cases
Description: Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland on Wednesday warned the United States not to politicize extradition cases, a day after President Donald Trump said he could intervene in the affair of a Chinese executive detained in Canada at Washington's request.

Headlines: Chinese state media urges Canada to defy U.S., free Huawei executive
Description: Canada should distance itself from U.S. "hegemonism" and grant unconditional freedom to Meng Wanzhou, a top executive of China's Huawei detained in Vancouver on Washington's request, state-owned tabloid Global Times said in a Thursday editorial.

Headlines: Japan rules out asking private firms to avoid telecoms gear that could be malicious
Description: Japan's government has no plan to ask private companies to avoid buying telecommunications equipment that could have malicious functions, such as information leakage, its top  spokesman, Yoshihide Suga, said on Thursday.

Headlines: Hyundai Motor Group to provide suppliers with $1.5 billion in funding
Description: South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co  plans to provide funding worth 1.7 trillion won ($1.5 billion) to stabilize management of its suppliers, the company said in a statement on Thursday.

Headlines: Nissan says ex-boss Ghosn still has no access to Rio apartment
Description: Nissan Motor Co's  ex-chairman Carlos Ghosn and his representatives still have no right to access a contested Rio de Janeiro apartment, the automaker said, after a fresh legal document showed a Brazilian court decision to grant access.

Headlines: After Trump comment on Huawei, official says Justice Dept. sticks to law enforcement
Description: A top U.S. Justice Department official pushed back on Wednesday against President Donald Trump's comment that he might intervene in a legal case involving an executive from the Chinese telecommunications firm Huawei Technologies Co [HWT.UL] if it would help secure a trade deal.

Headlines: U.S. tribunal to review ruling on Qualcomm request for iPhone ban
Description: The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) said on Wednesday it would review a ruling that a ban on imports of some iPhones into the United States was not in the public interest, even if Apple Inc  infringed a Qualcomm  patent.

Headlines: Trading Trump: Wall Street stresses over White House comments
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co's  trading desk was not buying what U.S. President Donald Trump was selling this week.

Headlines: Canada frees CFO of China's Huawei on bail; Trump might intervene
Description: A top executive of Chinese telecoms giant Huawei Technologies Co Ltd was granted bail by a Canadian court on Tuesday, 10 days after her arrest in Vancouver at the request of U.S. authorities sparked a diplomatic dispute.

Headlines: North America to weigh on Under Armour's 2019 revenue growth, shares slide
Description: Sportswear maker Under Armour Inc  on Wednesday forecast 2019 revenue growth and profit below Wall Street estimates on expectations of flat sales in North America, triggering a 11 percent drop in its shares.

Headlines: China's Zhoushan to go after Singapore marine hub's top billing
Description: China's port city of Zhoushan is planning to challenge Singapore's dominance of the multi-billion dollar shipping fuel industry, relying on proximity to some of the world's biggest ports and Beijing's support to give it an edge.

Headlines: United Airlines CEO doubles down on growth strategy as stock rides tailwind
Description: With many rival airlines scaling back plans to add travel routes and seats in a bid to protect margins, Oscar Munoz is taking United Airlines in a different direction.

Headlines: Nissan to boost external board seats, set up compensation committee: source
Description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd  plans to boost the number of external board members and set up a committee to oversee compensation as part of its effort to improve governance following the arrest of former Chairman Carlos Ghosn for financial misconduct, a source said.

Headlines: Wall Street closes up, investors optimistic on China trade
Description: U.S. stocks closed up on Wednesday afternoon, though well below their session highs as investors pulled back in the last few minutes of trading despite optimism about U.S.-China trade relations and some reassuring signs in British politics.

Headlines: Crypto startup AriseBank settles fraud accusations with SEC
Description: Cryptocurrency startup AriseBank will pay $2.3 million to the U.S. Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) to settle accusations of defrauding investors through claims such as building a cryptocurrency bank.

Headlines: Trade thaw lifts stocks, sterling rises on May bets
Description: A gauge of global stock markets rallied along with U.S. Treasury yields on Wednesday as optimism abounded for a trade thaw between the United States and China while sterling bounced on indications UK Prime Minister Theresa May would survive a no-confidence vote.

Headlines: FCC considers ending merger ban among broadcast networks
Description: The Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday voted to open a new review of U.S. media ownership rules and seek comments on whether the government should end a prohibition on mergers among the four largest broadcast networks.

Headlines: Norfolk Southern moves headquarters to Atlanta
Description: Norfolk Southern Corp  said on Wednesday it would shift its headquarters to Atlanta from Virginia, tapping a major hub for transportation.

Headlines: Toyota advances plans to replace Takata airbags in 65,000 vehicles
Description: Toyota Motor Corp  said on Wednesday it is advancing by a year plans to replace Takata airbags in about 65,000 Toyota and Lexus vehicles in the United States it had previously replaced.

Headlines: Intel plans 'stacked' circuits in bid to regain its chipmaking lead
Description: Intel Corp  said on Wednesday that it has developed a way to stack its computing circuits on top of one another in a bid to regain the lead in chip manufacturing technology that it has lost to rivals like Taiwan Semiconductor Co Ltd  in recent years.

Headlines: Exclusive: Airbus staff error led to fatal Mali copter crash - German official
Description: The fatal crash of a German armed forces helicopter in Mali last year was caused by the failure of mechanics from manufacturer Airbus to correctly set the aircraft's rotor controls after repairs, a defense official told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: United Airlines to add international routes from San Francisco
Description: United Continental Holdings Inc  said on Wednesday it would add flights to New Delhi, Toronto and Melbourne from San Francisco, as the No. 3 U.S. airline looks to tap higher-paying international routes.

Headlines: U.S. consumer prices flat; underlying inflation firm
Description: U.S. consumer prices were unchanged in November, held back by a sharp decline in the price of gasoline, but underlying inflation pressures remained firm amid rising rents and healthcare costs.

Headlines: Amazon aims at office workers with compact cashier-less food store
Description: Amazon.com Inc on Wednesday opened a compact version of its cashier-less Amazon Go food stores, broadening its footprint in the bricks-and-mortar world in a move to add shops in places such as office lobbies and hospitals.

Headlines: Amazon aims at office workers with compact cashier-less food store
Description: Amazon.com Inc on Wednesday opened a compact version of its cashier-less Amazon Go food stores, broadening its footprint in the bricks-and-mortar world in a move to add shops in places such as office lobbies and hospitals.

Headlines: U.S. not swayed by WTO reform proposals
Description: Proposals for reforming the World Trade Organization fail to deal with problems raised by the United States, the U.S. envoy  to the WTO told its General Council on Wednesday.

Headlines: China preparing plan to increase access for foreign companies: WSJ
Description: China is planning to replace an industrial policy with a new program that promises greater access for foreign companies, the Wall Street Journal reported https://www.wsj.com/articles/china-is-preparing-to-increase-access-for-foreign-companies-11544622331?mod=breakingnews on Wednesday, in a move to resolve trade tensions with the United States.

Headlines: Germany seeks to assist potential bank merger: Bloomberg
Description: Germany is holding high-level talks to facilitate a possible merger of the nation's two largest private banks - Deutsche Bank  and Commerzbank  - Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Zara owner Inditex hit by FX swings and warm weather
Description: Zara owner Inditex missed sales and profit forecasts on Wednesday, hit by adverse currency moves and an unusually warm September, leading investors to wipe more than $5 billion off the fashion retailer's market value at one stage.

Headlines: Incoming Thyssenkrupp board member Merz favorite for chairwoman: sources
Description: Incoming Thyssenkrupp  supervisory board member Martina Merz has emerged as favorite to become head of the steel-to-submarines conglomerate's supervisory board, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: China's Tencent Music raises nearly $1.1 billion in U.S. IPO
Description: China-based music streaming company Tencent Music Entertainment Group  said it raised close to $1.1 billion in its U.S. initial public offering (IPO) after pricing its shares at the bottom of its targeted range.

Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would intervene with the U.S. Justice Department in the case against a Chinese telecommunications executive if it would help secure a trade deal with Beijing.

Headlines: Washington takes center stage in bank branch battles

Headlines: Exclusive: Trump says Fed shouldn't hike rates, but calls Powell 'a good man'

Description: New Jersey Transit's board will decide on Wednesday whether to award the first part of an order for up to 999 cars worth as much as $3.6 billion to Canada-based Bombardier Inc , a copy of the agency's Dec. 12 agenda shows.

Headlines: S&P 500, Dow edge lower as U.S. shutdown threat, China trade in focus
