Description: The U.S. head of Nio Inc , an electric carmaker seen as one of the main Chinese rivals to Tesla Inc , will leave the company, the firm said in a filing on Friday, the first major management departure since its September IPO.

Headlines: Mitsubishi Motors ousts Ghosn as chairman, days after Nissan firing
Description: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Monday its board removed Carlos Ghosn from his role as chairman, following his arrest and ouster from alliance partner Nissan Motor Co last week for alleged financial misconduct.

Headlines: Financial wrongdoing allegations against Carlos Ghosn
Description: (This Nov. 26 story, corrects date and clarifies condition of deadline by which authorities must file charges against Ghosn or let him go, in first paragraph)

Headlines: Samsung Elec says it will cancel $4.4 billion worth of shares
Description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  said on Friday it would cancel 4.9 trillion won ($4.4 billion) worth of its shares.

Headlines: HP Inc revenue tops estimates on personal systems business
Description: HP Inc's  quarterly revenue beat analysts' estimates on Thursday, driven by growth in its personal systems business that sells notebooks and desktops and the acquisition of Samsung's printer business.

Headlines: Dell posts revenue jump ahead of voting on VMware offer
Description: Dell Technologies Inc  reported a 15 percent rise in quarterly revenue on Thursday, as businesses were forced to upgrade their systems running on older Windows technology and on strong performance by software maker VMware.

Headlines: AT&T commits to cutting up to $20 billion in debt in 2019
Description: AT&T Inc  said on Thursday it has committed to cutting its heavy debt load next year through a variety of measures, including a review of all of its non-core assets such as its stake in streaming video company Hulu for possible sale.

Headlines: Fed minutes: Further hike 'warranted soon,' debate opened on pause
Description: Almost all Federal Reserve officials at their last meeting agreed another interest rate increase was "likely to be warranted fairly soon," but also opened debate on when to pause  further hikes and how to relay those plans to the public.

Headlines: Fed may tweak excess reserves rate again soon: minutes
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve looks set to make its second adjustment in six months to the systems it uses to control interest rates as it appears on course for yet another rate increase at its meeting next month.

Headlines: Japan brokers readying for new client surge ahead of SoftBank's mammoth IPO
Description: Japan's stockbrokers are rubbing their hands ahead of SoftBank's record-breaking $21 billion share sale, banking on the telco's brand power and unprecedented marketing campaign to boost business in a country replete with IPO-hungry investors.

Headlines: Wall Street edges down as tech, bank stocks weigh
Description: Wall Street closed slightly lower on Thursday as tech and financial shares slumped, erasing earlier gains stemming from Federal Reserve minutes showing the central bank opened the debate on when to pause further interest rate hikes.

Headlines: Fed retunes message for 2019, opening door to 'slow down'
Description: With the Federal Reserve expected next month to raise rates to what some U.S. central bankers believe is at or near a neutral level, Chairman Jerome Powell is retuning his message to signal a more cautious approach on further rate hikes next year.

Headlines: German car bosses finalizing White House meeting next week
Description: Top executives from German carmakers Volkswagen , BMW  and Daimler  are finalizing plans for a White House meeting on trade policy next week, German and U.S. officials said on Thursday.

Headlines: World shares mixed as markets consider Fed, Trump impact
Description: Wall Street seesawed on Thursday, dragged down late in the day by technology and financial stocks, while the dollar and the U.S. yield curve flattened in the wake of U.S. Federal Reserve news.

Headlines: Oil rises as Russia indicates open to cuts with OPEC
Description: Oil reversed course and rose as much as 2 percent on Thursday, after industry sources said Russia had accepted the need to cut production, together with OPEC ahead of its meeting next week.

Headlines: Exclusive: Burger chain Jack in the Box explores sale - sources
Description: Jack in the Box Inc , a U.S. hamburger restaurant chain with more than 2,000 restaurants, is exploring options that could include a sale of the company after divesting its Qdoba brand earlier this year, people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. trade restrictions have hit $369 billion of Chinese exports: monitoring group
Description: U.S. trade restrictions have hit a total of $369 billion of Chinese exports this year, much higher than the $278 billion of goods impacted by tariffs alone, a regular monitoring report of G20 trade restrictions said on Thursday.

Headlines: Amazon's treatment of sellers comes under scrutiny in Germany
Description: Germany's antitrust authority has launched an investigation into whether U.S. ecommerce giant Amazon is exploiting its market dominance in its relations with third-party retailers who use its website as a marketplace.

Headlines: Bayer to sell businesses, cut jobs after Monsanto deal
Description: Bayer , the German drugmaker that bought U.S. seed company Monsanto, announced on Thursday the sale of a number of businesses, around 12,000 job cuts and 3.3 billion euros ($3.8 billion) in impairments.

Headlines: U.S. consumer spending rises strongly, inflation moderates
Description: U.S. consumer spending increased by the most in seven months in October, but underlying price pressures slowed, with an inflation measure tracked by the Federal Reserve posting its smallest annual increase since February.

Headlines: Trump coy on China trade deal before meeting Xi
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump sent mixed signals on Thursday about the prospects for a trade deal with China, saying an agreement was close but he was not sure he wanted one, just as he left for Argentina for a meeting with President Xi Jinping.

Headlines: Twitter tumbles on fear of conservative backlash
Description: Shares of Twitter Inc  tumbled 6 percent on Thursday after reports that Fox News had not tweeted for three weeks sparked fears of a backlash by conservatives protesting a perceived liberal bias by the company.

Headlines: Exclusive: Elliott steps in to boost Arconic's sale process - sources
Description: Elliott Management Corp, the activist hedge fund that sits on Arconic Inc's  board, is working to address potential liabilities weighing on the sale process for the U.S. aluminum products maker, according to people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: GM President Ammann will take over Cruise self-driving car unit
Description: General Motors Co  President Dan Ammann will take over as chief executive of the automaker's majority-owned Cruise self-driving car subsidiary, trading in the No. 2 job at one of the world's largest automakers for a front-row position in the race to render traditional cars obsolete.

Headlines: Trump says 'long way to go' on tariffs and China
Description: U.S. President Trump said on Thursday said there was "a long way to go" on tariffs with China and urged companies to build products in the United States to avoid them.

Headlines: U.S., China exploring deal to delay more tariffs, start talks: WSJ
Description: The United States and China are exploring a trade deal in which Washington would suspend further tariffs through the spring of 2019 in exchange for new talks "looking at big changes in Chinese economic policy," the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

Headlines: Unilever CEO retires after headquarters row, replaced by insider Jope
Description: Unilever's  Chief Executive Paul Polman will step down  next month after 10 years in the job, leaving insider Alan Jope to step into his shoes after the Anglo-Dutch group's failed attempt to shift its headquarters.

Headlines: Renault-Nissan crisis meeting fails to name interim boss
Description: Renault  and Nissan  vowed to stick by their  industrial alliance on Thursday but failed to name an interim boss to stand in for Chairman Carlos Ghosn, whose arrest has threatened the French carmaker's control of the partnership.

Headlines: Bull run finale for global stocks not far off now: Reuters poll
Description: An end to the bull run in global stocks is not far away, according to a Reuters poll which also showed a broad cut to forecasts for next year on concerns over global growth and tightening financial conditions.

Headlines: Volvo Cars has no current plans for stockmarket listing: CEO
Description: Volvo Cars, owned by China's Geely, has no current plans to go for a stockmarket listing, its chief executive said, more than two months after the Swedish carmaker postponed its flotation blaming trade tensions and an automotive stocks downturn.

Headlines: Jaguar Land Rover to lay off staff temporarily at UK plant
Description: Britain's biggest carmaker Jaguar Land Rover  is to reduce the workforce at its plant in Wolverhampton, central England, by about 500 in a temporary move, it said on Thursday.

Headlines: Goldman names co-chief operating officers for Asia investment banking unit, ex-Japan
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  has named Aaron Arth and Iain Drayton co-chief operating officers of its investment banking division in Asia Pacific, excluding Japan, according to a memo seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Marriott to open nearly 30 business hotels in Europe in two years
Description: U.S. hotel chain Marriott International Inc  said on Thursday it plans to open nearly 30 Courtyard by Marriott hotels in Europe in the next two years, as it targets newer markets including Finland and Iceland.

Headlines: France's Safran aims to topple U.S. rival as no.1 aerospace supplier
Description: Safran  unveiled ambitions to become the world's leading aerospace supplier in 15 years, overtaking United Technologies , as it pledged a research and development (R&D) spending drive while increasing cash returns to shareholders.

Headlines: Elon Musk ducks out of one Los Angeles tunnel but pursues another
Description: Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has scrapped plans for a high-speed passenger tunnel under the West side of Los Angeles but is moving ahead with a similar proposal across town designed to whisk baseball fans to and from Dodger Stadium.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler to spend 5 billion euros in Italy to fill plants, keep jobs
Description: Fiat Chrysler plans to spend more than 5 billion euros ($5.7 billion) on new models and engines in Italy over the next three years to try to make better use of factories and boost jobs and margins.

Headlines: Trump studying new auto tariffs after GM restructuring
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that new auto tariffs were "being studied now," asserting they could prevent job cuts such as the U.S. layoffs and plant closures that General Motors Co  announced this week.

Headlines: Former Nissan executive Kelly denies financial misconduct allegations: lawyer
Description: Nissan Motor Co’s  former representative director Greg Kelly denies allegations of financial misconduct at the automaker, his lawyer said on Thursday.

Headlines: Barry Callebaut, Dutch partners launch sustainable mass-market chocolate
Description: Swiss chocolate maker Barry Callebaut  on Thursday signed a partnership with Dutch No.1 retailer Albert Heijn to make its private-label chocolate fully traceable from 2019, reflecting consumers' growing interest in ethical sourcing.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank offices raided in money laundering probe
Description: Police raided six Deutsche Bank offices in and around Frankfurt on Thursday over money laundering allegations linked to the "Panama Papers", the public prosecutor's office in Germany's financial capital said.

Headlines: Nissan-Renault-Mitsubishi alliance won't appoint interim chairman
Description: Mitsubishi Motors'  Chief Executive Osamu Masuko said on Thursday that the company's three-way alliance with Nissan and Renault would not appoint an interim chairman and would shift instead to a system where the group would be led by the three CEOs.

Headlines: Abercrombie & Fitch forecasts upbeat holiday quarter, shares soar
Description: U.S. teen apparel retailer Abercrombie & Fitch Co  forecast same-store sales for the holiday quarter above analysts' estimates on Thursday, driven by strong sales at its Hollister and flagship stores, sending its shares soaring 24 percent in early trading.

Headlines: Ford backs PM May's Brexit plan to avoid no-deal 'catastrophe'
Description: Carmaker Ford backed Prime Minister Theresa May's Brexit deal on Thursday to avoid a no-deal "catastrophe," but said she still needed to guarantee long-term frictionless trade, which is key to the future of its plants in Britain.

Headlines: Amazon picks New York City, Washington D.C. area for new offices
Description: Amazon.com Inc  picked America's financial and political capitals for massive new offices on Tuesday, branching out from its home base in Seattle with plans to create more than 25,000 jobs in both New York City and an area just outside Washington, D.C.

Headlines: Factbox: Amazon to get billions in breaks for HQ2 development
Description: (The Factbox updated on Nov. 15 corrects to fix total New York City incentive figure to $2.81 billion from $1.525 billion.)

Headlines: BMW mulls converting hybrids to electric only mode in polluted cities
Description: BMW said it can force its hybrid cars switch to an electric-only mode in heavily polluted inner-city areas, helping its vehicles compete with pure battery-driven rivals as a raft of cities seek to create emissions-free zones.

Headlines: Factbox: Unilever names beauty unit head Alan Jope as new CEO
Description: Anglo-Dutch consumer goods company Unilever  said its CEO Paul Polman was retiring and would be replaced by the head of its beauty unit Alan Jope, 54, from January 1.

Headlines: Ad buyers skeptical as Snap looks beyond teens for growth
Description: Snap Inc  has pinned its hopes on the over-35 crowd to revive user growth for its photo messaging app, a shift ad buyers said could backfire.

Headlines: Unilever CEO change not connected to HQ climbdown: chairman
Description: The replacement of Unilever's CEO Paul Polman was not connected to a shareholder row earlier this year over a proposed move of the headquarters of the Anglo-Dutch consumer goods company from Britain to the Netherlands, said the group's chairman.

Headlines: South Korea indicts group for leaking Samsung display tech to Chinese firm
Description: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday said they have indicted nine people on suspicion of leaking Samsung Electronics Co Ltd flexible display technology to a Chinese company.

Headlines: Supply chain reaction: trade war refugees race to relocate to Vietnam, Thailand
Description: Fred Perrotta spent four years building a network of Chinese suppliers for his line of trendy backpacks, but as soon as the United States announced tariffs on almost half of its Chinese imports, he started looking for suppliers in other countries.

Headlines: Tokyo prosecutors plan to seek extension of Ghosn's detention: Kyodo
Description: Tokyo prosecutors plan to seek an extension of Carlos Ghosn's detention, after the ousted chairman of Nissan Motor Co  was arrested last week for alleged financial misconduct, Kyodo News reported on Thursday.

Headlines: Indonesia's Go-Jek starts trial launch in Singapore, challenges Grab
Description: Indonesian ride-hailing firm Go-Jek kicked off a trial launch in parts of Singapore on Thursday and plans to roll out an array of services through its app in early 2019, challenging dominant player Grab in the small city-state.

Headlines: Trump administration to study tools to raise U.S. tariffs on Chinese autos
Description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said on Wednesday that he was examining all available tools to raise U.S. tariffs on Chinese vehicles to the 40 percent duties that China is now charging on U.S.-produced vehicles.

Headlines: Japan central banker mum on alleged involvement in Ghosn transaction
Description: A Bank of Japan board member declined on Thursday to comment on a media report that she was involved in an alleged attempt by former Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn to shift personal investment losses to the automaker during her time at a commercial bank.

Headlines: Huawei seeks clarification after New Zealand intelligence agency rejects 5G bid
Description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd said it was seeking clarification from New Zealand after the country's intelligence agency rejected the telecommunication industry's first request to use the Chinese firm's equipment in its planned 5G mobile network.

Headlines: Volkswagen planning new North America factory for electric vehicles
Description: Volkswagen  is deciding where to locate a new factory in North America to build electric vehicles for the U.S. market, the German automaker's new head for the Americas said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Two U.S. pipelines rack up violations, threaten industry growth
Description: Energy Transfer LP  and its Sunoco pipeline subsidiary have racked up more than 800 state and federal permit violations while racing to build two of the nation's largest natural gas pipelines, according to a Reuters analysis of government data and regulatory records.

Headlines: Microsoft wins $479.2 million contract from U.S. Army
Description: The U.S. Army said on Wednesday that it has awarded Microsoft Corp  a $479.2 million contract to supply prototypes for the Army's augmented reality systems helping soldiers in training and combat missions.

Headlines: Altria in talks to take minority stake in Juul: sources
Description: Tobacco company Altria Group Inc  is in talks to take a minority stake of 20 to 40 percent in e-cigarette maker Juul Labs Inc, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. senators ask White House to probe ZTE work in Venezuela
Description: Two U.S. senators on Wednesday asked the Trump administration to investigate whether Chinese telecommunications company ZTE Corp  violated U.S. sanctions by helping Venezuela set up a database that monitors the behavior of its citizens.

Headlines: Tiffany sales to Chinese tourists disappoint, shares fall sharply
Description: Tiffany & Co  on Wednesday reported quarterly sales that missed estimates as Chinese tourists spent less than expected at the jeweler's stores in the United States and Hong Kong, a shortfall that sent the company's shares down as much 13 percent.

Headlines: Fed's Powell, in apparent dovish shift, says rates near neutral
Description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell injected investors with a strong dose of optimism on Wednesday, saying that the central bank's policy rate is now "just below" estimates of a level that neither brakes nor boosts a healthy U.S. economy, comments that many investors read as signaling the Fed's three-year tightening cycle is drawing to a close.

Headlines: Saudi Arabia inks deal for Lockheed's missile defense system
Description: Saudi Arabia will buy Lockheed Martin's  $15 billion missile defense system, a U.S. Department of State spokesman said on Wednesday, after aggressive lobbying by the administration to close the deal that included a personal call between President Donald Trump and Saudi King Salman.

Headlines: Wall Street jumps as Powell hints interest rate hikes may taper off
Description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell boosted U.S. stock markets on Wednesday when he said the policy rate is now "just below" estimates of a level that neither brakes nor boosts a healthy economy, comments that many took as signaling the Fed's three-year tightening cycle is drawing to a close.

Headlines: Jewish Americans sue Airbnb over West Bank listing ban
Description: A group of Jewish Americans sued Airbnb Inc on Wednesday in U.S. federal court, accusing the home rental company of religious discrimination over its decision last week to remove listings for about 200 homes in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

Headlines: Car market collapse outruns GM moves to keep up
Description: General Motors Co's monumental announcement on Monday that it will close three car assembly plants in North America and slash its workforce will only partially close the gap between capacity and demand for the automaker's sedans, according to a Reuters analysis of industry production and capacity data.

Headlines: Judge orders new talks in Fiat Chrysler diesel emissions case
Description: A federal judge in San Francisco on Wednesday ordered the U.S. Justice Department and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV  to hold new talks with a court-appointed settlement master to try to settle the government's civil suit over the Italian-American automaker's diesel vehicle emissions.

Headlines: Wall Street surges on hints of fewer rate hikes, dollar falls
Description: Comments by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell that benchmark U.S. interest rates were "just below" neutral sparked a sharp rally on Wall Street on Wednesday, easing investor worries about the pace of rate hikes by the U.S. central bank next year.

Headlines: Apple's iPhone XR is company's best-selling model, executive says
Description: Apple Inc's iPhone XR has been the company's best-selling iPhone model every day since it went on sale in mid-October, a company executive told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: Pimco buys all of $3 billion UniCredit bond: sources
Description: U.S. fund Pacific Investment Management Co (Pimco) has bought all of a $3 billion, five-year bond offered with a hefty return by Italy's top bank UniCredit  to comply with capital buffer rules, two sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: U.S. third-quarter growth unrevised, headwinds increasing
Description: The U.S. economy slowed in the third quarter as previously reported, but the pace was likely strong enough to keep growth on track to hit the Trump administration's 3 percent target this year, even as momentum appears to have moderated further early in the fourth quarter.

Headlines: Lampert's hedge fund and Cyrus Capital to team up for possible Sears bid: Bloomberg
Description: Sears Holdings Corp  Chairman Eddie Lampert's hedge fund and Cyrus Capital Partners LP are preparing a potential takeover bid to keep the bankrupt retailer running, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Microsoft's stock market value pulls ahead of Apple's
Description: Microsoft Corp's  stock market value surpassed Apple Inc's , pulling ahead by as much as $3 billion on Wednesday as the Windows software maker benefited from optimism about demand for cloud computing services.

Headlines: Detroit Three narrowing car production in North America
Description: General Motors Co and fellow Detroit automakers Ford Motor Co and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV continue to winnow production of cars in North America as demand for traditional sedans wanes. GM announced on Monday it will halt production at three North American assembly plants and slash thousands of jobs.

Headlines: Trump retweets item saying GM should pay back bailout money
Description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday retweeted a suggestion that General Motors Co should pay back the money the government spent to keep it afloat as part of the auto industry bailout if it doesn't keep jobs in the country.

Headlines: Ford reshuffles U.S. plants to beef up SUV, truck production
Description: Ford Motor Co  said on Wednesday it will reshuffle workers at several of its plants to meet rising demand for pickup trucks and large SUVs, a process that will require finding new positions for 150 workers displaced by the changes but not result in job cuts.

Headlines: Instant View: Fed's gradual rate hikes balance against risks - Powell
Description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said on Wednesday that while there was "a great deal to like" about U.S. prospects, the Fed's gradual interest-rate hikes are meant to balance risks as it tries to keep the economy on track.

Headlines: State-owned Israel Aerospace to partner with Boeing on potential aviation contracts
Description: State-owned Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) said on Wednesday it signed an agreement with U.S. planemaker Boeing Co  last week to cooperate on commercial and military aviation in Israel and some other markets.

Headlines: Fed's Powell: Financial risks 'moderate' despite vulnerabilities
Description: The U.S. faces only moderate financial risks despite elevated asset prices and concern over the possible impact of rising corporate debt, U.S. Fed chairman Jerome Powell said on Wednesday as the central bank released a broad overview of the health of credit markets and the financial system.

Headlines: Danske Bank charged over alleged violations of money laundering law
Description: Denmark's state prosecutor has filed preliminary charges against Danske Bank  for alleged violations of the country's anti-money laundering act in relation to its Estonian branch.

Headlines: Insurer AXA raises profit targets in wake of $15 billion XL deal
Description: AXA , Europe's second-biggest insurer, expects its profitability to improve in the next two years thanks to U.S. business brought in by its new XL arm, and said it would now focus on expanding in Asia.

Headlines: U.S. new home sales drop to more than 2-1/2-year low
Description: Sales of new U.S. single-family homes tumbled to a more than 2-1/2-year low in October amid sharp declines in all four regions, further evidence that higher mortgage rates were hurting the housing market.

Headlines: BMW chief says considering second U.S. manufacturing plant
Description: BMW  is considering a second U.S. manufacturing plant that could produce engines and transmissions, Chief Executive Harald Krueger said on Tuesday, shortly after a report that U.S. President Donald Trump would impose tariffs on imported cars from next week.

Headlines: Wall Street grows cautious but still optimistic: Reuters poll
Description: Fears of a prolonged U.S.-China trade war and a potentially overzealous Federal Reserve have left Wall Street strategists less optimistic about stock market gains next year, but they still expect a decent increase, a Reuters poll found.

Headlines: Daimler to start making electric cars in China in 2019
Description: Daimler  will start building electric cars in China next year as a way to meet Beijing's stringent anti-pollution quotas for carmakers, even as demand for conventional models like the Mercedes-Benz Maybach remains strong.

Headlines: NBA strikes betting data deals with Sportradar, Genius Sports
Description: The National Basketball Association (NBA) struck its first betting data partnerships, allowing Genius Sports and Sportradar AG to distribute data to licensed sports betting operators in the United States.

Headlines: Siemens CEO received pay rise in 2018: annual report
Description: Siemens paid its chief executive Joe Kaeser a total of 7.82 million euros ($8.82 million) during its 2018 financial year, the German engineering company said in its annual report on Wednesday, up from 7.65 million euros a year earlier.

Headlines: Bitcoin up 10 percent, on course for its biggest daily rise since April
Description: Bitcoin rallied 10 percent on Wednesday to more than $4,100, putting it on course for its biggest daily rise since mid-April as it pulled itself out of a recent slump.

Headlines: Seeds of Renault-Nissan crisis sown in Macron's 'raid'
Description: The arrest of Renault-Nissan boss Carlos Ghosn has triggered new attempts by the Japanese carmaker to shake off the control of its French parent - adding to the problems piling up on President Emmanuel Macron's desk in the Elysee Palace.

Headlines: Dismantling the oil industry: rough North Sea waters test new ideas
Description: (This Nov. 27 story has been refiled to correct spelling of surname of Oil and Gas UK decommissioning manager.)

Headlines: Deutsche Bank Americas head expected to leave: sources
Description: Deutsche Bank's  head of the Americas, Tom Patrick, is likely to leave the bank, possibly by the end of the year, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Bangladesh factory safety group seeks to delay closure, flags lingering risks
Description: A group set up by European fashion brands to improve factory safety in Bangladesh has sought a stay on a court order that calls for its local operations to end this week, its executive director said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Bitcoin gains 6 percent as it heads for best day since July
Description: Bitcoin bounced more than 6 percent on Wednesday, climbing above $4,000 and heading for its biggest daily jump since July as it clawed back ground after recent heavy selling.

Headlines: Cryptocurrencies to survive sell-off - Allianz's El-Erian
Description: Cryptocurrencies are here to stay despite a prolonged slump this year, and will gain wider acceptance after the recent entry of more institutional investors in the space, Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser at Allianz, said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Russia plans stiffer fines for tech firms that break rules - sources
Description: Russia plans to impose stiffer fines on technology firms that fail to comply with Russian laws, sources familiar with the plans said, raising the stakes in the Kremlin's fight with global tech giants such as Facebook  and Google.

Headlines: New Zealand rejects Huawei's first 5G bid citing national security risk
Description: New Zealand's intelligence agency has rejected the telecom industry's first request in the country to use 5G equipment provided by China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd, citing concerns about national security.

Headlines: 'Out of control': Chinese authorities slam ride-hailing giant Didi over safety
Description: Chinese authorities announced a broad crackdown on China's ride-hailing industry on Wednesday, targeting market-leader Didi Chuxing with fines following the deaths of two passengers in separate incidents earlier this year.

Headlines: Auditor had questioned Nissan on payments to Ghosn at heart of scandal: source
Description: Nissan Motor Co’s  auditor had repeatedly questioned transactions at the heart of allegations of financial misconduct by former chief Carlos Ghosn but Nissan said they were proper, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Brazil oil tanker collision reveals offshore regulatory gaps
Description: Brazil has more than doubled the number of risky ship-to-ship oil transfers this year, but its monitoring of such offshore maneuvers is lax, to a point where a July 2017 collision between two tankers was not reported, according to a Reuters review of government and shipping records.

Headlines: Trump threatens to cut GM subsidies in retaliation for U.S. job cuts
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened on Tuesday to eliminate subsidies for General Motors Co in retaliation for the automaker cutting U.S. jobs and plants, and the automaker also took fire from Canadian political and labor leaders for cutbacks there.

Headlines: U.S. court revives Mattress Firm defamation case against Sleep Number
Description: A federal appeals court on Tuesday revived for a second time a 11-year-old defamation lawsuit by bedding retailer Mattress Firm Inc against adjustable bed maker Sleep Number Corp .

Headlines: Single word keeps some farmers from getting Trump's aid to offset tariffs
Description: A Republican lawmaker wants to change a single word in the Trump administration's farm aid program saying some soybean growers in Louisiana cannot qualify for the payments designed to offset farmers' losses from tariffs against China.

Headlines: Trump says 'not even a little bit happy' with Fed's Powell: report
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday kept up his criticism of Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell, saying rising interest rates and other Fed policies were damaging the U.S. economy, the Washington Post said.

Headlines: Sears secures court approval for additional $350 million loan
Description: Sears Holdings Corp  won court approval on Tuesday for $350 million in critical bankruptcy financing that will keep the 125-year-old retailer operating through the holidays while it attempts to reorganize.

Headlines: Hong Kong's finance sector M&A deals fall prey to China crackdown
Description: Mergers and acquisitions targeting Hong Kong financial firms have slumped this year, with insurance sector deals particularly hard hit, as China's moves to tighten capital controls and crack down on corporate debt have driven mainland buyers away.

Headlines: Amazon adds antenna service for satellite data; courts space industry
Description: Amazon.com Inc  said on Tuesday it was starting a new antenna service for uploading and downloading data from satellites, in a bid to lure space industry and other customers to the cloud.

Headlines: Wall Street reverses losses after White House adviser's trade remarks
Description: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged higher on Tuesday after White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said a meeting between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart on Saturday was an opportunity to "turn the page" on a trade war.

Headlines: Oshkosh wins $1.7 billion U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
Description: Oshkosh Corp  has been awarded a $1.7 billion modification to a U.S. defense contract to exercise options for 6,107 vehicles and 22,166 kits, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Workers return to GM's Canada plant; union to meet Trudeau
Description: Workers returned to the assembly line at General Motors' Oshawa, Ontario, plant on Tuesday, a local union leader said, after walking out on Monday to protest news the plant had been scheduled to shut down in December 2019.

Headlines: Exclusive: China not seriously considering U.S. Treasuries as trade war weapon - envoy
Description: China's ambassador to the United States said on Tuesday he does not believe Beijing is seriously considering using its massive U.S. Treasury debt holdings as a weapon in the U.S.-China trade war, citing concerns that such a move would destabilize financial markets.

Headlines: Oil prices edge lower ahead of G20, OPEC meetings
Description: Oil prices dipped on Tuesday, weighed down by uncertainty over the U.S.-China trade war and signs of increased global crude production, but losses were limited by expectations that crude exporters would agree to cut output at an upcoming OPEC meeting.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank mulls shake-up of high-level executives: WSJ
Description: Deutsche Bank AG  is planning a high-level shake up that could result in the departure of top executives central to its relationships with key regulators in the United States and Europe, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

Headlines: World stocks finish higher on China trade-deal hopes; dollar rises
Description: Stocks on Wall Street logged modest gains on Tuesday as traders remained hopeful that the United States and China can work toward resolving their trade-related differences at the upcoming G20 Summit.

Headlines: Disney, Fox deny claims in $1 billion Malaysia theme park lawsuit
Description: Walt Disney Co  and Twenty-First Century Fox Inc  on Tuesday rejected claims in a Malaysia casino operator's lawsuit accusing them of abandoning a licensing contract tied to the planned construction of a Fox-branded theme park.

Headlines: TransCanada asks Montana court to allow preliminary work on Keystone XL
Description: TransCanada Corp has asked a Montana court to allow it to resume pre-construction activities on its Keystone XL oil pipeline after a U.S. judge blocked construction on the $8 billion project earlier this month.

Headlines: Former Facebook worker says firm not doing enough to deal with racial discrimination
Description: A former Facebook Inc  employee who worked closely with racial minority groups said in a blog post https://www.facebook.com/notes/mark-s-luckie/facebook-is-failing-its-black-employees-and-its-black-users/1931075116975013 on Tuesday that he left this month over frustration with the social network's "systematic disenfranchisement of underrepresented voices" and other diversity issues.

Headlines: Trump open to deal with Xi at dinner but with conditions: Kudlow
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump is open to reaching a deal on U.S.-China trade irritants over dinner on Saturday with Chinese leader Xi Jinping but is ready to hike tariffs on Chinese imports if there is no breakthrough, White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Fed official frets over risks to Apple Pay, other mobile payments

Headlines: Wall Street tumbles as Apple, internet stocks swoon
Description: U.S. stocks dropped and the Nasdaq fell 3 percent on Monday as investors dumped Apple, internet and other technology shares, further shaking confidence in a group of stocks that has propelled the long bull market.

Headlines: Northrop Grumman wins $490 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
Description: Northrop Grumman Corp  has been awarded a $490 million U.S. defense contract for the sale to Japan of Global Hawk unmanned surveillance aircraft, the Pentagon said on Monday.

Headlines: A key Fed official stays the course on U.S. rate hikes amid growing doubts
Description: The Federal Reserve is pushing ahead with gradual rate-hike plans next month as it marches toward a more normal policy stance that would keep the economy expanding, one of its most influential members said on Monday in the face of growing doubts in financial markets.

Headlines: Apple, trade woes sink stocks; growth worries drag on dollar
Description: World stock markets fell on Monday as worries about softening demand for the iPhone dragged down shares of Apple Inc and persistent trade tensions between China and the United States sapped investor sentiment.

Headlines: Crude rises slightly despite oversupply fears
Description: Crude futures rose ahead of settlement in choppy trade on Monday, supported by a reported drawdown of U.S. oil inventories, potential European Union sanctions on Iran and possible OPEC production cuts.

Headlines: Danske whistleblower says big European bank handled $150 billion in payments
Description: The whistleblower who revealed alleged money laundering involving Danske Bank  said on Monday that a major European bank helped process up to $150 billion in suspicious payments, or nearly two-thirds of the transactions under scrutiny.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank was correspondent bank for Danske Bank in Estonia: spokesman
Description: Deutsche Bank  processed payments for Danske Bank  in Estonia but ended the relationship in 2015 after it found suspicious activity, a spokesman for the German lender said on Monday.

Headlines: GE shakes up power unit leadership, taps retired exec to help
Description: General Electric Co  shook up its ailing power business again on Monday, naming a CEO for its new gas-power division and bringing a veteran GE executive back from retirement to help.

Headlines: Apple cuts production orders for all three new iPhone models: WSJ
Description: Apple Inc  has cut production orders in recent weeks for all three iPhone models launched in September, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing sources.

Headlines: American Airlines pilots seek new contract negotiations
Description: American Airlines  pilots union on Monday urged the carrier to begin negotiations for a new labor contract in January to boost compensation.

Headlines: Societe Generale to pay $1.4 billion to settle cases in the U.S.
Description: French banking giant Societe Generale on Monday agreed to pay U.S. federal and state authorities $1.4 billion to resolve pending legal disputes.

Description: U.S. stocks tumbled on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones industrial Average shedding about 2 percent and the Nasdaq down more than 3 percent.

Headlines: Petrobras should focus on oil exploration and production: incoming CEO
Description: The incoming chief executive of Brazilian state-controlled oil company Petroleo Brasileiro SA  said in a newspaper interview on Monday that BR Distribuidora , its fuel distribution unit, is not a natural fit for the company and does not generate returns.

Headlines: SocGen says $1.3 billion U.S. penalties will not affect 2018 results
Description: French bank Societe Generale  said on Monday it agreed to pay $1.3 billion in penalties to the U.S. authorities to settle a dispute over violations of U.S. economic sanctions, adding the fines were entirely covered by provisions.

Headlines: Barclays not liable to buyers of U.S. IPO before 2008 crisis: appeals court

Headlines: Musk hints at Tesla interest in Daimler van
Description: Tesla Inc  could be interested in partnering with Daimler AG's  Mercedes-Benz on an electric version of its Sprinter van, Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said in a tweet https://twitter.com/elonmusk/status/1064541185820114944 on Monday.

Headlines: People are our greatest asset. Wanna buy them?
Description: Eastern Europe's chronic labor shortage is feeding into corporate takeover activity, with some companies making acquisitions to snap up skilled workers or obtain expertise needed to expand their businesses.

Headlines: Bitcoin breaches $5,000, plumbs fresh 13-month low

Headlines: Disney's Fox deal gets China's approval
Description: Walt Disney Co  on Monday received unconditional approval from China for its deal to buy Twenty-First Century Fox's  entertainment assets, clearing one of the last major hurdles for the deal to go through.

Headlines: Timeline: How Danske Bank's Estonian money laundering scandal unfolded
Description: Danske Bank  is embroiled in a money laundering scandal that has triggered criminal investigations, forced out its CEO and chairman and rattled investors in Denmark's largest bank.

Headlines: France says Ghosn case not problem for Renault stability
Description: The arrest of Renault  CEO Carlos Ghosn and his imminent removal from the board of Nissan Motor Co.  does not pose a threat to the stability or survival of the French carmaker, France's finance minister said on Monday.

Headlines: France committed to Renault stability after Ghosn arrest
Description: France will ensure the long-term viability of Renault , Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Monday after Carlos Ghosn, chairman of the French carmaker's Japanese partner Nissan Motor Co  was arrested on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. home builder sentiment posts biggest drop in 4-1/2 years

Headlines: Nissan CEO to propose board oust Ghosn on Thursday

Headlines: France's Macron vows to maintain Renault-Nissan stability
Description: France will work to preserve the stability of Renault  and its alliance with Nissan , President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday, after the Japanese carmaker took steps to oust Chairman Carlos Ghosn over alleged financial irregularities.

Headlines: Carlos Ghosn, the cost cutter with a big price tag
Description: In his 40 years in the auto industry, the praise Carlos Ghosn has won for turning around businesses has regularly been matched by criticism over the amount he has been paid to do it.

Description: Carlos Ghosn, chairman of Japanese automaker Nissan, under-reported nearly 10 billion yen ($88.70 million) in compensation as nearly 5 billion yen, Jiji news agency reported on Monday.

Headlines: BlackBerry to buy cybersecurity firm Cylance for $1.4 billion

Description: T-Mobile US Inc's  Chief Financial Officer said there is a possibility that its $26 billion acquisition deal of Sprint Corp  will close as early as the first quarter of 2019.

Description: U.S. Deere & Co  expects to see demand for its farm equipment in Africa grow 8 to 10 percent annually in the coming years, driven by expansion in key markets like Ethiopia and Zimbabwe, a local company executive said.
