Headlines: Canada's Barrick Gold to buy Randgold for $6.5 billion
Description: Canada's Barrick Gold Corp has agreed to buy Randgold Resources Ltd in an all-stock deal valuing the Africa-focused miner at $6.5 billion, to create the world's largest gold producer in an industry under investor pressure to put capital to good use.

Headlines: Wall Street falls as U.S.-China tariffs kick in
Description: The S&P 500 and the Dow closed lower on Monday after a new round of U.S.-China trade tariffs kicked in, dampening last week's hopes for talks between the two countries, and as investors awaited a widely expected interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.

Headlines: Citigroup settles U.S. robo-signing case tied to consumer bankruptcies
Description: Citigroup Inc  will pay $5 million to address "robo-signed" proofs of claim filed in consumer bankruptcy cases involving 71,448 Macy's-branded credit card accounts, the U.S. Department of Justice announced on Monday.

Headlines: Global stock markets fall on trade war pessimism; oil rallies
Description: Stock markets around the world retreated on Monday amid concerns over the potential wider impact of a trade spat between China and the United States, while oil prices rallied to a four-year high after OPEC ignored U.S. calls to raise supply.

Headlines: Wall Street's S&P communication sector starts with slight gain
Description: The new S&P 500 communication services sector , which includes such high-profile names as Facebook Inc , Alphabet Inc  and Netflix Inc , made its debut on Monday with a small gain, after the largest-ever overhaul of Wall Street's broad business sectors.

Headlines: Walmart, Sam's Club to put food products on blockchain
Description: Walmart  and its unit Sam's Club said on Monday leafy greens suppliers will be asked to implement real-time, farm-to-store tracking using blockchain technology by next September, as the retailer tackles food-safety incidents.

Headlines: China says U.S. trying to force it to submit on trade as new tariffs kick in
Description: The United States and China imposed fresh tariffs on each other's goods on Monday as the world's biggest economies showed no signs of backing down from an increasingly bitter trade dispute that is expected to hit global economic growth.

Headlines: UK's Debenhams can grow again, says boss
Description: The boss of Britain's Debenhams  came out fighting on Monday, saying the department store chain's troubles had been exaggerated and insisting the business has a future.

Headlines: Michael Kors set to snap up Italy's Versace: sources
Description: U.S. fashion group Michael Kors  has agreed to take control of Versace in a deal that could value one of Italy's most prized designers at $2 billion, sources familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S., European Union still in 'exploratory' talks on trade - EU's Malmstrom
Description: The European Union and the United States are still in exploratory talks about how they can pursue a limited trade agreement, with no real negotiations yet started, EU Trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmstrom said on Monday.

Headlines: Sirius XM to buy Pandora in $3.5 billion streaming push
Description: Satellite radio company Sirius XM Holdings Inc will buy online music service Pandora Media Inc in a $3.5 billion all-stock deal that will help it battle growing competition from streaming rivals Spotify and Apple Music.

Headlines: United Technologies explores sale of Chubb Fire & Security: sources
Description: United Technologies Corp  is exploring a sale of its Chubb Fire & Security division for more than $3 billion, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: Sky's shares jump after Comcast wins auction with big bet
Description: Sky  shares jumped 9 percent on Monday to within touching distance of what Comcast  will pay to buy Europe's biggest pay-TV group after seeing off competition from Twenty-First Century Fox .

Headlines: Singapore fines Grab and Uber, imposes measures to open up market
Description: Singapore slapped ride-hailing firms Grab and Uber with fines and finalized restrictions to open up the market to competitors after concluding that their merger in March has driven up prices.

Headlines: Home modems, routers hit by U.S. China tariffs as 'smart' tech goods escape
Description: U.S. tariffs that hit some $200 billion worth of Chinese products on Monday spare many high-profile consumer technology items such as "smart" watches and speakers, but the less flashy home modems, routers and internet gateways that make them work weren't so lucky.

Headlines: T-Mobile revamps prepaid brand to spruce up image
Description: T-Mobile US Inc  said Monday it is renaming its prepaid brand to Metro by T-Mobile and adding two new unlimited phone plans that will include perks like Google One cloud storage and Amazon  Prime, in an effort to remove the perception that prepaid plans have subpar service.

Headlines: Symantec ends accounting probe without major revision to results
Description: Symantec Corp  said on Monday that it would not restate previous financial results except for a specific $13 million transaction, following a four-month long probe into the Norton anti-virus maker's accounting practices, sending its shares up about 4 percent.

Headlines: Iran says oil to rise as Saudi, Russia do 'little and late'
Description: Saudi Arabia and Russia won't add significantly more oil to the market because of a lack of capacity, a top Iranian official said on Monday, predicting prices will probably rise further.

Headlines: Volvo halts Iran truck assembly due to U.S. sanctions
Description: Swedish truckmaker AB Volvo has stopped assembling trucks in Iran because U.S. sanctions are preventing it from being paid, a spokesman for the company said on Monday.

Headlines: Danske Bank board close to appointing new CEO: Finans
Description: Danske Bank's  board is close to appointing a new chief executive to replace Thomas Borgen who resigned last week amid a money laundering scandal, Danish online media Finans reported on Monday, citing unnamed sources.

Headlines: Asian firms shuffle production around the region as China tariffs hit
Description: A growing number of Asian manufacturers of products ranging from  memory chips to machines tools are moving to shift production from China to other factories in the region in the wake of U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs on Chinese imports.

Headlines: Take Five: World markets themes for the week ahead
Description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

Headlines: Tech index refresh could give under-the-radar names their day in the sun
Description: A reshuffling of Wall Street benchmark industry sectors that transferred high-flying FANG stocks like Facebook Inc  and Google-parent Alphabet Inc  out of the technology label may be a boon to some under-the-radar companies that used to compete with them for investor attention.

Headlines: Canada PM says informal NAFTA talks likely in next few days at U.N.
Description: U.S. and Canadian officials trying to reach a deal on NAFTA are "very likely" to hold informal talks on the sidelines of a major U.N. meeting in the next few days, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said on Sunday.

Headlines: China to issue white paper on U.S. trade frictions: Xinhua
Description: China's state council will publish a white paper on the ongoing bilateral trade frictions with the United States, the official Xinhua news agency reported on Monday.

Headlines: Comcast demonstrates Sky-high ambition in global media shake-up
Description: U.S. cable giant Comcast scored a big win in the scramble for media assets by beating Rupert Murdoch, and his backer Disney, in the battle for Sky with an eye-watering $40 billion bid.

Headlines: Key companies to attend White House quantum computing meeting
Description: The White House will hold a meeting on Monday on U.S. government efforts to boost quantum information science, with administration officials, leading companies including Alphabet Inc , IBM Corp , JPMorgan Chase & Co  and academic experts taking part.

Headlines: Global spending on digital marketing nears $100 billion: study
Description: Spending on digital marketing grew by 44 percent last year in the United States and Britain to $52 billion, a study has found, estimating that global outlays on such tactics are approaching $100 billion.

Headlines: Global advertising expenditure to grow 4.5 percent in 2018: Zenith
Description: Global advertising expenditure is predicted to reach $581 billion at the end of 2018, with most of the growth coming from sponsored content in search engines and social media ads, according to industry forecaster Zenith.

Headlines: WPP preparing to merge Young & Rubicam and digital ad firm VML: WSJ
Description: The world's largest advertising company WPP Plc's  is preparing to consolidate some of its businesses in a bid to keep pace with the industry's digital shift, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

Headlines: European Banking Authority is asked to investigate oversight of Danske Bank
Description: The European Commisssion has asked the European Banking Authority (EBA) to investigate what went wrong in the oversight of Danske Bank's  Estonian branch, which is at the center of a major money laundering scandal, it said on Sunday, confirming a report in Financial Times.

Headlines: Volume spikes on sector reshuffle, quadruple witching
Description: An overhaul of Wall Street's technology and media sectors coincided with the quarterly expiration of futures and options, bringing a burst of volume to trading late on Friday that could continue in the days that follow.

Headlines: Low interest rates spawn rise in number of zombie firms: BIS
Description: Decades of falling interest rates have led to a sharp increase in the number of "zombie" firms, a report for the Bank for International Settlements said, potentially threatening economic growth and preventing interest rates from rising.

Headlines: Siemens CEO pushes plans to boost Iraqi power infrastructure
Description: Siemens  said its boss Joe Kaeser met Iraq's prime minister on Sunday to discuss a proposal by the German company to expand the Middle East nation's power production.

Headlines: Volkswagen's Porsche drops diesel in electric car push
Description: Volkswagen's  Porsche will stop offering diesel versions of its cars, the unit said on Sunday, sharpening its focus on hybrid and battery-powered vehicles instead.

Headlines: Fed's Powell between a rock and hard place: Ignore the yield curve or tight job market?
Description: Unemployment near a 20-year low screams at the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates or risk a too-hot economy. The bond market, not far from a state that typically precedes a recession, says not so fast.

Headlines: Timeline: Shell's operations in Nigeria
Description: Royal Dutch Shell pioneered Nigeria's oil and gas industry and remains a major investor in the West African country. But over the decades it has come under fire over spills in the Delta region and struggles with oil theft, corruption and oil-fueled violence.

Headlines: AstraZeneca CEO warns of medicine shortages after Brexit: Sunday Times
Description: Britain could see widespread medicine shortages if there is no deal to prevent friction at the border with the European Union after Brexit, the AstraZeneca chief executive told the Sunday Times.

Headlines: Comcast outbids Fox with $40 billion winning offer for Sky
Description: Comcast  beat Rupert Murdoch's Twenty-First Century Fox  in the battle for Sky  on Saturday after offering 30.6 billion pounds ($40 billion) in a dramatic auction to decide the fate of the pay-television group.

Headlines: Fox plans to concede defeat in Sky battle, review stake: source
Description: Rupert Murdoch's Twenty-First Century Fox  expects Sky's  independent directors to recommend Comcast's  $39 billion bid, after which Fox will concede defeat in the battle for the British broadcaster, a source with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: U.S. airlines score win as Congress drops 'reasonable fee' rules
Description: The U.S. airline industry scored a win on Saturday as bipartisan congressional legislation dropped plans to mandate "reasonable and proportional" baggage and change fees, but included other new passenger protections.

Headlines: BT approaches Worldpay's Philip Jansen to be new CEO: Sky News
Description: BT Group  is in advanced talks to appoint payment technology provider Worldpay's  outgoing co-chief executive Philip Jansen as its new CEO, Sky News reported on Saturday.

Headlines: White House optimistic on China trade; no date for more talks
Description: The United States is optimistic about finding a way forward in its trade dispute with China, but it does not have a date scheduled for further talks as it assesses Beijing's response to the latest round of tariffs, a senior White House official said on Friday.

Headlines: China cancels trade talks with U.S. as tariff threats escalate: WSJ
Description: China has canceled upcoming trade talks with the United States and will not send vice-premier Liu He to Washington next week, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources.

Headlines: Adviser says U.S. close to Mexico-only NAFTA deal, Canada unmoved
Description: The United States is getting "very, very close" to having to move forward on its trade deal with Mexico without Canada, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said on Friday.

Headlines: Mexico will seek deal with Canada if NAFTA talks fail: Lopez Obrador
Description: Mexico's incoming government will pursue a bilateral deal with Canada if talks to overhaul the North American Free Trade Agreement falter, Mexican president-elect Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador said on Friday.

Headlines: Caterpillar leans on old playbook to cope with Trump tariffs
Description: Six months into the U.S. tariffs on imported aluminum and steel, Caterpillar Inc  is finding that one of the best ways it can protect profits is a cost cutting strategy that is more than two years old.

Headlines: United Airlines pilots resist contract changes over regional routes
Description: United Airlines  pilots said they refuse to budge on the wording of their contract governing the outsourcing of regional flights.

Headlines: Dow hits new closing high ahead of index reshuffle
Description: Industrials led the Dow to a new closing high on Friday ahead of Monday's major sector reshuffle, capping a week that largely shrugged off trade worries.

Headlines: Lehman Brothers workers share memories 10 years after the fall
Description: Ex-employees of Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc met at Irish pubs near their former office in Midtown Manhattan on Thursday night to reminisce 10 years after the bank's collapse, in gatherings with the atmosphere of high school reunions despite marking the largest failure of the financial crisis.

Headlines: As new iPhones go on sale, studies reveal chips from Intel and Toshiba
Description: Apple Inc's  latest iPhones hit stores around the world on Friday, featuring components made by Intel Corp  and Toshiba  among others, according to two firms that cracked open the iPhone Xs and Xs Max models.

Headlines: Receding trade fears propel stocks to six-month peak
Description: The U.S. dollar rebounded and world shares hit a six-month high on Friday after China's moves to boost domestic consumption bolstered a rally driven by investor bets that the latest U.S.-China trade dispute was unlikely to dent global growth.

Headlines: Walmart warns Trump tariffs may force price hikes: letter
Description: Walmart Inc  said that it may hike prices of products if the Trump administration imposes a tariff on Chinese imports, according to a letter the company wrote to U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer two weeks ago and seen by Reuters on Thursday.

Headlines: General Electric says blade problem affects more gas turbines
Description: General Electric Co  said on Friday that turbine blade oxidation which forced Exelon Corp  to idle four electric power units in Texas also affects another model, widening the impact of the latest problem to hit GE's ailing power unit.

Headlines: Blackstone looks to manage $1 trillion by 2026
Description: Blackstone Group LP , the world's largest manager of alternative investments such as private equity and real estate, said on Friday it could be overseeing $1 trillion in assets by 2026.

Headlines: Nasdaq says Nordic trader whose deals went sour agrees to sell personal assets
Description: Nasdaq's Nordic commodities exchange has reached agreement on the sale of assets belonging to a private trader who defaulted on his commitments last week, it said on Friday.

Headlines: Farfetch tops price range in IPO in boon to luxury market
Description: Farfetch  priced its shares above its targeted range on Friday in a New York flotation that values the online luxury retailer at over $5.8 billion and underscores how big a bet web sales have become for high-end brands.

Headlines: U.S. agency accuses Walmart of pregnancy discrimination in lawsuit
Description: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission on Friday filed a lawsuit accusing Walmart Inc of forcing pregnant workers at a Wisconsin warehouse to go on unpaid leave and denying their requests to take on easier duties.

Headlines: French handbag maker Longchamp to invest in China to revive sales
Description: Longchamp, one of France's leading handbag makers, is increasing its presence in China and the United States to boost its sales, its CEO said, betting on celebrity tie-ups and its online platforms to revive sluggish growth.

Headlines: Comcast and Fox take $34 billion battle for Britain's Sky to the wire
Description: Comcast  and Twenty-First Century Fox  face a quick-fire auction for British broadcaster Sky  on Saturday after neither side backed down in a drawn-out $34 billion battle.

Headlines: British inquiry intensifies Danske Bank money laundering scandal
Description: Danske Bank's  money laundering scandal spread on Friday to Britain where the National Crime Agency (NCA) said it is investigating the use of UK-registered companies.

Headlines: Uber in talks to buy food delivery firm Deliveroo: Bloomberg
Description: Ride-hailing company Uber Technologies Inc [UBER.UL] is in early talks to buy food delivery company Deliveroo, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Headlines: KKR-backed Calsonic lines up 5 billion euro financing for Magneti takeover:  sources
Description: Calsonic Kansei has lined up around 5 billion euros ($5.9 billion) in financing from Japanese banks to fund its proposed acquisition of Fiat Chrysler's  unit Magneti Marelli, four sources familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Exclusive: AB InBev faces EU antitrust fine in Belgian beer case - sources
Description: Anheuser-Busch InBev  faces an EU antitrust fine for preventing cheaper beer imports into Belgium despite its efforts to settle the investigation, people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Rare auction showdown could decide fate of broadcaster Sky
Description: A protracted $34 billion bidding war for European broadcaster Sky  between U.S. rivals Comcast  and Twenty-First Century Fox  is likely to be settled by a quick-fire auction on Saturday.

Headlines: Finnish financial watchdog looks into Danske Bank money laundering scandal
Description: Finland's financial supervisory authority (FIN-FSA) said on Friday that it was watching developments in Danske Bank's  money laundering scandal.

Headlines: SandRidge says interim CEO not in race for top job
Description: SandRidge Energy Inc  said on Friday board member and interim Chief Executive Officer Bill Griffin would not be a candidate for the position of CEO but would continue in his role until a successor is appointed.

Headlines: Google defends Gmail data sharing, gives few details on violations
Description: Alphabet Inc's Google gave details about its policies for third-party Gmail add-ons but stopped short of fully addressing questions from U.S. senators about developers who break its email-scanning rules.

Headlines: French minister optimistic over buyer for Ford Blanquefort plant
Description: French Economy minister Bruno Le Maire said on Friday that talks with Belgian transmissions supplier Punch Powerglide over the purchase of Ford's  Blanquefort gearbox plant in southwestern France should be concluded next month.

Headlines: Wells Fargo to cut headcount by 5-10 percent in next three years
Description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Thursday it would reduce its headcount by about 5 percent to 10 percent within the next three years as part of a turnaround plan.

Headlines: Facebook to drop on-site support for political campaigns
Description: Facebook Inc  said on Thursday that it would no longer dispatch employees to the offices of political campaigns to offer support ahead of elections, as it did with U.S. President Donald Trump in the 2016 race.

Headlines: Tesla VP of global supply management resigns: Bloomberg
Description: Tesla Inc's  vice president of global supply management, Liam O'Connor, has resigned, Bloomberg reported https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-20/tesla-is-said-to-lose-supply-management-chief-as-exodus-worsens, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Headlines: Adobe to buy marketing software firm Marketo for $4.75 billion
Description: Adobe Systems Inc on Thursday agreed to buy Marketo Inc for $4.75 billion from private equity firm Vista Equity Partners Management, adding heft to its cloud-based digital marketing business.

Headlines: Industrials lead Dow to record high; tech boosts S&P, Nasdaq
Description: Trade-sensitive industrial stocks led the Dow Jones Industrial Average to a record closing high on Thursday, the last of Wall Street's main indexes to fully regain ground since a correction that began in January.    All three major U.S. indexes closed higher as trade worries subsided. Technology companies led the Nasdaq higher, along with the S&P 500, which also hit a new closing high.

Headlines: NAFTA deal not yet in sight, Canada stands firm on auto tariffs
Description: Canada and the United States showed scant sign on Thursday of closing a deal to revamp NAFTA, and Canadian officials made clear Washington needed to withdraw a threat of possible autos tariffs, sources said.

Headlines: American Airlines joins rivals in hiking U.S. baggage fees by five dollars
Description: American Airlines Group Inc said on Thursday it would raise domestic U.S. baggage fees by $5, joining major rivals in the price hike amid higher fuel costs.

Headlines: Barrett Business Services settles accounting fraud charges: SEC
Description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said on Thursday that Barrett Business Services Inc  and the company's former controller, Mark Cannon, have agreed to settle civil charges of accounting fraud involving workers' compensation.

Headlines: NY court overturns $115 million patent judgment against Samsung
Description: The New York State Court of Appeals on Thursday overturned a $115 million judgment against Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  over television patents.

Headlines: Stocks hit new highs as trade worries ease, dollar slips
Description: World stock markets rallied on Thursday, with the Dow and S&P 500 setting new highs, while the U.S. dollar slipped as investors viewed this week's fresh U.S. and Chinese tariffs on imports as less harsh than initially feared.

Headlines: Amazon adds Echo devices for home and car in bid to dominate voice gadgets
Description: Amazon.com Inc  on Thursday introduced a dozen new Echo speakers and related gadgets in a bid to stay ahead of rivals Apple Inc  and Alphabet Inc's Google  in the nascent category for voice-controlled devices.

Headlines: Vista Global sees higher demand for Bombardier 7500 after certification
Description: Canadian aircraft leasing company Global Vista, one of the largest customers for Bombardier's long-range Global 7500 business jet, said on Thursday it expects greater demand for the plane after Canadian and U.S. regulators certify the aircraft.

Headlines: Four General Electric power turbines shut down in U.S. due to blade issue
Description: General Electric Co  said on Thursday that four of its new flagship power turbines in the United States have been shut down due to an "oxidation issue" and warned it expects the problem to affect more of the 51 units it has shipped, sending shares lower.

Headlines: AT&T asks U.S. appeals court to uphold approval of Time Warner acquisition
Description: AT&T Inc  on Thursday asked a federal appeals court to reject the Justice Department's challenge to its acquisition of Time Warner, saying the government had offered no basis for second guessing key conclusions of a ruling upholding the transaction.

Headlines: Opel to further scale back production at Ruesselsheim: report
Description: Carmaker Opel, a unit of France's PSA Group , is planning to further scale back production at its Ruesselsheim plant, a local newspaper group reported on Friday.

Headlines: Trump says OPEC 'monopoly' must get prices down
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump linked American support for Middle Eastern countries to oil prices on Thursday as he again urged OPEC to lower prices.

Headlines: Animal health firm Elanco surges 41 percent on debut
Description: Eli Lilly unit Elanco Animal Health Inc's  shares jumped as much as 41 percent on their stock market debut on Thursday, adding to investor enthusiasm for the fast-growing pet healthcare market.

Headlines: Aston Martin aims to steer round Brexit to $6.7 billion IPO
Description: Luxury British carmaker maker Aston Martin is seeking a price tag of up to 5.1 billion pounds ($6.7 billion) in its stock market debut next month and has geared up for any Brexit outcome, it said on Thursday.

Headlines: Minneapolis prosecutors weighing evidence in JD.com CEO case
Description: Prosecutors are weighing whether to bring charges against Chinese businessman Richard Liu after the Minneapolis Police Department turned over the findings of its initial investigation into accusations of rape against the JD.com  chief executive, according to a statement released on Thursday by the Hennepin County Attorney's Office.

Headlines: Nike's Kaepernick ad spurs spike in sold-out items
Description: Nike Inc  has sold out 61 percent more merchandise since the controversial ad campaign featuring former NFL player Colin Kaepernick appeared earlier this month, according to data on the company's online sales from Thomson Reuters Proprietary Research.

Headlines: S&P sector reshuffle may do little for telecom stocks
Description: The S&P 500's three-company telecommunications services index  is about to be folded into a much higher-profile group, but a brighter spotlight may not be enough to boost the stocks as investors continue to favor growth sectors.

Headlines: BlackRock's Fink: U.S. a short-term 'big winner' in China trade war
Description: Larry Fink, chief executive of BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager, on Thursday said the United States is "a big winner" in the trade war with China "in the short-term," but not necessarily over time.

Headlines: Emirates, Etihad airlines deny report they may merge
Description: State-owned Emirates and Etihad, two of the Middle East's top airlines, denied a Bloomberg report on Thursday which quoted unnamed sources as saying Emirates was seeking to take over smaller Etihad to create the world's largest carrier.

Headlines: GE says four HA turbines in U.S. shut down due to blade problem
Description: General Electric Co  said on Thursday that four of its flagship power turbines in the United States have been shut down due to a problem with turbine blades that was discovered at an electrical power plant in Texas owned by Exelon Corp .

Headlines: Under Armour to cut 400 more jobs in turnaround push, shares rise
Description: Under Armour Inc   announced 400 job cuts on Thursday and raised its forecast for adjusted profit to the high-end of an earlier range, deepening cost-cuts in the face of rising competition from Nike  and Adidas .

Headlines: Morgan Stanley sues six Illinois brokers who left for Stifel
Description: Morgan Stanley  has sued six brokers who left an Illinois branch of the firm last week to join competitor Stifel Nicolaus , alleging that they have been soliciting Morgan Stanley clients in violation of employment agreements.

Headlines: VW rejects Trump envoy's take on Iran pullout
Description: Carmaker Volkswagen AG  rejected on Thursday a report suggesting it had decided against doing business in Iran after coming under pressure from Donald Trump's ambassador to Germany, saying its position on the country had not changed.

Headlines: U.S. existing home sales unchanged in August
Description: U.S. home sales flatlined in August but inventory increased for the first time in three years as the housing market continued to struggle despite strength across the broader economy.

Headlines: Tesla Model 3 gets 5-star rating from U.S. safety agency
Description: Tesla Inc's  Model 3 sedan has been awarded a five-star rating by the U.S. auto safety agency NHTSA in tests that are standard for cars in the United States.

Description: (This September 19 story corrects paragraph five and six to clarify that only one FANG stock will remain in its current sector)

Headlines: Alibaba's Jack Ma says U.S.-China trade war ends 1 million U.S. jobs promise: Xinhua
Description: Alibaba  Chairman Jack Ma said the company can no longer meet its promise to create 1 million jobs in the United States due to U.S.-China trade tensions, Chinese news agency Xinhua reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Alibaba's Jack Ma says people should prepare for 20 years of China-U.S. trade war
Description: Jack Ma, co-founder of Chinese e-tech giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd , said on Thursday that people should make preparations for 20 years of China-U.S. trade frictions.

Headlines: U.S. weekly jobless claims fall as labor market strength continues
Description: The number of Americans filing for unemployment benefits unexpectedly fell last week, hitting near a 49-year low in a sign the job market remains strong.

Headlines: Japan fashion guru Maezawa lands first SpaceX moon flight
Description: SpaceX, Elon Musk's space transportation company, on Monday named its first private passenger on a voyage around the moon as Japanese billionaire Yusaku Maezawa, the founder and chief executive of online fashion retailer Zozo.

Headlines: Factbox: How the auction process for Sky will work
Description: A nearly two-year battle to take over UK-based broadcaster Sky  could finally be settled in a quick auction this weekend, Britain's Takeover Panel said on Thursday.

Headlines: Under fire Danske Bank faces fresh money laundering inquiry
Description: Danske Bank  faced a new Danish money laundering inquiry on Thursday as political anger spread over a scandal involving 200 billion euros ($234 billion) in payments, many of which were suspicious, through Estonia.

Headlines: Nestle aims to shed skin unit to focus on food, nutrition
Description: Nestle  put its skin health unit up for sale on Thursday, as the maker of Nescafe and Perrier water ditches underperforming businesses and fends off criticism from an activist investor demanding an overhaul.

Headlines: Facebook and Twitter must comply with EU consumer rules or face sanctions
Description: Facebook  and Twitter  face sanctions unless they comply with European consumer rules by the end of the year, the EU said as its regulators continue to their crackdown on U.S. social media giants over privacy concerns.

Headlines: LVMH watches head Biver to drop operations role
Description: Jean-Claude Biver is dropping his operational responsibilities as the head of LVMH's  watch division, he told Reuters over the phone on Thursday, confirming media reports.

Headlines: Lime's next stop in scooter global expansion: Florida and Austria
Description: Scooter- and bike-rental startup Lime is expanding to dozens more cities this year, its CEO said, leveraging the hundreds of millions of dollars in funding it has raised in an effort to dominate the North American and European markets.

Description: (This September 19 story corrects to read Gracia, paragraph 13)

Headlines: Japan clothing magnate Maezawa chases spot in business firmament
Description: Japanese fashion billionaire Yusaku Maezawa's first meeting with role model and SoftBank Group Corp  boss Masayoshi Son came in 2010 when they bathed together - a popular communal activity in Japan - on the 26th floor of the tech giant's headquarters.

Headlines: China urges U.S. to show sincerity, correct behavior in trade actions
Description: China hopes the United States will show sincerity and take steps to correct its behavior, its commerce ministry said on Thursday, after both countries slapped new tariffs on each other's goods this week in an escalating trade war.

Headlines: China paper warns it won't play defense on trade as Trump lauds tariffs
Description: (The Sept. 17 story corrects the date of the senior Chinese diplomat's visit to New York to next week, not this week, in paragraph 21)

Description: China plans to reduce the average tariff rate on imports from most of its trading partners as soon as October, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

Headlines: Volkswagen pulls out of Iran, according to U.S. official: Bloomberg
Description: Volkswagen AG  will end almost of all its operations in Iran, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing a U.S. official who led the discussions with the carmaker.

Headlines: Trump intends to nominate ex-Fed economist Liang for Fed board seat: White House
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump intends to nominate former Federal Reserve economist Nellie Liang to the U.S. central bank’s board of governors, the White House said on Wednesday.

Description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said on Wednesday he wanted to see flexibility from the United States if the two sides are to reach a deal on renewing NAFTA, which Washington insists must be finished by the end of the month.

Headlines: British American Tobacco has candidate to replace retiring chief exec
Description: British American Tobacco Plc  said on Wednesday its board has identified a lead candidate to succeed Chief Executive Nicandro Durante, who has said he intends to retire on April 1, 2019, after nearly 37 years with the company.

Headlines: U.S. judge dismisses GM ignition switch criminal case
Description: A federal judge in New York on Wednesday dismissed a criminal case brought against General Motors Co in 2015 over the largest U.S. automaker's handling of an ignition-switch defect linked to 124 deaths.

Headlines: S&P 500, Dow up as rising treasury yields boost banks
Description: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average rose on Wednesday, with the Dow hitting its highest closing level since late January as rising Treasury yields boosted the financial sector and trade worries subsided.

Headlines: Goldman names Dan Dees as new investment banking co-chief
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  named Dan Dees as investment-banking co-chief on Wednesday, according to an internal memo, the latest change in leadership at the Wall Street bank's business units before David Solomon becomes chief executive officer next month.

Headlines: Mars aims to tackle "broken" cocoa model with new sustainability scheme

Headlines: Trump 'likely' to announce new China tariffs as early as Monday: source
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump is likely to announce new tariffs on about $200 billion on Chinese imports as early as Monday, a senior administration official told Reuters on Saturday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Saudi Arabia to auction detained tycoon's real estate assets - sources
Description: Saudi Arabia will auction real estate owned by indebted billionaire Maan al-Sanea and his company starting next month to help repay billions of riyals due to creditors, sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: BMW to recall more than 139,000 of its 3-series cars in China from November
Description: German automaker BMW  will recall more than 139,000 of its 3-series cars in China from Nov. 9, because of a defect in the air-conditioning system, the market regulator said.

Headlines: BMW drives to cut battery costs, share costs on autonomous vehicles: executive
Description: German luxury vehicle maker BMW AG  plans more deals with mining companies to secure electric vehicle battery materials, and is open to forming alliances to share the costs of developing autonomous-vehicle systems, the automaker's research and development chief told Reuters.

Headlines: Credit Suisse CEO targets annual profit of 5-6 billion Swiss francs: newspaper
Description: Credit Suisse  is aiming for an annual profit of 5 to 6 billion Swiss francs for the next two years as the bank puts its problems behind it, Chief Executive Tidjane Thiam told Swiss newspaper NZZ am Sonntag in an interview to be published on Sunday.

Headlines: Iran says Saudi Arabia and Russia have taken oil market 'hostage': SHANA
Description: Iran's OPEC governor said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia and Russia have taken the oil market "hostage" as U.S. President Donald Trump seeks to impose fresh sanctions on Iranian oil sales.

Headlines: Campbell, Third Point urge shareholders to vote for two different boards
Description: Campbell Soup Co  and hedge fund Third Point LLC on Friday filed preliminary proxy materials urging the food company's shareholders to vote in favor of two entirely different slates of board nominees.

Headlines: Brazil space station open for small satellite business
Description: Brazil is ready to launch small commercial rockets from its space base near the equator as soon as it agrees to safeguard U.S. technology that is dominant in the industry, the Brazilian Air Force officer managing the space program said on Friday.

Headlines: Oil mixed as China tariff talk scotches early rally
Description: Oil prices pulled back on Friday on concerns additional U.S. tariffs would be placed on Chinese imports, after an earlier rally triggered by worries that more sanctions on Iran might constrict supply.

Headlines: Lockheed wins contract for U.S. Air Force GPS satellites
Description: The U.S. Air Force said on Friday it had chosen Lockheed Martin  to build 22 next-generation Global Positioning System satellites worth up to $7.2 billion, part of a major effort to modernize the GPS constellation of satellites.

Headlines: Trump readies tariffs on $200 billion more Chinese goods despite talks: source
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump has directed aides to proceed with tariffs on about another $200 billion of Chinese goods, despite Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin's attempts to restart trade talks with China, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday.

Headlines: Volkswagen to end production of the Beetle next year
Description: Volkswagen  said on Thursday it would stop producing its Beetle compact car in 2019, ending a model that looked backward to the 1960s counterculture as the automaker prepares for a leap toward a future of mass-market electric cars.

Headlines: Volvo Cars seeks U.S. tariff exemption for Chinese-made SUV
Description: Volvo Cars has asked the Trump administration to exempt the company's Chinese-made mid-size XC60 SUV from new 25 percent tariffs, the latest automaker to seek relief from new levies on imports from China.

Headlines: Trade conflict looms but higher rates, oil prices help some stocks
Description: A world stock index climbed as bank and energy shares rose on Friday, but the momentum was sapped by a report that Washington may fire a new salvo in its trade war with Beijing.

Headlines: Wall Street flat as looming tariffs offset gains in financials
Description: U.S. stocks ended little changed on Friday as financials  gained with bond yields, while news that President Donald Trump instructed aides to proceed with tariffs on about $200 billion more of Chinese products limited gains.

Headlines: Yellen: Fed should commit to future 'booms' to make up for major busts
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve should commit to letting economic booms run on enough to fully offset collapses like the 2007 to 2009 Great Recession, former Fed chair Janet Yellen said on Friday, urging the central bank to make "lower-for-longer" its official motto for interest rates following serious downturns.

Headlines: Fed faces 'quite challenging' period keeping recovery on track: Yellen
Description: The Federal Reserve faces a "quite challenging" period in trying to keep the U.S. recovery on track amid a risk that low unemployment could lead to an overheated economy, former Fed chief Janet Yellen said on Friday.

Headlines: Daly appointment shows diversity gap between regional Feds
Description: The appointment of Mary Daly as the second-ever woman to head up the San Francisco Federal Reserve makes plain that some regional central banks continue to make strides in creating a diverse leadership as criticism intensifies about the Fed's hiring policies while others fall behind.

Headlines: Mary Daly, labor expert, picked to run San Francisco Fed
Description: Mary Daly, a labor economist who dropped out of high school, later earned a PhD from Syracuse University, joined the San Francisco Fed's research department in 1996 and led it since 2017, was picked on Friday to be the bank's next president after a five-month search.

Headlines: U.S. House Democratic leader: NAFTA should stay a trilateral deal
Description: U.S. House of Representatives Democratic Leader Nancy Pelosi on Friday warned the Trump administration that NAFTA should be maintained as a trilateral pact between the United States, Mexico and Canada and not just as a U.S.-Mexico arrangement.

Headlines: Allergan says revenue from aesthetics unit may double by 2025
Description: Allergan Plc  said revenue from its medical aesthetics business could double by 2025, even as it faces increasing competition for its blockbuster wrinkle treatment, Botox.

Headlines: The home of Fiat says 'ciao' to Sergio Marchionne
Description: The home of Fiat bid farewell on Friday to Sergio Marchionne, one of the auto industry's most exacting and determined leaders, who rescued the Italian car giant and U.S. Chrysler.

Headlines: U.S. union urges states to look into T-Mobile purchase of Sprint
Description: The Communication Workers of America labor union, which opposes T-Mobile's proposed purchase of rival Sprint, has written to all 50 state attorneys general to highlight potential job losses from the proposed deal as well as antitrust concerns.

Headlines: Britain's FCA bans ex-Deutsche Bank trader after Euribor rigging
Description: Britain's Financial Conduct Authority has banned former Deutsche Bank trader Christian Bittar from performing any function related to any regulated financial activity, the financial watchdog said on Friday.

Headlines: Borrowers branch out
Description: LONDON (IFR) - Blue-chip corporates including Nestle are seeking to diversify their funding to avoid exposure to individual market risks.

Description: U.S. retail sales recorded their smallest gain in six months in August as consumers cut back on purchases of motor vehicles and clothing, but upward revisions to July data kept intact expectations of strong economic growth in the third quarter.

Headlines: Airbus says worst-case Brexit would hit its sites beyond BritainL Spiegel
Description: A worst-case scenario Brexit would affect Airbus's sites not only in Britain but also in the rest of Europe, board member Tom Williams has told the German magazine Der Spiegel.

Headlines: Citigroup pays $12 million to settle dark pool probe
Description: Citigroup Inc on Friday was ordered to pay more than $12 million by U.S. regulators after it was found that the bank's investment banking and financial advisory unit misled users of a "dark pool" operated by one of its affiliates.

Headlines: Metro puts struggling Real hypermarket chain on the block
Description: German retailer Metro AG plans to sell its struggling Real hypermarkets and is confident of interest in the chain, though bankers played down talk it might attract Amazon and a price tag of up to 1 billion euros ($1.2 billion).

Headlines: U.S. House Democratic leader says NAFTA should remain trilateral
Description: U.S. House of Representatives Democratic Leader Nancy Pelosi on Friday warned the Trump administration that the NAFTA trade agreement should be maintained as a trilateral pact between the United States, Mexico and Canada and not just a U.S.-Mexico arrangement.

Headlines: L Brands to close all Henri Bendel stores, website
Description: Victoria's Secret owner L Brands Inc  on Thursday said it would close all 23 of its Henri Bendel stores and the Henri Bendel e-commerce website in January.

Headlines: Fed policy to turn mildly restrictive in 2019, Evans says
Description: The Federal Reserve's interest-rate hikes will begin to drag on U.S. economic growth and employment by next year, a U.S. central banker said Friday, as the level of borrowing costs appropriately turns "mildly restrictive" after more than a decade of acting as a stimulant.

Headlines: Fed's Evans says premature to read much into yield curve
Description: A narrowing gap between long-term and short-term borrowing costs does not necessarily signal a coming recession, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Charles Evans said on Friday.

Headlines: Fed's Evans sees one or two more rate hikes this year
Description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Charles Evans said on Friday that two further interest-rate hikes this year by the U.S. central bank would not be surprising, given the strength of the economy.

Headlines: U.S. imposes sanctions on Thai company it accuses of aiding Iran
Description: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions against a Thai aviation company that it said was acting on behalf of Iran's Mahan Air, which it accused of ferrying troops and supplies into Syria in support of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad.

Headlines: UK public pension group to oppose Ryanair at AGM
Description: Ryanair faced growing criticism from unions and investors on Friday about how it has handled an industrial relations revolt ahead of its annual shareholder meeting next week when its veteran chairman's position will be challenged.

Headlines: Brexit endgame nears as series of summits begins
Description: Brexit talks are set to intensify over the coming week, with the first of three summits that European Union leaders hope will settle a divorce deal for departing Britain within the next two months.

Headlines: Amazon's Bezos says Trump should be 'glad' of media scrutiny
Description: Amazon.com Inc  Chief Executive Jeff Bezos said on Thursday the company would announce a decision on where it will build a second headquarters before the end of the year, and also said that President Donald Trump is wrong to "attack the media."

Headlines: U.S. health secretary backs proposed FDA crackdown on e-cigarettes: CNBC
Description: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Alex Azar told CNBC on Friday he was "completely in support" of the Food and Drug Administration's proposed crackdown on e-cigarettes.

Headlines: U.S. business inventories increase solidly in July

Headlines: U.S. auto sector output boosts industrial production
Description: U.S. industrial production rose in August, as strong output in auto manufacturing offset lackluster production in the rest of the factory sector.

Headlines: U.S. import prices post largest drop in more than one-and-a-half years
Description: U.S. import prices recorded their biggest drop in more than 1-1/2 years in August amid declines in the cost of fuels and a range of other goods, suggesting a strong dollar was curbing imported inflation pressures.

Headlines: U.S. retail sales post smallest gain in six months
Description: U.S. retail sales recorded their smallest gain in six months in August as consumers cut back on purchases of motor vehicles and clothing, but upward revisions to July data likely keep intact expectations of strong economic growth in the third quarter.

Headlines: Wells Fargo sees total expenses dropping by $3 billion by 2020: CFO
Description: Wells Fargo & Co's chief financial officer said on Friday the bank expects to reduce total expenses by about $3 billion by 2020.

Headlines: VW board to discuss future of Audi CEO Stadler on Monday: Spiegel
Description: The supervisory board of Volkswagen will meet on Monday to discuss the future of Rupert Stadler, the suspended chief executive of its premium brand Audi, German magazine Der Spiegel reported on Friday.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank's retreat to Germany gets tepid welcome at home
Description: German manufacturer Voith has been a customer of Deutsche Bank  for more than a century. But as the maker of hydropower and paper plants expands abroad it said it has started to hire other international banks where it would have previously considered Germany's largest lender.

Description: Hyundai Motor Group promoted heir apparent Euisun Chung on Friday to a role of overseeing the conglomerate, moving him a step closer to succeeding his octogenarian father as head of South Korea's second largest group.

Headlines: Takeda gets China's approval for $62 billion Shire purchase
Description: Takeda Pharmaceutical Co Ltd said on Friday China approved its purchase of Shire Plc, the latest regulator to clear the $62 billion deal and bring the Japanese group closer to becoming a global top 10 drugmaker.

Description: The United States on Thursday imposed sanctions on a China-based tech firm, its North Korean CEO and a Russian subsidiary, accusing them of moving illicit funding to North Korea in violation of U.S. sanctions.

Description: Australia's corporate watchdog sued Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd  on Friday over a troubled A$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion) share placement, flexing its muscle amid criticism levied at regulators for being soft on finance firms.

Description: Mexican telecommunications company America Movil has cut its stake in Dutch telecoms company KPN to slightly more than 16 percent, a filing at financial watchdog AFM showed.

Description: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi Inc  said on Friday it will rejig its businesses and create new leadership positions aimed at building a second tier to CEO Lei Jun, amid increased scrutiny of governance and successions at Chinese tech firms.

Description: Jeff Bezos, Amazon.com Inc's  founder and the world's richest person, said on Thursday he will commit $2 billion to helping homeless families and starting pre-schools for low-income communities.

Headlines: China says world trade system not perfect, needs reform
Description: The current world trade system is not perfect and China supports reforms to it, including to the World Trade Organization, to make it fairer and more effective, Beijing's top diplomat said.

Headlines: Sears' same-store sales losses narrow but warns it may go out of business
Description: Sears Holdings Corp  reported a smaller decline in quarterly same-store sales on Thursday, but warned again that there is doubt about the company's continued operation as it awaits approval to sell some of its businesses to its chief executive's hedge fund.

Headlines: IKEA targets home delivery by electric vehicle in five major cities by 2020
Description: IKEA Group, the owner of most IKEA stores worldwide, said on Friday all its home deliveries in the inner cities of Amsterdam, Los Angeles, New York, Paris and Shanghai would be made by electric vehicles or through other zero-emission means by 2020.

Description: Apple led a rebound in technology shares and boosted all three major U.S. stock indexes on Thursday, while trade worries eased after China welcomed new talks with the United States.

Headlines: SEC rescinds guidance that bolstered proxy advisers
Description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission handed public companies a procedural victory on Thursday in their efforts to reduce the influence of proxy advisory firms, rescinding a pair of staff letters that critics said encouraged mutual funds to rely on their recommendations.

Description: Signs of movement in the U.S.-China trade stand-off and an interest rate hike in emerging market trouble-spot Turkey sent an index of global stocks higher on Thursday as risk appetite returned.

Headlines: UPS plan to boost business shipping falls short with investors
Description: United Parcel Service Inc  is doubling down on shipments between businesses as part of a $20 billion overhaul aimed at automating its facilities and offsetting the profit squeeze from lower-profit home deliveries from large retailers like Amazon.com .

Headlines: Canada PM says he wants a good NAFTA deal soon, hazy on deadline
Description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said on Thursday he wanted a good NAFTA deal as soon as possible, but did not answer directly when asked if he agreed with Washington that the end of September was the final deadline for talks.

Headlines: Atlanta Fed's Bostic: Rate hikes can continue for several more quarters
Description: There may be room for the U.S. jobs market to improve further without pressure on inflation, an argument for the Fed to be patient as it considers further rate increases, Atlanta Federal Reserve bank president Raphael Bostic said on Thursday.

Headlines: Walmart's Jet.com to offer Nike products in bid for urban consumers
Description: Walmart's Jet.com said on Thursday it will sell Nike Inc products and offer more delivery options, beginning in its top market of New York City, in a bid to sharpen its aim for affluent, urban consumers and better compete with e-commerce rivals like Amazon.com Inc.

Headlines: Company veteran named Airbus sales chief after ex-Rolls executive quits
Description: Airbus  named its second new sales chief in less than a year on Thursday after chief commercial officer Eric Schulz abruptly resigned nine months after being poached from Rolls-Royce  to lead the battle for jet sales against Boeing.

Headlines: Trump's antitrust enforcer considers shifting up a gear
Description: The chairman of the Federal Trade Commission, which stops mergers it believes will push up prices, signaled Thursday he was willing to consider tougher enforcement, a move that could affect high profile big tech companies but also energy producers, drug makers and a big swath of the U.S. economy.

Headlines: GM to recall about 1.2 million vehicles worldwide
Description: General Motors Co  is recalling 1.205 million pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles worldwide due to issues with a temporary loss of power steering, the No.1 U.S. automaker said on Thursday.

Headlines: JPMorgan sees small drop in third-quarter markets revenue vs year earlier
Description: Third-quarter markets revenue at JPMorgan Chase & Co  is down by a small percent from a year earlier after adjusting for tax law changes, Chief Financial Officer Marianne Lake said at an investor conference on Thursday.

Headlines: Second round of tariff-related aid to farmers may come in December: USDA
Description: A second round of tariff-related aid to U.S. farmers could be announced in December, according to a white paper released by the U.S. Department of Agriculture on Thursday.

Headlines: Ex-Deerfield partners get prison in case over U.S. agency leaks
Description: Two former partners of the hedge fund Deerfield Management were sentenced to three years in prison on Thursday after being convicted of taking part in what prosecutors have described as an insider trading scheme based on leaks from within a federal healthcare agency.

Headlines: Exclusive: Hedge fund Diamondback founders Schimel and Sapanski plan new fund - sources
Description: The founders of Diamondback Capital, one of a handful of hedge funds touched by the U.S. government's insider trading probe, have reunited and are working on a new investment project, people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: VW's Skoda unions object to renewed talks on production moves
Description: Trade unions at Volkswagen's  Czech unit Skoda Auto on Thursday rejected any idea of moving some of the production of its premium sedan model Superb to German plants.

Headlines: U.S. labor board to ease companies’ liability for contractors' labor practices
Description: The U.S. agency that enforces federal labor laws took the first steps on Thursday towards loosening an Obama-era standard that made it easier to hold companies liable for illegal labor practices by their contractors and franchisees.

Headlines: Goldman names new operating chief, finance head in executive shakeup
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc on Thursday announced its biggest management shakeup since naming David Solomon as Chief Executive Officer Lloyd Blankfein's successor.

Headlines: Roche steps up efficiency drive to take sting out of biosimilars
Description: Roche , the world's biggest producer of cancer drugs, is stepping up cost cuts in an efficiency drive made unavoidable by competition from cut-price copies of three mega-brands from its famed U.S. Genentech biotech stable.

Headlines: Ryanair faces one-day strike in five countries over contracts
Description: Ryanair faces a one-day walkout by cabin crew across five countries on Sept. 28 as unions step up pressure on Europe's biggest budget airline to accept local contracts.

Headlines: U.S. consumer prices rise slowly; jobless claims near 49-year low
Description: U.S. consumer prices rose less than expected in August as increases in gasoline and rents were offset by declines in healthcare and apparel costs, and underlying inflation pressures also appeared to be slowing.

Headlines: Kroger misses same-store sales estimates, shares drop 11 pct
Description: U.S. supermarket chain Kroger Co missed quarterly same-store sales estimates on Thursday, sending shares down as much as 11 percent, as changes to the way it stocks merchandise on shelves kept some customers away from its stores, analysts said.

Headlines: Three Italy cabin crew unions reach labor agreement with Ryanair
Description: Unions representing three of Ryanair's  Italy-based cabin crews said on Thursday they had reached an agreement in principle for a three-year collective labor agreement, according to a statement.

Headlines: Fidelity Investments winds down $3.5 billion index fund
Description: Fidelity Investments is winding down a fund that had more than $3 billion in assets last year, with the Boston-based money manager citing an overlap in holdings of other funds used in its target-date products to explain the rare move.

Description: Airbus said in a statement it had appointed Christian Scherer as Chief Commercial Officer, replacing Eric Schulz, who has decided to leave the company for personal reasons.

Description: The U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has filed suit against Future Income Payments, a Nevada company that offers cash advances in exchange for future pension benefits, which the regulator said are actually exceptionally high-interest loans.

Description: Target Corp said on Thursday that it plans to hire about 120,000 seasonal workers for the holidays, up 20 percent on last year, as the retailer gears up for the busiest time of the year.

Headlines: Trump denies pressure for trade deal as China welcomes U.S. talks invite
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the United States was under no pressure to make a trade deal with China, even as Chinese officials welcomed an invitation from Washington for a new round of talks with more U.S. tariffs looming.

Headlines: Peugeot's DS brand adds mini-SUV to bolster rebounding sales
Description: French carmaker PSA Group unveiled an SUV version of its DS3 upscale mini as it builds on a sales rebound underway at the eight-year-old premium DS brand.

Headlines: Canada's maturing Big Weed hits up Europe hoping for expansion cash
Description: A favorite of DIY stock pickers, Canadian cannabis firms are trying to bolster their institutional investor base by ramping up efforts to woo European funds as countries across the region approve marijuana for medical use.

Headlines: New Apple watch could take bite out of Swiss market
Description: The Swiss watch industry faces an increased threat from a new Apple Watch able to detect heart problems that is likely to appeal to older shoppers, industry experts said on Thursday.

Headlines: Tennis star Osaka named Nissan ambassador, gives hope to biracial Japanese
Description: Japan's Nissan Motor Co has signed U.S. Open champion Naomi Osaka as its next brand ambassador, the automaker said on Thursday, tapping the tennis star's youth, drive and Japanese roots to appeal to younger customers.

Headlines: U.S. consumer prices increase less than expected in August
Description: U.S. consumer prices rose less than expected in August as increases in gasoline and rents were offset by declines in healthcare and apparel costs, and underlying inflation pressures also appeared to be slowing.

Headlines: U.S. weekly jobless claims drop to near 49-year low
Description: The number of Americans filing for unemployment benefits unexpectedly fell last week, hitting its lowest level in nearly 49 years and pointing to robust labor market conditions.

Headlines: Singapore's ST Engineering to buy aircraft part maker from GE for $630 million
Description: Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd on Thursday said it had agreed to purchase aircraft part manufacturer MRA Systems from General Electric Co for $630 million.

Headlines: BlackRock gets regulatory approval to set up new firm in France
Description: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, has obtained regulatory approval to set up a new alternative investment firm in France, in another sign of Paris' increasing post-Brexit appeal for financial firms.

Headlines: Bayer's pharma unit head Weinand quits to join Sanofi
Description: Bayer, which is revamping its drug development activities, is losing the head of its pharmaceuticals division Dieter Weinand, who will join Sanofi to stem a decline in prices in the French drugmaker's anti-diabetics and established drugs.

Headlines: Sonny's roadshow: How Trump's Ag chief sells a trade war to farmers
Description: Breaking off from a tour of dairy operations on a farm in upstate New York, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue tramps across a muddy path to take a sample of sweet corn from an adjacent field.

Headlines: Apple iPhones get bigger and pricier, Watch turns to health
Description: Apple Inc introduced its largest-ever iPhone and a watch that detects heart problems on Wednesday in an attempt to get customers to upgrade to more expensive devices in the face of stagnant global demand for smartphones.

Headlines: Rebuilding lives, 10 years after Lehman's fall
Description: It is an image that became a symbol of the global financial crisis -- about 20 bankers, their backs turned to the window, attending an emergency meeting at the London office of Lehman Brothers as the firm slid toward collapse.

Headlines: Ryanair cabin crew to strike September 28 in five countries: union spokesman
Description: Seven Ryanair cabin crew unions from five countries will hold a 24-hour strike on Sept. 28, a Belgian union spokesman said on Thursday.

Headlines: Qualcomm targets $16 billion in share buyback

Description: American companies in China are being hurt by tariffs in the growing trade war between Washington and Beijing, according to a survey of hundreds of firms, prompting the U.S. business lobbies behind the poll to urge the Trump administration to reconsider its approach.

Headlines: Pilots in Italy to join Ryanair cabin crew strike: unions
Description: Italian pilots for Ryanair will join a cabin crew strike across five countries on Sept. 28 and unions may continue with industrial action once a month until they win changes to labor contracts, cabin crew unions said on Thursday.

Headlines: Takeda weighs sale of Shire's eye care business to cut debt: Bloomberg
Description: Japan's Takeda Pharmaceutical  is considering selling Shire Plc's  eye care business once it closes its $62 billion purchase of the London-listed drugmaker, as it looks to cut the debt raised to fund the deal, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

Headlines: China says Beijing, Washington do not want to see trade war escalate further
Description: China's commerce ministry believes China and the United States do not want to see their trade war escalate further, it said on Thursday.

Description: China will show off its growing military aviation strength at its biggest airshow in November, with fighter jet flypasts and its largest display of weaponry ever, an air force spokesman said on Thursday.

Headlines: China welcomes U.S. invitation for trade talks

Headlines: Exclusive: Adobe in talks to buy marketing software firm Marketo - sources

Description: The Trump administration has invited Chinese officials to restart trade talks, the White House's top economic adviser said on Wednesday, as Washington prepares to further escalate the U.S.-China trade war with tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods.

Description: The chief executive of South Korea's LG Display , Han Sang-beom, was determined to deliver a strong message when he appeared before 1,000 employees at the firm's main manufacturing plant last spring.

Description: Hershey Co  said on Wednesday it would buy Pirate Brands from B&G Foods Inc  for $420 million in an all-cash deal, giving the chocolate maker rights to snack brands such as Pirate's Booty, Smart Puffs and Original Tings.

Headlines: Fitbit falls, Garmin shed gains on new Apple watch

Description: Trustees of British Airways-sponsored Airways Pension Scheme are close to a deal with Legal & General  to insure more than 4 billion pounds ($5.22 billion) of its historic pension liabilities, Sky News reported on Wednesday.

Description: The executive producer of the CBS television program "60 Minutes," Jeff Fager, is leaving CBS News, according to a company memo on Wednesday, amid reports of inappropriate behavior.

Headlines: As Trump embraces more tariffs, U.S. business readies public fight
Description: After months of waging a behind-the-scenes war against President Donald Trump's trade tariffs that have escalated far beyond what business groups once imagined, more than 85 U.S. industry groups launched a coalition on Wednesday to take the fight public.

Headlines: Brent reaches $80 a barrel after fall in U.S. crude stocks
Description: Oil futures rose on Wednesday, with Brent reaching $80 a barrel, after a larger-than-expected drop in U.S. crude inventories and as U.S. sanctions on Iran added to concerns over global oil supply.

Headlines: Volvo shows off self-driving, electric truck with no cab
Description: Sweden's Volvo, the world's second-biggest truck maker, presented a new self-driving electric truck on Wednesday, which it said should help respond to the boom in ecommerce and a shortage of freight drivers.

Headlines: Tesla investor says SEC asked it about 'funding secured' tweet
Description: Tesla Inc's  biggest institutional investor said on Wednesday it was questioned by U.S. securities regulators about Elon Musk's now-abandoned plans to take the electric carmaker private and that the chief executive needed help running the company.

Headlines: U.S. incomes rose but inequality widened in 2017: data
Description: The median U.S. household income rose for a third straight year in 2017 to the highest on record since 1967 by one measure, but the gap between white- and non-white households widened, government data showed on Wednesday.

Headlines: JPMorgan's Dimon backtracks after saying he could beat Trump
Description: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase & Co , quickly backtracked on Wednesday morning from having said he could beat President Donald Trump in a campaign but not liberal Democrats.

Headlines: Chinese electric carmaker NIO shares rev up after shaky U.S. debut
Description: Shares of Chinese electric carmaker NIO Inc  recovered sharply from a 15 percent fall in their market debut on Wednesday, a day after the company's IPO was priced at the lower end of the expected range.

Headlines: Verizon names new CEO for Oath
Description: Verizon Communications Inc  on Wednesday named K. Guru Gowrappan as the new chief executive officer of its media and advertising business, Oath, replacing Tim Armstrong.

Headlines: Some U.S. businesses postponing investment due to trade concerns: Fed
Description: U.S. businesses have scaled back or postponed investments in several parts of the country due to concerns about international trade tensions, the Federal Reserve said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Thyssen interim CEO plans shake-up of engineering unit: source
Description: Thyssenkrupp's  interim boss Guido Kerkhoff is working  on a restructuring of the German conglomerate's plant engineering and shipbuilding division, a source familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Canada's Freeland plans NAFTA talks Thurs, much work remains: source
Description: Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland is planning to return to Washington to hold more talks on NAFTA on Thursday but plenty of work remains before the two sides can strike a deal, a well-placed Canadian source said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Comcast says Sky shareholders have until October 6 to accept offer
Description: Comcast Corp's bid of 14.75 pounds for each Sky share will now remain open for acceptance until early October, the U.S. cable giant said on Wednesday, adding that it has received valid acceptances for shares representing 0.29 percent of Sky Plc to date.

Headlines: Ryanair defiant as strike grounds flights in Germany
Description: Pilots and cabin crew at Ryanair  in Germany staged a full-day walkout on Wednesday and threatened further strikes as management at Europe's largest low-cost carrier struggled to rein in an industrial relations revolt.

Headlines: Online firms to risk EU fine if extremist posts linger
Description: The European Union's chief executive on Wednesday proposed hefty fines on Google, Facebook, Twitter and other online platforms if they fail to remove extremist content within one hour.

Headlines: Exclusive: Deutsche Bank weighs overhaul that could make deals easier - sources
Description: Deutsche Bank is considering an overhaul to loosen the bond between its retail and investment banks, according to three people with knowledge of the matter, a move that could make it easier to merge some or all of the group with rivals.

Headlines: Boeing 737 recovery plan 'taking hold' amid factory snarl: CEO
Description: Boeing Co expects to deliver roughly as many 737 narrowbody jetliners in September as the company delivered in August as it works to bounce back from a manufacturing logjam triggered by supplier delays, its CEO said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Amazon, Apple, others to testify before U.S. Senate on data privacy September 26
Description: Six major Web companies and internet-service providers, including AT&T Inc, Twitter Inc and Alphabet Inc's Google, will detail their consumer data privacy practices to a U.S. Senate panel on Sept. 26, according to a congressional statement on Wednesday.

Description: Alphabet Inc, Facebook Inc, Netflix Inc and others will be in focus on Sept. 24 when they are moved out of the tech and consumer discretionary sectors into a deepened pool of communication and media stocks.

Headlines: United Tech to pay $14 million for illegal foreign payments: U.S. SEC
Description: United Technologies Corp will pay $13.9 million to settle charges it made illegal payments or provided trips and gifts to officials from Azerbaijan, China, Kuwait, South Korea, Pakistan, Thailand and Indonesia in order to obtain business, the top U.S. securities regulator said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Macy's to hire 80,000 for holiday rush, boost online staffing

Headlines: Blackstone, Centerbridge consider joint bid for Santander HQ in Spain: sources
Description: U.S. investors Blackstone and Centerbridge are considering a 3 billion-euro ($3.5 billion) offer for Banco Santander's headquarters in Madrid, two sources with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: VW ex-CEO, Bosch CEO won't testify in Stuttgart trial: judge

Headlines: U.S. producer prices post first drop in one-and-a-half years

Description: New York has overtaken London as the world's most attractive financial center, a survey said on Wednesday, as Britain's decision to leave the EU prompts banks to shift jobs out of the city to keep access to Europe's single market.

Headlines: Takeda to pack up Illinois HQ, nearly 1,000 workers to be affected
Description: Japan's Takeda Pharmaceutical Co Ltd said on Wednesday it plans to shut its U.S. headquarters in Deerfield, Illinois and move it to the greater Boston area, following the closing of its Shire Plc acquisition.

Description: Citigroup Inc.'s chief financial officer said on Wednesday the bank expects to exceed its previous targets for returns on shareholder equity and cost savings, helped in part by tax reform.

A decade later, house-flipping is making a comeback, but this time in some Rust Belt cities the last boom passed by.

Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  will provide $500 million over five years to promote economic opportunities in selected cities, including some outside the United States, the bank said Wednesday.

Description: A former Goldman Sachs Group Inc  partner had raised concerns about some unethical practices at the bank before he left in 2015, the New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing people close to the matter.

Headlines: Musk's U-turn on Tesla deal could intensify his legal, regulatory woes
Description: Tesla Inc Chief Executive Elon Musk's decision to abruptly abandon a plan to take his electric carmaker private will not resolve his mounting regulatory and legal woes, and may even make them worse, some securities lawyers said.

Description: Volkswagen's  external compliance monitor on Monday said he disagreed with some VW executives' use of privacy and attorney client privilege rights to withhold information about a $27 billion global emissions cheating scandal.

Description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau spoke to Mexican President Enrique Pena Nieto on Sunday and both agreed to the tri-lateral nature of the NAFTA deal, the prime minister's office said on Monday amid news that the United States and Mexico have reached an agreement on trade.

Headlines: Canada says will continue to work for new NAFTA deal
Description: Canada is encouraged by the continued optimism shown by its NAFTA partners and will continue to negotiate for a deal, but will only sign a new agreement that is good for Canada, a spokesman for Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland said on Monday.

Headlines: Mexico's President says to speak with Trump on NAFTA advances
Description: Mexico's President Enrique Pena Nieto said on Twitter on Monday that he will speak with U.S. President Donald Trump shortly on advances made in the renegotiation of the NAFTA trade deal so that Canada can rejoin trilateral talks.

Headlines: Advent to invest $485 million in Walmart operations in Brazil
Description: Advent International, the private equity firm that acquired 80 percent of Walmart Inc  's Brazilian operations, is going to invest 1.9 billion reais ($485.66 million) in the existing stores as part of an agreement with the world's biggest retailer, according to a document published in Brazil's official gazette.

Headlines: Take Five: World markets themes for the week ahead
Description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

Headlines: Trump to make trade announcement Monday morning: White House
Description: President Donald Trump will make a trade announcement at 11 a.m.  (1500 GMT) on Monday, the White House said, as anticipation builds that the United States and Mexico are close to an agreement between the two North American Free Trade Agreement nations.

Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday suggested the United States and Mexico were close to a "big deal" on trade after days of negotiations between the two partners in the North American Free Trade Agreement.

Description: U.S. and Mexican trade negotiators are close to squaring away bilateral differences on the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and will resume talks on Monday morning, Mexican Economy Minister Ildefonso Guajardo said on Sunday.

Description: Turkey's currency crisis has roiled emerging-markets investors far and wide, including the U.S. state of Tennessee, where the state's retirement system is the biggest institutional holder in a Turkey exchange-traded fund (ETF).

Headlines: U.S.-Mexico NAFTA talks to continue Monday: minister

Headlines: Mexico minister says can't declare NAFTA victory yet
Description: Mexico's Economy Minister Ildefonso Guajardo said on Sunday that he couldn't yet declare victory in bilateral talks with the United States over the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

Description: U.S. stock futures hit a record high early on Monday in Asia after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell said on Friday that a gradual approach to raising rates remains appropriate to protect the U.S. economy and job growth.

Description: At a trade show in southern Beijing, children and parents crowd around a group of pink and blue dancing robots that resemble toddler-sized Power Rangers.
