Headlines: HP Inc tops revenue estimates, raises forecast on PC demand
Description: HP Inc  reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and raised its full-year profit forecast on Tuesday, helped by strong demand for its notebooks and desktops.

Headlines: Wall Street shares slide with Italy in focus
Description: U.S. stock markets tumbled on Tuesday, on downbeat trading guidance from JP Morgan and worries over Italy putting the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average on track for their biggest one-day drops in seven weeks.

Headlines: Delays and 'poison pills': team Trump runs out of road in NAFTA talks
Description: President Donald Trump is running out of time to deliver a revamp of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) he promised for this year and people involved in the talks say the crunch is largely of his administration's own making.

Headlines: Worsening Italian crisis batters stock markets
Description: A spiraling Italian political crisis provoked a global stock market sell-off on Tuesday, cut the euro to a 10-month low and spiked borrowing costs for the government in Rome.

Headlines: San Francisco subpoenas Uber, Lyft on driver classification
Description: San Francisco's city attorney on Tuesday subpoenaed Uber Technologies Inc [UBER.UL] and Lyft Inc to turn over records relating to how the ride-hailing companies classify drivers, as well as driver wages, health care and other benefits, the latest demand in a year-long investigation.

Headlines: Opel agrees job guarantees, investments at German sites
Description: German labour leaders on Tuesday agreed with PSA Group's  Opel unit on an investment plan and job guarantees for German factories in return for wage concessions.

Headlines: Coca-Cola Co to increase investments in Argentina
Description: Coca-Cola Co  said on Tuesday it would increase its investments in Argentina over the next three years, giving embattled President Mauricio Macri's government a boost at a difficult time.

Headlines: Canada pension funds may be long-term buyers of Kinder pipeline
Description: Canada's biggest public pension funds could be long-term buyers of Kinder Morgan Canada Ltd's  Trans Mountain pipeline but are unlikely to invest until the C$7.4 billion ($5.7 billion) project has been built, several pension fund sources said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Time is right for RBS share sale, bankers and analysts say
Description: The British government should go ahead and sell more shares in state-backed Royal Bank of Scotland , bankers and industry experts said, even though it would likely mean a big loss to taxpayers.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler investors want electric road map in CEO's swan song
Description: Fiat Chrysler (FCA)  boss Sergio Marchionne is expected to outline new plans for electric and hybrid cars in a strategy presentation on Friday, aiming to ensure the world's seventh-largest carmaker remains in the race in the absence of a merger.

Headlines: Factbox: Fiat Chrysler's track record and challenges ahead
Description: Fiat Chrysler  will present its next five-year business plan on Friday, the last under outgoing CEO Sergio Marchionne.

Headlines: Bayer says EU approves BASF as buyer of antitrust divestments
Description: Bayer  said on Tuesday said the European Commission had approved BASF  as a suitable buyer of the businesses Bayer will divest to win regulatory approval for the planned acquisition of Monsanto.

Headlines: Singapore Exchange postpones launch of Indian derivatives products
Description: The Singapore Exchange (SGX)  has postponed the launch of a set of India derivatives products after an Indian court on Tuesday referred a dispute around the proposed offerings to an arbitrator.

Headlines: Vedanta prepares legal challenge to India copper plant closure after fatal protest: sources
Description: Vedanta Resources is working on a legal challenge to an Indian state's closure of one of its copper smelters, but it will not proceed until tensions over the deaths of 13 people during protests last week have eased, two sources told Reuters.

Headlines: U.S. consumer confidence rebounds, house prices increase
Description: Consumer confidence rebounded in May, but households were a bit pessimistic about their short-term income prospects even as they  expected strong job growth to persist, which could restrain consumer spending.

Headlines: U.S. sets public hearings on auto import tariff probe
Description: Less than a week after the Trump administration threatened to impose tariffs of up to 25 percent on foreign-built automobiles, the U.S. government on Tuesday said it would hold public hearings on whether the import of vehicles and auto parts represents national security risks.

Headlines: SandRidge fights back against Icahn over board control
Description: SandRidge Energy Inc  warned shareholders on Tuesday they would be handing control of the company too cheaply to activist investor Carl Icahn if they elect his new nominees to the board at an annual meeting next month.

Headlines: Exclusive: Mexico central bank ready for election, could support peso-Diaz de Leon
Description: Mexico's central bank is prepared for different scenarios resulting from the country's July 1 presidential vote, central bank chief Alejandro Diaz de Leon said late on Monday, adding that policymakers could act to support the peso if liquidity dries up.

Headlines: China surprised at White House trade statement -ministry
Description: China expressed surprise on Tuesday at a White House statement that the United States will continue to pursue action on trade with Beijing, saying it was contrary to the consensus both sides reached recently.

Headlines: Not enough time for tech customs solution to Brexit: Aston Martin
Description: The boss of carmaker Aston Martin warned it was probably too late to roll out the kind of technology needed for the post-Brexit customs plan that is favoured by many British eurosceptics.

Headlines: Alibaba leads consortium in $1.4 billion deal for stake in Chinese courier ZTO
Description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd  on Tuesday said it has led a consortium of investors to buy about 10 percent of Chinese courier ZTO Express (Cayman) Inc  for $1.38 billion, as part of the e-commerce firm's push into offline services.

Headlines: Vienna Airport woos low-cost carriers to secure growth
Description: Vienna Airport  is banking on budget carriers' expansion into eastern European countries to secure its long-term growth, its co-chiefs said.

Headlines: BlaBlaCar and AXA launch car insurance product
Description: BlaBlaCar, whose amateur chauffeurs share costs with passengers on long-distance journeys, and AXA  said on Tuesday that they had launched a new car insurance product.

Headlines: U.S. May auto sales expected to dip 1 percent: J.D. Power and LMC
Description: U.S. automobile sales are expected to decline 1 percent year-over-year in May, industry consultants J.D. Power and LMC Automotive said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Deutsche bank says Moscow restructuring done, no plans for new staff cuts
Description: Deutsche Bank  views Russia as a priority, has completed a transformation of its operation there, and does not plan to cut its workforce there materially, the bank's Russia head told Reuters in an interview.

Headlines: France's Iliad ventures into Italy with low-price mobile offer
Description: French telecoms operator Iliad  launched its first foray outside France on Tuesday when it presented its new low-price  mobile offer for Italy as it looks to offset weakness at home.

Headlines: Canada likely to buy Trans Mountain pipeline project: Bloomberg
Description: Canada is likely to buy Kinder Morgan Canada Ltd's Trans Mountain oil pipeline and its proposed expansion project in an attempt to ensure that it is built, Bloomberg reported on Monday, citing a person familiar with the talks.

Headlines: UK watchdog says most clients will get all cash back from Beaufort
Description: Thousands of customers of failed British brokerage Beaufort are likely to get all their money back, regulators said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Danish dairy group Arla says to cut 350 jobs
Description: Danish dairy group Arla said on Tuesday it would cut around 350 jobs as part of a three-year cost-cutting programme that it announced in April.

Headlines: RBS to stop financing new coal plants, oil sands or arctic oil projects
Description: Britain's Royal Bank of Scotland  said on Tuesday it had tightened restrictions on project finance and general lending for high-carbon energy projects and companies, joining other banks like HSBC  in shoring up its climate policies.

Headlines: In Portugal, trust in China is the art of the deal
Description: Utility company EDP may balk at the meager 5 percent premium offered for its shares by China Three Gorges (CT) but the battle for Portugal's biggest business has largely played out already.

Headlines: Sixt CEO says efforts to push electric cars are a political mistake
Description: The CEO and major shareholder of German car rental company Sixt  said a political effort to push the mass rollout of electric cars is a costly political error.

Headlines: No antitrust probe for Lufthansa over fares after Air Berlin collapse
Description: Lufthansa  will not be investigated for market abuse over rising ticket prices following the collapse of local rival Air Berlin , the German cartel office said on Tuesday.

Headlines: How the world's biggest private equity oil and gas industry bid collapsed
Description: Blame it on Trump, Iran or Venezuela. Rising oil prices combined with a heavy debt load killed the world's biggest private equity oil and gas industry deal last week.

Headlines: Nestle plans to cut up to 500 IT jobs in Switzerland
Description: Nestle  plans to eliminate up to 500 information technology jobs at its Swiss home base as its shifts work to an existing tech hub in Spain and other locations, the food and beverage giant said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Investors find little appetite for consumer staples
Description: The consumer staples index , the S&P 500's biggest laggard for 2018, could have further to fall and may even look less appealing as a defensive play in the event the economy turns sour.

Headlines: U.S. and China clash over 'technology transfer' at WTO
Description: Chinese and U.S. envoys sparred at the World Trade Organization on Monday over U.S. President Donald Trump's claims that China steals American ideas, the subject of two lawsuits and a White House plan to slap huge punitive tariffs on Chinese goods.

Headlines: Swiss watch exports rise in April as Hong Kong booms
Description: Swiss watch exports rose 13.8 percent in April to 1.76 billion Swiss francs ($1.77 billion), powered by a boom in the crucial Hong Kong market, trade data showed on Tuesday.

Headlines: Olympics: Sporting events put Japan businesses in the mood for love
Description: (Refiling item from May 25 to change name to 'Russell Mark' in 6th paragraph)

Headlines: U.S. and EU again at odds over Airbus subsidies at WTO
Description: The European Union told the World Trade Organization's dispute settlement body on Monday that it had acted within days of a WTO ruling to bring its funding of planemaker Airbus into line with WTO rules, a trade official who attended the meeting said.

Headlines: Oil hits multi-week lows on fears of growing supplies
Description: Oil prices extended losses on Monday as Saudi Arabia and Russia said they may increase supplies while U.S. production gains showed no sign of slowing.

Headlines: EU trade chief to meet U.S. peers Ross, Lighthizer in Paris on Wednesday
Description: Europe's top trade official Cecilia Malmstrom will meet U.S. counterparts Wilbur Ross and Robert Lighthizer in Paris on Wednesday, two days before a temporary reprieve from U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs is due to expire.

Headlines: Italian concerns knock stocks, euro off early highs
Description: European stocks gave up early gains and bond yields recovered from lows as early elections loomed in Italy after the anti-establishment 5-Star and League parties abandoned plans to form a government.

Headlines: French industrialist Serge Dassault dies at 93
Description: French billionaire industrialist Serge Dassault, whose group builds the Rafale war planes and owns Le Figaro newspaper, died in Paris on Monday aged 93, a spokesman for Dassault Group said.

Description: Germany's Transport Ministry quizzed Daimler  Chief Executive Dieter Zetsche on Monday over how many Mercedes-Benz vans and cars need to be fixed after a regulator said it had found illegal software in one of its models.

Headlines: Britain could sell 10 percent stake in RBS as soon as this week: Sky News
Description: Britain could sell a 10 percent stake in Royal Bank of Scotland  as soon as this week, Sky News reported on Monday, citing banking sources.

Headlines: Indian trader group objects to Walmart-Flipkart deal
Description: An Indian trader body has raised objections to Walmart Inc's  $16 billion acquisition of e-commerce firm Flipkart, though lawyers and sources said the complaint to the country's antitrust regulator is unlikely to threaten the deal.

Headlines: China's Anbang says investor selection work under way
Description: China's Anbang Insurance Group [ANBANG.UL] said on Monday that the selection process for a strategic shareholder has begun, reiterating that it has ample cashflow and is operating normally after its state-backed bailout.

Description: Record crude oil volumes exported from the United States will be heading to Asia in the next couple of months to take another piece of the market away from Russia and producers in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

Description: Germany is seeking to end a dispute between the United States and the European Union over President Donald Trump's decision to impose high tariffs on steel and aluminum imports, Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Monday.

Description: U.S. private equity giant Blackstone Group  is seeking to deepen its exposure to Australian commercial property with a A$3.08 billion ($2.3 billion) bid for Sydney-focused company Investa Office Fund (IOF) .

Headlines: Japan's PM defends its automakers against U.S. import probe
Description: Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said on Monday he would seek to convince President Donald Trump of the crucial role his country's automakers play in boosting the U.S. economy.

Headlines: Trading in Samsonite shares halted, pending statement
Description: Trading in shares of Samsonite International SA  was suspended on Monday pending a statement from the world's largest luggage maker, just days after a short seller accused it of questionable accounting practices and poor governance.

Headlines: Australia increases Takata air bags recall to just under four million cars
Description: Australia said on Monday it was recalling an additional 1.1 million cars fitted with Takata Corp  air bags, increasing the size of the country's biggest ever compulsory recall to just under four million cars.

Headlines: German carmakers morally obliged to refit dirty diesels: minister
Description: German carmakers have a moral obligation to refit heavily polluting diesel vehicles on the country's roads, environment minister Svenja Schulze said, but conceded that the government had no legal means to make them do so.

Headlines: As clock ticks, doubts grow over Kinder Morgan's Canada oil pipe expansion
Description: As a hard deadline set by Kinder Morgan Canada Ltd  for scrapping a key pipeline expansion looms, there is growing doubt among investors, contractors and government officials about reaching a deal to save the C$7.4 billion ($5.7 billion) project.

Headlines: Bombardier launches longer-range variants of Global business jets
Description: Canada's Bombardier Inc on Sunday announced two new longer-range variants of its existing large-cabin Global business jets, which the company expects to generate higher revenues during a time of recovering appetite for corporate planes.

Headlines: Qualcomm to meet China regulators in push to clear $44 billion NXP deal: sources
Description: Qualcomm Inc  is expecting to meet this week in Beijing with China's antitrust regulators in a final push to secure clearance for its proposed $44 billion acquisition of NXP Semiconductors NV , three sources told Reuters.

Headlines: Cyclone shuts Sembcorp Salalah water production plant
Description: Sembcorp Salalah Water and Power Co , which operates an electricity generation and seawater desalination plant in Oman, said its water production plant had been temporarily shut down because of rough seas as a result of a tropical storm.

Headlines: Tencent chairman pledges to advance China chip industry after ZTE 'wake-up' call: reports
Description: Tencent Holdings chairman pledged to advance China's semiconductor industry, saying the blow to ZTE Corp from Washington's ban on U.S. firms supplying telecommunications company was a "wake-up" call, local media reported.

Description: Daimler  faces an investigation of 40,000 diesel Vito vans and 80,000 C-Class model cars for possible illicit software that allowed the vehicles to emit excess pollution without detection, Bild am Sonntag reported, citing no sources.

Headlines: Oil output could return to October 2016 level, says Russia's Novak
Description: A return to the oil production levels that were in place in October 2016, baseline for the current deal to cut output, is one of the options for easing curbs, Russia's energy minister said on Saturday.

Headlines: Trump metals tariffs make Granite City great again, but at what cost?
Description: After Donald Trump was elected president in 2016 on a pledge to "Make America Great Again" and revive the country's old industrial heartland, Dave Chrusciel hoped someday to return to his previous job at the steel mill here in this southern corner of Illinois.

Headlines: Miner Grupo Mexico blames freight train derailments on 'sabotage'

Headlines: Audi CEO says diesel crisis not over and vows to stay on: report
Description: Audi Chief Executive Rupert Stadler said the diesel emissions affair was not over and promised to stay at the helm of the German luxury car maker, a German newspaper reported on Saturday.

Headlines: U.S. reaches deal to keep China's ZTE in business: congressional aide
Description: The Trump administration told lawmakers the U.S. government has reached a deal to put Chinese telecommunications company ZTE Corp back in business after it pays a significant fine and makes management changes, a senior congressional aide said on Friday.

Headlines: Tesla seeks to dismiss securities fraud lawsuit: U.S. court document

Headlines: U.S. jury fails to reach verdict in latest J&J talc trial
Description: A South Carolina jury on Friday could not agree on a verdict in a case of a woman whose family said her long-term use of Johnson & Johnson's Baby Powder led to her death from asbestos-related cancer, resulting in a mistrial.

Headlines: Mexico minister: 40 percent chance of NAFTA deal before July election
Description: There is about a 40-percent chance of concluding the renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) before Mexico's presidential election on July 1, Mexican Economy Minister Ildefonso Guajardo said on Friday.

Headlines: Canada's Trudeau raises U.S. auto import probe concerns with Trump
Description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday and raised "strong concerns" about a U.S. probe into car and truck imports that was launched this week, the prime minister's office said.

Headlines: S&P, Dow fall as oil drop hurts energy; chipmakers boost Nasdaq
Description: The S&P 500 and the Dow eased on Friday after a steep drop in oil prices pressured energy stocks, but losses were limited by gains in chipmakers and retail stocks.

Headlines: S&P 500 companies return $1 trillion to shareholders in tax-cut surge
Description: S&P 500 companies have returned a record $1 trillion to shareholders over the past year, helped by a recent surge in dividends and stock buybacks following sweeping corporate tax cuts introduced by Republicans, a report on Friday showed.

Headlines: Exclusive: Tesla flies in new battery production line for Gigafactory
Description: Tesla Inc has flown six planes full of robots and equipment from Europe to California in an unusual, high-stakes effort to speed up battery production for its Model 3 electric sedan, people familiar with the matter told Reuters this week.

Headlines: Tesla agrees to settle class action over Autopilot billed as 'safer'
Description: Tesla Inc on Thursday reached an agreement to settle a class action lawsuit with buyers of its Model S and Model X cars who alleged that the company's assisted-driving Autopilot system was "essentially unusable and demonstrably dangerous."

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler recalls 5.3 million vehicles for cruise control defect
Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV is recalling more than 5.3 million vehicles in North America over a defect that could prevent drivers from deactivating cruise control, the company said on Friday, warning owners not to use the function until they get software upgrades.

Headlines: Oil price fall hits energy shares, dollar rises
Description: Growing expectations of increased oil supply hit crude prices on Friday, lifting the U.S. dollar and weighing on energy shares, while political upheaval in Europe and uncertainty over a U.S.-North Korea summit restrained equity markets.

Headlines: Oil prices slump as OPEC and Russia consider output boost
Description: Oil prices fell more than $2 per barrel on Friday as Saudi Arabia and Russia discussed easing production cuts that have helped push crude prices to their highest since 2014.

Headlines: FBI warns Russians hacked hundreds of thousands of routers
Description: The FBI warned on Friday that Russian computer hackers had compromised hundreds of thousands of home and office routers and could collect user information or shut down network traffic.

Headlines: T-Mobile says ex-Trump campaign manager advising on Sprint merger
Description: T-Mobile US  said it is getting advice on its proposed $26 billion merger with Sprint Corp  from a lobbying firm whose staff includes several members of President Donald Trump's election team such as former campaign manager Corey Lewandowski.

Headlines: Meghan Markle makes gold sales sparkle
Description: The Meghan Markle effect has spread to yellow gold jewelry, helping boost United States sales in the first quarter of 2018 with further gains expected, jewelers said.

Headlines: Bayer cuts Monsanto synergy target by $300 million due to divestments
Description: Bayer  said positive synergy effects from the planned takeover of U.S. seeds maker Monsanto  would be about $300 million below its previous target because it will sell more businesses than initially expected to get antitrust approval.

Headlines: Tesla hires new chief financial officer for China
Description: Tesla Inc  on Friday announced a number of key executive hires including former GE and General Motors executive James Zhou as its China CFO and Neeraj Manrao, a former Apple executive, as director of energy manufacturing.

Headlines: EU states agree rules to make search engines pay for news
Description: Search engines like Google  and Microsoft's Bing  could be made to pay for showing snippets of news articles under draft copyright rules endorsed by European Union ambassadors on Friday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Total's Saft plans over 200 million euros investment in next generation battery
Description: French battery maker Saft, a unit of oil and gas major Total said on Friday it plans to invest over 200 million euros ($233 million) in a next generation European battery alliance project.

Headlines: New privacy law forces some U.S. media offline in Europe
Description: Major U.S.-media outlets including the LA Times and Chicago Tribune were forced to shutter their websites in parts of Europe on Friday following the roll out of stringent new privacy regulations by the European Union.

Description: LafargeHolcim , the world's largest cement maker, will close its head offices in Paris and Zurich, eliminating 200 jobs as part of a cost-cutting drive.

Headlines: Icahn sells some of his Herbalife shares, remains biggest investor
Description: Billionaire investor Carl Icahn, who spent years defending Herbalife Nutrition Ltd  against prominent short-seller William Ackman, said on Friday that he has sold some of his shares in the nutrition and weight loss company because the position had become too big for him.

Headlines: Nestle, under pressure, combines key R&D units
Description: Food giant Nestle plans to combine its scientific research operations into a single unit in an attempt to speed up development of new products at a time when competition from smaller rivals is intensifying.

Headlines: Half of Walmart's workforce are part-time workers: labor group
Description: Part-time workers account for half of Walmart Inc's  workforce, up from 20 percent in 2005, according to a labor group report on Friday that examined the company's increased shift away from more expensive full-time employees.

Headlines: Tax-dodge strategists probe loopholes in new U.S. law, IRS wary
Description: Tax experts for global corporations are hot on the trail of loopholes in the sweeping tax law approved in December by President Donald Trump and Republicans in the U.S. Congress.

Headlines: Leonardo shares rise on Canada helicopter fleet plans
Description: Shares in Italian aerospace and defense group Leonardo  jumped on Friday after Canada said it planned to work with the company to refurbish its fleet of search-and-rescue (SAR) helicopters.

Headlines: Daimler threatened with recall of over 600,000 diesel models: Spiegel
Description: Daimler faces a recall order for more than 600,000 diesel-engine vehicles including C-Class and G-Class models because of suspected emissions manipulation, German magazine Der Spiegel reported on Friday.

Headlines: Exclusive: China Inc tightens reins on debt, raises specter of slowdown
Description: Debt growth for Chinese companies has slowed to the lowest rate in more than a decade, according to Reuters analysis, which could provide relief for policymakers worried about the fallout from years of loose lending practices across the economy.

Headlines: Saudi minister Falih says Aramco IPO likely in 2019
Description: Saudi Arabia is most likely to hold the initial public offering (IPO) of oil giant Aramco in 2019, Energy Minister Khalid al-Falih said on Friday, confirming a delay from the initial plan to list the company this year.

Headlines: U.S. jury awards Apple $539 million in Samsung patent retrial
Description: After nearly five days of deliberations, a U.S. jury on Thursday said Samsung Electronics Co Ltd should pay $539 million to Apple Inc for copying patented smartphone features, according to court documents, bringing a years-long feud between the technology companies into its final stages.

Headlines: Siemens backs Northvolt's $5 billion Swedish battery plant
Description: Siemens  has become the latest company to contribute to the Northvolt project to build Europe's largest lithium-ion factory in northern Sweden.

Headlines: Russia's standards agency says informed about recall of 4,794 Mercedes cars
Description: Russia's standards agency said on Friday it had been informed about the voluntary recall of 4,794 Mercedes-Benz cars produced by German carmaker Daimler  and sold from 2014 to 2017.

Headlines: Mexico's Pena Nieto 'optimistic' on NAFTA as country makes new offer
Description: Mexican President Enrique Pena Nieto on Thursday expressed optimism about NAFTA talks that have been thrown into disarray by a U.S. probe exploring auto tariffs, while a source said Mexico had made a new offer to seek a deal.

Headlines: U.S. Commerce's Ross to visit China for trade talks in early June
Description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross will visit China early next month for another round of talks amid ongoing trade frictions between the world's two largest economies.

Headlines: Uber disabled emergency braking in self-driving car: U.S. agency
Description: Uber had disabled an emergency braking system in a self-driving vehicle that struck and killed a woman in Arizona in March even though the car had identified the need to apply the brakes, the National Transportation Safety Board said in a preliminary report released on Thursday.

Headlines: Google tries to ease tensions on eve of new EU privacy law
Description: Alphabet Inc's Google sought to ease online publisher concerns on Thursday about the effects European data privacy rules going into effect in just a few hours will have on their ad business.

Headlines: Stock market value of Netflix eclipses Disney for first time
Description: Netflix's  stock market value ballooned to a record $153 billion on Thursday and eclipsed Walt Disney Co  for the first time, making it the world's most valuable entertainment company, following a monumental shift by viewers away from cinemas and cable television.

Headlines: Oil slips further below $80/bbl on talk OPEC may lift output
Description: Oil prices fell about $1 on Thursday, with expectations building that reduced supplies from Venezuela and Iran could prompt OPEC to wind down output cuts in place since the start of 2017.

Headlines: Wall Street dips after Trump cancels North Korea summit; Netflix gains
Description: U.S. stocks ended down slightly on Thursday after President Donald Trump canceled a planned summit with North Korea's Kim Jong Un and threatened to impose tariffs on auto imports, though losses were limited by gains in Netflix and General Electric.

Headlines: Pfizer to pay $23.85 million to settle U.S. co-payment kickback probe
Description: Pfizer Inc  agreed to pay $23.85 million to resolve U.S. charges that it used a purportedly independent charity to pay illegal kickbacks to Medicare patients, covering their out-of-pocket costs for its prescription drugs.

Headlines: Nixed U.S.-North Korea meeting, trade fears sink global shares
Description: Shares sank worldwide on Thursday as U.S. President Donald Trump canceled a planned June meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, while tariff fears hit auto stocks and safety buying ramped up.

Headlines: Tesla's Musk bashes media, proposes credibility check

Headlines: U.S. launches auto import probe, China says will defend interests
Description: The Trump administration has launched a national security investigation into car and truck imports that could lead to new U.S. tariffs similar to those imposed on imported steel and aluminum in March.

Headlines: Factbox: Big U.S. auto dealers have significant import exposure
Description: Several U.S. auto dealers derive a significant portion of their revenue from imported vehicles, which could be affected if tariffs are imposed on auto imports.

Headlines: J&J must pay $4 million in punitive damages in latest asbestos cancer trial

Headlines: Deutsche Bank axes at least 7,000 jobs in trading retreat
Description: Deutsche Bank  is slashing more than 7,000 jobs to cut costs and restore profitability, while keeping its international reach as its new CEO seeks to reassure investors and clients.

Headlines: Facebook launches searchable archive of U.S. political ads
Description: Facebook Inc  on Thursday launched an archive of U.S. political ads that appear on the world's largest social network, showing who paid for them and other details, after an outcry over Russians' alleged purchase of such ads during the 2016 elections.

Headlines: Electric vehicles seen driving cobalt crunch by mid-2020s
Description: The increasing popularity of electric vehicles may create a crunch for supplies of cobalt in the early-to-mid 2020s, miners and analysts say, adding that small operators trying to start up mines outside Africa could play a bigger role over time in satisfying demand for the metal used in rechargeable batteries.

Headlines: Olympics: Taxi! Tokyo tackles tourist boom with accessible cab
Description: Tokyo's taxi industry is undergoing some radical changes as Japan, already dealing with unprecedented levels of tourism, gears up to host two major sporting events in the next 26 months.

Headlines: Tight supply weighs on U.S. home sales; job market strengthening
Description: U.S. home sales tumbled in April as an acute shortage of properties limited choices for potential buyers, the latest sign that the housing market was struggling to regain momentum.

Headlines: UAW accuses Musk of threatening Tesla workers over unionization
Description: The United Auto Workers union (UAW) has filed a complaint accusing Tesla Inc Chief Executive Elon Musk of illegally threatening to take away benefits from workers who join the union.

Headlines: U.S. auto import probe fans tariff fears, riles Asia, Europe
Description: A U.S. threat that it may introduce tariffs on foreign auto imports drew strong criticism on Thursday from the country's main business lobbying group, which warned of a "staggering" blow to the industry and the prospect of a global trade war.

Headlines: Merkel woos China as Trump poses new trade challenge
Description: China said on Thursday it would "open its door wider" to German businesses, giving a warm reception to visiting Chancellor Angela Merkel, who has wooed Beijing to counterbalance trade threats from U.S. President Donald Trump.

Headlines: Republicans in Congress slam Trump probe of auto imports
Description: Some of President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans in the U.S. Congress said on Thursday that his administration's national security investigation of car and truck imports amid a trade spat with China is being pursued under false pretenses and could hurt U.S. consumers.

Description: Shares of General Motors  and Ford  inched only marginally higher before the bell on Thursday after the Trump administration launched a national security probe into car imports which could lead to new tariffs on foreign competitors while also stirring trade tensions.

Headlines: Fashion and sport brands clash in luxury sneakers race
Description: What do you get when luxury fashion meets sport? $10,000 sneakers.

Headlines: Kroger's meal kit deal reheats Blue Apron shares
Description: Shares of Blue Apron  climbed on Thursday after Kroger said it was buying Home Chef to broaden its menu in the home meal kit market while stock of Calavo Growers, whose unit partnered with Kroger on another meal kit service, slumped.

Headlines: Sanctions-hit tycoon Deripaska asks Kremlin to buy some of his aluminium: source
Description: Russian aluminium producer Rusal has asked the Russian government to purchase some of its output, a government source said on Thursday, in an effort to alleviate the pain inflicted by U.S. sanctions.

Headlines: German regulator orders recall of Daimler diesel van
Description: Germany's road vehicle authority ordered Daimler  on Thursday to recall its Mercedes van model Vito 1.6l Diesel Euro 6, saying engine control features to reduce exhaust emissions were in breach of regulations.

Headlines: Tariffs on auto imports could hurt U.S. jobs, raise consumer costs: Toyota
Description: Japanese automaker Toyota Motor Corp  said on Thursday that imposing tariffs on imported vehicles "could hurt American jobs" and boost consumer costs.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank mistakenly transferred $24 billion in 2014
Description: Deutsche Bank  erroneously transferred 21 billion euros ($24.62 billion) to Macquarie  in 2014,  a spokesman said on Thursday, the latest such error to come to light.

Headlines: Oleg Deripaska asks Russian state to buy aluminum from Rusal: government source
Description: Russian tycoon Oleg Deripaska, major shareholder in aluminum producer Rusal, has asked the Russian government to start state purchases of aluminum from Rusal, a senior Russian government source said on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. Senate finance committee chairman blasts possible auto tariffs
Description: The chairman of the U.S. Senate Finance Committee on Thursday criticized the Commerce Department's decision to potentially levy tariffs on imports of automobiles, trucks and automotive parts, calling it "deeply misguided."

Headlines: About $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen since 2017: cybercrime group
Description: Criminals have stolen about $1.2 billion in cryptocurrencies since the beginning of 2017, as bitcoin's popularity and the emergence of more than 1,500 digital tokens have put the spotlight on the unregulated sector, according to estimates from the Anti-Phishing Working Group released on Thursday.

Headlines: Indian state seeks permanent closure of Vedanta's copper smelter: officials
Description: India's Tamil Nadu state said on Thursday that it was seeking a permanent closure of a big copper smelter run by London-listed Vedanta Resources  after 13 people died in protests demanding the closure of the plant on environmental grounds.

Headlines: Uber will soon detail plan to stop using diesel cars in London
Description: Uber [UBER.UL] said it will provide more information in the coming weeks on how it plans to stop diesel using cars in London and of a proposed scrappage scheme, as the court date nears for the taxi app to defend its right to operate in London nears.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank's chairman defends abrupt change in CEO
Description: Deutsche Bank  chairman Paul Achleitner on Thursday defended his decision to abruptly change top management last month.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank says revenue environment in second quarter remains challenging
Description: Deutsche Bank's  new chief executive, Christian Sewing, said generating revenue continues to be a challenge in the current quarter, especially for the investment bank.

Headlines: U.S. could seek American compliance officers at ZTE: Ross
Description: The United States has not made a final decision on changes to its ban on ZTE Corp , but any alternative remedy could include installing U.S. compliance officers at the Chinese telecoms company, Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross said on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. launches criminal probe into bitcoin price manipulation: Bloomberg
Description: The U.S. Department of Justice has launched a criminal probe into whether traders are manipulating the price of bitcoin and other digital currencies, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

Headlines: BNP Paribas CEO rules out big deals when asked about Deutsche Bank
Description: BNP Paribas  chief executive Jean-Laurent Bonnafe effectively ruled out a tie-up with struggling German rival Deutsche Bank  on Thursday, saying the French lender is not considering any large takeovers or mergers.

Headlines: U.S. auto import probe borders on 'provocation': Germany's DIHK
Description: A U.S. decision to launch a national security investigation into car imports marks a further low point in business ties with Europe and will hit both manufacturers and consumers, Germany's DIHK Chambers of Industries and Commerce said on Thursday.

Headlines: General Electric's power unit fights for growth as wind, solar gain
Description: Vistra Energy Corp  and Dominion Energy Inc  – which serve about 5.5 million electricity customers in more than a dozen U.S. states – both say they are done building combined-cycle natural gas-fired power plants.

Headlines: EU parliament gets Facebook answers after Zuckerberg meeting
Description: The European Parliament distributed on Thursday what it called a first set of written replies from Facebook to oral questions put by lawmakers to CEO Mark Zuckerberg at a meeting in Brussels on Tuesday.

Headlines: UK's Sainsbury's tweaks pay proposals after staff pressure
Description: Sainsbury's , Britain's second largest supermarket group, has bowed to pressure from employees and trade unions by changing some of the pay proposals it detailed in March as part of a move to simplify the company's wage structure.

Headlines: China's Premier Li says China and Germany uphold free trade
Description: China's Premier Li Keqiang said on Thursday China has always supported a unified and prosperous Europe and that China and Germany uphold free trade.

Headlines: Investor Elliott's stake raises pressure on Thyssenkrupp CEO
Description: Activist hedge fund Elliott said on Thursday it would step up  pressure on Thyssenkrupp's  leadership to revive the German industrial conglomerate's fortunes, confirming it had taken a stake of less than 3 percent.

Headlines: Procter & Gamble commits to Russia despite rising risks
Description: U.S. consumer goods group Procter & Gamble (P&G)  will keep investing in Russian plants in 2018 and beyond, reaffirming its commitment to the market despite political risks.

Headlines: Toyota to ramp up hydrogen fuel cell vehicle sales around 2020
Description: Toyota Motor Corp  on Thursday said it plans to set up a  facility to mass manufacture hydrogen fuel cell stacks, a key component of fuel cell vehicles, as it seeks to ramp up production of hydrogen-powered cars and expand their usage as a zero-emission alternative to gasoline vehicles.

Headlines: EU competition chief Vestager to announce antitrust decision on Thursday
Description: European Commissioner for Competition Margrethe Vestager will hold a news conference on Thursday to announce an antitrust decision, which is expected to be on Gazprom .

Headlines: Qantas says has been given more time to clarify description of Chinese territories
Description: Australian airline Qantas Airways  said on Thursday that it has been given more time to clarify how it refers to Chinese territories on its website, as a deadline set by Chinese authorities approaches.

Headlines: Deadly protests land a blow to Indian resources magnate Agarwal's ambitions
Description: Indian billionaire Anil Agarwal often talks about his dream to turn his London-listed company Vedanta Resources into a global resources giant. He has already bought stakes in big mining companies, such as Anglo American Plc, and says he plans to spend at least $1 billion on investments in Africa.

Headlines: Trump urges a new 'structure' for U.S.-China trade deal
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump has signaled a new direction in U.S.-China trade talks and said any deal would need "a different structure," fueling uncertainty over current negotiations.

Headlines: China says has good potential in cooperation with Germany in new energy cars, AI
Description: China's commerce ministry said on Thursday that the nation has good potential in cooperation with Germany in sectors such as digitalization, new energy cars, artificial intelligence and driverless cars.

Headlines: China says hopes to work with Japan, South Korea on FTA as soon as possible
Description: China hopes to work with Japan and South Korea to reach a mutually beneficial free trade agreement as soon as possible, the Chinese commerce ministry's spokesman said on Thursday.

Headlines: China says has not promised to cut trade surplus with U.S. by a certain amount
Description: China's Commerce Ministry said on Thursday that it had not pledged to cut the country's trade surplus with the United States by a certain figure, and hopes the United States implements measures promised during trade negotiations as soon as possible.

Headlines: China fines Muji for packaging that lists Taiwan as a country
Description: Japanese retailer Muji has been fined 200,000 yuan (23,445 pounds) in Shanghai for using packaging that lists Taiwan as a country, underscoring China's growing sensitivity to how companies refer to the self-ruled island.

Headlines: United Air CEO grilled over NRA discount, workers rights at annual meeting
Description: United Airlines executives faced questions about ending its discount for a gun rights group and how it treats its workers at the carrier's annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday.

Headlines: Why Caterpillar can't keep up with a boom in demand
Description: Orders for the mining machines and construction bulldozers made at this sprawling Caterpillar Inc.  factory in central Illinois have jumped, in general, three-fold over the past year.

Headlines: Uber shuts Arizona self-driving program two months after fatal crash
Description: Uber has shut down its self-driving car operation in Arizona two months after a fatal crash involving one of its vehicles, the company said on Wednesday.

Headlines: U.S. Commerce Dept will probe whether auto imports hurt national security
Description: The U.S. Commerce Department said on Wednesday it will open a so-called Section 232 investigation into whether imports of vehicles and auto parts harm national security.

Headlines: Comcast prepares to top Disney's $50 billion offer for Fox
Description: Comcast Corp  confirmed on Wednesday it was preparing a higher, all-cash offer for most of the media assets of Twenty-First Century Fox , setting up a bidding war with rival Walt Disney Co , which already has agreed to a $52-billion deal with Fox.

Headlines: J&J hit with $21.7 million verdict in another talc asbestos cancer case
Description: Johnson & Johnson  and its talc suppliers on Wednesday were hit with a $21.7 million jury verdict in a lawsuit by a woman who said she developed cancer after being exposed to asbestos in the company's Baby Powder.

Headlines: Wall Street dominance over Europe's struggling banks hits record
Description: Wall Street's dominance over struggling European banks has reached record levels as U.S. firms reap the benefits of booming markets at home, while their transatlantic rivals are trapped in endless restructurings, data showed on Thursday.

Headlines: Starbucks calls anti-bias training part of 'long-term journey'
Description: Starbucks Corp  on Wednesday revealed details of the employee anti-bias training program that will take place behind closed doors at 8,000 U.S. company-owned cafes on the afternoon of May 29.

Headlines: Uber trims losses and grows business, plans new stock sale
Description: Uber cut its losses almost in half and its ride bookings jumped 51 percent since one year ago, the Silicon Valley ride-services firm said on Wednesday, showing that months of scandal and retreating from overseas markets have not slowed its business.

Headlines: Ackman makes roughly $1 billion bet on Lowe's
Description: Billionaire investor William Ackman said on Wednesday that his hedge fund had taken a roughly $1 billion stake in Lowe's , revealing his third large investment this year.

Headlines: Trump mulling probe of auto imports on national security grounds
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump is considering launching a trade investigation of auto imports on national security grounds, a senior Trump administration official said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Wall St. ends up as Fed seen keeping gradual approach to rate hikes
Description: U.S. stocks ended with small gains on Wednesday after minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting suggested higher inflation may not result in faster interest rate hikes.

Headlines: Macron tells global tech CEOs: 'There is no free lunch'
Description: French President Emmanuel Macron told executives from the world's biggest technology firms that he believed in innovation but that he wanted tougher regulations and for them to contribute more to society.

Headlines: Trump administration weighs new tariffs on imported vehicles: WSJ
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration is weighing a plan that would impose new tariffs on imported vehicles on national security grounds, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

Headlines: Tesla shares seen rising despite 'fever pitch' of bad news: analyst
Description: Negative news stories about Tesla Inc have hit "fever pitch", but the electric carmaker's stock price is likely to surge as output of its Model 3 sedan improves, according to an analyst research report.

Headlines: Equities pare losses, dollar gains cut after Fed minutes amid U.S.-China trade concerns
Description: Global stock markets pared losses and the dollar cut gains on Wednesday after the release of minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's May 1-2 meeting amid heightened concerns that setbacks to U.S.-China trade talks would undermine world economic growth.

Headlines: China signals to state giants: 'Buy American' oil and grains
Description: China will import record volumes of U.S. oil and is likely to ship more U.S. soy after Beijing signalled to state-run refiners and grains purchasers they should buy more to help ease tensions between the two top economies, trade sources said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Oil falls on shock U.S. stock builds, OPEC supply worries
Description: Oil benchmarks fell on Wednesday after an unexpected build in U.S. crude and gasoline inventories despite strong demand, and as traders weighed a possible increase in OPEC crude output to cover any shortfalls in supply from Iran and Venezuela.

Headlines: GE cannot guarantee dividend, still fixing some units, CEO says
Description: General Electric Co  cannot guarantee its 2019 dividend and is still fixing its power and capital units, Chief Executive John Flannery said on Wednesday, sending the industrial conglomerate's stock down nearly 8 percent.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank looks to cut 10,000 jobs to reduce costs: source
Description: Deutsche Bank  plans to cut 10,000 jobs, or about a tenth of its global workforce, as part of efforts to reduce costs, a person with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp CEO feels heat after investor vote of no confidence
Description: Heinrich Hiesinger's position as Thyssenkrupp's CEO is more precarious than it has ever been as he prepares to unveil a new strategy to placate impatient investors, including Cevian and Elliott, people familiar with the matter said.

Headlines: Target's profit miss overshadows sales growth, shares tumble
Description: Target Corp's  first-quarter profit came in below analyst estimates as price cuts, higher wages and investments in its online business ate into margins, sending shares down 5 percent in afternoon trade on Wednesday.

Headlines: UPS hits customers with new fees for oversized packages
Description: United Parcel Service Inc  will begin charging an extra $150 next month to handle oversized packages and pallets, along with a new charge for packages with mislabeled dimensions, the company said on Wednesday.

Headlines: China's Sinopec to boost U.S. crude imports to all-time high: sources
Description: Sinopec, Asia's largest refiner, will boost U.S. crude oil imports to an all-time high as China tries to reduce its trade deficit with the United States, two sources with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: U.S. Senate panel to hold hearing on Sprint T-Mobile merger
Description: A U.S. Senate committee plans to hold a hearing on June 27 on the proposed $26.5 billion merger of U.S. wireless carriers T-Mobile US  and Sprint Corp .

Headlines: Facebook users unite! 'Data Labour Union' launches in Netherlands
Description: Activists in Amsterdam on Wednesday launched the 'Datavakbond' or "data labor union", which hopes to elect leaders to negotiate directly with Facebook and Google over what they do with users' data.

Headlines: India court halts expansion of Vedanta's copper smelter after protest killings
Description: One person died and others were wounded by gunfire in southern India on Wednesday in fresh violence related to protesters' demands that a copper smelter be shut on environmental grounds. The day before at least ten people were killed by police during a mass demonstration against the plant.

Headlines: UK's Vedanta core profit, revenue beat; says working to restart Indian plant
Description: British mining and energy conglomerate Vedanta Resources Plc reported better-than-expected growth in full-year core profit and revenue on Wednesday, driven by stronger commodity prices.

Headlines: Consumer groups ask U.S. agency to probe Tesla 'Autopilot' ads
Description: Two U.S. consumer advocacy groups urged the Federal Trade Commission on Wednesday to investigate what they called Tesla Inc's "deceptive and misleading" use of the name Autopilot for its assisted-driving technology.

Headlines: Trump floats management changes instead of sanctions for China's ZTE
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday floated a plan to fine ZTE Corp   and shake up its management as his administration considered rolling back more severe penalties that have crippled the Chinese telecommunications company.

Headlines: Pompeo says no final decision made yet on China's ZTE
Description: No decision has been made by the Trump administration over removing a ban on Chinese telecoms firm ZTE Corp, U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Wednesday during congressional testimony.

Headlines: Tesla Model 3 registrations zip past rivals in California
Description: Tesla Inc's Model 3 sedan recorded more registrations in California than its class rivals BMW 3-Series and Mercedes C-Class in the first quarter, according to a report by the California New Car Dealers Association (CNCDA). Model 3 registrations totaled 3,723, or 14.3 percent of the near-luxury segment, compared with 3,323 for the Mercedes variant and 3,260 for the BMW model, the CNCDA report said.

Headlines: German cabinet agrees compensation for utilities due to nuclear exit
Description: Chancellor Angela Merkel's cabinet agreed on Wednesday to grant compensation of up to 1 billion euros to utilities for income lost due to Germany's planned phasing out of nuclear power, the environment ministry said.

Headlines: Small banks trump Wall Street on Dodd-Frank rewrite
Description: Congress on Tuesday rolled back some of the restraints imposed on banks after the 2007-2009 global financial crisis, but big players like Goldman Sachs Group Inc , Morgan Stanley  and JPMorgan Chase & Co , will not be breaking out the champagne.

Headlines: Uber widens health cover in Europe as new CEO meets France's Macron
Description: Uber plans to offer all its European drivers an upgraded version of the health insurance it already provides in France in a drive to attract independent workers and fend off criticism over their treatment.

Headlines: IBM announces new hiring in France as CEOs meet Macron
Description: IBM  announced new recruitment in France before a meeting between President Emmanuel Macron and the bosses of IBM and Microsoft .

Headlines: Tesla trims up to $14,000 off Model X in China after tariff cuts
Description: Tesla Inc has slashed up to $14,000 off its Model X in China after Beijing announced major tariff cuts for imported automobiles, a potential sales boost for the U.S. firm as the world's largest auto market pivots towards electric cars.

Headlines: Alitalia nationalisation would be tricky, sale process must go on: minister
Description: Italy should not push to nationalise insolvent airline Alitalia and the government should not drop the sale process that already attracted interest from other carriers, Industry Minister Carlo Calenda said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Russia's VTB Bank says no longer lending to Deripaska: CNBC
Description: VTB , Russia's second-largest bank, has stopped lending to sanctioned Russian metals tycoon Oleg Deripaska, VTB's President Andrei Kostin told CNBC in an interview released on Wednesday.

Headlines: Staff reject Macron rail reform in 'referendum', unions say
Description: Workers at France's state-owned SNCF rail company on Wednesday resoundingly rejected President Emmanuel Macron's planned overhaul of the railways in an internal ballot organized by labor unions.

Headlines: France's rail unions say workers overwhelmingly vote against reforms
Description: France's hardline CGT union on Wednesday said 95 percent of all rail workers who voted in an internal referendum on President Emmanuel Macron's proposed reform of the SNCF voted against the plan.

Headlines: Wynn shareholders reject executive compensation plan
Description: Shareholders of casino operator Wynn Resorts Ltd  voted against the company's executive compensation plan at its annual meeting last week, Wynn said in a regulatory filing late on Tuesday.

Headlines: China's ZTE estimates at least $3.1 billion loss from U.S. sanctions: Bloomberg
Description: China's ZTE Corp is estimating losses of at least 20 billion yuan ($3.1 billion) due to Washington's ban on U.S. firms supplying the telecommunications firm, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources.

Headlines: Consumer Reports to retest Tesla Model 3 after brake fix
Description: Consumer Reports said Tuesday it will retest brakes on Tesla Inc's new Model 3 sedans after Chief Executive Elon Musk promised a software update, but the potential hit to sales from the magazine's negative review weighed on Tesla shares.

Headlines: Clarks shoes made in Britain after 12-year hiatus
Description: Clarks, the British shoemaker and retailer, will return to large-scale manufacturing in the UK for the first time in over a decade when a new factory in southwest England joins plants in Vietnam and India in making its iconic Desert Boot.

Headlines: EU's Malmstrom says thinks U.S. considers EU trade proposal insufficient
Description: A proposal to get exemption from U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum and promises of closer trade ties may not be sufficient to convince the United States government, EU trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmstrom said on Tuesday.

Headlines: EU doubts if offer can prevent Trump tariffs or steel caps
Description: European Union proposals to open its markets wider to U.S. products, including cars, appear not to have persuaded Washington to lift the threat of import tariffs on EU steel and aluminium, the bloc's trade chief said on Tuesday.

Headlines: EU must push hard to secure U.S. tariff exemption: Altmaier
Description: German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday it was unclear whether Europe's appeal to the United States to be exempt from import tariffs on steel and aluminum would succeed, but the bloc would push as hard as possible in the coming days.

Headlines: Workers hit McDonald's with new sexual harassment claims
Description: Ten women who work at McDonald's restaurants in Detroit, Chicago, Los Angeles and six other cities have filed sexual harassment complaints in the past few days with the federal government against the company and its franchisees, which they said ignored or retaliated against them for such complaints.

Headlines: Wall St. slips on U.S.-China trade talk uncertainty; energy falls
Description: U.S. stocks ended lower on Tuesday, weighed down by lingering uncertainty over the outcome of trade talks between the United States and China and declines in energy and industrial shares.

Headlines: Facebook face-off: EU gets little news from Zuckerberg
Description: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg sailed through a grilling from EU lawmakers about the social network's data policies as  lengthy questions left the 34-year-old American little time to answer.

Headlines: OPEC may decide to ease oil supply curbs in June: sources
Description: OPEC may decide to raise oil output as soon as June due to worries over Iranian and Venezuelan supply and after Washington raised concerns the oil rally was going too far, OPEC and oil industry sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters.

Headlines: Wall St. dips on latest U.S.-China comments, European shares rally
Description: Global stock markets tipped downward on Tuesday as Wall Street investors locked in recent gains while taking a cautious view of fresh U.S.-China comments even as European shares approached four-month peaks and China moved to further open up its economy.

Headlines: Ex-Valeant, Philidor executives convicted of kickback scheme
Description: A former Valeant Pharmaceuticals International Inc  executive and the former chief of mail order pharmacy Philidor Rx Services were found guilty on Tuesday of defrauding Valeant through a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme.

Headlines: Civil rights groups warn Amazon about govt use of facial recognition
Description: U.S. civil liberties groups on Tuesday called on Amazon.com Inc to stop offering facial recognition services to governments, warning that the software could be used to target immigrants and people of color unfairly.

Headlines: GE stock recovers from lows as key CEO presentation nears
Description: A year ago, Jeff Immelt told investors at an industry conference there was a "mismatch" between the performance of company he led, General Electric Co , and its stock price.

Headlines: Canada says top NAFTA officials in constant contact on trade talks
Description: Top U.S., Canadian and Mexican officials are in constant contact about slow-moving talks to revitalize NAFTA and are ready to meet at any time to push the process forwards, Canada's foreign minister said on Tuesday.

Headlines: In bipartisan effort, two U.S. lawmakers ask Trump to be tough on ZTE
Description: Two U.S. lawmakers, including the Republican chairman of a powerful House of Representatives committee, asked President Donald Trump on Tuesday not to lift penalties on Chinese telecommunications company ZTE Corp .

Headlines: Exclusive: GE seeking to shed troubled insurance business - sources
Description: General Electric Co  is working with investment bankers to find ways to shed its insurance business, which has caused it to book hefty charges while sparking shareholder lawsuits and an investigation by U.S. regulators, people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Facebook not done enough to prevent misuse: Zuckerberg
Description: Facebook Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg apologized to EU lawmakers on Tuesday, saying the company had not done enough to prevent misuse of the social network and that regulation is "important and inevitable".

Headlines: Highlights: Facebook's Zuckerberg faces EU Parliament grilling
Description: Facebook Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg apologized to the European Parliament on Tuesday for a massive data leak, his latest attempt to draw a line under a scandal that has rocked the world's biggest social media network.

Headlines: China, U.S. near deal on ZTE reprieve; Beijing cuts auto tariffs
Description: Washington neared a deal to lift its ban on U.S. firms supplying Chinese telecoms gear maker ZTE Corp, sources said on Tuesday, and Beijing announced tariff cuts on car imports, further easing trade tensions between the world's two largest economies.

Headlines: Americans report stronger finances in Trump's first year: Federal Reserve
Description: The share of Americans who report they are doing "at least okay" financially rose in President Donald Trump's first year in office, according to Federal Reserve data published on Tuesday.

Headlines: Treasury chief says any ZTE penalty changes won't hurt security
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Tuesday that any changes to stiff Commerce Department penalties on Chinese telecommunications equipment maker ZTE Corp will ensure that U.S. national security is maintained and sanctions are enforced.

Headlines: Facebook director to start after annual meeting, avoid shareholder vote
Description: Facebook Inc named a new director this month and timed his appointment to avoid a shareholder vote, raising concern among some investors who want to see more accountability from the social media company.

Headlines: Russia's Shuvalov picked to head state development bank VEB: sources
Description: Igor Shuvalov, the former first deputy prime minister, has been selected to head Russian state development bank VEB, three sources told Reuters, although they said it was not clear if final documentation for the move had been signed.

Headlines: J.C. Penney CEO Ellison jumps ship to Lowe's; shares sink
Description: J.C. Penney's  Chief Executive Officer Marvin Ellison is leaving the struggling retailer to join home improvement chain Lowe's Cos Inc , the companies said on Tuesday, sending shares in the U.S. department store chain down as much as 8 percent to an all-time low.

Headlines: Trump says there is no deal with China to lift ban on ZTE Corp
Description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday said there is no deal with China on ZTE Corp, as lawmakers from both parties worked to block him from easing penalties on the Chinese telecommunications company.

Headlines: BP to cut 3 percent of upstream jobs by year-end
Description: British oil giant BP Plc said it plans to cut 3 percent of jobs in exploration and production, as part of a restructuring of its global upstream business to make the division more efficient and competitive.

Headlines: Japan, Russia, Turkey bring potential U.S. tariff retaliation to $3.5 billion
Description: Japan, Russia and Turkey have warned the United States about potential retaliation for its tariffs on steel and aluminum, the World Trade Organization said on Tuesday, bringing the total U.S. tariff bill to around $3.5 billion annually.

Headlines: Tesco closure of non-food website puts 500 jobs at risk
Description: Tesco , Britain's biggest retailer, said on Tuesday it will close its non-food website Tesco Direct in July, having decided it could not make the loss-making business profitable.

Headlines: Sony in $2.3 billion deal for EMI, becomes world's biggest music publisher
Description: Sony Corp  said on Tuesday it would pay about $2.3 billion to gain control of EMI, becoming the world's largest music publisher in an industry that has found new life on the back of streaming services.

Headlines: U.S. Senate's top Democrat warns on relaxation of U.S. sales ban on ZTE
Description: The top Democrat in the U.S. Senate on Tuesday warned against relaxing a U.S. order banning American companies from supplying Chinese telecommunications firm ZTE Corp, saying it would be a capitulation to Beijing by the Trump administration.

Headlines: EU antitrust official sees more scrutiny for Facebook, others
Description: Facebook and other tech giants may attract more regulatory scrutiny in future because of their market power, a senior EU antitrust official said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Airbus says obeying WTO subsidy verdict as sanctions loom
Description: Airbus  said on Tuesday it had taken steps to comply with a World Trade Organization (WTO) ruling on subsidies for its A350 and A380 jets, which has seen the United States and Europe trade legal blows on behalf of Boeing  and Airbus.

Headlines: Airbus confirms amendments to comply with WTO over subsidies
Description: European planemaker Airbus  said on Tuesday that the company - along with France, Germany, Spain and the UK - had made some changes regarding loans for the A380 and A350XWB planes to comply with the World Trade Organization (WTO).

Headlines: Germany says up to U.S. to avoid damaging trade row escalation
Description: The European Union has reached out to the United States to talk about strengthening free and fair trade within the framework of the World Trade Organisation and it is up to Washington to respond, Germany's economy minister said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Activists turn tables on companies as EU privacy law comes in
Description: Big companies are used to harvesting vast amounts of data from customers to find out what makes them tick. Now, as Europe's new data protection law comes into effect this week, activists are looking to turn the tables.

Headlines: European shares eye four-month high, Italy sell-off relents
Description: European shares inched toward four-month highs on Tuesday, as an easing of pressure on Italy's debt markets coincided with China's latest move to open up its giant economy to the rest of the world.

Headlines: Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi VC invests first $50 million in startups
Description: The Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi alliance's new venture capital fund has agreed five investments in four months totaling $50 million and will present another to its supervisory board next week, the fund's head said.

Headlines: Shell shareholders adopt CEO pay by 75 percent majority
Description: Royal Dutch Shell  shareholders on Tuesday approved the 2017 management remuneration, including Chief Executive Officer Ben van Beurden's 8.9 million euro ($10.51 million) package, by a majority of 75 percent.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank chairman Achleitner to feel investor ire
Description: Deutsche Bank  investors, fed up with a languishing share price and dwindling revenue, will call on its leaders to deliver quicker results at this week's annual general meeting.

Headlines: U.S. farmers plow ahead with plantings as China trade war fears ebb
Description: U.S. farmers said they would push ahead with plantings planned before U.S.-China trade tensions eased and, now that the two countries have resumed talks, take a wait-and-see approach to President Donald Trump's promises for more sales to China.

Headlines: Lufthansa to offer Economy 'Light' fare on North American routes
Description: Lufthansa  will introduce an Economy "Light" fare on transatlantic routes this summer, the German airlines group said on Tuesday, following a similar move by rival British Airways in an effort to compete with low-cost carriers.

Headlines: Rio Tinto presses Mongolia to shore up copper investment
Description: Rio Tinto on Tuesday called on the Mongolian government to honor the contracts that underpin its Oyu Tolgoi copper project and said the mining world was watching, as anxiety mounts after a series of high-profile arrests.

Headlines: AccorHotels to decide on Huazhu board seat after Huazhu buys stake in company
Description: AccorHotels  said on Tuesday it will decide in the coming weeks whether to grant Huazhu Hotels  a board seat after the Chinese hospitality group bought 4.5 percent of its capital.

Headlines: Uber pulls up in Japan with taxi-hailing service
Description: Uber Technologies plans to launch its first taxi-hailing pilot service in Japan that will connect passengers to other taxi providers, as it seeks to expand in the country where the U.S. firm has been blocked from setting up its own fleet of drivers.

Headlines: VW recalls 11,000 Audi cars in Russia: watchdog
Description: Russia's standards agency said on Tuesday it had been informed about the voluntary recall of 11,003 Audi  cars sold since last year.

Headlines: LaSalle Hotel accepts Blackstone's $3.7 billion cash offer
Description: (This story corrects paragraph 9 to remove wrong reference to La Salle owning 'W' Los Angeles in May 21 story.)

Headlines: Beer maker AB InBev pumps up the volume in Africa
Description: By Tiisetso Motsoeneng, Philip Blenkinsop and Martinne Geller

Headlines: As Zuckerberg heads to Brussels, British lawmakers ask for answers
Description: British lawmakers want their European counterparts to quiz Facebook FB.O CEO Mark Zuckerberg about a scandal over improper use of millions of Facebook users' data, as he will not give evidence in London himself.

Headlines: Boeing technicians in South Carolina to vote on unionization: WSJ
Description: Some Boeing Co  workers at the planemaker' s factory in South Carolina will vote on union representation later this month, the Wall Street Journal reported https://on.wsj.com/2xav6Px on Monday, citing U.S. labor regulators.

Headlines: Exclusive: Ousted MGM CEO explores bid for the U.S. movie studio - sources
Description: Former MGM Holdings Inc  Chief Executive Officer Gary Barber,  who was ousted earlier this year, is speaking to investment banks about financing an offer to acquire the privately held U.S. movie studio, five people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. DOJ says pursuing investigations related to Malaysia's 1MDB
Description: The U.S Department of Justice said on Tuesday it would continue to pursue investigations into 1 Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and looked forward to working with Malaysian law enforcement authorities, which have reopened a probe into the fund following a change of government this month.

Headlines: Trade war fears ebb as U.S., China agree to continue talks
Description: Washington and Beijing both claimed victory on Monday as the world's two largest economies stepped back from the brink of a global trade war and agreed to hold further talks to boost U.S. exports to China.

Headlines: Tesla Model 3 fails to get Consumer Reports nod due to 'big flaws'
Description: Influential U.S. magazine Consumer Reports will not recommend Tesla Inc's  Model 3 sedan, saying on Monday it braked slower than a full-sized pickup truck, taking the shine off a day of gains for shares in Elon Musk's electric car company.

Headlines: U.S. commodity exports to China to rise amid trade talks, but volumes are capped
Description: China has pledged to buy more U.S. goods to reduce America's huge trade deficit and help avoid exacerbating a trade war between the world's two biggest economies, with energy and commodities high on Washington's list of products for sale.

Headlines: U.S. Treasury says updates Trump on Chinese investment concerns
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin has given President Donald Trump an update on Treasury's efforts to address concerns about Chinese investments in the United States, a Treasury spokeswoman said on Monday.

Headlines: GE to merge transportation unit with Wabtec in $11.1 billion deal
Description: General Electric Co  announced a $11.1 billion deal on Monday to merge its transportation business with U.S. rail equipment manufacturer Wabtec Corp , with GE and its shareholders owning just over half of the combined business.

Headlines: Wall St. rises on trade war truce; industrials lead
Description: U.S. stocks rose on Monday and gains in industrials helped propel the Dow to a more than two-month closing high, after a truce between the United States and China calmed fears that a trade war might be imminent.

Headlines: Companies win big at U.S. top court on worker class-action curbs
Description: The U.S. Supreme Court delivered a blow to the rights of workers on Monday by allowing companies to require them to sign away their ability to bring class-action claims against management, agreements already in place for about 25 million employees.

Headlines: France to absorb 35 billion euros rail operator SNCF debt: Les Echos
Description: The French government plans to absorb about 35 billion euros ($41.20 billion) of national railway operator SNCF's  debt burden of around 47 billion euros as part of planned reforms to SNCF, French business daily Les Echos said on Monday.

Headlines: Rising oil prices help ground U.S. airline stocks; could make them cheap
Description: Shares of U.S. airlines have been depressed by rising oil prices this year, but their descent to relatively cheap levels could position them for takeoff.

Headlines: Fifth Third Bancorp pays $4.7 billion for MB Financial's Chicago muscle
Description: U.S. regional bank Fifth Third Bancorp  has agreed to buy smaller rival MB Financial Inc  in a stock-and-cash deal valued at about $4.7 billion, as it looks to expand in Chicago and broaden its middle market customer base.

Headlines: U.S. and Canadian regulators open probes into cryptocurrency scams
Description: U.S. and Canadian state securities regulators announced Monday they have launched dozens of investigations into cryptocurrency scams.

Headlines: Tesla's Model 3 review falls short of Consumer Reports endorsement
Description: Consumer Reports on Monday said that flaws with Tesla Inc's  Model 3 sedan prevented it from earning its recommendation.

Headlines: Carl Icahn files lawsuit against AmTrust, controlling family
Description: Activist investor Carl Icahn filed a lawsuit on Monday against AmTrust Financial Services Inc  and the family that controls the company, accusing them of trying to take the insurer private at the wrong time and at the wrong price.

Headlines: Socially responsible funds dump or rethink Facebook over data privacy
Description: Several socially conscious investment firms are selling or rethinking their Facebook Inc  holdings, unsatisfied by the company's moves to strengthen personal data protection and online safety after scandals involving the improper sharing of users' information.

Headlines: Trump says China to buy more U.S. farm products, offers no details
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday said China had pledged to buy "massive amounts" of American agricultural products but gave no other details about planned commitments from Beijing following U.S.-China trade talks last week.

Headlines: U.S. Commerce chief to travel to China next week: Mnuchin
Description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross will travel to China next week to help finalize a trade agreement after Washington and Beijing reached an initial framework last week, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S.'s Mnuchin: 'Significant' issues remain over NAFTA
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin on Monday said major issues remained in talks between the United States, Mexico and Canada to renegotiate the North American Free Trade Agreement(NAFTA).

Headlines: Aston Martin gears up for more growth ahead of possible flotation

Headlines: Exclusive: BP back on its feet but CEO senses no respite
Description: After the near collapse of his company following the 2010 Gulf of Mexico disaster and a three-year slump in oil prices, BP Chief Executive Officer Bob Dudley is hardly relaxed.

Description: BP  shareholders on Monday approved Chief Executive Bob Dudley's 2017 remuneration package by a more than 96 percent majority.

Headlines: Britain unlikely to investigate Comcast bid for Sky, says minister
Description: Britain said it was unlikely to refer Comcast's  bid for Sky  for a lengthy investigation after an initial review found that the $30 billion offer did not raise public concerns about media ownership.

Description: A European Parliament meeting on Tuesday with Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg will be broadcast live, parliamentary officials and the company said on Monday after controversy over plans for a closed-door hearing.

Headlines: PayPal expands retail payments with $2.2 billion Zettle buy

Headlines: Italy must present Monte dei Paschi exit plan by 2019: CEO tells paper
Description: Italy must present the European Commission with a plan for its exit from lender Monte dei Paschi  by 2019, Chief Executive Marco Morelli told daily Corriere della Sera.

Description: Seven years ago, two middlemen launched civil lawsuits to seek payment for helping arrange a $1.3 billion oil deal in Nigeria.

The Snail White  branding - plus some positive internet reviews - is enough to have Chinese tourists recently lining up to buy the slime-infused product.
